title: Not working.
review: tried many headphones none of them worked. Never gotta return it because it past the time frame. Tossed.

title: About what I expected for the price
review: I'm a broke audiophile so I had to settle for something cheap as my PC speakers were gacking. These seemed like the best solution overall for the lowest price. They are about what I expected. I would recommend them for people in a similar position: If you need cheap speakers but $9.99 ones are going to drive you insane and break your audiophile heart, and headphones hurt your ears and restrict your movement. These aren't good, but for cheap basic PC speakers I can tolerate them until I have the funds to upgrade.

title: Comfortable, clean sound
review:
These are surprisingly comfortable and that's directly related the selection of different sized ear pieces. The physical buttons are easier to use than a phone only or touch sensitive only controls.

Using these earbuds for audiobooks or music while outside doing chores is nice. The sound is crisp and clear even when my phone is 20 feet away. The noise cancelling feature works reasonably well when I'm out in the wind too.

title: Great for traveling
review:
I wanted a light, inexpensive set of earbuds for traveling. Something that lets me do a Zoom meeting on my phone or just listen to music or an audio book on the go.

These are reasonably comfortable and paired easily with both my Pixel and Note 20 phones. The sound quality id perfectly fine for my needs and if I lose this set, it's not a big deal. The battery life 2as still above 50% after a little over an hour.

title: Long battery, reasonable sound
review: These are comfortable enough for my uses and the overall sound quality for music is fine. I am using these out hiking or while working around the barn on chores. The addition of a memory card is certainly useful when you don't want your phone nearby for a bluetooth music link - like when you're cleaning water troughs. Calls are fuzzy though and that was with both a Pixel 5 and a Note 20 phone, so it's the headset rather than the phones or connections. That's not really a deal breaker for me though.

title: Fit well, decent sound & connection
review:
These are inexpensive earbuds that actually work well for basic stuff. The buds do fit in my ears without pressure or pain after an hour.

I primarily listen to audiobooks and 80s Rock or Country music, so I don't know or care about a lot of bass. For my needs, these are working well.

I've only connected them to a Pixel phone and the range is about 20 feet line of sight before I notice any degradation of the connection.

title: Fine for audiobooks
review:
I listen to audiobooks through the day whenever possible. I have a pair of wireless earbuds and wired versions. But my wireless get staticky once they reach a 50% charge level and that drives me nuts.

These are comfortable to wear and the sound quality is fine for books and basic music. Mostly though, the sound does not deteriorate as the battery discharges.

title: Nice sound with classical music and audio books
review:
As a rule, I prefer over the ear headphone style for comfort. But there are circumstances when ear buds are safer and more practical - like riding horses. These buds are better than expected and suit my needs pretty well.

The case is the actual charger and you can charge the buds without the case being plugged in as long as it has residual power. You do need to put the buds into the case at the precise angle or they don't charge. These do come with small, medium and large ear pieces so you can get the correct fit for your ears. I do wish the right and left markers were more obvious and easier to see.

I listen mostly to audio books and country, 80s or classical music. I don't use or care about heavy bass in earbuds at all, so I cannot speak to that performance quality. The do fine with the 80s pop and hard rock and behave nicely with classical music as well. There is an option for noise cancellation - called Through Sound. It actually works and there is a very noticeable difference when it's on. I'm pretty impressed by that. I do not like having to put yet another app on my phone to set these up and get full functionality out of the ear buds.

title: Nice sound for classical music, more comfortable than other earbuds I've tried
review:
As a rule, I don't particularly care for in ear earbuds, I usually choose the traditional headphones instead. These come with different size ear pieces so I was able to get the most comfortable fit I could. They aren't bad and I've been able to wear them for an hour at a time with no real discomfort.

I had no trouble connecting these to my phone and using them working around the barn and horses. The sound quality is good for my needs. I mostly listen to audio books and a mix of country and classical music. Bass isn't a thing really for me. The clarity of sound is decent for Beethoven and current composers like Hans Zimmer.

I've gotten a couple of hours at a time without needing to recharge, but I haven't tried to run them down fully. The charging storage box is very handy. The earbuds can be stored and kept clean and charge at the same time - clever. box

title: Light and easy to use
review: I don't need a headset like this often, typically just a couple of times a week to do a video call with my Mother. The headphones help me block distractions and hear her more clearly. This is a very light weight set and the plastic feels a bit flimsy. I don't expect this to last more than a year with my light use, but in the meantime they do work for my needs.

title: Comfortable, noise cancellation actually works well.
review:
I have a very good pair of Bluetooth Sony earphones with pretty good noise cancellation, but I wanted a second set that could be used with a regular 3mm plug with my phone. Traveling brings enough aggravation without worrying about battery life on one more gadget.

These are very comfortable on the ears for an hour or two while listening to an audio book and my ears don't get hot. These are light enough not to cause cauliflower ear either. I tested the noise cancellation feature both at home with the tv and in a semi truck idling. Those trucks are pretty quiet inside compared to standing next to one outside, but the noise is still there and it impedes sleep if you're not used to it. I'm pretty pleased with how well these block external noise - it's an absolute difference and a little better than my Sonys.

Music is a pleasure with these also. There are adjustments to increase bass etc if you're so inclined. My primary use though is audio books. The full production Audible Originals with a full cast and sound effects are especially nice with these headphones - you can hear the background noises and details clearly and not the dog barking next door. I find myself reaching for these almost every day lately.

title: Nice choice for audiobooks
review:
Sometimes, I like to listen to my audio book in bed while my husband watches TV. In order to avoid disturbing him, I use a fancy pair of noise cancellation earphones that vost several pretty pennies. They work well, but can feel heavy after an hour or two.

This set is a decent substitute that I won't feel bad about breaking/dropping etc. They are extremely light and don't have noise cancellation, but that's fine. The fit is decent and the ear covers are soft and don't feel hot. The sound quality is better than expected - audiobooks are clear and clean. I listened to a bit of country and classical music with these and the music sounds right, but not quite as pure as with my Bose headphones - of course, that's not a fair comparison. Still, these are a good option for basic stuff.

title: Work well in high humidity working outside - stay in place without pinching
review:
I normally avoid in ear earbuds and use wireless headphones or do without. My ears are small and most earbuds hurt within minutes, but I have one really inexpensive set that works ok, but if I'm outside working in the horse barn, they can get sweaty and slippery. These are far better than I expected.

They come with three different size ear bud attachments so you can get the right fit - the smallest set fits me well and they don't pinch or hurt even after an hour of wearing them. The over ear hook isn't hard and it's thin enough to fit over each ear love when with my glasses on. I work with horses and the associated barn chores so that means sweat and lots of movement which can be a problem with earbuds. These have impressed me. After daily use for a week, they haven't fallen off, slipped out of place or lost the connection to my phone despite sweating, shoveling, riding and high heat.

The sound quality is fine for my needs. I listen to mostly audiobooks and some classical music while out with the horses. I can clearly hear the violins vs a harp or French horn without distortion. The only real complaint is when I get a call. I can hear the caller clearly, but they say I sound like I'm in a tin can.

title: Works fine for basic phone calls indoors and audiobook streaming. Battery lasts for hours
review:
I have the Jabra 35 headset also and this one is noticably different with regard to the quality of phone calls, but that's really the only material difference I can find in my day to day use. The other unit does offer some noise cancellation effects that this one doesn't have and people you call can definitely tell the difference. My husband said that he could hear background noise much more clearly when I called him from this 15 than with the 35.

As far as battery life, this thing is really solid. I've used for three hours on two different days without recharging between days. I primarily use it to listen to audiobooks while I'm doing my barn chores and checking fence lines. I have noticed that I'm pretty limited with the distance I can stray from my physical phone before this headset begins to stutter to lose signal - it seems to be about 20 feet with my Sony Xperia phone.

title: Can be uncomfortable for small ears, nice for audiobooks while doing chores
review:
I like the idea of a single ear microphone and little speaker for when I'm out at the horse barn or riding. This unit is significantly better than a really old one I had several years ago. It paired with my Sony Xperia phone in moments without any trouble.

I mostly use this for listening to audiobooks while I do barn chores and the occasional phone call. The sound is decent with calls, I haven't had trouble hearing anyone clearly. The audio books are clear and the volume is fine for my needs - if I were trying to use this in a moving car, it might be a bit too low. My husband says that he can hear me fine on the other end, but he does get more background noise compared to when I just call directly through my phone.

I do think my big Bluetooth headphones have better range than this unit away from my physical phone. I can set my phone on the gate post and ride in the big arena and never lose the signal with the headphones, but this one stutters a bit after I get 20 feet away. I'm not a huge fan of the ear hook - I have small ears and getting any sort of earbuds to fit comfortably can be tricky. This fits, but it takes some finagling to get it just right. In the end, I think my husband will take possession of this for his daily use on the road - it definitely fits his physical ear better.

title: Basic ear buds that simply work. Comfortable to wear while doing barn chores
review:
Sometimes you just need a super basic pair of ear buds that aren't fancy or expensive. I have a pair of high-end, very pricey Bluetooth over the ear headphones for use in the house. But I don't like wearing them working out at the farm or riding horses.

These are very light and work fine with my LG V10 phone for music and audio books. The buds have three different size ear pieces - my ears are a bit small and the small ones fit comfortably. Using these while shoveling horse stalls was nice and the thin cord just tucked away in my jacket pocket. I much prefer doing chores while listening to a book and these allow me not to worry if I drop them or they get damaged.

title: Excellent product  at a good price
review: Nice headphones for a bargain price. Good fit with no cabbage ear after a couple of hours - sound is clear and crisp. Bought these to keep my husband from driving me crazy with the sports at full volume on the television. Worked like a charm!

title: More junk ear buds STOPPED IN 4 months... Same as usual
review: Ok for a few months then as usual the left side STOPPED WORKING!!!! More worthless products (Earbuds)-

title: Dont buy
review: The headphones worked great for the first time. Then after the first charge, the headphones gave my daughter an electric shock and now she scared to use them.

title: Dont buy
review: They were great until after about 2 minths, the left ear stopped working. Then a week after that, the headphones would make my calls drop and control other apps on phon.e

title: Nice looking, but cheaply made
review:
This is my daughter's third MP3 player.
She wanted to try this one, since she loved the look of the design.
We figured how bad can a player be, right?
After seeing hers, my son ordered the same player.

Well, they do play music - for a while.
They also play videos nicely, albeit very small and hard to see.

As of today, with neither one a year old yet, one has had be to be sent back
to Sansa for work (totally locked up and could not even be rebooted). They took a
month to send back a refurb, rather than the one my son sent in with his music on it.

My daughter's lasted a little longer, but does freeze up often.
However, the latest trick is that it has part of the sound going out.
She had purchased four pairs of various headphones trying to get the sound to stop
cutting out, thinking it was the headphone's problem. Nope - turns out, it is the
player. Don't know what is wrong, but one of the stereo sides cuts in and out endlessly.

She'll be shopping for a new one, but it won't be this model anymore.
They are just too cheaply made to last. The technology has been around for a long time now,
and it shouldn't be that hard to make a decent, affordable player.
However, it seems like it might just be too hard for Sansa.

title: Noise cancellation is t great
review: Even at top volume the noise cancellation on this set of headphones isn’t great. With a name like Microsoft I expected more from the product. Since this is about the best set I’ve found for the money I will be keeping them, but it hasn’t been my best purchase this year.

title: Poor Sound Quality
review: Sound quality is very poor. Battery life doesn’t last until lunch at work. When volume is all the way up on iPhone and doesn’t get very loud. Purchased a linklife earbud instead and gave these away.

title: Not Too Bulky / Good Quality
review: Very satisfied from battery life to product quality. The dual drivers are incredible, and allow for lower phone volume with loud music still. They come with extra earbuds in different sizes. Those are an odd material, a little different from standard earbuds. More firm I’d say but nothing wrong with them still. More over, the actually earpiece isn’t bulky and fits very nicely without sticking out of your ear very far. Overall very pleased, worth the extra few bucks I’d normally spend on some earbuds.

title: My first earbuds ...
review:
OK, so I waited awhile before purchasing my first pair of earbuds. I finally decided I needed the so that I could watch videos/etc. while sitting in public spaces (coffee shops, libraries, etc.) without disturbing anyone.

Bear in mind that I'm 71 yrs old and although I spent my career in IT, I was a SOFTWARE person, not hardware. So anything hardware related is always a bit intimidating for me.

These were relatively easy to set up. Pairing with my iPad and iPhone was a breeze. They seem to hold a charge quite nicely. The noise canceling feature is wonderful! Very happy with that.

I'm a classical musician, so I'm kind of picky when it comes to speaker sound, and I experimented these earbuds using a variety of my favorite classical hits. The sound I'm getting is excellent -- a bit surprising as I wasn't expecting it to be as good as it is.

No problems so far -- highly recommended!

title: Best of the group of comparably-priced earbuds ...
review:
I own several pairs of earbuds. I just seem to accumulate them like I do my reading glasses -- several pairs in each room where I tend to use them. Most of mine are in the price range $20-30, so those are the ones I'm using for comparison. Based on that, these new Pioneer earbuds seem to be the best of that group.

I listen mostly to classical music with a smattering of other genres (folk, 1960s-70s rock, Broadway). These provided acceptable performance for all genres, but do seem to lack some low-end bass response. One of my test recordings is the Erich Kunzel/Cincinnati Symphony recording of Tchaikovsky's "1812 Overture" with cannons, and the low-end loss was noticeable. Still, the rest of the sound is excellent, and these will work just fine for my day-to-day listening -- music that I have going on in the background while working on something else. For serious listening, I'll use my over-the-ear headphones.

Good performance for the price. I like these.

title: So far, so good ...
review:
I wanted to give this a good try out, so I took it along on a cross-country train trip, where my iPad was the only way I had to stay in touch.

It weathered the trip quite well. It worked well whether I was using the iPad on my lap (in the train stations during layovers) or on the drop-down table in the sleeping compartment, where I could prop it up using the flap/stand.

My only quibble is the lack of just a bit more space to accommodate a stylus. I use a stylus that has a "toggle" that fits in the earphone jack on the iPad so I don't lose it, and it *almost* fits in snuggled between the iPad and inside case spine, but not quite. The cover won't close quite all the way with the stylus there.

Still, it's an excellent case, and holds up well to a lot of use/abuse.

title: PERFECT!
review: Good looking, sturdy (one heavy all-metal piece; no assembly required!), well-engineered, stylish.  Exactly what I was looking for to protect my expensive wireless headphones.  Couldn't be more pleased.

title: Marketing promises KEPT!!
review:
I'm not a buyer of high-end ear buds. At my age my hearing isn't acute enough to hear much of the nuance of music through headphones, but I do like the sound to be much better than if I were holding a can and string up to my ears. That being said, these are the best earphones I've ever owned. When I first put them on, the bass response actually startled me and the middles and highs were present and clear --without any adjustment to my player. The "stays in your ears" feature actually works; you give them a twist in your ear and they stay put, as well as keeping out sweat. You can hear ambient noise just fine, but unless there's a high wind or other competing sound, you continue to hear the audio just fine.

I don't agree with other reviewers who report that the plastic earbuds fall off easily. I think those reviewers must be actually pulling the buds off to clean them and I don't believe that's the manufacturers' intentions. I clean mine with a mini-fiber cloth well moistened (but not soggy) with rubbing alcohol without removing them from the actual earpieces.

The reason I didn't give these earphone five stars is that there is no inline control --no mute off, or volume control. I like them VERY much, and would buy them again if I needed to replace.

title: This is a high quality canvas & leather bag
review: The quality exceeded my expectations. This is a nice roomy, sturdy bag. Holds pistols, extra magazines, ammo, headphones etc. Perfect to take to the range!

title: A huge hassle to set up.
review: I have a degree in software development and I'm an internet streamer. I spent 8 hours trying to get the sound on this thing to work on any of my apps. I'm still not even sure what it was that finally fixed it. The whole time I was trying to set it up, it would emit a loud scratchy sound for about a second, then be silent for half a second, and this would repeat with the sound getting louder and louder each time. I'm still worried it may have done damage to my headset speakers and my soundbar. Once it started working, it was fine, but getting to that point was a huge hassle.

title: Works for me
review: I’m not really an audiophile but I will say the sound from these seems adequate but not life changing. I will use them for audiobooks and watching movies when I don’t want to disturb my husband. For those purposes I think these will be great. I just got them and they’re easy to pair without the instructions. I cannot speak to the durability or battery life yet but I’ll update. I have never in my life been able to get a pair of earbuds to go in let alone stay in my ears. This is a great new technology for me. I’ll probably invest in a high end pair in the future:

title: Tis Loud! Has great bass & long lasting battery!
review:
Alot of headphones lack good bass and sometimes cuts out, but not this set, these earbuds have great bass without over doing it.

Not a bad price to boot, and they're Skullcandy, nough said

title: Works great
review: I basically bought an earbud for everyone for Christmas. It was just an easy and thoughtful gift. This earbud was no problem setting up. It connects nicely and the sound is very clear

title: Quality for less
review:
These earbuds are very stylish, they fit right into your ears comfortably without falling off when you walk around.
Am absolute gift idea especially for stockings stuffing.
The sound is very clear and the price for the quality of the product you're getting, you cannot beat it

title: Giftable
review: I absolutely cannot function without a bluetooth earbud. I bought this earbud for my car, and it have made graciously made my life easier plus it'll be added as my go to giftable item.

title: Second purchase
review:
This is my second pair of these earbud. The sound is solid clear, no background noise and it is very easy to operate. It also stays on
Definitely a great buy

title: Great buy.
review:
My hubby talked me into buying this. It's a replacement for my broken Samsung earbuds and I am pleasantly surprised on how good it works. No weird sounds plus it's below $100 so it is a win win in my opinion
Update I have bought more of these as presents this holiday season. Loving everybody of it

title: Wasn't what I thought, but was still usable
review: I thought these would be able to be stretched over, like an elastic type closure, to be able to just slide over an existing headphone pad that came loose.  Unfortunately, that is not the case.  However, we still got it to work by totally removing the prior pad and wrestling this one over the earphone part.  It is soft and comfortable and easy to hear out of once put in place.

title: Satisfied customer!
review: Great purchase! This was an awesome addition to my workouts. I'm able to pop these babies in, get in the zone and crush some workouts. It makes time pass by so much faster and jamming to some music makes me work that much harder when you really get into the feel of a song. These earbuds fit snug and comfortably in your ear, the sound quality is awesome (besides the ocassional popped ear muffled noise you get sometimes if they're pushed too far into your ear or not positioned right) and they're super convenient to have! One complaint I have is although it is so nice to be able to play/pause and skip songs with a simple push of a button on the earbuds, you have to press just right if you're trying to skip a song. I usually end up pausing it instead, have to play it again and then skip the song on my phone or smartwl watch. Other than that, I'm super satisfied with my purchase for the quality and price!

title: Well made Earbuds, does the job I ordered them for.
review: I bought these mainly for use at home for using with my iPad.  Sound quality meets my needs so I am happy with them.  The noise cancelling at home does have an effect, but will test them next week on the plane in place of my corded Bose headphones.  It will be nice to reduce the bulky case from my carry on.  Will revise my review if need to after trying them on the plane.  But fairly simple to use for this senior.  Very nice packaging as well.  Reminded me of the apple packs.  But with more color.  :-)

title: Great when working
review: I’ve bought about 10 pairs over the years because the cord tends to get frayed and one side starts cutting out after about four or five months of daily usage. I’m sure a lot of that has to do with the constant tugging and stretching due to the fact I sleep in these, which act as both headphones and sleep mask. Despite this, I keep buying them because I’ve yet to find any other headphones as comfortable to wear in bed.

title: SERVICEABLE HEADPHONES FOR THE PRICE
review: I've had these headphones for 2 years now up to the date of this review. Inexpensive and adequate but obviously not for the audiophile! Light so they don't hurt your ears after long wear. Dynamic range is within it's price range. A reasonable value for a knock around set of headphones. The vinyl coating over the ear covers has worn off on both sides and the covering flakes off onto you when you wear them. I guess it might have been affected by how I must put them on and off. Still using them and they still provide adequate sound.

title: Doesn't Stay Plugged in Most Devices - Not Comfortable
review:
I purchased this for my son, to replace his previous headphones, because he had nibbled through the cord sheathing. I liked that this was cheaper, cute, and had one wire off one of the ear pieces, instead of the kind that look like a necklace that come from each ear and rest on your chest. I started using these headphones on his E-Reader and it just doesn't stay plugged in, because the L-shaped plug doesn't allow it to go in far enough, and it easily pulls/falls out. Now, I am going to go buy the slightly more expensive, but much better quality Kidz Gear headphones. I couldn't have known that this was really going to be an issue, until I got them, so I just wanted to help let others know.

My son, today, after using the headphones for the first time of more than 20 minutes, he declared, "These are hurting me." So, my four year old would like to add that to this review, as well. He was always really comfortable in the other headphones, even able to fall asleep with them on (even though they look bulky, they were even comfortable to me).

title: Great Product and Provides Outstanding Quality for its Price
review: Been searching for reliable headphones for awhile, been an avid user of Beats Headphones (Owned 1 Solos and  2 studios)  for years. Last one broke after 3 years of usage with the occasional wear and tear.  Decided to give these Avantree headphones a shot for its price and i was amazed by how its sounded. title: Very Disappointed In The Sound Quality
review: I had high hopes for this product.  Originally, I purchased 2 to use with a Bluetooth transmitter for my TV.  However, poor latency of the transmitter squashed that plan and I decided to return 1 of the speakers along with the transmitter.  But, when I linked it to my phone and listened to a number of tunes that sound and play well with headphones, the sound was terrible.  Virtually everything I played sounded "muddy".  I tried adjusting the sound with the equalizer in my audio player (MediaMonkey) and it didn't help much.  I even downloaded the speaker's app and that didn't help either.  I made sure the bass boost was off when doing all of this, so that wasn't the cause.  To make matters worse, while playing many of the songs I head only one channel - the other was extremely faint.  And on one instance, a song that wasn't very bass heavy actually made the speaker "rattle".  I'll probably return this speaker also.  It's too bad.  I was considering buying a few for Xmas gifts this year.

title: Noise Canceling Is Useless Outdoors
review: I bought these headphones from an Amazon vendor and am glad I did because I didn't have to pay Amazon's price - $25 higher at the time.  However, if I had to do it again, I wouldn't buy them.  I use my iPod while commuting on public transportation and thought these headphones would be a good replacement for another pair of Sony noise-canceling headphones I had been using for 3 years.  However, when I'm outdoors and have the noise-canceling function turned on, any wind is magnified tremendously.  The function is virtually useless outdoors.  I've resorted to turning the feature off and turning up the volume.  The only other complaint I have with this product is that they're not portable enough.  I may be wrong, but I thought the product features indicated they were foldable - they're not.  This makes carrying them around a little tougher than foldable headphones.  Again, I'm glad I didn't pay full price for these things.

review: Money well spent for this device.  I had an ASUS laptop that had the HDMI port too close to the VGA Port.  Therefore, I couldn't only use one or the other.  I wanted 3 monitors. I decided to give a competitor's cheaper USB3 to HDMI inline converter a try, but it failed horribly. I installed the CD ROM it came with, and it recognized my 2ndary Samsung monitor connected via HDMI instantaneously.  I pushed the limits and tried to use the HDMI and the DVI on the unit at the same time, but couldn't get it working, it's unclear whether they support that modality.  It could be a bad cable or something else I forgot, I didn't fiddle with it too long. USB 3.0 seems to deliver the 60Hz refresh rate, I don't see any lag or ghosting at 1080p, so I am well pleased with the performance.  I plugged my headphones in, and it immediately transferred the audio.  Looks nice, feels like great engineering.  It's been going strong for about 2 weeks now without a hiccup.  I recommended this product to 6 other co-workers.

title: Stereo Bluetooth headsets are way better than they used to be ...
review:
I've only had the August EP650 for a couple days now, and there are a number of quality, comprehensive reviews -- so I thought I would write something specifically from the perspective of someone who hasn't owned a stereo Bluetooth headset since they first came out.

The tech has come a long way, and I'm really quite pleased by how good these are for the price. If you're like me and have a bad recollection of the early days -- with the flaky connectivity and the terrible, tinny sound -- you'll be pleasantly surprised.

Build quality feels pretty decent for the price; comfortable; buttons are easy to find with the headset on, and I've been putting them on while taking public transit, without playing anything, just so I can concentrate on reading, and not the prattle.

So, thumbs up. If you've not been happy with Bluetooth cans in the past and don't want to spend too much to check them out again, the August EP650 is a very good option.

title: comfortable, good sound, sits securely over ears, plenty of options, very pleased
review:
LOVE these over the ear air conduction earphones. I have a pair of bone conduction earphones that I fell in love with, and I wanted another pair of different style to for use when working out (my others stay at bedside for evening podcast listening, music, meditation). These looked like they hook over the ear securely, and they do! If new to this style, be prepared to play around with them a bit, and take advantage of the ear plugs as they help deepen the sound. I personally find the sound to be good and clear. I have some auditory sensitivities, and these just feel right- no irritations, aggravations, or off sounds.

The reason why I dont use IN ear ear buds is because they always bother me- usually pain or some headache or nausea ensues. I can wear them for short periods of time as needed, but I do not enjoy them for longer duration- ie listening to music while working out. I can never find just regular headphones that hook over the ears without going in. So that is basically how I got to know bone conduction. Now that style is my go to. I also like that I can still sense/hear what is around me with these, again perfect for working out. Being waterproof puts me at ease when I sweat profusely.

Pair with a bluetooth MP3 player, or add to memory card for direct play through the headset.

Good price, good quality, so far really good experience. I recommend!

review:
THE GOOD:
-------------
* My daughter loves unicorns, and the color pink. These fit her nicely, and she says they are snug and comfy.
* Decorative changeable stickers.
* Volume-limiting circuitry. You can set it at 94db, 85db, or 75db for toddlers.
* Connect wirelessly -Up to 20 hours on one charge, or use the headphone cables.
* USB-C charging port. This is generous and puzzling, since they have a $100 headphone that has micro-usb, which is antiquated and prone to damage. Go figure that their cheaper headphones have the better charging port.
* Study mode feature enhances vocals. So if your children are listening to a lesson plan, the teachers voices will have more clarity.

THE BAD:
-----------
* The price tag. They sell high end headphones. At $50, this is actually their more affordable lower tier products. Even still, there are way more economical options on the market. We'll go 4-Stars overall.

review:

THE BAD:
-----------
-The price tag. Wow! There are other headphones that claim these features, but do not charge this type of price. So the verdict is still out. I'll need to see how long these headphones last.
-Micro usb charging port? It's 2021, and you're charging $100, yet you can't do USB-C? Micro usb cables are prone to damage and have dominated electronics for way too long. USB-C is finally taking over, and for $100, I was surprised to see micro usb.

review: These are a nice set of affordably priced headphones. The headphones are comfortable and the sound reproduction is very good. I got these for my daughter who prefers them to ear buds. title: Great For Television or Computer
review:
I got this product because I like to ride my stationary bicycle while I watch a film on my computer. In the past, I used a set of headphones for audio. However, the cable was cumbersome and got in the way. With this product I can listen to my computer without having annoying wires interfering with my enjoyment of the film.

The headphones are high quality and feature great sound reproduction. The purchase price includes headphones, a transmitter, a power cable, a micro USB charging cable, an RCA converter cable, a digital optical cable, and a 3.5mm audio cable. The USB cable can be used to charge the headphones, or you can use the transmitter which features a headphone cradle.

I elected to connect this to my computer with the 3.5mm audio cable and it works great. The headphones have a volume key which is easy to operate while you're wearing them. This is a high quality item that is comfortable to wear and provides good sound. The packaging is also very attractive which makes this a thoughtful gift idea.

title: Great Concept, Solid Execution
review:
I like to listen to audio books as I go on bike rides, so I've been looking for a product like this. When I run I use over the ear headphones, but I can't fit those on over or under my cycling helmet. These sunglasses are a great solution. There are speakers underneath the arms that broadcast music almost directly into your ears. The effect is an open ear speaker system that allows you to hear your music, but also lets you stay mindful of ambient noises.

The sunglasses have enough of a tint to be comfortable, but not so much that they are impractical in low light. The arms rest easily on your ears and the nose piece is a solid bit of plastic that does not pinch the bridge of your nose. The glasses are very light even with the battery and speaker system.

The sunglasses connect to your cell phone via Bluetooth without any issues. There is a large power button on the right arm that is easy to locate by touch. I preferred these for comfort and for sound quality to ear buds. The sound quality is about what you'd expect for tiny speakers mounted to the arms of sunglasses. It's not concert hall quality, but it gets the job done, and it's better than a lot of other speakers on the market.

These sunglasses are great for athletes who like to listen to music while they're out exercising. Also included is a case, a bag, a lens cloth, and a charging cable.

Those things still work after all these years which is a testament to this company's quality.

title: My favorite soundbar!
review:
I've tested a few soundbars for Amazon and this by far is my favorite! I'm actually giving away my old ones and putting this one front and center with my 65" tv permanently! Very impressed!

For music- it definitely gets PLENTY loud. It has a little bit of a thump to it bass wise, about what you'd expect from a soundbar. Not going to vibrate your walls off but not extremely weak. You can feel the little speakers pumping air out if you put your hand in front of them which is pretty cool!

For tv- it had me put the headset thing on and move around the room to calibrate it. I did this and then watched a couple movies. VERY impressed with this for watching movies too!

Overall this is just a fantastic bar!! I don't want speakers all over my living room taking up space and junking up the place so I wanted one nice soundbar and this certainly fits the bill for that! It's a very sleek looking long soundbar that gets as loud as I'd ever need it to and gives me a good clear quality audio. My only room for improvement would be to offer a matte finish, I hate the glossy top as it'll show scratches later. My easy workaround? Just get a roll of good quality vinyl in your choice of color and carefully cut it to fit! We did this and now we have a neon green topped bose soundbar! Love it!

Definitely grab this soundbar and give it a try!

title: Vivid beautiful clear picture- amazing tv for the price!
review:
Beautiful bright, sharp, vivid picture from this tv! Has very deep nice blacks which is something I always look for. Google setup on this is easy and the A frame legs are easy to put on. Tv was pretty easy to wall mount and looks beautiful on the wall!

The sound is really good, I don't even need to use a soundbar with this tv! I love the acoustic auto calibration- you sit on the couch and start it- it blasts sound in several directions thru the speakers and the mic on your remote picks it up and adjusts the sound based on where you're sitting and what kind of room you're in. Another amazing sound feature is the bluetooth they added in on this one, you can use bluetooth headphones with this!

The motion on it is pretty decent, it has enhanced motion features you can turn on for say sports and gaming but for regular tv watching, you won't want them on. This tv can adjust the brightness based on the lighting in the room which is impressive.

Tv switches between apps and thru the apps extremely smoothly! Overall I think this is an amazing tv packed in at a really modest price that won't send you to the poor house! If you have a higher budget and want top of the line, check out Sony's 90J series which is a step up from the 80J. But on a budget- this tv will certainly make you happy, it's an amazing machine!

title: Good Overall
review:
I use these for work, 8 hours a day in a work from home call center. I have a large head and am a big guy. The sound is fantastic for voice communication, I would never use these for gaming, music or multimedia. The audio range is not good enough for those applications, it is great for voice. The microphone works beautifully and others can hear me clearly and crisply.

To say that these are "passive" noise cancelling is laughable. There is really no such thing as passive noise cancelling, it's just how much noise is blocked out by wearing the headphone. Do not take that into consideration when buying headphones, unless they totally cover the ear. You can hear everything going on around you.

The ear pads are pretty comfortable, much more than a foam ear pad on standard headphones. I do need to pull these away from my ears every now and then to restore circulation and reduce soreness. Durability of the pad itself is in question, but I have not had these long enough to figure that out. First impression is the pad might last 6-12 months using 5 days a week for work. To me the pads seem to be a weak spot durability speaking.

Overall a great headphone for work. If these had active noise cancelling and a more comfortable/durable ear pad, they would be perfect. I have no experience with microphone filtering yet.

review: These were basic earbuds. They worked fine for the price. I could hear them ok. They were not as adjustable as they could've been. They are small and easy to carry. Convenient for a plane or somewhere you don't have a lot of space.Overall a decent buy.

title: Great for kids
review: I don't care for earbuds for my kids so I really like these over the ear headphones. All my kids need these for school. title: These are great headphones. They really stop outside noise thanks to ...
review: These are great headphones.  They really stop outside noise thanks to the great padding, and they aren't tight enough to cause me pain.  One note:  the cord is hard to connect the first time, it needed to be pushed in at a particular angle and turned to lock in place.  I don't read instructions, and I almost sent these back as defective because only the right channel was working and it was going in and out as I moved.  My face is red, hopefully this review stops your face from being red too!

title: Decent Headphones If You Have Cold Ears!
review: Here's the thing:  I have earbuds (expensive ones that are amazing) which are about the same as these headphones.  So why so big?  Are you trying to keep your ears warm?  Because these do!  But that being said, the audio quality (speaker and mic) is excellent.

title: Not The Best On The Market, But Decent
review: I don't normally wear a gaming headset, but I tried one and it was convenient.  Handsfree does have it's advantages.  As far as the quality goes, it isn't a $500 Sennheiser headset.  But it isn't a $10 no-name one either.

title: Terrible case for the HS700
review: I have the HS700 and this case (because it isn't rigid) constantly presses the button, putting the headset into discovery mode.  This should have been an aluminum hard case with room to keep that from happening.  You could also call that a design flaw in the headset, but either way you should get the combination of this case with that headset!

title: Saved my headset
review:
These SOULWIT Cooling-Gel Ear Pads Cushions were not made for my headset, which is a USB gaming headset by [[ASIN: B01E8RS598 Sades]], which is no longer being sold.

Ear cups are pretty much the first thing to go on a headset and unless you have an expensive brand, it is hard to find a replacement cup for your specific headset. After two years of use, the cup of my gaming headset was falling apart and leaving little bits of plastic on my face after I use it. Rather than throwing away the headset, I wanted to try and find something that might work with it. I got lucky with this SOULWIT ear cup. It is attached via a stretchable flap, which is exactly how my old cups attached to the headset.

As you can see from my pictures, the shapes of the cups weren't the same as the originals had an odd angle to them but in the end, they fit and they are really comfortable.

The material is glossy on the sides, but where it touches your head, it is a soft cloth. I don't sweat a lot when I wear these so sweat being absorbed into the cup isn't an issue here, but I can see where someone who sweats will have problems with it. The gel is soft and comfortable.

I really love the new cups and the fact that I'll get more years of use out of my headset.

title: Survived the wash, but I wouldn't suggest that you try it yourself!
review:
These Omidyi True Wireless Sleep Earbuds are my second pair because I accidentally threw my previous pair in the wash. Surprisingly, my original pair survived and this pair is now my backup.

Here is my original review:
These earbuds aren't bad at all, if you use earbuds to fall asleep. The advantages these earbuds have over wired ones are, of course, the wires. I used to go through wired sleep earbuds fairly quickly because I tend to pull on them quite a bit when I sleep. There are no wires to tangle here.

What makes these earbuds "sleep" earbuds are that they are much smaller than normal wireless earbuds (see my picture). They sit flush in my ears and don't protrude. In general, depending on your ears, these may actually allow you to lay sideways and still be comfortable. In my case, I can lay against my right ear without it hurting me but I can't do the same with the left. I often end up using only the right bud.

In terms of sound quality, due to their size, these earbuds will not be loud nor will they have great sound depth. The battery life also lasts about 5 hours due to their size.

I still really like these buds because I do like them more than wired ones but I don't use them any other time.

title: Not bad for sleeping but won't replace other earbuds
review:

title: Simple pair of earbuds that work well for video conferencing
review:
These SUYUZREY 3.5mm Jack Wired Earbuds were for my daughter who needs it for her laptop when she is doing video conferencing during her group study sessions. This means that sound fidelity wasn't the primary purpose for their purchase.

These earbuds are comfortable for extended study sessions and with the included memory foam ear pieces, there's a good variety of sizes and comfort. Voices come through clearly and the microphone works well, but of course suffers the same problem as any other on-wire microphone: It can be a little far from the mouth and rubbing against the cloth can creating noise.

There isn't much else to say about a simple pair of earbuds like these.

title: All-Metal.  That's good and bad...
review:
I listen to audiobooks to fall asleep at night so I wear "sleep" earbuds as to not disturb my wife. I usually buy the soft silicone type, which never have good audio quality, but does the job. They usually break withing a couple of months because I tend to tug on them a lot when I sleep so this time, I decided to try out these ceramic Wired Headphones with Microphone.

My initial impressions of these earbuds are that they have better sound quality than the other sleep earbuds that I've tried. They also have excellent build quality. There are silicone reinforcements at all of the wire connection points to protect them from failing due to tugging and the shape of the earbuds are as flat as possible.

When in my ears, these metal earbuds do not protrude at all, they lie flat. I tested by lying on my side to see if they would hurt but they seemed okay because nothing protrudes. Then after a couple of nights, I found that while direct downward pressure doesn't hurt, the earbuds do hurt when they are nudged from side to side, which happens when I'm shifting positions at night.

So overall, I'm still using these earbuds and have gotten used to them, but they do still hurt occasionally, depending on how much I move at night.

title: These are NOT bone conduction headphones
review:
The only thing these headphones have going for it is a respectable battery life. Everything else is just a disappointment, unfortunately.

I've been trying to find a good but affordable pair bone conduction headphones because I keep a headphone on my head almost all day while I work and write my code but I end up shutting the rest of the family out and miss half of the conversations going on in the house. When I discovered open ear bone conduction, it seemed to be the perfect solution.

So far, I have not found a good one. The specific problems of this pair of headphones is that it is not bone conduction. It is a simple pair of speakers set next to your ear. There is no bone shaking going on. With bone conduction, you can put in earplugs and still hear the audio fairly clearly, with these, the sound is clearly muffled and hard to make out.

In addition, there is a half-second delay on these headphones meaning they are no good for watching videos. I have not experienced bluetooth delay in quite a few years so I wasn't expecting it. Further, there is no charging light, meaning there is no way to tell if they are charged or not.

Then there's the price they are charging for this thing. Everything is just NO.

title: Broken on first day.  Do NOT charge without first turning off the device
review:
I received my Tayogo Wireless Bone Conduction Open-Ear Headphones this morning and used it the entire day. While the sound quality isn't as good as a true on-ear headphone or earbuds, the advantage of a bone conduction headphone is the ability to keep your ears open to your surroundings. It was exactly what I needed.

It was a little bit odd to feel the bass vibrating my head at first, but I soon got used to it. I really did like this style of headphones.

At the end of the night, I plug the headphones in and I see the charging light come on. A couple of seconds later, it goes off and from then, I couldn't get any response from the headphone at all. No matter how long I try to hold the power button, it just won't turn on.

I realized that I forgot to first turn off the headphones before plugging it in. I believe that may be what caused the problem.

Quite disappointed to have a device work only for 1 day.

title: Very good value for Active Noise Cancelling headphones.
review:
I don't know how it happens but I somehow ended up buying over 20 pairs of bluetooth headphones over the course of my life. I'm also finding that I can't pass up a good pair of bluetooth headphones.

So of the over-head style bluetooth headphones, I've run across problems with short battery life (had one pair that lasts only 3 hours), too tight against the head, presses on the ear (supra-aural) and gets sweaty, active noise cancelling that can't turn on independently of the bluetooth function, and no carrying case.

This pair of RCA Active noise cancelling headphones don't have any of those problems. I sit at my desk all day with an air outlet behind me that is constantly blowing. I'm able to use them the entire day with music playing without the batteries running down. I don't keep the noise cancelling on the entire time but when I do, the fan noise is completely blocked out. Being circumaural headphones, the ear cups completely surround my ears and do not press on them. In addition, the spring isn't too tight to make me feel like my head is being squeezed in a vice.

As far as sound quality, because the speakers are not pressing against the ear, the sound seems to have a wider-room feel, making me feel even more like I don't have headphones on.

Overall, I'm quite satisfied with this purchase and don't feel the need to splurge and buy the much more expensive Sony and Bose products.

title: I love to be hands free in the car and a ...
review:
I live in a tourist town and at all times there is traffic. I can't tell you the amount of wrecks I see daily just due to people being preoccupied with their cell phone.

I love to be hands free in the car and a big way to accomplish that is with a Bluetooth headset.

Likes:
*Easily syncs with phone
*Rings through the headset to alert of incoming call
*Push to answer/disconnect directly on the headset
*comfortably sits in the hear
*Sound quality is clear

Dislikes:
*I've been told it sounds like I am on speakerphone when wearing the headset but I am still able to be understood by my callers

Overall this is a nice headset I would recommend it for anyone that travels or needs to be handsfree.

I received this product at a discount to review. My assessment is my own after prolonged personal use.

title: I like volume with my music
review: Why the 4 stars you say? Well, frankly, I like volume with my music.  I really hoped with the Harmon Kardon signature sound that  the sound would be dynamic; it's just not. I'm not even a huge bass head, but I like to be allowed to have a decent amount and it just doesn't get loud enough. Also, the Tone Pros (the next model down) have true noise reduction; these do not. On both models however the sound on phone calls is the best I've ever experienced. I really like the retractable concept; I found with the LG Tone Ultras that the dangling of the earbuds got caught in things, and I like that I can wear the Infinium around my neck and retracted while waiting for the next call.

review:

As with any ear pad tips you’ll have to figure out what size fits you best. I’ve found the medium size fit me best. After I figured that out I ordered another set in all medium size so I could switch out all my ear bud tips.

title: EXCELLENT 10’ CHARGING CABLES
review:
Now there are so many devices that are charged via a USB plug that are not phones. Flashlights, battery chargers, portable electronics, headphones, remote controllers, hand held video game systems, it seems more and more products are going to having a built in battery that is recharged in this way making having dependable cables critical.
