At first I was skeptical as I own a pair of Bose QuietComfort i20's (the noise canceling earphones at $323.98, (CA tax included)), and wanted to compare the two. To my surprise, they are as the internet (collectively) said it does sound like a more expensive pair of earphones. The sound quality on these KZ's are quiet nice and hold a better base than my beloved Bose do but, for me, they do tend to fall out when not in a stationary position, i.e. walking around, running, biking, etc. They look like they cost more also, feels expensive and have a reassuring weight to them. Overall, these are a good buy and well worth it compared to more expensive earphones. (I also recommend the Bose, noise cancelation is worth it when the world gets a bit too overwhelming and all you want is some peace & quiet.. and music.)

title: Amazing Product, but Just "Good" Noise Cancelation
review:
The build quality, sound quality, wireless connection strength, and battery life of these headphones is incredible. I think that they are the best value headphones I've every bought. They sounds as good as my Senn HD280s.

The only downside is that the active noise cancellation doesn't work nearly as well as some systems I've tested (Here One Earbuds, Airpod Pro, Bose QC), but does cut out most consistent noise.

title: Great budget earbuds
review:
EDIT: One of the earpieces developed a loose connection. I contacted MEElec and they exchanged them for free in 4 days! I'm quite impressed by their level of customer service.

This is the first time that I've purchase earbuds after doing research, and boy am I glad that I did. These blow the SkullCandy and Samsung earbuds that I've had out of the water and compete with the Sennheiser overear headphones I've heard.

Sound:
Good balance, a little bass-heavy surprisingly
Treble is good, but could be a little sharper (cymbals sound slightly sloppy)
But those are just if I'm being nit-picky, they sound spectacular.

Build:
Nice case
Plenty of rubber earpieces for best fit
Look nice
Had a sharp edge that I had to sand off, but that would never touch my ear.

title: Don't believe the hype!
review: I got these because many commenters said the sound quality is good and they're super comfortable. Well, I call BS because the sound quality was what I expected from a cheap headset (read: crap) and the earpieces were too heavy on my ears. Returning and would not recommend.

title: Fits tightly into Shure SE215, light, flexible, good quality, great sound
review:
I needed a cable for my SE215 earbuds, and after looking at what was available, decided to get these. I'm quite happy I did: the fit into the SE215 is nice and snug, the 3.5mm is also good, and the cable appears to be well-constructed. The sound is excellent. (The sound source is VLC Player rendering FLAC and MP3 audio files, coming through my computer's usb port via a FiiO BTR30Pro in DAC mode.)

I'm not convinced that for the low currents needed for earbuds all this 6-core/8-core stuff makes a difference, so I think any good quality cables would be fine. But the MMCX fit matters a lot: I had a cable that didn't fit tightly into the SE215, and that meant I had problems whenever my head moved ... ugh! So just for that reason I'd pay up for a decent cable.

title: The sound is excellent, the features are convenient, but I found it not too comfortable to wear
review:
I really like these headphones at first: the Soundcore app made them easy to configure and update, and in LDAC mode the sound was very very good. So that was great. But then I found that I couldn't wear them for long periods, and this might just be me, your mileage will definitely vary. I wear glasses, and after a while over-the-ear headphones can make my outer ears hurt, and can make them hot. (I have a pair of gaming headphones that I use for conference calls, that are a bit more comfortable, but even those I can wear for about an hour at most.)

So I'm rating these 4 stars, giving them full credit for sound and convenience, and taking a point off for discomfort, although that might just be a personal thing.

title: Good optical audio cable
review:
I had to laugh when I saw the gold tips on this cable: while gold connectors might make sense on cables that carry electrical signals (analog or digital), they're irrelevant for optical cables, the tips are just the mechanical connection into the socket which aligns the optical fiber-ends. So there's no difference between this tip and the black tip of other cables like this (such as the Amazon Basics one).

That said, this cable does fit into the proper sockets just fine, and works as well as the other such cables I've tried. I used it to connect my SBX4 sound card with an Fiio BTA30Pro DAC, and listened to it with earbuds as well as external speakers, didn't experience any problems. I didn't expect, and didn't perceive, any audio superiority to the Amz Basics optical cable I had been using, so there's no reason there to prefer one over the other. Physically though this one is just a bit more stiff, so I tend to prefer the more pliable Amz cable. If that's not a concern, I would recommend buying whichever is available and cheaper.

title: Excellent sound (with LDAC)
review:
I like the sound of these earbuds way more than I expected: they're clean and clear through my hearing range, and I didn't even have to fiddle with the EQ settings to get there. I also have the Liberty 2 Upgraded version, and while those are very good, these are clearly superior.

I did use the Soundcore app to update the firmware and enable LDAC: you'll definitely want to do this before you begin using them. Also, there are other settings on the app you might find useful.

They are also very comfortable to wear for long periods (I use them at my desk while working), and even using LDAC (which uses a lot more power) the battery lasts as long as I've needed so far. The case is nice and compact, and of course charges the earbuds quickly. The only thing I would grumble about (and now I'm being very fussy) is that I have to turn the earbuds over to get them into the right position for the case.

Another note: Anker was offering a "used like new" item for a much lower price, so I decided to try them. I'm very happy I did, since they really were just like a new product, seemed unused (probably a quick return). All the earpiece bits were new, of course.

Highly recommended for excellent sound and comfort at a very affordable price (new or used).

title: Works well, easy way to connect 3.5mm connector to RCA stereo connectors
review:
I needed to connect my desktop speakers (with the usual 3.5mm audio plug) to a DAC's RCA connectors, and this little product worked perfectly. It's hard to get picky about the sound from your basic desktop speakers but these work as well as I would expect: certainly the improved sound I get from my Sound Blaster X4 carries through just fine.

An alert reader would note that I could have connected the 3.5mm plug directly to the SBX4, and I did do that at first, but there were convenience reasons for me to move the plug to the DAC: this way I can just use one device to determine whether I'm listening to my headphone or letting the sound go to the speakers. (TMI for more people, I think.)

title: Very nice product, but documentation is pretty limited
review:
This is a very nice package, containing a decent DAC with a bluetooth receive/transmit capability (supporting AptX HD and LDAC). Now that I have it set up and connected, I'm very happy with the sound quality, both through the stereo amp to speakers, and through bluetooth headphones using LDAC. For the price, this is really an excellent value, I haven't found anything else nearly as good for this price.

Setup is a bit involved and tricky, and the documentation is quite poor. (Fiio has this reputation.) I hooked it up to my computer using USB, to update the bluetooth & DAC firmware. Then I used the Fiio Control app on my phone to complete the setup, choosing the desired EQ settings and BT codecs. Pairing the headphones was a bit tricky: I found very sketchy instructions on their forum (there's also a Youtube video), which worked after several tries.

But the end result is that I have excellent results for a very moderate price. So if you're a bit technically inclined and not afraid of doing some digging and figuring things out, check this product out. I would recommend it highly.

title: Excellent earbuds, great sound
review:
These earbuds are really very good. The sound is balanced and clear, and it's a pleasure to use them to listen to all kinds of music, from classical to rock/pop to country. They're more than adequate for phone calls and online conferences. They're pretty comfortable to wear: I have a difficult time with most earbuds, especially with the ones that need a large hard object sitting inside the earlobe, so I might wish these were a tad softer, but really I haven't had any trouble wearing them for an hour or so.

The little charge case is nicely made, and very easy to use. I use it for more than an hour or two per day, and at that level I think the box only would need charging every few days, making it pretty convenient.

Are they worth the price? I got these from the VIne program, so price wasn't a consideration for me, and I haven't compared these with other items in a similar price range. The sound is better than some very nice earbuds I have that cost quite a bit less, so at least I can say that they're delivering some value for the extra money.

title: Waste of money: poor sound, controls are difficult to use, lacks mute function
review:
This was a mistake. It's a pretty bad headset overall. Despite adjustment, the sound is poor, and makes it really hard to carry on a conversation with the echoing hollow sound effects. The controls are, at least for me, nearly impossible to use while wearing the headset, and not all that good even when it's off. And, to add a last kick, it lacks a convenient mute function: this is just absurd to me.

I recommend going quickly past this one and considering other headsets instead.

title: very nice headset, excellent sound
review:
I've used this headset quite a bit over the last few weeks, for work-related conference calls. Although I really like my tiny BlueAnt headset for casual use, I find myself reaching for this one for the ease-of-use convenience and better sound.

Firstly, the setup and the usage is quite well designed, as simple as it could be. I was suspicious of the voice prompts & messages ("phone connected", "answering call", etc.), but have found them quite useful and not at all intrusive.

I find the cord attaching the control pod (has on/off, volume control, and mute button) is a bit too long for my tastes, but some might need a longer one, so can't complain. The controls themselves are very useful to have where you can see them, you don't have to try to find something behind your ear to manipulate while you're on a call.

The sound is excellent: what I hear is always very clear. What others hear, whether I'm in a somewhat noisy room, or in a car, is also reported to be very clear, I've never had to raise my voice or repeat myself. BTW, the mic boom swivels out of the way easily when needed.

I'd give it 4.5 stars perhaps, with half a star off for my personal discomfort with a large-ish earpad (makes my ear hot after a while). But that's nit-picking, and probably won't bother many people.

title: excellent sound
review:
4.5 stars -- see below.

These headphones have excellent sound, as good as or better than a more expensive headset I have. If you line in-ear headphones, these are definitely worth your consideration. I use them with my computer and my ipod and my Droid, find them quite satisfactory -- I've stopped using my other headphone.

The reason I docked a star (should really be half) is that the default earpieces were not comfortable for me. I don't know if that's just my ear -- but they just felt wrong, even apart from the size. I changed them out for another pair (several are provided), and happiness was restored.

title: excellent bluetooth headset, good sound, nice multi-phone feature
review:
This is an excellent headset -- I have to say that I'm puzzled by all the negative reviews. (Which did make me hesitate for a bit.)

The pairing works, and easily, and the first time. I paired it with my Samsung Renown, and my iPhone GS, and now when I turn on the headset, it pairs up with both phones (as promised), answers whichever one is ringing or connects with the one being used for a call.

The sound is clear at both ends, without any of the ugly distortions you sometimes get with such devices.

I like it, am happy with the purchase, and consider it a great value at under $40. I continue to be happy with every BlueAnt product I've acquired.

title: works fine, but uncomfortable
review:
I've had this headset for about a year now; I use it with a Razr. It's a fine headset from a technical perspective: the sound is fine, it's easy to pair and use, etc. I haven't run into any problems using it in a car, or out of doors.

However, it's really not very comfortable: the hook that goes over the ear is just a bit too stiff and edgy, I wouldn't want to wear it for a long call (more than 15-20min say).

For comfort and performance, consider the Plantronics Voyager 510 (around $50 at Amazon); I've had one of those (now used by my son), and it is excellent. If you're into new gadgets, check out the Jawbone sets -- I haven't used one, but a colleague swears by the one he's been using for a couple of months.

title: very uncomfortable, poor volume
review:
I recommend AVOID. This item is poorly designed -- it's very uncomfortable (the ear-hook is odd and stiff, there is no soft cushion against the ear), the volume is poor and can't be adjusted much, and the cord for some odd reason comes out on the inside of the mike boom. (Whose brilliant idea was that?)

I can't explain all the great reviews, which induced me to buy this, so I won't even try.

Consider the M175 if you want a really nice headset at a reasonable price.

title: Lovely listening for your ears!
review:
I have had all sorts of earbuds, but must admit for the price these are simply wonderful--and absolutely beautiful! I tend to listen while sitting or lying down, and these have wonderful sound for such use. I also love the simple beauty of the wood.

On the other hand, I am not so sure these would be the best choice if you are jogging or working out --- they might not stay put.

So bottom line, if you are not working out and relatively still I think you will love these! Superb sound and a great price!

title: The item does not work for me
review: The item does not work for me. The microphone only moves at 45 degrees. Meaning I can't change sides of the headset. My PC seats on the right side, so the cable is strangling me...

title: Poor Sound Quality
review: Nice headset but the sound quality is garbage... Very muffed and no distinction between trebke and bass. Just horrible. Paid for what I got I guess...

title: What's not to like.  EXACTLY as described!  Great product
review: Great little product.  Built very sturdy, and a great little item for putting headphones.

title: Perfect!!
review: I needed these to replace the original covers on 2 sets of earbuds that I got as gifts. They fit PERFECTLY. Excellent quality.

title: Very good
review:
These headphones are absolutely amazing for what you pay!
The sound is great, and the value is unbelievable.
I recommend these to everyone !

title: Kimwoodwiredearbuds
review: I really like these.  I chose these because I can't use the wireless ones or the gummy earbud types. Great sound for the price. I adjusted the equalizer on my player and I heard music that I haven't heard on buds in this price range.

title: ok for the price. Like the style
review: They were a gift  for someone for their first pair of wireless earphones. I wanted ones with this style of earbud rather than ones that are rubbery.They were easy to pair with a cell phone.I thought the sound was average. .  The recipient thought the sound was ok and endorses them.

title: Good for the price
review: A little more expensive than average earbuds. These are comfortable in the ear and block out a good part of sound. Nicely packaged, with instructions.  Good sound, would have to pay a lot more for better sound. Suggestions: make cord a little easier to handle (non-tangle); offer in white (if not doing so already). Thanks for the earbuds.

title: Made for small/narrow faces; otherwise fine
review:
I bought these on sale without, and I can't quite bring myself to return them because they are otherwise serviceable, but they feel quite tight on my head and there's no proper way to adjust them out, just longer or shorter. Because these are on ear headphones, that lack of adjustability means that my ears are smashed pretty tightly against my head and quickly become uncomfortable and warm. For reference, my head is between 21" and 22" around at the top of my ears... which appears to be average per Google.

TLDR: If you are an adult with an average size head, these may not be as comfortable a fit as you'd expect.

title: Amazing!!!
review: Simply amazing! Don’t hesitate! Very loud with amazing clarity of sound. The base is unbelievable for this small earbuds. I still didn’t check Buttary life but it look like amazing product. The charging box of and the earbuds looks like a high-quality and very cool looking. I’m super happy!

title: Softest  cussion on me ears
review: These headphones are soft and non-sweating. I wear these all day to talk on my phone , and listing on social media. Most headsets tend to make my ears sweat after wearing them to long..but not these. They Light weight and foldable.and the sound is evenly distributed in both ears. Love them

title: Did NOT Work on Jabra earbuds
review: The fact that they did not work isn't the product's fault.  I should have done better research.  They were never meant to fit my earbuds. I simply didn't know enough at the time I ordered them.  I returned them.

title: UPDATE:  Oh YEAH...but, uhmmm
review:
Incredible sound. I can't take them off!!

UPDATE: I had been enjoying these earbuds up until a few nights ago. I was removing them when the bud in my right ear came apart, in pieces, as I removed it. What a shocker! There were telltale signs of glue (small, short strands) that might indicate not enough glue was used during assembly. Nevertheless, I am returning them and ordering another pair. The sound is as good as my $89 pair of Klipsch earbuds I had a few years ago.

title: Grado SR60's are Totally AWESOME
review: I recently purchased the Grado SR60 headphones after spending hours reading online reviews of headphones. I decided to try Grado and I am so glad I did. The sound on my IPOD is incredible--it sounds like I am in a concert hall at a live concert. And they have a 1/4 plug for your stereo/surround system. I watched SpiderMan and listened with my Grados. DAMN! I am really excited about this purchase. And the bass is great, too. Comfortable? I don't know why people complain. I put my Grados on at 2:00PM and listened to music on my IPOD and watched movies until 8:00pm. I found them totally comfortable. I did not experience any pain or discomfort. This is a great product. I highly recommend them.

title: pretty good
review: These actually worked better than i expected. They are very thin so you can still put your earbuds in the case to charge without taking them off. I didn't have a problem putting them on because i read someone else's suggestion of putting them on inside out. My only complaint is that they slip off really easily. I've pulled them off several times just handling the earbud and they are harder to get on when they are not new.

title: Great Headphones at a Great Price Point!
review:
I just discovered that my Moto Phone had a super-cool FM Radio app. But it needs a WIRED headphone to act as an antenna in order to get the most out of the app. All I had were my earbuds so I needed a good set of headphones. I found these and was skeptical but thought I'd give em a go. So glad I did!!

1. Great Sound...really good sound...I added a bass boost equalizer app to my phone and WOW these 'phones really bang.
2.Comfortable fit...could wear em all day if I wanted...
3. Super good price...for $20.00 can't be beat.

Highly recommended!!!

title: Solid headphones for a solid price
review: I like these headphones for their quality and price. I have these and Samsung Galaxy buds. The Galaxy buds win in terms of convenience and features due to me having a Galaxy phone, but the X5 wins in terms of volume and bass. I like to listen to music with bass and the Galaxy buds just don't have that at all, plus noise cancelling is gimmicky on the buds and eventually I have to up the volume to truly drown out all noise, which is easier to do with the X5. Both headphones shine in different respects. When it comes to interacting with my phone I prefer the features provided by Galaxy buds, but when it comes to listening to music and comfort then I prefer the X5, plus the X5 is way more economical. The mic on both for calls were not impressive. They work well enough in a quiet room but when I'm in my car I have to turn off my AC to use them (the AC isn't blowing on my face, they just really pick up on the air blowing around in general). Overall I don't think most people will be disappointed with this purchase.

title: Great headphones for price.
review: Great headphones for the price. You can obviously get better sounding headphones, but you will probably pay a lot more for them. I'm not an audiophile but I do enjoy listening to music. These will give you a solid performance and let you enjoy your listening experience.  5 stars overall for quality and price.

title: This product is junk.  It broke after 1 month
review: Product is junk. Right earbud stopped working.  Only solution was to mail back the product which I don't have time to do. Wouldn't send a new one or refund. Don't waste your money

title: easy to use
review: The video quality of my laptop isn't the greatest, and since I'm on video calls a lot more, I figured I'd give this webcam a try. It comes with its own little tripod (and a cap for the camera), and is so easy to set up (plug in the attached USB cord). The video quality is decent - not the best, but better than my laptop's. The audio quality is... ehhh, you'll probably want to stick with what's available on your pc or use a headset.

title: all right bluetooth headphones for the price
review:
These are a decent set of 'noise cancelling' headphones for the price with bluetooth capabilities. The on-ear headphones are rather small (part of the lower rating) - my husband found them a little uncomfortable for that reason, and if you're moving around they jostle and shift, which means they're not a good fit. I'm smaller and noticed that they didn't give the best coverage, so yes, the size is a problem.

As for the 'noise cancelling' quality - there's a button/switch which produces a low, crackling 'white noise' which helps offset any sound. It's not the best. It does help cancel outside noise, but again, smaller headphones/not total muffling means you still hear some noise. I've other headphones that are larger and more insulating that do just as good a job of not better (but then they also cost more).

You can hook these up directly to a device with the cord or use the bluetooth option. Not too difficult to set up and the range is good. So is the battery life (well over half a day). I'd say these probably will work well for a kid or teen, maybe not too many adults but I could be wrong. You get what you pay for in the end.

title: fancy earbuds
review: These are rather pricey for what they do, which is cord free earphones/buds. The case which holds and charges them (with a USB cord) is rather nice and handy, and lights up (red or green) to let you know when they're charged. They also charge relatively fast, which is good, and have various molds to help ensure a good fit. But yes, you'll be charging these a lot if you use these daily or often, be forewarned. Also, the controls are a little tricky to figure out and you might fumble with them a bit, considering you're pressing the things, basically, no nice cord with clear buttons. The sound quality is decent, not quite what I'd expect for the price, since part of the price is for the cordless nature of these things (that and the internal storage and the google speak and...). So yes, they've got a lot of nice options to them which make them more than just earbuds.

title: lightweight and decent sound quality
review: These are very nice looking earphones with denim and fabric accents (denim on the band, fabric wrapped cord), recycled aluminum and even some 'wood'. All in all, very nice. They are lightweight as well and they fit comfortably - then again, I'm on the small side. The sound is good, nothing spectacular but consider the price range. The music I'm playing comes in nice and clear so I'm happy. You have a microphone feature with them to take calls, but being able to pause music or adjust volume would be nice as well.

title: pretty good but expensive wireless headset
review:
The Klipsch KG-300 Pro Audio Wireless Gaming Headset is a very nice headset and easy to install - right out of the box you can plug in the base via USB (batteries included in the headset) and start using them. The audio is pretty good for a gaming headset, with the sounds of the game coming through clear, and people on the other end can easily hear what is being said. The headset is mostly comfortable - they're not the lightest and a bit bulky/padded, but they fit well.
Now, for the price of this headset, one thing that did surprise me is how much background noise DID come through. While it is true that they don't claim to be noise cancelling, considering the price and the padding, I didn't expect to be picking up so much background noise while wearing them. Definitely won't have to worry about anyone sneaking up on you while wearing these.

title: great sound quality, works good for Apple products
review:
I've tried a couple of high quality headphones and earphones lately, and have to say that these are probably the best. The sound quality is exceptional, for pc, iPhone and mp3 player listening, providing clarity and definition of both bass and tremble. It was easy to pick up elements to the song that other - lesser quality - earphones left out, and the Munitio earphones were comfortable to use (in part thanks to the three different sizes of earbuds that they provide to ensure the best fit).

The microphone and the control buttons work well with any Apple products, which is nice (one day it'll be great to come across a universal product), and the design is appealing with the thick, flat cord (which isn't entirely tangle-free but less likely to knot up like some other earphones I've come across, especially those which are fabric wrapped) and the bronze accents. Munitio provides a nice, flat bag to carry your earphones in which can be easily tucked into a pocket or bag.

There are probably higher end earphones that provide just as good if not better listening quality, but for the price, I'd have to recommend these.

title: Great quality!
review: These earbuds are great for the price! They are pretty sleek and the charging box is very compact. Easy to throw in my purse and go. Easy to use. Clear instruction manual.

title: I recommend rolling/wrapping the cord and NOT just stuffing them somewhere ...
review: I use these as a "backup" pair of earbuds. I have had my pair for well over a year & they still work well. I recommend rolling/wrapping the cord and NOT just stuffing them somewhere in a drawer because the cord tends to "crease" up a little bit.

title: Durable, attractive, just the right size.
review: This is great, especially for CDs. So glad it also plays cassettes, serves as an AM/FM radio, etc. and can be used with headphones.

title: Excellent sound and very comfortable
review: Excellent sound and very comfortable. The only potential negative is that the smallest width may be too broad if you have a small head. I'm using these headphones to listen to music as well as to watch movies. Very good buy.

title: It's ok
review: It's an OK product.  Not exactly the best at noise cancelling on a plane.  The fit is a bit uncomfortable on a long haul flight.  I get a better sound quality from my Apple headphone.  For the given price, it's only an ok product.

title: Good enough inexpensive headphones.
review: Got for my son for school, needed standard old school headphones with cord....works well for that.  Price is right.

title: Sharp looking and excellent noise cancellation headphones.
review: I really like these headphones.  I took off one star because the gold union that you can see on the cord in the picture came undone on one of them.  The sound quality is excellent.  Noise cancellation is very very good.  To give you an idea when I am waiting for the train at Newark train station I can listen to Podcasts without changing the volume even when a train comes in on the next track.  You can still hear what is going on around you but without a doubt you can also hear what you have playing through the headphones.  I have difficulties with headphones staying in place in general. The one ear is fine but the other slips out occasionally, that said it is better than most.  I found the only ones that really fit me are the old fashion round disc types.  The cord and other parts are good quality, though speaking of the cord it does tangle fairly easily.  Final note as the plug is at a 90 degree angle not straight out it is good for in pants pockets, very good for walking.

title: Good folding headphones for the price.
review: Good headphones for the money.  Sound is not as good as an expensive pair but they are nice in that they fold.  They have been pretty durable my son used them for school and then were brought back home and we have used them around.  They are light/plastic so quality is what you would expect in this price range.

title: Overly Aggressive Bluetooth
review:
sounds fantastic, but the bluetooth connection is overly aggressive considering you can't turn it off without unplugging it. Whenever i try to use another bluetooth audio device anywhere in my house it gets booted in favor of this. I like how consistent it is about reconnecting, but i shouldn't have to unplug or unpair the dang thing to be able to make a phone call with a BT headset. The best looking solution i could find would be to wire it up to be powered by whatever speaker system you are using, so it would power on & off with the speakers, but that's a lot of effort for something that would have been easily resolved with a power switch/button.

If you don't use any other bluetooth in the general area of this receiver this is a great product. If you use other bluetooth audio devices ever, this is gonna be annoying.

title: disappointing mic reception.
review:
i can hear great but i am told that i sound far away while using it. I use the same headset on my computer for voip calls and have no problems, so i know it isn't my headset.

Update: 3stars to 1 star, being told that I am unintelligible while using this. great for listening, bit if i cant talk with it then it is useless.

title: Somewhat Disappointing
review:
no major problems so far, but the left ear is a bit quieter than the right, and the over-all sound quality is poor. I had no trouble setting it up, they are comfortable and easy to use, but at the end of the day, they just don't sound good. I understand not being able to produce a heavy bass in a wireless earbud, but every bass track on pop & rock songs i have listened to so far has either been muffled to the point of being inaudible, or just produced a crackly static.

TL:DR : good physical design, crap audio.

UPDATE: Customer service contacted me and said my pair seems to be defective and offered to send me an updated pair. changed from 2 star to 3 for good customer service

title: From 5 to 1
review:
When i first got these i was living out in the woods in a very rural area and i gave them 5 stars. The sound quality of both the headphones and Mic are beautiful, the surround sound is mind-blowing, and i loved being able to walk around my house listening to stuff without bothering my family.

I have moved into an apartment complex recently and these are now a useless decoration. whenever I try to use them there is so much interference that it causes the connection to the wireless usb to cut out all the time, to the point they are unusable. it comes with a nice long cord to charge it, but even plugged in it only sends data wirelessly, so they are fully powered and unable to maintain a connection.

amazing headset, but with this crippling flaw they are useless in dense population areas.

title: After 6. 5 months the charging dock stopped recharging ...
review:
After 6.5 months the charging dock stopped recharging the headphones batteries.
I am not sure how the 2-year limited warranty works.

title: Great Headset !
review:
When I bought my Samsung Galaxy SII Skyrocket LTE smartphone I found out that the Samsung Stereo Headset included in the package doesn't have "+" and "-" buttons to adjust the device volume during a music playback or phone conversation.
This one - HTC Stereo Headset for HTC EVO 4G (Black) has the volume buttons and the volume control works great on my Galaxy! Sound quality is great too!
Price ($5) is unbelievably low.

title: Awesome case!
review: Love how easy it is to snap in your headphones. Charging is easy and fits so well. Have yet to drop it and don’t want to test it but overall fits like a glove!

title: Aesthetically Pleasing
review: It’s very pretty, there isn’t much noise cancellation.. but that’s okay. It’s super comfy which is important for me since I have so many piercings and my ears are kind of small, so it’s hard to find comfy on ear buds. Another perk, is the superb battery life! But just average earbuds that was mainly purchased because they were pretty.

title: So cute awesome product!
review: I love it this is so cute! The top portion sticks on with a little sticky tape that is provided and it's still intact. I love it. Great product and wat to personalize my earbuds.

title: Finally I can pretend to listen to people talk while I do the dishes
review:
Sound quality is really good for phone calls. On all my other earphones people used to hear everything around me just as loudly as my voice. With this device I can walk around, tidy the house, be outside in the wind, and people still hear me just as well.

I took a star off cause it's pricey and doesn't sit snugly enough on my head (tends to slide off a bit unless my head is completely upright). Audio quality and comfort don't enable this to be my music-listening device, so I basically only use it for phone calls. That makes it very overprices. But for a person who makes a fair amount of phone and zoom calls, if you can afford it, it's a worthy investment.

title: Good for hands free calls
review: I’ve made some long calls with these and so far they work very well. I was looking for something to be hands free on my iPhone. Each call let me know they could hear me well. I could hear them clearly, too. The earbuds are comfortable.

title: Perfect for the kiddo!
review: Cutest pair of headphones I purchased for my 4 yr old. He loves them, the volume control is great, and they’re durable.

title: LOVE these
review: I absolutely love these. I am extremely organized and pretty much label everything. When we got a new desktop computer with new speakers and new webcam, there were cords going all over the place! These labels were recommended to me by someone, so I ended up purchasing them... And I was NOT disappointed. Super easy to use and there are a LOT of them. Plus, I like that they give you 5 different colors. The labels stick on the tabs just fine and the tabs themselves seem quite sturdy. Not only did I label all the cords running underneath the computer, but I also labeled everyone's phone chargers, the camera charger cords, and the wireless headphone charger. My dad saw what I had done (my masterpiece) and quickly bought some for himself so he could label his thousands of Christmas lights & cords... Really, they can be used to label pretty much anything. (Keep in mind that the tabs are zip-ties, so you can label anything that can be zip-tied.) I would highly recommend these to anyone!

title: Not what I was looking for
review:
I am surprised to admit I did not like these earbuds at all. Skullcandy is usually very reliable and I've never had a problem with them before. I am quite disappointed with my purchase.

Structurally, I do not like the "button" on the earbud "strings." Although it comes in handy when you want to pause a song you're listening to, it is very difficult to switch to a different song (double-clicking the button). Also, it always started playing by itself when I put it in my pocket or purse, which completely wore out the battery.

Functionally, the right ear plays more loudly than the left. It is very annoying trying to listen to music when you can only decently hear out of one ear.

I would be very hesitant to buy these particular earbuds again.

title: Would not connect with my Sony WF-1000XM3
review:
I purchased this specifically to connect to my Sony WF-1000XM3 headphones; it would not do so, regardless of my attempts to engage it. The same headphones connected to my Motorola Smartphone, and later, to a 1Mii Miilink Bluetooth transmitter/receiver. With this one, though, it would not.

May be a fine transmitter for other devices, and theoretically should work with the WF-1000XM3 as the protocols are supported, but it just would not pair. So would not recommend it for that purpose.

title: Does not fit the jabra Pro 920
review: The cushions feel like they are decent quality, for headset cushions anyway. Another review mentioned that these would work for the Jabra Pro 920 headset. This is not the case - it doesn't fit, and therefore would not fit the 930 either. The only reason I am making this review is to articulate that point.

title: Great cable for a receiver
review:
I use this cable to connect a pair of stereo headphones to my receiver, so I can wander around my study while still listening to music and other content. It works well for this purpose, there is minimal attenuation. The cable is sturdy and heavy enough not to get too tangled on things (including itself) and the connector seems to hold quite securely. No problems, despite it being kicked and pulled around corners for a few weeks.

Would recommend.

title: Surprising impact on sound
review:
I've had my AKG K701 headphones for many years, so I didn't really notice the breakdown of the (original) pads until right after I washed them a month or two ago. Soon after, the headphones were increasingly uncomfortable to wear and I realized that my ears were resting directly on grill covering the drivers - that's how degraded the pads had become. I considered ordering new OEM pads, but honestly I've now replaced the driver on one side of these headphones, resoldered the connection, repaired the wire and chewed up the outer cups in the process so I supposed it didn't really make a difference. I just needed my headphones to be wearable again.

These fit the AKG K701 perfectly. The material itself is not as nice as the OEM - you'd probably have to pay ~$80 for a pair of similar pads - but it is sufficient. Cushioning is okay, a little firm at first, I'm guessing they'll break in over time. They are still fine for people with glasses, like myself.

The one thing I didn't expect is the boost in sound quality, which is truly remarkable. Improvements across all frequencies, everything is crisper and clearer with these new pads, enough that I feel like I'm wearing a new pair of headphones. I suppose people who know headphones well probably see this as obvious, but for me it was a very pleasant surprise.

Would recommend for basic replacement pads for the AKG K701 headphones.
