review: This is like one of those too good to be true products for the price.  It looks really good and claims to be a very good product but the price point is very low and the brand is unheard of (at least to me).  Surprisingly the headphones look great, are durable, and the sound is excellent.  Thank you.

title: They work great!
review: I waited it out on getting a pair of Bluetooth Headphones.  I have had 0 problems with these. They work great!

title: Good while they last
review: these are my third pairs, yes i should have learned my lesson. I had version 3 and they lasted  3-4 months but folks at XLeader were kind enough to send me version 5 as a free replacement. Well, version 5 were great for about 7 days until they could not be turned on. XLeader, again was kind enough to send me another pair of version 5. Again, they were awesome.....for 3 weeks, yes 3 weeks. One of the earbuds would not turn on and there seemed to be some type of green leakage around the charging port. I'd give them 10 stars for customer service, the earbuds? 4.5 when they work, if you like to dispose your earbuds every 30 days, get them.

title: Probably the Best Headphones for the Price
review: I realize that these are not inexpensive headphones. I wanted really decent headphones that had a really large bass response. Beats are known for their quality and so that's what I was looking for. Fast charging that will last for a long time, meaning that I only seem to need to charge it every few days, and I use it a lot. Also very beautiful. It has invisible controls on one side of the headset, meaning that if you press one of the sides things will happen, like volume control, and most importantly, if push twice it will skip to the next song depending on how you have your source music set. I have mine set to play randomly so I don't know what is playing next. That is controlled by your unit, not the headphones. These are Bluetooth headphones and you can hook them up to anything that Bluetooth's. It also has an incredible range on it. This is my second apartment I have had them at and it actually goes perfectly from floor to floor right through the cement without sound deterioration of any kind. No I don't know what the range is, and so it may depend on your own situation, but I simply do not think that there are better headphones out there for the price. Like I said, if you are looking for excellent bass response, and I like bass, because I listen to a lot of rock 'n roll and heavy metal, then these headphones are the right ones to get. They are also very sturdy and they fold up so if need be you can put them in your coat pocket. Highly recommended.

title: Excellent for the Money
review: I have had it for about a month now and everything works just fine. It will change tracks on your smart phone, meaning music by pushing the button on the microphone. The telephone side of the works excellent as well. It fits very well over the head and is very comfortable. The only small drawback is is a little bit lacking in bass, but I guess that's to be expected for the price. I really wanted something that would change my musical tracks without having to take my smart phone out of my pocket and was also very comfortable. I would say that this is a very nice unit for traveling outdoors and going places. If you're looking for something just to listen to music to at home, I would recommend a more powerful bass response headphone system. But everything works and messy important thing. You push the button twice no changes to the next track, whether you have a your system on shuffle or you are playing an entire album. So everything works fine.

title: There is a design flaw in the band
review: .The headphones have pretty good sound as long as you're not moving around. There is a design flaw in these particular headphones and it is not in the sound. Most headphones have a thick band that keeps it on your head, especially when you're moving around. These have none. I have never seen a pair of headphones that to not have some kind of thicker band is so that it stays on your head properly. So if you're walking around or sitting someplace and look down, the headphones fall off your head. Every time. If you're just sitting up in bed and not moving, well then okay. Anyplace else, and the coming off your head. This is a design problem. I have a little bit larger head, and so it is not feasible to believe that this is made for a larger head or smaller head. With use, the band stretch out of proportion and makes it even worse. I recommend going with the different Sony product. You can see by the picture that it has no substance in the center of the band

title: Great quality for children
review: What I really like about these headphones, is that even if the kids try to put the volume on max, it’s still relatively low, so it won’t damage their hearing.

title: Really nice
review:
very comfortable fit and adjustable. i really liked the pouch thats included in the pack. audio quality is top notch and it does a good job of dampening background noise with it snug earpiece. bluetooth connection delivers clear and crisp audio. if you dont have a bluetooth system, you're still in luck. this unit comes with a micro usb-audio jack cable that converts it to a regular headset

my only grouse is that the touch sesnsitive audio control doesnt work with a lot of my devices when i'm playing music

title: Solved my dilemma
review: I bought a headset that only worked with a split audio/mic connection, so I had to plug it directly into sound card, leaving my desktop speakers unused. I didn't want to have to keep changing the audio out (from headset to speakers to headset), so I bought this and now my speakers are usb and everything remains plugged in where it is.

title: Great investment
review: I ordered the beats and was ready to send them back because they kept falling out my ears. It didn’t matter if I had the small medium or large size earbuds on the beats they would always fall out. I happen to come across these and ordered them and it made an immediate difference. My beats are now secure in my ear and I can do almost anything without worrying about them falling out! The best part about it is the variety of colors that I have! I would definitely recommend these, worth the money!

title: The worse !
review:
These headphones are the worse! There is a joke that if a product is so terrible you can find it in a gumball machine, well it’s too big for one, though the lack of quality is apparent The side where you put the plug to charge it is small and almost a cut out insert that you struggle with and then no light to let you know it charging and for how long. Without going down the list of all that is wrong with these headphones I’d have to say a strong no all the way around. Honestly they’d be overpriced at ten dollars let alone $32.
I’m a firm believer of sticking to name brands when it comes to technology and this reinforces my belief. Thought I would take a chance and I was wrong. Hence the saying - live & learn.

title: Be cautious!
review: WiFi doesn’t work, sound low, headphones had to be held into jack because does not fit properly. Too bad because it was a nice looking computer though had to return before I faced more problems later on.

title: The best headphones on the market for the price
review: The best headphones on the market for the price! For years I spent money replacing the ones I bought at Walmart- didn't matter which brand, some I paid more than this price. After having Sennheiser, I will never return to commercial ones again. Great quality.

title: These headphones are way better than I expected
review: These headphones are way better than I expected. The sound is amazing! Also they’re super secure. I like boxing (hitting mitts/heavy bag) and I didn’t have to adjust them at all. Oh the memory earbuds are an amazing touch! Complete cancel out noise and I hardly know I’m wearing them.

title: Works great for car trips!
review: This is great for car trips for kids! It holds their device as well as you can hang a bag with additional activities or snacks in it. I also use it to hold the headphones and additional power charging cords. We use the extra hook sometimes to hang a portable speaker to increase the volume of my daughter's device because she often cannot hear it over the noise of the vehicle and wind

title: Stopped turning on.
review:
ONE YEAR OLD REVIEw. DO NOT BUY

Trash the wires are all busted. My husband is an electrical engineer. He took apart and the entire set or wires are broken and ripped in too many places

Stopped working. Pretty crappy now. Don’t waste your money. As you see my first review was a good. They just didn’t last long. I only wore doing house chores while baby slept

this is my first pair of on ear head phones and my husband is already jealous!
These are amazing headphones.
Sound is wonderful!

title: Good buy!
review: Earbuds. Sound comes out of them. Sound continues to come out of them to this day. Good buy! :)

title: Exactly what I was looking for
review: These are great. They’re the only earphones I’ve found that will stay in my ears, while working out. VERY noice canceling! Love that you don’t have to recharge them after every use and they charge themselves in the case, so I don’t have to worry about accidentally leaving them behind before heading to the gym. I think I used them 7 times before needed to charge the case again.

title: Cute headphones
review:
These cat ear headphones are pretty cute, my 6 year old daughter loves them. The sizing is a little big on her even on their smallest size but she would rather use these than her other headphones because cat ears =)

The sound quality is not great but it is decent.. better than most of the other kids headphones we have. If you're looking for sound quality probably look elsewhere but if cuteness is more important to you than sound quality then you will probably love these.

It uses a CR-2032 battery which is kind of annoying but I do like that they include an extra battery (one comes pre-installed and there is a spare in the package).

title: Mediocre sound quality, fit issues
review:
These headphones don't really hit the mark for me -- maybe because I have a small head and smaller ears. They stay on and don't fall off even when running but I can't get the fit correct where the driver stays sealed in my ear the way its supposed to (tried all sets of tips included). When they come loose the sound quality is very bad since these are a sealed design headphone and rely on creating a seal with your inner ear to reproduce low frequencies, so they sound very tinny and harsh. Even when I use my fingers to hold the drivers in place though, the sound quality of these is pretty mediocre compared to my other sony BT headphones.

Also when I tighten the band in the back to prevent cable noise when running, that makes the control pod be on the back of my neck which is kind of awkward to use. I also don't like the overall design which looks and feels kind of bulky, at least they are pretty light weight though. These headphones worked as expected and had no issues with syncing, if they fit better I would have given them 3 or 4 stars but I have a pair of sony bluetooth headphones that sound better, fit better, and look better for about the same cost so I really can't recommend these.

title: They look really fancy and expensive but are a very ...
review:
They look really fancy and expensive but are a very reasonable price. I was really excited to have a set that can work well for video or music. Unfortunately after only 2 weeks the left earbud stopped working. I have yet to find a decent earbuds set that both earbuds work for longer than a few weeks!

Update: The company contacted me and sent me a replacement set. Great and quick customer service. I have changed my review from 2 stars to 4.

title: Junk. They were cheap, but that just means they are cheap junk.
review:
Used them at first in the gym. Constantly interrupted sound, sometimes only in one, sometimes in both earpieces, with the phone ~1ft away. Thought maybe it's the congested environment with so much WiFi & Bluetooth traffic.
So yesterday I used them on the bicycle. Out in the open, nobody around, earphones ~3ft from my phone. Started out okay, but after 10mins same thing, music constantly cutting out. Complete junk. Glad I can return them.

title: I ordered a few BlueTooth earbuds to test and kept only these
review:
I ordered a few BlueTooth earbuds to test and kept only these. They paired quickly with my phone. Audio quality is good (though I have to say I'm not an audiophile). Voice quality during a call is good as well. Usually when I go riding my bicycle I prefer to have music in only one ear, the TrueShift 2 can be used alone if wanted, only the left or the right earpiece.
They have pretty good noise-isolation and are very light (my kitchen scale said 6g (~1/5 oz) each earpiece). Additionally got them for a great price, so really nothing to complain about.

title: Worth the value for my home office
review: Ever since COVID I have been working from home, March 16th. I converted my guest room to an office and have been stuck using a headset. I purchased this product in hopes they I could not have to wear something around my head the entire time. This product is much smaller than the pictures. It almost fits in the palm of my hand. What truly stands out though is how well it works for it’s size. I have it placed nicely on my desk and it doesn’t take up too much space.

title: Helps relieve desk congestion
review: This is a pretty neat headset stand. I like that it seems sturdy and is pretty easy to use. Didn’t really think I’d have to put it together; however, it wasn’t bad. I assembled it at my work desk in about 5 mins. It even came with a handy brush.

title: Good buy, very durable
review: I needed a headset for my classes. This product did as stated. It has also been very durable. I let my family member use it when they went to college after me. It’s still in circulation in my family.

title: Great
review: These are great! Great price and good product. They are stylish and wireless with Bluetooth access. It’s nice to not have cords from headphones while using your phone.

title: WORST - Mic is HORRIBLE, making this UNUSABLE
review: I STRONGLY recommend NOT buying this.  The microphone sounds like there is a bad ground.  Nothing but a loud hum/buzz.  The headset itself is comfortable and sound quality is good.  The mic though... unusable.

title: Perfect
review: Instantly recognized by Windows 10. Was able to connect my Bluetooth headset immediately.

title: Built in mic, easy installation
review: I purchased this camera because I am taking my Summer college courses online. I wasn’t able to get a webcam from any stores because they are sold out. I like this one it has a built in mic so I don’t have to wear my unfashionable headset. Easy to fit on screen and adjustable. Very clear picture.

title: Great for cord management
review: Now that I'm working from home, my desk is full of all kinds of wires that I have to plug/unplug throughout the week. I've been wanting to buy a cord holder for a while and found this set. Which is PERFECT! They come in different sizes and works for every cord - Macbook, Apple chargers, headphones, etc. Happy with my purchase. Will order more for my hubs office.

title: Basic MP3 player
review:
The device is very small and very light, the closest thing I can think to compare it to is a medium sized disposable vape. Battery life is pretty good and I didn't have any trouble running various TF cards.
Playing MP3s worked fine, though it doesn't support playlists. It plays files in order of when they were copied to the card, so you'll have to tediously copy any folders that need to stay in order one at a time.
I really wish they'd have a separate audiobook app from the music player just for convenience.
Video support is a joke - things have to be encoded at thumbnail res. The ebook reader is also iffy - out of around 10k ebooks in varying formats, it only recognizes 13 of the hundreds of text files. The FM won't even try to transmit over bluetooth - when the transmitter is in the same room, I shouldn't need the headphone wires for an extended antenna. Navigation is a bit irritating - instead of a D-pad, the left and right buttons are the only ones that navigate, the center button is enter, and the bottom one is back. There's no on-board memory, the storage card is it's only storage.
The other tools seem to work well.

title: TWS doesn't connect
review:
The biggest thing is that these are meant to be true wireless stereo headphones, and they're not - all the manual says is that they will automatically connect to each other after turning on and before connecting to a phone; I left them in TWS pairing mode for several minutes without them connecting.
I was able to connect to them as two separate devices and got mono sound through both simultaneously. The sound quality wasn't as bad as I've heard on cheap headphones, but it was in the lower 20% - they're basically just very small (and cheap) speakers that sit above the ear canal. There is no bass, and mids/treble are a bit flat. They also do not get very loud due to the design. I will say that I like the concept of having them fit into the top part of the ear and project down and into the canal, but the execution was poorly done.
If I wanted to run dual-output every time I use them, I think they would work well for audiobooks and podcasts, as the vocal range are the frequencies the headphones favor most, and I typically don't feel the need to crank the volume on my audiobooks.

title: Comfy, good mids and highs
review:
I'm wearing these now and they're quite comfortable to wear for extended periods. Connection was easy. I wish they had more control buttons instead of just the one. The charging port is also in an odd place (presumably to keep people from charging while wearing) (it's on the left ear-pod).
Sound quality is a little funky and I guess to be expected on a cheap pair of headphones: the biggest thing is that they don't reproduce bass really at all, I can feel the bass hits when the pod hits my ear, but the bass isn't making it to my eardrum; at highest volume there's a bit of distortion but they don't really get /that/ loud; otherwise, at low-medium levels and for treble and mids, the sound reproduction is excellent. I suspect I'm going to like these more for podcasts and audiobooks than music.
If you're not into really bass-y music, and you don't need substantial volume, these will probably be perfect for you.

title: Sound great, interesting design
review:
For buds that sit outside of the ear canal, these sound really good. Frequency range seems superb, bass response is decent for earbuds.
I haven't had anything with a cable braided quite in this manner, but they don't tangle at all. The drivers disconnect from the wires and the plug is swappable. The swappable plugs are really cool for international use, but I don't understand why the drivers aren't permanently attached.

title: Worth Paying a Little Extra for the High Quality
review:
I had purchased some cheap dongles before and I think they damaged my laptop because they were always disconnecting at the slightest bump. My headphones were also difficult to connect with them.

I can't even describe what a difference these high quality dongles make. They never disconnect and the sound is much better in my headphones.

title: Wonderful Once You Figure Out How To Get Them To Work
review:
Did not come with a disk or any kind of software and the website is no help at all. I had to find the drivers online (with help from a review here). I almost accidentally downloaded from a commercial site (which would have installed adware) before finding the original software sites. Sorry, it's been a while and I don't have the details. Also, had to search YouTube for a (cellphone) video to figure out how to get the headset to be recognizable by the computer (hold the 'on' button until it starts flashing both red and blue lights).

Once it got going, however, I could not ask for more. They are amazing. Good sound, lightweight, comfortable, long charge time.

title: Good for the Price
review: The sound is not as good as I was expecting based on other reviews but it is a good enough headset for the times when my wireless headset is recharging.

title: Great Buy!
review: Good sounding headphones. Material is rubbery and not like the last pair I had just like these. But the rest is fabulous! I’d buy it again!

title: Simply the best
review: I have two pair for battery continuity.  They're that good.  I know people complain about Bose, but these are simply the best headphones I have ever owned.  Bass response is amazing.  High notes are amazing.  I love the easy to use control on the cord.  This is my go to.  I have other earbuds and what not, but don't like them.  This is what I use and you should to.  You won't be disappointed.

title: Not my favorite, but decent and great Alexa integration
review:
I've been using these for a couple of months and find that while I like them, I prefer a competitor's product in terms of sound quality and the ability of the product to stay in my ear. I have tried the different options that come with them to get a better fit and stay in my ear tighter to no avail.

For outdoor activity, I cannot wear these. They fall out of my ear and I lose them. However, indoors I love the Alexa integration. If they could make them in a way they stay in my ear, they would be perfect. Last night, one fell out and went into the garbage disposer. Luckily, it was not on and water wasn't running or it would have been gone.

As they work loose quickly, sound quality and volume diminishes. They do have good bass response when tightly fitted in your ear. If I am sitting still listening to music or an audio book, they work great. As I start to move around, they loosen up and sound poor and are at risk of falling out.

Overall, I do have a use for them. I love the ability to use Alexa. I wish they could do Alexa independent of a mobile device via wi-fi, which they cannot. I love the ability to recharge them from the case when traveling. The case is hard shell and very protective of the earbuds. The case is probably the best part of the product.

title: Works as intended
review: This is a good quality cable and works perfectly to split the output of sound from my laptop.  I bought this so a friend could share my screen with headphones on a long flight.  It worked perfectly.  Of course the one downside is that it's only a splitter so if you are using headphones, you both have to listen at the same volume level.

title: Decent headphone for the price
review: Good headphones.  The highs are clear, but the lows aren't as good as they are with some other headphones.  Overall, the sound quality is very good.  I would buy these again.  For the price, they're about as good as any!

title: Worked well  but not for me
review:
I've only had them for two days. My own error, I didn't click all the thumbnails--these are over the ear headphones, but not cups, and I didn't catch that. I prefer cup headphones so I can have that seal and since these were not that style, they were really uncomfortable for me (pushing on tragus/forward helix piercings).

That being said, the sound was pretty good considering they had no seal. Definitely not something I'd use in a library but for watching movies late at night and not wanting to disturb others, they're perfect. I never tested the range/battery life though so unfortunately this isn't a lot of help.

title: Great budget friendly headset!
review: This is a great budget friendly headset! And the battery life is crazy ridiculous! I bought these for my husband whose is constantly on the phone at work. This set stays charged for at least 6 days

title: Batman headphones for small heads
review: They are good but the cushion on the top prevents the headphones from fitting my son. He has to wear them off the back of his head to have the headphones cover his ears.

title: Buy a decent case, get headphones for free.
review: These are really crappy, uncomfortable headphones with a pretend noise cancelling feature. First off, they do not fit comfortably around your ear, they squish it and still do not fully seal it. Second, the noise cancelling feature creates a noticeable noise, somewhat muting ambient noise, but in no way cancelling it. Third, the sound output is horrible, so much so that while on an airplane, I could not hear my movie! I ended up using ear buds inside of these things. I would return these, but I know you get what you pay for, so I'll end up just giving them to my kids. Loom elsewhere, these headphones are disappointing all around. The case is nice though.

title: Samsung does it again!
review: Absolutely love these!  Samsung never disappoints me.  Absolutely no complaints.  I have issues with fitting headphones in my small ears and these fitike a glove.

title: ... as long as any others but at a much better price.
review: I beat up headphones wile I work and theis seem to last as long as any others but at a much better price.

title: These are the best sounding headphones I have ever owned
review: I am a huge Bose fan and have owned several pairs of Bose headphones over the years. I have wanted the Quiet Comfort 35 II Wireless Headphones for a long time, but they were just a little out of my price range. A couple of months ago they there on sale one day and I decided to go for it. I absolutely love these headphones. They are comfortable, the noise counseling feature works great and the sound is very clear no matter what type of music you like. If I had to make one suggestion I would say the bass could be ramped up a bit, but overall I love these headphones.

title: much better than some other earbuds I have had costing 15x ...
review: these headphone wires are very well insulated, much better than some other earbuds I have had costing 15x the price of these. My only rub on these is that the cord that goes around the ear is not moldable to your ear shape.

title: perfecto
review:
I can't count how many earphones I have bought in the past few years. I would much rather have bought one very expensive, DURABLE set, then all the other pieces of junk I have bought. And I have spent 150 on the "nice" Bose earphones. I got these and have been extremely happy with them. They fit well and sound great. Even after a 3-4 hour bike ride, when others begin to hurt my ears, these still feel great.

Highly recommended....But I will amend this review should they stop working.

title: Great, if they fit your ears
review: I loved the short cable and the sound was great...They are also the best insulated cables on earbuds that I have found.  But I just couldn't get a good seal and they always felt like they were going to be falling out.  Bummer!

title: Didnt work waste of time
review: Well i was told would work with my logitech Bluetooth headset since my last usb receiver broke at airport...followed all directions and mo go couldnt get it to work at all so frustrating gave up and returned!

title: Great use for bedside necessities
review:
I use this to plug in my phone and headphones at night. Its very convenient because whatever I need at my bedside, I can have there. My lamp, laptop, charger for back massager can all be plugged in at once because there are so many outlets and the USB ports. Those are the best because I can't always locate my charger block.
This was a great buy. The price compared to most other durable equipment with this much variety is great. It does heat up in certain spots if something is left plugged in and on for over 24 hours though.

title: the plugins fit kinda loose into the headphones and cp ...
review: the plugins fit kinda loose into the headphones and cp jacks! I have to wiggle them a bit to make both earphones work, but its okay for the price!

title: So useful!
review: Ordered these for sleeping since I was always losing my AirPods in bed and get paranoid that my dog might chew them up. The headphones work great, charge quick and the battery lasts a good long while. The sound quality isn’t as great as my beats or AirPods Pro but for what I use these for they are perfect. I’ve washed the headband several times in the washer and it’s held up nicely. The headphones pop in and out very easily. I was so impressed with this product I ordered one for my husband to use also and have considered ordering them for my kids since they’ve been known to snap regular headphones on multiple occasions and these are so compact and convenient.

title: Best Headphones for the Gym Hands down
review: The one complaint I have is that the charge doesn't seem to last very long, but given how small and light they are, I can't complain too much. That one small gripe aside, they're a fantastic headphone, they sound great and despite a bit of a learning curve getting an optimal fit, they're very comfortable and secure fitting.

title: my kind of headphones
review:
I have RS160 and enjoyed it for many years.
Time to replace it.
I toyed with Bluetooth Headphones.
Yes, Bluetooth technology is what everyone is going now with
and I like Bluetooth technology and I use it on some of my other
devices.
None is as good as this Sennheiser TV Headphones
for TV listening. I have some hearing problems
and this baby is what I need.
Also, it is easy pressure on a head and
very comfortable.
TV sound quality is what swayed me to go with RS175.

title: tiny but powerful!
review:
This tiny transmitter really does a great job.
So simple but so impressive.
I paired it with AudioMX HB-S3 Wireless Bluetooth 4.1 Headphones.
They both work together just great.
No Latency whatsoever.
The reach goes 30-35 feet without a problem
and it includes going to another room like a kitchen.
A little further in it and it starts producing cracking sound.
All in all, very happy!

title: Amazon Music Rocks with these Headphones! 👍👍
review:
So far so good! The sound is much louder and better on these than my other wireless headset! I like that when I'm talking on the phone through them; the person at the other end can hear that I'm watching t.v. but; it's not loud like the other ones.
My only complaint is the 30 day Register for Warranty card that they sent me was an Insecure Sight.

title: Nice case, but much thicker than it needs to be for MDRZX110NC headphones
review: This is a nice case, but it is bigger than it needs to be for MDRZX110NC headphones. The thickness of the case is more than 2.5". When folded, MDRZX110NC are less than 1.5" thick. So unless you are planning to carry other stuff in the upper compartment of the case (with the mesh holder) quite a lot of space is wasted. If this case was 1.75"  or so, it would be the perfect size.

title: Superb for a good price
review:
Saw the ratings for these earbuds and liked the ear loop design, fit, and comments. Am very impressed.

Pros: Price; Sound quality borders 5-star; Ear inserts stay in; Simple
Cons: Cord gets bundled
Suggestions: Would bay $50-$100 more for a noise-cancelling version; Memory foam ear inserts

title: Superb vaue and great sound...
review:
Very impressed by the sound quality of these headphones. One of the best headphones I have and at a fraction of the cost of others. Red cording really pops visually and they hold up to life and gym use. Super value!

Superb communication, fast arrival, and item fit its description perfectly. Great buying experience.

title: MADE DAILY SWIMS LESS BORING AND TIRING
review: I used these headphones all summer for daily swims. I found French contemporary music online which fit perfectly the pace for learning free style. The sound quality was good and cancelled out the joyful noise of children playing and diving. I found that I could swim a lot longer without getting bored or tired.

title: Perfect
review: If the cord goes bad from use, just spend a couple of bucks for a new one, you don't have to replace the whole thing... genius. My autistic child is hard on wires and the headphone itself has survived really well, since she drops it a lot (that's why we can't buy wireless, they are more fragile).

title: Best headphones for sleep I’ve found yet.
review: I’ve had several different headphones similar to this one. I like the way this is designed better. The headphones don’t fall out of their pouches like my last one did. It’s comfortable. It’s cute. It’s easy to use. The best part though is that the charge lasts FOREVER. I charge it for an hour maybe two and it lasts for about 16 hours. Which is amazing! It isn’t a normal usb but a USBC charger so that kinda sucks cuz if you lose your charger you’re probably out of luck on charging it because a lot of people don’t have those kind of chargers. But I love this headband the most out of all of them I tried. It’s worth the money. :)

title: Inexpensive and reliable headphone extension cable
review: I use this cable as an extension between a computer dock and my headset.  I ordered the calbe in late March. I've been using it for several hours 5 days a week since then, taking conference calls with multiple headsets.  The right-angle plug is useful to help gather and bundle cables coming out of the dock.  Audio quality is good.  The cable looks good and blends in well.  The braided sheathing is a nice touch.  I would buy this again.

title: Decent case for a decent price
review: This is a nice headphone for a very reasonable price.  I bought it to carry an Mpow 071 USB headset in a backpack.  It's an inexpensive headset and I wasn't looking for the "best" case, as much as something that would get the job  done without costing an arm and a leg.  This case fits that bill.  I'd happily buy it again.

title: comfortable compact over-ear headphones, wired or wireless, mediocre bass, no equalizer app
review:
I like over-ear headphones. I find them to be more comfortable and better sounding than most on-ear or earbud headphones. These headphones are comfortable to wear, even on my larger head or when I am wearing glasses. They are not too heavy or too bulky when I am wearing them. I like that they fold up compactly for travel. I would prefer a hard case, but the included soft bag is better than nothing.

These headphones pair easily with the Bluetooth on my phone. I like that I can also use wired mode which I like to use when I'm watching movies on my PC.

The sound is clear and noise-free. It sounds natural in the midrange and higher frequencies. Bass is unfortunately mediocre compared to other over-ear headphones that I own. This is more important for rap or dance music than for pop or rock or classical music. Unfortunately, the included SXFI app does not work with streaming music. There is no equalizer app like many other headphones are including these days.

title: better features and performance than expected for the $60 price
review: These earbuds are currently $60, making them some of the cheapest wireless earbuds that I own. For $60, you get a lot of features including noise cancellation, great battery life, pretty good sound quality, a comfortable secure fit and customizations and updates via the app. Noise cancellation is not fantastic, but many other brands don't any noise cancellation in this price range. 9 hour battery life without recharging is a couple of hours longer than most of my other earbuds. Sound quality is loud and not noisy but sometimes a little muddy in the midrange, but not too bad for this price range. Compared to other earbuds in this price range that I have tried, these are the most comfortable and the most secure fitting. Many other brands don't have any app support for earbuds in this price range, but I love being able to customize the equalization to improve clarity for different types of music. I also love the ability to improve performance and fix bugs with firmware updates, if the company provides them. In summary, I can hear the difference in sound quality and performance difference between these earbuds and $120 earbuds from different brands but I'm not sure the difference is big enough to justify the 2X price difference. If you only have $60 to spend, these are a fine choice for you. If you're the type that is constantly losing wireless earbuds, these aren't so expensive that you will be really upset if you lose them.

title: works great with OnePlus phones, mediocre-to-OK with other Android phones and iPhones
review:
If you own OnePlus smartphone, these earbuds are easy to recommend. The budget-friendly $80 price matches the demographic that OnePlus has been cultivating. More importantly, some of the features of these earbuds only work with OnePlus phones. This includes Dolby Atoms and low-latency gaming playback.

Sound quality is clear, but very bass heavy. Unlike more better quality earbuds, these have no equalizer feature to help you get a more natural sound profile. Curiously, these earbuds do have the AAC CODEC for iPhones, but no aptX that Android phones prefer.

Noise cancellation is pretty good for this price range, though it does reduce your battery life somewhat. Battery life without noise cancellation is about average for the budget-price point, but not as good as what more expensive earbuds offer.

There is no wireless charging, though I'm not a huge fan of that anyway, especially for headphones.

I give 5 stars for OnePlus phone owners, but only 3.5 stars for everyone else.

title: inexpensive earbuds work OK with my Google Pixel 6 phone but sound isn't very rich
review: At just $15, these earbuds are inexpensive, especially for a USB-C connector. They work OK with my Google Pixel 6 phone with clear audio and no minimal static. The sound isn't very rich, but no worse that expected for the $15 price. Build quality is good for $15, especially with the carrying case included. I'll use them for listening to sports and audio podcasts, but the sound quality isn't good enough for listening to music.

title: sturdy stereo splitter, sound quality is good
review: This is a sturdily built stereo splitter. Works great to connect my phone to two stereo speakers or headphones. Sound quality is fine with no noise issues. Price is a little high for what you get, though.

title: does not work with Google smartphones
review:
I own a Google Pixel 6 smartphone with a USB-C port and no stereo audio port. I ordered these headphones because the product title says they will work with Google phones. These headphones do not work with my phone. They plug in to the USB-C port fine, but the phone does not recognize them. The product title says Google phones are supported and the product description says "universal compatibility with USB-C devices". Both statements are false. I own other USB-C headphones that work fine. 1 star.

I see Amazon selling a lot of products from this brand. I am now hesitant to order any of them.

title: noticeable step down from the Soundcore A2 earbuds
review:
I got a chance to try both the Soundcore A1 and Soundcore A2 earbuds. The price difference between these 2 models is relatively small, but I think additional features on the A2's is more than worth the price. The A1's might be a little over-priced at $60, while the A2's are a bargain at $80.

The A2's have noise cancellation, many more equalization settings that are easy to set via the smartphone app, upgradable firmware, and larger speaker drivers. The Soundcore smartphone app does not work with the A1's. All the extra features give the A2 earbuds noticeably better sound quality while also being easier to use. The A1's have decent sound quality, but there are a lot of $50 wireless earbuds that are just as good. On the other hand, the A2's feature and sound combination is better than any other $80 wireless earbuds that I have tried.

title: excellent sound quality and features for the $80 price
review:
The first couple of generations of Soundcore headphones were pretty mediocre. I'm glad the company keep improving their products. This year's models are really good for the price.

I got the Life A2 model. For $80, these earbuds come with features that I usually see on earbuds that cost more than $100 like equalization, noise cancellation, and upgradable firmware. These features all work great. I especially like the equalization that noticeably improves sound clarity.

Overall, the sound quality is great for earbuds that cost less than $100. Bass is not boomy, but great if you like a more natural sound. Stereo separation is excellent. Clarity at the higher frequencies is excellent when I set the equalizer to type of music that I'm listening too. Volume is better than average for true wireless earbuds.

These earbuds are on the larger side, but they don't stick out of my ears too much, so I don't constantly knock them out like I do with Apple-style earbuds. They are comfortable and secure enough in my ears.

I'm using an Android smartphone and the earbuds pair easily with my phone. Bluetooth connection has been solid. The Soundcore Android app is necessary to manage the equalizer and upgrade the firmware and both features work great. The app also shows your battery levels. Unfortunately, the app does spam me occasionally with unrelated Anker product announcements. I wish they wouldn't do that. Anker spams me enough by email.

title: [Life Q30] very good travel headphones
review:
These are very good travel headphones. Over-the-ear style is very comfortable when worn for hours at a time. The headphones are relatively lightweight and compact. They fold nicely into the included EVA soft-shell case, which fits easily into my carry-on bag.

The headphones pair easily with my Android smartphone. The Soundcore smartphone app is required for upgrading the headphones' firmware. The app also lets you customize the equalization to one of the presets or you can design your own. Depending on the kind of music you are listening to, the equalizer can make a noticeable difference in clarity and balance.

Unfortunately, the app spams me with notifications about unrelated Anker products. Hopefully this will not be frequent.

Noise cancellation works well. There are 3 modes: on, off (normal), and transparency that lets you talk to people around you without taking the headphones off. Noise cancellation can be toggled both from the app and from a button on the headphones themselves.

Overall, sound quality is good. More of a balanced sound than the boomy default effects that some headphones give. I mostly listen to acoustic music, so this works well for me. Clarity is good. Bluetooth connectivity has been great so far.

title: not really hard shell, but more protection than a soft case
review:
This case is made from somewhat stiff EVA, like the cases for headphones, etc. It does give you a lot more protection than soft cases, but it is not a hard case like the ones made from ABS or fiberglass or aluminum. It does bend with just hand pressure.

The interior size of the case is shown in the product description. The case is an inch deeper than my 13 inch Chromebook, but I knew that from the product description before I received it. It may be a snugger fit for Macbooks.

I like that they use sturdy genuine YKK zippers since zippers are always the first part to break on cases like this.

There are no handles of any kind on this case. There is one slim non-padded interior pocket that you could use for papers.

title: good but not great sound quality for $130, no noise cancellation or ambience mode
review:
These earbuds sound good, but not as good as some $100 earbuds that I own and not much better than $80 earbuds that I own. Sound is crisp and clear, but bass is a little weak in rock and roll music. Volume is adequate, but not as loud as some other true wireless earbuds.

I downloaded the Yamaha Headphones Controller app from the Google Play app store. The app lets check for firmware updates (none available) and enable "listening care", which is a basic equalizer that improves music clarity a little. There are no settings for different listener preferences or music styles. There is no noise cancellation or equalizer profiles, which my $100 earbuds have. There is no ambience passthrough mode, which even my $80 earbuds have.

6 hour battery life is great, but my $100 earbuds have similar battery life with more volume.

These earbuds have a simple plastic look and feel. They fit in my ears securely and I'm not worried about knocking them out (like I am with earbuds that stick farther out of my ears).

In summary, these earbuds sound pretty good, but there are many cheaper earbuds that sound just as good and have more features.

title: durable construction
review: This is a nicely built cable; should last longer than the cheap cables with thin wires and plastic connectors. Works great for connecting older stereo devices that use RCA jacks to newer speakers or headphones that use 3.5mm stereo cables.

title: smaller 7x5x4 case is perfect size for folding over-ear headphones
review: I got the smaller 7x5x4 case. This is the perfect size for my folding over-the-ear headphones with space for some spare cables in the upper compartment. This is a standard EVA case that protects the contents from bumps and dirt, but is not really crush-proof if you sit on it, etc. No complaints for the $8 price, so 5 stars.

title: excellent for the $18 price, works fine with Google Pixel 2 phone
review: I am using these headphones in the USB-C port on my Google Pixel 2 phone. They work great for the $17 price. Music is crisp and clear with good stereo separation and decent bass; better than expected for $17. Lots of volume. The package includes 3 pairs of different sizes of eartips. The silicone ear tips are not as comfortable (to me) as memory foam, but are very good for this price. The thin wire does tangle more easily than the thicker or flat cables of some other headphones, but I'll excuse that at this price level. 5 stars for good performance at a value price.

title: pricey for memory foam tips, but very comfortable and great sound quality
review: Amazon sells a lot of different memory foam eartips and these are above average in price. They work well. They have a stiff plastic inner sleeve so they attach to my earbuds securely. I find the foam to be much more comfortable than the silicone eartips that usually come with earbuds. Foam eartips also give me a better fit than silicone. Sound quality is great for me, but I think this is mostly because they fit well.

title: handy case for organizing cables, headphones, chargers when traveling
review: This is a handy case for organizing my cables, headphones, chargers when traveling. I use the elastic loops for cables and headphones. Wall charger goes in the zippered pocket. There's a little more space for other miscellaneous items. The case doesn't have much padding, so I wouldn't put a cellphone in here unless I was packing this case in sturdy briefcase. I like that it is thin and doesn't take up much space when not loaded.

title: inexpensive, loud, mediocre sound quality, works with Google Pixel 2
review: I am using these earbuds with my Google Pixel 2 phone's USB-C port. These are the cheapest USB-C earbuds that I own. They do not sound terrible. They are loud and not noisy. Musical quality is mediocre with worse clarity and worse bass than other USB-C headphones that i own. The earpieces don't fit all the way into my ear canals, so they do let in background sound, which is fine for listening to announcements on the train, but it also lets in noise that I don't want.

title: more comfortable than the silicone ear tips that came with my headphones
review: These fit better and are more comfortable than the silicone ear tips that came with my headphones. Since they fit better, I also get better noise isolation. Glad to see that a large set of tips is available at a reasonable price. I don't expect these to last as long as the silicone tips. I took a chance and ordered the smaller 4.5mm size and that works with some of my earphones, but is too small for others. I'm going to order the larger size as well and hopefully that will fit the others.

title: average sound quality for necklace-style earbuds
review: Necklace-style earbuds seem to be going out of style these days. They are bulkier and heavier and generally less comfortable than the more compact earbuds, but they do have important advantages. The necklace lets them hold a much bigger battery than compact Bluetooth earbuds, especially compared to the "true wireless" style and thus the battery life is tremendously better (up to 15 hours with the noise cancelling turned off). Sound quality of these earbuds is good: generally loud and clear with a good frequency range. Noise cancelling seems weak to me, though I've never been a fan of noise cancellation on earbuds, since the earbuds block so much external noise already. My main complaint is that these earbuds are much more expensive than LG or Motorola necklace-style earbuds that I have found to have about the same sound quality.

title: pretty good for this price level, water resistant, comfortable, average sound quality
review:
These earbuds are pretty good for this price level. The sound is smooth, not tinny like you usually get with cheap headphones. The sound is not as detailed as more expensive earbuds, though. There is enough bass for the acoustic music that I usually listen to, but it is not thumping like with some headphones. Higher frequencies are not as bright and clear as on more expensive earbuds.

There are a lot of different ear tips in the box. The pair that were pre-installed didn't give me very good sound quality, but different size/shaped ear tips (that were included) worked much better for me. If you're hearing weak bass, switching eartips can often fix that problem as well as improve comfort.

10 hour battery life is pretty good for lightweight earbuds like this; much better than the "true wireless" style of earbuds. Sound quality is also much better than "true wireless" earbuds in this price range.

Lightweight and water resistant makes these earbuds great for running and other workouts. Many earbuds are heavier and quickly become uncomfortable when I'm working out.

I like that a simple carrying case is included to keep these from getting tangled and broken when I'm carrying them in my gym bag.

title: great bass, great stereo separation, mediocre high frequency response, great battery life
review:
These are good earbuds for people who like boomy bassy music. I hear much more bass on these than with any of my other earbuds(even some very expensive ones). Stereo separation is great and I hear a lot of midrange detail on both channels. The main negative is that these earbuds lack brightness at the higher frequencies, so they are not too good for acoustic music.

Comfort is average for sports-oriented headphones. I like the ear hooks, which are a bit of a hassle to get into, but then are very secure when I'm running or working out. The hooks are comfortable enough. They also give you the option of using ear-wings, which I'm not a fan of, but I suppose some people like. The ear pieces come in 4 different sizes instead of the 2 or 3 sizes that most other brands supply. Picking the right size is important for getting the best sound quality.

The earbuds are sweat and weather resistant, which is great for sports. 11 hour battery life is tremendous and these charge pretty quickly as well.

title: better than most $50 true wireless headphones, but mediocre compared to higher priced headphones
review:
I've used a few other true wireless headphones in the $50 price range (mostly unknown brands) as well as some more expensive brand name models (B&O, Plantronics). This set is better than most headphones in the under $50 price range. Sound is clear and noise free. Volume is loud enough for earbuds, but not booming at full volume. Bass is kind of weak, though that is a common problem in this price range. 3 hour battery life is about average for this price range. Comparing $50 headphones to $100 headphones is not really fair, but if you do want to spend more money, most headphones will give you much better bass and richer overall sound quality. More expensive headphones also give me better battery life (usually at least 4 hours without any recharging). On the other hand, if I'm out running or riding on the subway, I'd rather use these $50 headphones instead of risk losing much more expensive headphones.

I am impressed by the build quality of these Soundcore headphones. They headphones feel solid. They are comfortable in my ears. The case is sleek and the recharging system works well. The buttons that control the headphones work easily and reliably. I do wish they used a modern USB-C charging system instead of the old-fashioned micro-USB.

title: very good Bluetooth earbuds for sports, but really do not like the proprietary charging dongle
review:
These are very good Bluetooth earbuds for sports use. Construction is very lightweight, but still very durable. Earpieces are very secure when I'm running or working out at the gym and more than comfortable enough for hour-long workouts. Sound quality is pretty good out-of-the-box, but a little thin at the higher frequencies (especially noticeable with acoustic music). Fortunately, Jaybird has a great smartphone app you can use to equalize the sound. I was never very good at designing my own equalization profiles by ear, but the app has several ready made profiles so I just picked the one that sounded best with my favorite music (boosting higher frequencies more than lower frequencies). There is no noise cancellation, but noise isolation is very good with the included foam eartips (not the default eartips).

I really do not like that you need a special dongle to recharge this headset. You can't just plug a standard USB cable directly into these, like with most Bluetooth headset. This may have something to do with the headset's waterproof rating, but other headsets I own are also waterproof and can still be recharged with a standard cable. I am concerned that the proprietary charging dongle will get lost or broken or I will just forget to bring it with me when traveling.

title: good sound quality for sports headphones, sweat resistant, secure when running
review:
I'm surprised by the negative reviews that these headphones are getting. I think they sound great for sports headphones in this price range. Bass sounds natural, not boomy. Midrange is very clear with great stereo separation. Volume is very good for Bluetooth earbuds. I'm using a Google Pixel 2 phone, so YMMV if you pair with something else.

The headphones are very comfortable and secure when I run with them. They are sweat-resistant and feel durable to me (no problems yet). Battery life is great at 8 hours. Most newer electronic devices use USB-C power plugs, so seeing the older micro-USB on this is disappointing. I'm also disappointed that they do not include a storage case.

title: excellent Bluetooth earbuds for sports
review:
These are great Bluetooth earbuds for sports use. Construction is very lightweight, but still very durable. Earpieces are very secure when I'm running or working out at the gym and more than comfortable enough for hour-long workouts. Sound quality is pretty good out-of-the-box, but a little thin at the higher frequencies (especially noticeable with acoustic music). Fortunately, Jaybird has a great smartphone app you can use to equalize the sound. I was never very good at designing my own equalization profiles by ear, but the app has several ready made profiles so I just picked the one that sounded best with my favorite music (boosting higher frequencies more than lower frequencies). There is no noise cancellation, but noise isolation is very good with the foam eartips.

I really don't like that you need a special dongle to recharge this headset. You can't just plug a standard USB cable directly into the thing. This may have something to do with the headset's waterproof rating, but other headsets I own are also waterproof and can still be recharged with a standard cable. I am concerned that the proprietary charging dongle will get lost or broken or I will just forget to bring it with me when traveling.

title: mediocre sound quality, great battery life, good volume, comfortable to wear
review: These earbuds are small and light; very comfortable to wear. Volume is loud enough. Battery life is great. Unfortunately, sound quality is mediocre. There is decent bass, but higher frequencies are more muddy than crisp. Not very enjoyable for the music I like to listen to. Even at this budget price level, I rate these earbuds are below average because of the sound clarity.

title: the best sounding Bluetooth earbuds I have ever tried
review: These are easily the best sounding Bluetooth earbuds that I have ever tried. Bass sounds natural without being artificially boosted like in some earbuds. Excellent clarity in the mid and upper frequencies. Acousting music and vocals sound really great. Overall volume can be louder than I ever want. 8 hour playing time puts those Apple earbuds to shame. A couple of minor complaints: I don't like devices that still use the outdated micro-USB connectors, especially now that USB-C is becoming widespread. At least they do include a cable. Also, the buttons are a little confusing with the big central button controlling on/off, play/pause, and phone answer/call/redial. I don't make many phone calls through my earbuds, but if you do, the controls may be a problem for you.

title: Works great for charging my Pixel 2 smartphone while listening to music with wired headphones
review: Works great for charging my Pixel 2 smartphone while listening to music with wired headphones. There are a lot of similar products on Amazon and I bought this one because it was the cheapest at $19. Connecters feel solid and the metal case feels durable.

title: inexpensive over-the-ear bluetooth headphones have very good build quality but mediocre sound quality
review: These headphones are relatively inexpensive for build quality, compared to the name brands. They look and feel solid. Comfort is fine. Splashproof/sweatproof design is great for use outdoors or in a noisy gym. The bluetooth syncs quickly and easily with my Android smartphone. My phone shows the headphone power level so I can remember to recharge them. They conveniently fold up and fit into the included carrying bag. Actual sound quality is mediocre, as is typical of bluetooth headphones in this price range. Vocals are fine, but music detail is a little muddy. If you're looking for inexpensive comfortable over-the-ear headphones for use while jogging or working out or working in the yard, these are worth checking out. If you want to listen to music from a high quality player in a quiet room in your house, I think investing more money in your headphones is a good idea.

title: cheaper, but worse sound quality and much worse battery life compared to LG or Motorola necklace-style bluetooth earbuds
review: I also own and enjoy LG Tone and Motorola Buds necklace-style bluetooth earbuds. These iHome earbuds are cheaper than LG and Motorola, but you get what you pay for. Battery life on the iHome product is much worse than LG or Motorola (6-7 hours vs 10-12 hours) and long battery life is one of the main reasons I prefer the necklace-style earbuds vs the simpler styles. Music volume is louder on the iHome buds, but LG and Motorola were loud enough for me. At similar volumes, iHome has noticeably lower clarity than the other brands.

title: much better sound quality than expected for the $10 price, mediocre battery life
review:
These earbuds are cheap ($10) and look and feel like toys. Very lightweight all plastic exterior. I wasn't expecting much, but the sound is very good for this price level. At the moderate volumes that I like to use, the music does not sound distorted or tinny. Not as much detail as from a bigger heavier headphone, but this is fine for listening to MP3s on my cellphone when I'm jogging. The lightweight construction means it doesn't fall out of my ears as often as heavier earbuds. I have tried some of the other cheap bluetooth headphones from Amazon, and this is the best that I have used for under $10. It even uses one of the newer Bluetooth standards that shows headphone power level on my phone screen; as someone who is always worried about rechargeable devices running out of power, this is a really great feature. Unfortunately, battery life is somewhat less than the advertised 5 hours. Even at moderate volumes, I'm down to about 50% battery after an hour and a half. That's fine for a gym workout or a subway commute, but not for airline travel.

It comes packaged in a self-destructing pile of paper and plastic. I wish they had included a carrying case instead of all this garbage.

title: pricey, but very good sound quality, good build quality, and more comfortable to wear than most earbuds
review:
Very good headphones. Smallish ear pieces and the black plastic shell is not real attractive, but they feel solid and well made. Rubber ear tips are comfortable for long periods of time and 3 different sizes of replacement tips are included. Bass is very good and overall sound clarity is much better than with cheap headphones. Full volume is more than loud enough for me and distortion at the highest volume is tolerable (unlike with cheap headphones). Wrap-around cables can be a hassle, but these have thicker wires and don't tangle as much as others that I have tried. Wrap-around cables really prevent the earbuds from falling out when I am working out. A simple nylon bag is the only carrying case included in the oversized box, but better cases are available at dollar stores.

Yes, Apple is trying to kill off wired headphones, but wired headphones still have huge advantages over Bluetooth, such as not having to worry about battery life, being able to recharge your phone at the same time you are listening to music, and of course the sound quality of wired headphones is usually better than similarly priced Bluetooth headphones.

title: Surprisingly good sound quality for the price ($19 when I bought them)
review: Surprisingly good sound quality for the price ($19 when I bought them). I found them comfortable to wear when walking or jogging. Volume is good once I figured out how where the volume control was (default volume setting is too low). The on/off button is a hassle compared to the simple slider on my LG-Tones. Another negative is that these are an inch longer than the LG-Tones, so all the cheap LG-Tones cases you see on Amazon will not fit these headphones.

title: essentially the same as other LG Tone cases sold on Amazon
review: There are a bunch of these LG Tone cases on Amazon. I bought this one and one other, mostly because they were the cheapest (this case was $8 at the time and the other was $7). Quality of the 2 products is similar. This one is half an inch shorter than the other one, but otherwise no noticeable differences in quality or performance. My headphones fit fine in both cases and these cases offer plenty of protection for my use (dropping the headphones in my backpack). We have 2 of these headsets in our family so only need 2 cases, but if we ever need another case, we'll just buy whatever is cheapest.

title: essentially the same as other LG Tone cases sold on Amazon
review: There are a bunch of these LG Tone cases on Amazon. I bought this one and one other, mostly because they were the cheapest (this case was $7 at the time and the other was $8). Quality of the 2 products is similar. This one is half an inch longer than the other one, but otherwise no noticeable differences in quality or performance. My headphones fit fine in both cases and these cases offer plenty of protection for my use (dropping the headphones in my backpack). We have 2 of these headsets in our family so only need 2 cases, but if we ever need another case, we'll just buy whatever is cheapest.

title: average sound quality for the price
review: These are not great earbuds, but for the $20 price, they are average. Soft ear tips and angled ear pieces are comfortable to wear for long periods. The volume and pause buttons work properly with my Samsung Android phone, unlike most headphone controls that only work on iphone. The flat wires don't tangle as easily as thin round cables, but are still lightweight enough not to bounce around uncomfortably when running. Sound quality is mediocre, however. Bass is strong, but midrange lacks clarity. For about the same price, there are more popular brands with better sound quality (especially midrange clarity).

title: best for smaller heads, sound quality is mediocre
review:
These are OK for the $20 price, but could be better. The short cable between the 2 ear pieces make these best for small-to-medium sized heads. I wear a size 7.5 hat (large, but not extra large) and the cable is too short to wrap around my ears like the advertising photo shows. Sound quality is only average with less clarity than in-ear type Bluetooth earbuds (available for about the same price on Amazon), though this type of headphone that doesn't fit all the way in your ear may be more comfortable for some people.

On the plus side, this headset pairs easily with my phone and is very compact and easy to store (unlike headphones with long wires that are always tangling or snagging). No case is included, however.

title: great sound for $10, minimal accessories with this packaging
review: These headphones sound much better than most other $10 headphones that I have used. Since I loose them often, I get to try a lot of headphones, and I also value the low price of this set. I'm only giving these 4 stars however, because of the disappointing set of accessories that you get. All other MEElectronics headphones that I have bought come with a nice carrying case and twice as many different ear tips to guarantee a comfortable fit. This set comes in a plastic bag with a minimal set of extra tips.

title: poor Bluetooth sound quality; mediocre when wired
review:
These are big heavy headphones, but the large well-padded ear cups make them comfortable to me, even over glasses. The fold up design makes them reasonably portable for travel use.

I see a lot of good ratings here, but I found the Bluetooth performance to be mediocre, with muddy sound at all frequencies (but especially noticeable at higher frequencies). Maybe this is just an incompatibility with my Android phone, but other Bluetooth headphones sound fine to me when paired with my phone. Using the cord, I get much better sound quality, but still not as clear as other headphones that I use and enjoy. Really cannot recommend these at this price.

title: below average price, below average sound
review: These headphones are pretty disappointing. They are lightweight and comfortable enough. Bass is decent. However, the midrange and higher frequencies sound muffled and compressed. I found the sound quality to be less pleasing than even good quality earbuds (costing about the same as these headphones). Compared to more expensive headphones, these are significantly worse (though none of the other headphones I regularly use is this cheap). If you can't use earbuds because of comfort or fit issues and you don't want to wear expensive headphones in a noisy environment like a public bus, then these may be good enough for you. If you're listening to music in a quiet environment (like in your home), I have to recommend spending a little more for much better sound quality from other products.

title: very comfortable over-the-ear headphones, excellent neutral sound
review: I'm not an audiophile, but I do like my music and I've heard a lot of awful headphones over the years (including awful and expensive). These are great all-around headphones. They are not real heavy or real bulky, but they still fit over my ears, which is much more comfortable than on-ear headphones, especially if you wear glasses. Sound quality is very clear and neutral at all frequencies. The bass is not overwhelming like you get with some designer headphones. The microphone works with my Android phone, though only the middle button works (to answer calls or pause music). The up and down buttons are unfortunately only for iphone. I like that these headphones fold up for easy portability, though not including a protective carrying case is disappointing (you just get a cloth bag).

title: different design may be more comfortable for some people, average sound quality for this price
review: Unlike most earbuds, these do not have soft rubber tips that fit in your ear and seal off outside sound. If you find the rubber tip style to be uncomfortable, you may want to give this design a try. These earbuds have once-size-fits-most hard plastic tips that are fairly comfortable in my ears. I've used a lot of headphones and these are about average in sound quality for this price. Sound is balanced, unlike some popular brands that over-emphasize the bass and only sound good with rap or rock music. Midrange clarity is pretty good. Volume is OK; these do not get as loud as some other earbuds, but probably get loud enough for most people. Build quality is pretty good, with midweight cords that resist tangling, but are not so heavy that they bounce around uncomfortably when running. No carrying case is included, unfortunately.

title: good but not great sound, great value for $8
review: These are not the best earbuds that I own, but the sound pretty quality is good, making this a really great value at $8. Vocals are clear and the bass is rich. Build quality is very good for this price. Microphone works with Android, not just iphone. I bought 5 more before the price goes up.

title: good value for $10
review: Most $10 headphones sound tinny. These actually sound decent. Not as accurate as $50 earbuds, but decent bass and good clarity in the midrange. These also come with much better accesories than other earbuds in this price range. The case is very useful and you get 5 pairs of ear tips to guarantee a comfortable and clear sounding fit. The wires are not thick and heavy like you get in a lot of better headphones, but heavy cables are a negative if you use the headphones for running since they uncomfortably bounce around. These cables are thick enough to reduce tangling problems, but not heavy enough to cause problems when exercising. I really can't complain about anything for the $10 price and you regularly can find these for $10 from various vendors, including Amazon at times.

title: disappointing sound quality
review: I have the Marley "People Get Ready" headphones and like those, so wanted to try these, too. I think the sound is disappointing with limited bass. Not recommended.

title: Mostly works with Android, great sound and value for $24
review:
I use these with my Android cell phone. The controls mostly work. I can make calls with the microphone and answer calls with the middle button. When playing music, the middle button also pauses/resumes the playback. The volume control buttons appear to have no functionality with Android.

Very happy with the sound from these headphone. There is very good bass as well as good detail in the higher frequencies. If you're using the stock headphones that came with your phone or MP3 player, these will give you a significant improvement in sound quality.

The drivers on these headphones are very large compared to many other products, with a large chunk sitting outside your ear. Seems comfortable enough, but the headphones will be very noticeable to people who see you on the street.

The thick cords are both good and bad. The good is that they are very tangle-resistant. The bad is that they are heavier than wire cords and bounce around uncomfortably when running. I'm going to use different headphones for running. I haven't had any problems with durability yet, but I haven't had them very long.

Now that the price has dropped to $24, I ordered 3 more. I have used a lot of headphones over the years and these are clearly the best that I have ever bought for less than $30. I don't give out 5 stars ratings very often, but will do so here because of the unbeatable value at the $24 price, despite the volume buttons not working with my phone.

title: great for the $20 price, if you like bass
review:
I have a couple of these Marley earbuds, as well as more expensive Klipsch S3 and S4 earbuds. These Marleys have a noticeably stronger bass sound than the Klipsch products, but it is smooth, not harshly amplified like in cheaper products. If you like bass or like music that sounds good with heavier bass, then give these a try. You're not going to find much better for $20. The Klipsch models are a little more accurate in the mid and higher frequencies, which is great for classical music or opera.

The Marley earbuds do have a cloth-wrapped cord which looks kind of cool, as well as adding strength and reducing tangles. The microphone and push button work great with my Android smartphone. The rubber ear tips are comfortable for me even during hours of continuous listening, though they don't seal quite as well as the oval Klipsch ear tips. No quality issues after months of use.

title: good case for the price
review:
This is a decent padded case for the price. There is a lot of padding, so it is good for fragile objects or unusually shaped objects. I use it for my ContourHD camera and the side pocket fits my spare battery. You could also put an iphone (just barely) or ipod in there and put your headphones in the pocket. Check the dimensions to see if another item will fit. The case is not very thick, so thin pocket video cameras like Flips and Vados should fit, but boxy P&S compact cameras may not.

Note that this case is shorter than the similar looking, similar priced Case Logic case. If you have one of those Android phones with a bigger screen than the iphone, you should get the Case Logic case instead.[[ASIN:B001S0PWWC Case Logic TBC-312 Pocket Video Camcorder Case with Storage (Black)]]

title: works like magic
review:
I don't know what this thing really does, but it is magic. Without it, plugging my NookColor into my decent quality portable speakers created awful static noise. The noise was so bad that I almost returned the NookColor as defective (my ipod and cell phone work fine with the same speakers). A friend recommended this PAC device, which he bought for $20 at a local car stereo store, but I bought for $13 here at Amazon. It is magic. Music played from my NookColor now sounds wonderfully clear.

The PAC device uses no batteries; just plug it in like a headphone cable. My friend says it matches the impedence from a music player and incompatible speaker systems. I don't know what that means, the Amazon description is not helpful, and the device comes with no useful documentation, but it really does work.

title: presses the headset button!
review: This case is worthless with my Motorola HS815 headset.  Every time I put the headset in the case, the case squeezes the activation button on the headset.  Maybe it will work with headsets that do not have the activation button on the outside surface.

title: Suprisingly good!
review: I ordered these and did not expect much. These are amazing. They are almost a dupe for my original iPhone earbuds. The sound quality is excellent. I had them in and my doorbell rang, I barely heard it ringing! I have only had them for a couple of days, but so far, so good. I have wanted wireless earbuds, but I have been having trouble with connecting them or I have lost them, so I guess I will stick with my trusty "wired" earbuds.

title: Definitely recommend
review: I bought 4 wireless headphones and ear buds off Amazon and I reason is cause the left ear on each one kept breaking randomly and I only had them for awhile so I got to annoyed and purchased these wired headphones, delighted I did I love the look of them and the quality etc is brilliant I'm very happy with them! And the packaging was really nice. I would recommend.

title: Perfect!!
review: Most comfortable headphones that fit in the ear that I’ve ever used. All others that I’ve tried have been painful and these aren’t. I’m beyond thrilled!

title: Sturdy. Easy to find!
review: Great for for headphones. I like the color for ease detection while packing. Hardshell better then the one the headpieces arrives with fitting purchase.

title: Great accessories
review: I bought this along with my new headphones and they all work great in the differnent areas I will be on the air planes and the gym. I can plug into the computer at home the television and then on a bus while traveling from one area to another in my travels.

title: Really Great Headphones!!
review: I work in an area where there is a lot of noice and my radio wil not pick it up. But with these headphones and I bought these to 'drown out the noice" and they work!! The two day delivery was fast and very smooth. I really like the way they move when I am sitting and tying as well.  These are a nice looking pair of headphones to travel with in the future. I like the way they pack away in my overhead back pack. Great buy!!

title: Super Tight
review: These headphones are great, they have wonderful quality, they are just too tight for my head. I have to find a way to stretch them out so they are comfortable. As they are now, they squeeze my ears really tightly. Otherwise, they are definitely worth the money. The microphone works terrifically. Great sound.

title: Stereo Headset with Noise Canceling Mircophone DYNEX
review: This is a great microphone and headset, wish there was an extra mic cover and ear speaker covers but it's great. Thanks, love noise reduction. I use it a lot when I am dictation to Dragon Naturally Speaking (on one computer) or my IBM Via Voice (on the other computer).

title: Not for the Mac Pro
review:
This product might be the best microphone since Marconi but it didn't work for me. I bought this because the Mac Pro doesn't have an internal mic. Amazingly it also doesn't have a mic port. It has 3.5 mm headphones and speaker ports. I thought I could plug this into one of those ports. No luck.
The headset port apparently requires a 4 conductor 3.5 mm TRRS plug. Neither the computer maker nor the mic/headset maker ever give you this type of critical information. I probably should have purchased a USB mic instead. So now I either buy a USB mic or a USB adaptor.

My general comment about microphones and headsets is that the descriptions (both Amazons and the manufacturers) are almost always weak on connectors, adaptors and compatability (PC/MAC/etc). This is the most important feature and should be at the top of any description. After all if it doesn't fit or work what good is it.

title: No Warranty Support - Terrible Service
review:
The headset sound quality is at best, decent. It is nothing better than that. The build quality is exactly what you would expect for the money.

The reason I would NEVER recommend this manufacturer because when it came time to honor a simple warranty repair it was hopeless. Poor-Poor-VERY POOR!

At this price point there are many other better options. I now have a MPOW set(s) and while the build quality is somewhat similar, the important thing is that when I needed a simple replacement part to complete a very easy repair they had the item needed to me inside of THREE-DAYS from the date of my request to them. Excellent.

title: Good sound with ? QC
review: I very much wanted to like this headset.
