I like the idea of the wings as supports in theory, but they are not adjustable.  So if the angle is wrong, it's wrong.  The wings hold it up really vertically, which is not an angle that usually works well for me.  I'd get a different case if I were to purchase again, but I suppose this provides protection so we will stick with it for now.  That's a lot of plastic to just throw in the landfill because it's not perfect.

title: Nice Pair of headphones for the price
review: Great pair of inexpensive headphones. Workmanship quality seems to be very good (after experiencing a couple other brands in the same price range) and sound quality is great.

title: Ugh! Do not buy these earphones!
review: I just went through my second pair of these. I bought the first pair in February, and they died on me a couple of months ago. Then i bought another pair. After 1-2 months, I find that I am getting shocked by them!! I do not abuse my headphones; I use them at work in my cube so they don't move around a lot, so I'm not sure why they are shocking me. They're too inexpensive to bother sending back.

title: Love these headphones
review: To be fair, I haven’t used a “proper” set of noise canceling over-the-ear headphones before, so I don’t have a good comparison. I will say that when I put them on and then power them, the environmental noise is immediately and dramatically reduced. The sound quality is very nice. Again, I’m not a sound engineer, but I feel the range of tones is great. Nice full sound, noise suppression, and light weight. And it doesn’t make my ears sweat even after a few hours of wearing them.

title: Works for Old BT that Auto-Pairs
review: Works for things that auto pair. Most BT devices don’t anymore. I wish Baile would sell BT headlhones that work with it. I bout their BT headphones hoping for that but nope. Great headphones though. The only thing I can get it to pair with is a cheap bluetooth speaker which is not what I ordered it for.

title: Excellent sound, good isolation.
review:
These headphones are an upgrade from the Sony MDR-7506 that's I've been using for the last 10 years. Better separation, larger sound stage and more complete isolation. I am perfectly please with them, particularly given the less than $150 price tag.

The hard case was a nice add, not changing the cost in an appreciable way, and I have gotten more use from it than I expected that I would.

title: Excellent sound, good isolation.
review: These headphones are an upgrade from the Sony MDR-7506 that's I've been using for the last 10 years. Better separation, larger sound stage and more complete isolation. I am perfectly please with them, particularly given the less than $150 price tag.

title: Great headphones for kids!
review:
My daughter loves these headphones! Especially the attachable kitty ears!

I actually used them one night and the sound quality is great for such I expensive headphones. They do great with noise cancelling too, but that's a downside with kids....they can't hear you calling them....or maybe it's actually a benefit!

My daughter is 5.5 and a pretty small child but they fit her perfectly, and they are saving my sanity!

title: Don't like earbuds, tried the headphones that wrap around back ...
review: Don't like earbuds, tried the headphones that wrap around back of head, but those always slip, and this type works the best for me.  Sound is very good.

title: I DO really like how these fit in my ears [Updated 2017-05-14]
review:
When I'm walking, I have to carry my phone in my front pocket instead of in my usual back pocket if I want a somewhat reliable stream of music that doesn't break up all the time. Surprised by this - I thought the Bluetooth would be more robust.

I DO really like how these fit in my ears - generally I don't like these sorts of headphones, but with the multiple fit options Anker included, I was actually able to achieve a comfortable and secure fit without feeling like the headphones were jammed into my ear canals.

Update 2017-05-14: Anker Customer Service contacted me and arranged for replacement and return of my first pair of these. Unfortunately, I have the same Bluetooth issues with the second pair. :( HOWEVER - I commend Anker Customer Service for their responsiveness and for working to compensate me for my trouble with both pairs. It was much appreciated. (And since, from reading reviews here, it sounds like Anker continues to tinker with these headphones to improve them, I'm definitely interested in the final version of these that they come up with.)

title: Good quality, great fit, excellent integration
review: Good quality, great fit, excellent integration. No drawbacks that I can tell compared to others. I have Apple pro pods as well. These feel and work just as well, but are a tiny bit heavier so they give the impression of being more durable. My favorite earbuds are Ankers. These compare favorably. It's great to be able to talk to Alexa and get what you want without touching the earbuds while you're working out. My wake word is Alexa and my trainer knows it, so sometimes he'll walk by and yell, "ALEXA PLAY CARDI B!" And he knows I HATE TO LISTEN TO CARDI B!!!  Some fun. I recommend these earbuds, especially at any discounted price.

title: Ideal for Bluetooth, charger cable, earpods, Shuffle, etc.
review: This is the first of the CASEBUDi's that I purchased via Amazon.  It's small, clips onto things (I have it clipped onto my purse), has a tiny mesh pocket for holding earpods, Shuffle, etc., and can still carry something else (small charger cable, Bluetooth earpiece, etc.).  I've since ordered two more in different colors (pink, white) for carrying even more little things.  They easily slip into my purse or wherever I need and still afford protection (they are somewhat rigid without being overly plastic-y).  Despite what I've read from other reviewers stating they are made cheaply or the carabiners don't work, I haven't had a single problem.  I ordered another one to use with other small headphones of mine during travel.  I love that I can clip them to things whereas other brands' similar products do NOT come with a way to clip them on.  I like the 'modular' nature of CASEBUDi products.  I would recommend them to anyone.  See for yourself why they are so handy!!  You could even use them to carry a small pill box, a spare key, etc.  I hope they eventually come in even MORE colors to choose from.  Orange would be great!

title: Dead inside the return  window, don’t buy these
review:
I’ve had these for about a month or so, I don’t love how they feel in my ear, but they worked fine…until yesterday. The earbuds are still functioning but they’re running out of power. After further investigation, I found that the case is dead, it will no longer take a charge. Earbuds are functioning fine. Amazon CS agent was not helpful, but that’s not always the case.

I went through their trouble shooting videos (waste of time and very obvious help instructions I had already done). The case is dead, which renders the still functioning earbuds useless without a charging source.

Don’t by these, you’ll be shelling out for yet another pair in a matter of months, maximum.

Instead of sending me a new case, I am yet again expected to make a trip UPS to return another set of earbuds that die within the return window or just outside of it.
I’m tired of this. I wonder if AirPods are any better in lifespan, as I’ve spent more than their $250 cost on these cheaper sets.

title: Just not good
review: I'm very easy to please with things like this:  if it works, it works.  But at least for me, this cable has terrible connection and sound quality.  There is a constant buzzing sound when it is connected between my phone and headphones, and the sound quality is TERRIBLE.  Harsh bad sound that almost (literally) hurts my ears.  It is not good at all.  I won't be using it.

title: Love it!  Exactly what I was looking for
review:
THIS is exactly what I was wanting for swimming! I have used it maybe 4 times now, and it is working like a charm. I am no longer bored in the pool. I just started swimming laps for exercise, and I love it, but listening to music and audiobooks and podcasts has now immediately extended my swim time. I love it!! The library's website has so many free audiobooks to rent, and I can easily download them and load them onto this. It has a shuffle feature, which is nice.

The only negatives: I am having trouble "resetting" the player to the beginning. It plays songs in order of alphabet (so I have numbered all of the files on my computer so that audiobooks are at the beginning and then songs, etc), but if I get to say the 50th song and then want to go back to the beginning of the playlist...I cannot figure out how to do that, although in the instructions there is a way.
I initially had some trouble with the earbuds causing pain in my ears when they would seal, but switching to some of the smaller pieces that are included has helped with this.

This is exactly what I was looking for, and i bought the $11 warranty for 3 years, so I have no fears about it going dead on me. I cannot recommend this product enough for those looking for an underwater mp3.

title: TheWirecutter.com's Best Non-Sealing Bluetooth Earbuds
review: I LOVE these headphones! I wanted wireless headphones that did NOT seal out surrounding sounds, mostly because I find the sealing kind of earbuds very uncomfortable. I ordered these after reading a recommendation from TheWirecutter.com, which rated them as the best non-sealing Bluetooth earbuds. I'm very happy with them! They're comfortable, charge incredibly quickly, and are easy and reliable to use, with an impressive Bluetooth range. They're even water-resistant - I have showered with them on!

title: Order during Cyber Monday lightning deals. Got a defective ...
review: Order during Cyber Monday lightning deals.  Got a defective pair that will not hold a charge and never turns on.  Won't replace the item so I am only getting a refund.  Now my money is tied up with that and I still need a pair of headphones.

title: Great Value for a Great Set of Headphones
review: These are incredibly good headphones at any price.  The only issue I have with them is the plastic coating on the wires make it really hard to maneuver.  Not sure what it is but the plastic does not seem pliable enough.  Sound is wonderful and the little storage bag it comes with is a great little benefit.  I would definately buy again if I needed another pair.

title: Significantly reduces noise cancellation capability of headphones.
review:
I purchased this to replace the ear muff that came with the headphones, since Sony incredibly doesn't offer replacements.

They are a bit more stiff than the standard ear muffs, but I don't consider that an issue.

However, having only replaced one of the ear muffs, I learned immediately that they allow a substantially greater amount of sound in than the standard ear muffs. The difference is comparable to passive noise cancellation vs active noise cancellation. I can hear very little through the stock ear muff, but can hear most sounds (albeit quieter) through the right ear muff, which is the one I replaced with this product.

I haven't been on a plane since getting these, but I don't think it would be sufficient anymore.

If you are just looking to be able to use your headphones again, I'd recommend this. However, if noise cancellation is what you need, I cannot recommend these.

title: Smells like chemicals and urine. Smell transfers to everything in case.
review:
I was excited to get this, and it seemed to do a good enough job of protecting my new pair of headphones, albeit a very tight fit. I used it shortly after getting it for a trip back home for the holidays.

Initially, it had a strong chemical odor, so I thought airing it out would do the trick. However, after letting the thing air our for several days at my office, there is still a persistent, strong smell of burning plastic and urine.

This scent then got on everything I put in it, including my new expensive headphones, which is absolutely unacceptable. Fortunately, the smell is only noticeable on the ear muffs when I smell them, but still, something that cost $200 dollars now has a slight urine smell on it...

If you like the smell of urine and burning plastic, then this case is for you.

title: Sound quality is like listening to music in a loud bar with cheap earplugs.
review:
I bought these to replace some headphones I left in a rental car. Although these look absolutely stunning, the quality of the audio is atrocious. There is absolutely no treble for any of the music I played through them. The base really booms, but that's all you can hear. The first thing I thought of after listening to music with them on was having my head wrapped in a blanket, and putting headphones over that. For lack of a better way of putting it, I can't hear all of the music that I can with other headphones/headsets. I listened to the same music through my gaming headset to see if I was imagining things, and sure enough I was not, and my gaming headset is just fair for listening to music.

I was really excited because the reviews were fantastic, but I've yet again been burned by a bad product with good reviews.

0/10 would not recommend.

title: It's OK. Worth $60, not $120
review:
I got this instead of trying to get a replacement for an older kindle. The font looks nice, and there is an option to adjust the font size and spacing. This is fantastic because it allows for you to make the font easier to read while walking or working out, but smaller for when your in a chair or bed.

Other than that, it's OK. It has less features and cost more than the older version, which it replaced. There is no option for headphones, like the older one, and there is no option to turn the light completely off.

My biggest issue is that the screen looks blue in the dark, which is the exact opposite of what you want when you will be going to sleep soon. A quick google of "blue light and sleep" will explain why I say this.

The lighting on the screen is also not consistent. The bottom of the screen has darker spots which is really irritating, and probably deemed a replacement acceptable, but since I use it primarily for daylight, I chose to ignore it.

I'd say this item is worth about $50 or $60 bucks tops. Most certainly not worth the $120 asking price.

title: Exactly what I was looking for
review:
I have bought so many speakers for my office. I just hate plugging in my iPhone when I arrive at the office. I want the podcast I'm listening to to just switch to my office speaker when I arrive. And that's exactly what happens. I do have to turn the speaker on first. At that point my iPhone assumes the speaker is my choice so long as I leave BlueTooth switched on in the iPhone general settings.

I'm seriously considering buying a second one for home now. I'm becoming something of a fan of BOSE. I have a lot of their gear these days. If you're a teen looking for a seriously loud loud-speaker, perhaps this isn't for you. I don't blast music at the office. I listen to a little music and office acceptable levels. Mostly, I listen to Podcasts while on the way to work, and I typically want to finish them as I walk in the office. And I don't want to have to plug the phone into something. I just want the speaker to take over for my headphones. That's what this does.

I wish it had a remote though. I can change the volume from my phone, but the screen goes into screen saver mode and it takes a few strokes to do it. Sometimes I'd appreciate it if it had a mute on a remote so when a phone call comes in I could quickly cancel the sound. I can double-tap the iPhone and get the quick player controls and pause it. Not too bad.

I'd give this a solid 4/5 stars.

title: Get headphones
review: I've got a big old cabinet filled with my collection of vinyl albums, and decided it was time for a new player since my kids are all grown up (they destroyed the old one when they were little).  This one does a pretty good job.  That said, invest in a set of good headphones.  The built in speakers are there, but the sound is 'small and tinny'.  Phones make the sound sound just fine (but I'm not a fussy audiophile) for revisiting the past.

title: Perfect Out of the Box
review:
(Sept. 3, 2022) I bought this for a 2008 Thinkpad T61 that dual boots Linux Mint 20.3 XFCE (Ubuntu/Debian based), and MS Windows 10. YMMV if you are using other hardware and/or operating systems.

Linux:
I plugged the dongle in, opened the Bluetooth control panel, and paired the laptop with an iPhone SE 2020 and then paired it with a MPow Flame Bluetooth headset. Both devices worked fine, and the audio was clean and clear.

I shut the machine down and the booted it into Windows 10:
Same as above. I plugged the dongle in, opened Bluetooth Settings, and added the iPhone and then the headset. No muss, no fuss. I opened iTunes and listened to music and spoken word, and everything sounded fine.

I plan to install this dongle internally using a Mini PCI-E to USB3.0 PCI Express Card I found elsewhere.

title: Comfy
review: They fit an old Sony set of headphones I had lying around. Comfortable pads, and OK acoustinc transparency.

title: Good sound, great fit
review: OK, these aren't audiophile-quality earbuds. But they sound just fine, they fit comfortably in my ears, and they seem sturdy enough to hold up well -- unlike those super-cheap earbuds that break the third time you use them. A good option for someone who just needs a decent pair of comfortable earbuds.

title: Works great with Rosetta Stone
review: I gave these headphones to my daughter to use at school with Rosetta Stone. They are comfortable and work well. Couldn't ask for anything more!

title: Clear & Comfy - Great Box Office Tool
review:
This headset has saved my life (and my neck). It fits so comfortably on my head, never pressing into my ear, allowing me to freely multitask and assist patron; hands free to do their work.
Also, when recording my voicemail answering messages, the result is very clear and professional.
I'm so glad I added this to my box office hardware!

title: Not Terrible (pretty good)
review: My daughter uses these during school and finds them to be comfortable and they do a decent job at blocking out ambient sound. I tried them out and they are not terrible but I am accustomed to wearing full sized professional over ear headphones running a sound board so my perspective of them is not based on typical end user experience.

title: These seem like they'd be great... if they weren't cutting out every 10 seconds
review: I received these as a gift from my husband awhile ago and have tried using them multiple times when mowing the lawn (failure) or going for a walk (semi-failure) or sitting absolutely still staring at my phone (success). The sound cuts out every 10 seconds when doing anything with these earbuds in and trying to listen to YouTube on my phone unless I'm sitting stationary without moving at all. If I try to walk around, it cuts out UNLESS the phone is no more than 1 foot from the earbuds themselves, i.e. in a chest pocket. But that's not always practical. If I try to mow the lawn with these in, the sound cuts out so much I have been tempted to rip them off and throw them in the mower's path. I've un-paired and re-paired, haven't changed my phone at all, so I'm not sure what the problem is, but these will go in the closet and probably ignored for another year. Very frustrating. The two stars are for the nice sleek case and the decent form factor of the buds themselves. Everything else has been aggravating!

title: Good sound, but not easy to remove/reinsert frequently, plus questionable durability of cable
review: I bought these to use on a flight to Europe, and while these do tend to block out the ambient noise, they can be a little cumbersome to insert.  This is really only an issue if you remove them constantly, but I found myself doing so to either talk to my husband, a flight attendant, listen to announcements, go to the restroom, etc. so having to reinsert them each time was a little annoying.  I ended up using other headphones for the rest of the flight to make things a little easier.  My other issue with these earphones is the cable; it is thin and flimsy, and they could have really gone for a more robust cabling, either a thicker plastic or a wrapped plastic.  I worry about the durability of these units as a result, but will keep them around as a backup option.  The sound from these earphones is pretty good once you get them inserted and wait until the memory foam fills the ear canal.

title: Unpredictable Controls/Great Sound and Battery Life
review:
The noise cancellation and sound on these very comfortable headphones are, well, BOSE. My complaint about them is the swipe and button controls. I find that the smallest angle change can cause a video or song to skip to the next one and the “favorites” button works sometimes and sometimes not making, for example, changing to various levels of noise cancellation unpredictable. Besides being sometimes unresponsive, the buttons are sometimes over-sensitive: I’ve raised my arm to put something on a shelf and brushed a button with my sleeve and toggled the voice activation options many times.

All that said, the battery life, comfort and awesome sound are great. I just wish the controls were better.

title: These ones have been the longest lasting and most comfortable I've found
review: I use these for running and I tend to destroy headphones with decent regularity. These ones have been the longest lasting and most comfortable I've found. I love that the over-ear portion is adjustable too, not just the earbud size. It makes it much better for us more petite folks.

title: I think these would be a fine choice for someone with just slightly bigger ears than ...
review: I purchased these for use while running. The sound clarity is decent but I experienced occasional cutting out, I'm not sure how much of that is the headphones versus just the Bluetooth connection. They stayed on well but were a little bit too big for me to get a decent fit, even with having three sizes of the in-ear bits. I've been spoiled with previous headphones that had adjustable over-ear parts. I think these would be a fine choice for someone with just slightly bigger ears than me. They were easy to use, came in a nice case, and connected no problem. I like having the volume control on the earpiece too.

title: Broke after 7 months
review: These headphones shorted out after about 7 months of frequent wear. They are comfortable and stay on decently while running, but sweat WILL eventually get to them. Also the clip is weird and annoying, it comes off easily and is awkward to use. They may be better for a more casual user, I wore mine 3-5 times a week during that time and I tend to sweat pretty hard. It's also worth taking into account that they are fairly inexpensive for 7 months of use.

title: Great Customer Service & Great Product
review: The pair fits really well into my ear, great noise cancellation function with good sound quality.  I couldn't reset the Tozo earbuds, then contacted the customer service.  I had a great experience with them - very prompt responses and helpful.  I would buy this again for others.

title: A very nice earbuds as good as apple
review:
It looks nice and is very comfortable, you barely feel it in your ears, looks cool in ear also.

Have been using for 3hr straight and there is still around 40% battery left in the earbuds. The box use type C to charge and its design looks good. There is no lid but only use magnets to secure the ear phones. Maybe a lid option so no dust get into the charging box. One downside is there is so far no "skin" available for the charging box.

The Bluetooth connection is good, real low latency. The touch control on both ear pieces is also pretty cool, there are two modes which u can set in the app. (the app for the earbuds looks ugly but does its job.)

Haven't test its mic yet. But the sound quality is as good as the apple airPods.

Overall, for a Bluetooth Earbuds looks good, feels good, have apple level sound quality (I know how plain it is but its a wireless airbud, 13.1 mm speaker is good enough for these), this thing worth every penny.

But Please update the app so it fit different size of screen.....

title: Meets or exceeds my expectations
review: This is the size and shape that works best for me.  I bought it for music, recording, and radio.  All the other stuff is just a bonus.  I have big hands and the display and controls work almost perfectly for me.  Fits in my shirt pocket and Bluetooth earbuds make it so I can go anywhere and do anything (except swim) with this player.  The touch icon area could be just a little more spread out and sensitive to get five out of five for me.  Been enjoying the use of this player for a month now and look forward to at least 60 more.

title: Bluetooth headphones
review: Came in package good. The product itself was great for about 6mths. The right earbud speaker went out and about a week later the left one went out. Was very disappointed with this part of the purchase. Would have given 5 stars but it lasted under a year.

title: I helped her pair it to her Samsung S6 and it was very easy. I've seen her wear them on her lunch ...
review: This was actually a gift for my co-worker and so far she loves it. I helped her pair it to her Samsung S6 and it was very easy. I've seen her wear them on her lunch break listing to YouTube. Most importantly she loves them when she is at the gym. Her last bluetooth headphones were not sweat proof and they started to 'crackle' after a couple days of extensive workouts. These so far have been excellent for her workouts and the sound she says is great.

title: Pretty good, a little uncomfortable
review: Pretty good bluetooth headphones. The battery life is definitely good, at the very least the headphones will get uncomfortable before they get to low battery, I was able to wear them for about 6 hours straight before they got too uncomfortable. Before that point they are super comfortable though, I found the medium silicone ear pieces fit best for me and while theres no active sound cancelation the fit does block out a decent amount of sound. The sound isnt as great as a lot of people implied in my opinion, but These are also my first pair of bluetooth earbuds and Im not sure what the standard is. these are VERY bulky and as some people mentioned most of the weight is pretty far from the ear, which is part of what makes them uncomfortable over long periods of time but also makes them super awkward to wear due to how far they stick out. I will probably be returning these and looking into a different set that is less bulky and more comfortable.

title: not good for anything but making phone calls or phone music
review:
bit dissapointing considering i was really looking for The One pair of headphones, otherwise i wouldnt have spent so much. Trying to use these headphones is a struggle. on phone, no problem, but as soon as you connect it to a pc the headache starts.

you cant listen to anything else while using these for a call. fine feature on mobile, but totally deafeats the purpose if you are trying to play games while in something like a discord call because you cant hear anything else on your computer and as far as i know no way to change that.

I have a snowball microphone I want to use that has better mic quality, but I cant find a way to make my computer forgot these headphones have mic so it wont use the proper devices half the time.

The sound itself when these work is ok. the bass is ok but for songs that already have a good balance it kind of ruins them and i findyself constantly turning the extra bass on and off. ill likely be returning these, not worth the hassle.

title: Genuine ear-cushions are the solutuion.
review: My MDR-V6 headphones are from the 80's, and so rather than attempt to 'fix' these oldies, I went shopping for new phones. That just turned into one bad experience after another. Seems I was being forced into a world of dark-clouded bass. Why all the push/want for extreme bass, that just covers up the rest of the music spectrum? So, I decided to take the chance and try to fix my old phones. Was most concerned about the drivers themselves, aging to the point of becoming stiff/hardened, irreparably messing up the frequency response. Not!... These new original ear cushions solved everything! I'm happy to report that the low end is completely restored, the dynamic range is there, and the overall frequency response is where it has always been. The drivers never were the issue. A proper 'seal' from using the correct/original cushions is imperative, for these headphones to perform like-new. I'm ordering more cushions right away! Ron Tozier

title: Save Your Money
review: Grossly disappointed with this.  For the money I expected something of much better quality.  Instead this is flimsy plastic, something that would be expected on a much cheaper model.  The ear pieces do not stay in the ears.  The audio quality is abysmal.  I have cheapie $7 earbuds that are superior to this $50+ headset.  My transcription job is demanding in that I am describing audios recorded in difficult environments with difficult and hard to understand interviewees.  Every word, every interjection, every breath sound is important and this headset only picked up the big sounds, and even then that was a strain. I have no alternative but to return these.

title: I find the over the head headset a better feature for me as it seems sturdier
review: I transcribe for a living.  The type of audios I transcribe have to be transcribed verbatim; every uh, um, uh-huh, gasp, sigh, cuss word, slang, malapropism, must be clearly heard and transcribed and this headset goes a long ways towards making that possible.  I've compared and contrasted different headsets and earbuds with the same audio on the same day with all the same equipment, save the headset, and this *clearly* comes in ahead of all others.  I find the over the head headset a better feature for me as it seems sturdier, better environmental noise control.  I have UPDATED this from a five star to a three star rating.  The headset does indeed produce voice clarity that is superior to others that I have paid twice as much for.  HOWEVER, the quality of the this piece of equipment seems to be lacking.  I was purchasing it every six months because the ear cups would break or the wiring would start to fray and on my last purchase add the voice "swished" from one side of the headset to the other, depending on how I held my head, LOL.  I wish the company would take more pride in the manufacture of their product as this truly could be a superior product.

title: Some very good headphones...
review: Bought as a replacement to in the ear buds, my ears had grown tired of them.  These are some high quality headphones for not much money.  Can be run as a cord free Bluetooth or a use a male to male cord and use them as a wired set for even better sound.

title: Better than cheap cables BY FAR...
review:
I had the cheap junky audio links, I didn't really have any idea how much a difference that a decent/good set makes. I made a great snap purchase with these. I actually bought a 3' for the car and the 6' for my headset in the office, my ears were getting sick of plugs in them. I found out that 6' is just a wee bit too short to roll around and look at Elec. DWG's so I also bought the 9'.

Long story short...you really cannot go wrong with these bad boys, gold plated, 2 year warranty, excellent sound. Get them.

title: Review by Allyson Ware
review: These headphones work really well. I love that you can touch them to pause or turn up the volume or even different things while you are on a phone call or picking up a call. The battery is amazing. I also love that you can hook them up to different devices with ease.

title: Review by Allyson Ware
review: These headphones are incredibly nice. Barely noticeable in ear. My husband uses them to watch TikTok’s in bed at night and I cannot hear the videos and he cannot hear me when I speak. Also very nice that you can use the case as a power bank for your phone.

title: Big improvement over the stock pads on my M50x's
review:
While I liked the sound and feel of my Audio Technica ATH-M50x's, the idea of nabbing some velour pads was always something I thought about. There are a number of reviews that suggest these may trash the sound of the headphones. At any rate, I finally pulled the trigger and bought these. They were a snap to install, once they arrived. I couldn't be more pleasantly surprised! The overall comfort level is extremely noticeable. These are cooler and softer than the stock pads. Since they are a little thicker, I found that they did alter the sound. There's a slight drop in bass, and a slight increase in treble. I also noticed that the soundstage seems a bit wider, which makes sense.

I'm glad I made the purchase, and would encourage anyone to give them a shot!

title: These are nice!
review:
I've been looking for some sub-$200 open-back headphones for a while. Reddit seems to be obsessed with the Sennheiser HD560s... but the construction looked cheap to me. These popped up under a pro-audio forum when folks were talking about recording headphones, so I decided to dig further. They looked exactly like what I was looking for, so I pulled the trigger.

Comfort and Construction
These are by far the most comfy headphones I've ever tried on. The clamping pressure is just right. The earpads feel like pillows around my ear, and they don't get nearly as hot as my closed-back headphones. They're also made of a little bit more metal than my Audio Technica headphones.

Sound
I would say these are a bit flatter in the low end and midrange than my Audio Technicas, with a bit more high end to them. They're incredibly clear and the sound is quite spacious. I do find that they benefit from a bit of added bass and a slight cut in the high end, but that's my personal preference.

Overall, I'm quite pleased with my purchase, and I feel that anyone shopping for some open-back headphones should give these a look!

title: So far, so good!
review: Bought this for my ATH M50x headphones.  It's a little longer than the shortest cable that comes with the headphones, which is nice.  I haven't had any complaints when using the mic.  The cable is a bit thinner, however.  For the price, I say go for it!

title: Great sounding, though possibly fragile
review: I needed a replacement from my old Sony headphones.  I prefer the over-ear design as to buds.  Just like my old Sony's, these sound great.  The retractable cord is a nice feature, though I don't know how long to expect it to last.  The wires are quite thin, so I would recommend that those who abuse their equipment to look for something a bit more durable.

title: They do not block out sounds as good as other headphone I have used in the past
review: These are working out very well.  They do not block out sounds as good as other headphone I have used in the past.  And in total silence there is a 'rush' sound at low volume which the directions say is "Normal".  And for my ears they are just a little bit of a tight fit.  For these reasons I am only giving four stars.  But otherwise they are working just fine and battery life seems to be nearly forever.

title: Plenty of volume
review: My ears ring and I have partial hearing loss but not enough for a hearing aid.  This headset has enough volume that I can use it without straining to hear even while driving my soft-top Jeep at highway speeds!

title: Nearly as good as a much more expensive name brand
review: I have owned a few noise cancellation headphones over the years.  In my experience you usually get what you pay for.  But that is not true with these Panasonic headphones.  The quality of these is equal or better than models costing three times as much.  These are a very good value.  I give four stars because they are not totally silent like a $200 - $300 product is - in other words these are not 'perfect'.  If I could give a half-star I'd give 4.5.

title: Best Earbuds I've ever owned
review:
I had some Beats bluetooth headphones that were good, but on calls you couldn't hear yourself talk. These earbuds are awesome. Not only do they sound better than the Beats, they have an "ambient noise" setting so you can hear yourself talk as well as your surroundings.
Very happy with the purchase.

title: Amazing Wireless Earbuds!
review:
The noise cancellation on these earbuds are awesome. Will buy again if needed in the future.

They also have a great range so leaving your phone/pad on your desk and heading to the kitchen or even outside is pretty much possible.

title: Muffles your microphone
review: My husband’s beats headphones came with an audio cable. Mine did not. We do a lot of Webex meetings for work and I didn’t care for the headset they provided me with. I wanted to use my beats, but it won’t connect to my work computer via Bluetooth. So I bought this cord. Every time I use this cord I am told that I sound muffled. I use my husband’s beats cord and I sound fine. I bought this because the title said it was a replacement cord for beats dr Dre headphones. This is not the case. The sound quality is okay…but I can definitely hear a difference between the two cords. If you were only using it occasionally you could probably get by, but I would not get these if you want to look good in front of a client.

title: Not for bigger headphones
review: It's a good stand, really attractive and quite sturdy, but my MTH50x headphones are a little too big for the stand without folding them or hanging from a slight angle. Definitely useable but if you have larger headphones you'll want to consider a bigger stand.

title: Works Well Enough, but Hurts my Ears (Pressure)
review: Headphones work OK but are uncomfortable for me - too tight for my ears. But sound is good and mic works well for phone calls. I'm moving on.

title: Greatl Little Mp3 Player
review:
I just purchased the Sony E-340 Series 8GB video mp3 player. Two actually one in black as a gift and one in red for my self. This is one of the best purchases I have made in awhile. This little unit is easy to download, works very, very well with my exsisting music stored on my computer. Easy to understand. The sound quality from the little earbuds that come with the player really could use some improvement..but they are just stock headphones, and for the very affordablity of this little player they are adequate. I happened to have an extra set of a little better grade of headphones and once I got the equalizer set up to my liking the sound is beyond belief.

I have the Beatles boxed set of the Stereo remixes on my player and WOW!! What an experience it is to hear them in stereo and through headphones...and in my car oh, my!!

The FM radio is a nice touch...easy to program. I cannot say enough about how nice it is to be able to have my photos with me on the player, the video quality is super.

So, if you are in the market for a nice little mp3 player that is reasonably priced, chocked full of nice little features and easy to use. I cannot recommend this unit enough. Can't wait for walking weather!!

title: A little Overrated
review:
I bought this product based on many positive reviews and was a little disappointed in it. It definitely delivered on style and small size, but there are two things that make me frustrated with my purchase.
First, the cover is very flimsy and just waiting to be snapped off. I am sure this is what people come to expect with electronics that have a functional life of 2 years, but I am afraid to do much anything active with this guy for fear of breakage. Changing CD's is a continual process of fear that I might put a few too many grams per square inch pressure on the lid and watch it snap off. Pretty frustrating, but I can manage, I just keep it in my bag when I am listening and use caution when changing discs. A forgivable problem.
This next one is not so forgivable - You cannot fast-forward through MP3 files. What gives? Did Panasonic just decide that consumers only need to FF through CD audio, and because you can fit vast quantities of audio on one MP3 CD you have no possible reason to FF through the multitude of songs? Very frustrating. Much less forgivable.
So to sum up:
The plusses - small size, sleek design, great battery life, nice corded LCD remote
The minuses - flimsy design, terrible headphones, cannot FF through MP3.
If I knew what I know now about this one I probably wouldn't buy it unless it were $20 cheaper.

title: budget iems but i got a defective pair?
review: I’m not much of an audiofile, bought these to replace my earbuds that had died and to use as my commuter earbuds.  They wear nicely and dont slip as much as apple earbuds or similar. However, I’m giving it 3 stars because the volume is too loud. Im have to toggle the lowest settings on my devices. I wish i had more room to change the volume level, especially because id like to hear some bass without making my ears bleed. Another reason is because my pair is defective; one iem tends to pop off the cable connector. And i just missed the return cut off by a day. I bought these to take to the gym and I’ve had to crawl on my hands and knees to look for the missing iem that popped off and rolled under a treadmill or into some nook. It’s become looser and i don’t remove the iems from the cable to put away either. I wanted to really like my first pair of iems but i had bad luck with these.

title: Works Well With Mac
review:
This device can be used through USB if you set to "USB AUDIO" for output in Settings.

The sound is pretty good...I think it's comparable to the Fiio E10 I was using before but this has a little more control and better midrange. Because the power comes through a second USB connection I think the sound is much cleaner than the Fiio. It drives my Sony MDR-1A headphones quite well and, even on the lowest volume, still maintains a balanced sound.

This was a pretty good deal and I would recommend it to people who want decent sound and don't want to pay too much for it.

As a bonus, you can plug a Galaxy phone into it with USB-C and use it as an amp for that. I haven't tried the optical or coax output from it but I expect it to sound just as good.

title: Good Sound for the Money
review:
Not a bad value for the money. Be careful to plug in headphones AFTER powering up, as pushing POWER with headphones in sends a THUMP down the headphones that is very unpleasant. Jiggling the headphone cable causes a shinning noise, so keep this stationary.

Sound quality is great and this works well when driving higher impedance headphones. Also an excellent amplifier for smartphones. I plug my LG G4 into this, cue up some FLAC tracks and put in my 64 ohm headphones and adjust the volume until it's perfect.

I don't know how long the tubes will last but this is a pretty fun unit even if it's disposable.

title: A Hidden Gem
review:
I own the HARX900 (2 pairs) and got these as laptop headphones. I connect these to a USB DAC and can really get good sound with the laptop's EQ and the DAC pushing the voltage. These aren't too heavy for my head, have a comfy band and, most important of all, they don't mess with my glasses or press my ears into the glasses. Fully closed headphones tend to be too tight around the ears for glasses and open types have too much sound bleed and environmental intrusion so this semi-closed design is wonderful for me. The 50mm drivers pump tons of good sound and, if you have the right hardware, these sound excellent even at lower volumes. The sound is very balanced and isn't super bass heavy. These are good for jazz, rock, spoken word, and just about anything else. I enjoy the longer cord because I can run this into a mic jack behind a desktop PC and still have plenty of slack. At 48ohms, these take a little more to push than the regular 32ohm cans, but most cell phones will still sound great with these.

The only bad thing is that the pleather ear pads WILL degrade after a couple of years of constant usage and there aren't really any easy ways to replace them. You buy at your own risk in the aftermarket world, but if you can locate a good source of earpads, these are worth keeping for the long haul once you've burned them in. They sound just as good for most applications as the HARX900 and you will want to get a pair for home and for the office.

title: A Good Set of Phones
review:
I got these at the discontinued price and I am glad I did before they were all sold out! They have cushioned vinyl pads that rest against the ears and so there is some passive noise reduction and the headband part has a cushion underneath that keeps the plastic off of your head.

The sound is excellent, with plenty of bass, midrange and good highs. There is SOME sound bleed because of the design, though, so watch out for that. For people with big heads, the adjustable headband is good, but had to be stretched to max to feel comfy on my head. The mic is high quality and the button is solid.

Gripes:
1. The vinyl can make your ears feel sweaty after a couple of hours
2. The cord doesn't detach and is a little short

But, overall, this is an excellent set of headphones that doubles as a great mic/headset combo. Works VERY well with Android smartphones, but I never tested the app.

title: Only the Best!
review: I am not sure how these sound, but when I am strangling a farm-raised ostrich for a gourmet meal, only the FINEST tools will suffice.  Needless to say, the headphone wire on these is great for ostriches and it probably works on cassowarys, too.

title: Good buy and great sound!
review: Read plenty of reviews for these headphones and was excited to receive them. I am happy that while I'm at the gym they stay in my ears despite sweating and working out. Sound is terrific and love that orange was an available color. Great product and extremely happy with the quality.

title: A Superb Option for Moderate Hearing Loss
review:
~Comfortable for hours. These are light years ahead of earbuds, on ear, or over ear phones. No part of my ear was pinched or scrunched, even though I wear glasses. I have an over-sized melon and large, flat ears. I can't tolerate buds for more than about 30 minutes, and most headphones in this range are pinchy somewhere.
~I normally watch movies/videos at full sound with Closed Caption on iPad or laptops. I'm at half volume -- no CC -- wearing these phones. I was able to easily pick up male and female voices, including foreign accents.
~NOT noise cancelling. I could still hear the whir of a fan, my kids talking, etc., but they couldn't hear any noise coming from my headphones. For me, this was ideal. I don't have the luxury of tuning out the world most of the time.
~Requires several hours of break-in. I usually listen to Winterspell from Two Steps to test buds and phones. It sounded tinny on first listen, and amazing about 10 hours in.
I highly recommend these if you have moderate hearing loss. I can't differentiate consonant sounds, and certain voices and accents are nearly impossible for me to follow on screen. These didn't feel loud, just incredibly clear -- it was like hearing like a kid again.

title: Only so so, it doesn’t stay secure in usage
review: I usually give Belkin products five star reviews, but not this one. In use I find it doesn’t stay secure in my iPad Pro. The pull of the lightweight cable on my headphones is more than enough to consistently pull the USB C connector out of the slot. Also, my iPad doesn’t seem to like the hardware as I frequently have to plug it in a few times before the circuitry will handshake and transfer the audio to the headphones from the internal speaker. Bottom line, if you’re using some legacy hardware like my old (but very high end) headphones, look for a different product. On this one, Belkin is just a name… without the quality usually associated with that name.

title: Buy this product, yes, it’s that good!
review: I’m usually pretty skeptical about a lot of add-on products. But this one gets a five star review and strong recommendation to buy. Why? Because it really does protect your very expensive battery case extremely well. I carry my Bose earbuds case in my iPad bag. The case rubs against everything and is going to turn into a crazy quilt of scratches in no time. So, I go on Amazon and look for a protective case. This product from Spigen attaches via adhesive to the Bose case without adding a lot of weight or thickness and it certainly scores for durability as well. My only caution is to be very careful when peeling off the film to expose the adhesive, the adhesive will tear if you tug too hard. The case comes with an extra set of adhesive strips, but you won’t need them if you’re careful the first time. I’ve had this for over a month now and my bag lives in my flaming hot car here in South Florida when I’m out and about. If the adhesive was going to fail, it would have by now. If you’ve got the Bose case, buy this Spigen product, you’ll be very happy with the combo.

title: Not bad at all
review:
Nice little pair of blue tooth earbuds. The volume control is nice since they are actually amplified. The pic on the page is a bit different than the actual product. There are times that it sounds like the buffer can't hold the input and then the song will have about 1/4 second dead air. Works great for phone use since the mic is also noise canceling I suppose.
overall is good stuff

title: Surprising sound out of such light weight head phones.
review: Nice set of wired over the ear headphones.  Was actually really surprised at the tonal response from such a light weight set.  I will date myself here and say that the last pair of headphones I liked as much as these was back when all audio connections were 1/4 inch... and the cord was coiled. I'm not saying that these will match Bose, or HK's etc.  But for the price point? You could do far worse.  I also like how the ear muff area turns so they can store in a much smaller area.  Over all pretty good stuff.  In the spirit of transparency, got this item for free to beta test them.

title: My Break-in of the HD 598 SE: Ick!
review:
Recording my listening experience with the Sennheiser HD 598 which I bought after breaking my pair of HE-400 headphones. I own Grado Labs SR80, BModed Fostex T50, Sennheiser HD-600, Hifiman HE-500.

Hour 1:
Pro: Looks good for plastic and reasonably comfortable.
Con: heavy handed, muddy, base reminds me of a one-note subwoofer, and the signature reminds me of a cheap pair of Skullcandy headphones. You could get better sound from a pair of Beat headphones. I am feeling ripped off and don't recall the last time listening to music made me MAD!
One word: Garbage!

Hour 10:
The headphones have opened up some. Vocals feel recessed. Bass still feels one dimensional. Upgraded rating from one to two stars.

Hour 15:
I am baffled by the positive reviews of this product. Yes, headphones and their sound signatures are very much a personal preference, but these are so grossly bad that I can only assume my ears are damaged or the headphones are defective. Returning them to Amazon.

title: My kid now has an excuse to ignore me
review:
I bought these for my son because I really don't want to listen to his YouTube or video game music. They work so well he no longer listens to me because he says, "the headphones, Mom. They don't let me hear what you say, only MY stuff."

Having a son who ignores me is a very small price to pay for an hour of coffee-drinking peace.

These do go pretty loud, so I've set noise-safety rules--I check to see that they are low enough from time to time so they won't damage his ears.

These fold up nicely, are durable, and the cord is wrapped with a woven material so it stays secure in the headphone, doesn't break, and survived one dog attack. They make my son think he's got a popular teen-brand approved headphone, but I didn't pay nearly that much in the end. These are nice.

title: These have held up pretty well for the price
review: These have held up pretty well for the price, I'm surprised! They aren't great sound quality but if that's what you're looking for you should really invest! I'm a musician and these are just back up headphones. I hate earbuds and these serve my purposes of walking to work and listening to podcasts and then shoving them in a bag. They've held up well, as long as you're expectations for sound quality aren't too high, I'd recommend them.

title: Forget the expensive ones
review: Excellent value. Works just as good as the expensive ones. The battery life is good. I have a pair of Samsung earbuds and these work better and last longer.

title: Just Okay
review: I normally don't write reviews but thought I would on this one. When I received these they worked great. After about a month of using them, people I was talking to would tell me that when I wear the right ear bud that it would sound crackly and would break up. The sound quality on my end was fine. Now, 2 months after purchasing them, the base doesn't stay charged and the left earbud doesn't stay charged. I am glad I purchased these on sale because the quality has gone done significantly since I bought them. They are fine to listen to music or podcasts but not great for phone calls. I am thinking about returning them since they started going down hill after one month of having them.

title: Will be buying again, 'cause they've lasted
review: Great. I'll be getting more. They've lasted a few months, which is more than most earbuds do with me. Sound is good, too, but I'm no audiophile, so take that with a grain of salt.

title: Won't stay on my head unless I stay completely still
review: If these are actually Skullcandy headphones, I'm disappointed, because I can't tell if they sound okay or not, since the d@&m things won't stay on my head unless I sit absolutely still. But since the picture doesn't match the product I got, I'm inclined to think that these are knock offs like some of the other reviews said. If they are the real deal then Skullcandy, which I've always had good luck with, just have a badly designed product.

title: Fine with Moto G, L Shaped plug, sound not great but okay *and* they keep working
review: I'm no audiophile, but even I can tell that these don't sound as good out of the box as my Skullcandys. Or JLabs. The reason I keep using them is that the L shaped plug means they keep working, which the others don't always do. They are also really comfortable, and the control button works on my Moto G, so I hope that like most earbuds, they will sound better with time.

title: Stopped working and were uncomfortable for my son
review: Should have known that $15 headphones would be uncomfortable for my kid and wouldn't last more than a month. Waste of money.

title: Love these!
review: Love, love, love these headphones. The charge lasts a long time, people can hear me well when on the phone, they drown out outside sound, and fit perfectly and comfortably over my ears. I have in-ear bose headphones too, but had gotten a daith piercing for migraine relief so needed something to go over my ear and these have been perfect!

title: Crisp and Clear!
review: My husband has an older model of Bose headphones that I kept borrowing for calls. I finally got a pair of my own and first went with a higher line of Skullcandy headphones which turned out to be horrendous. So, I returned those and ordered these. I've only had to use them a couple times but both times they were fantastic!!! The carry case that comes with them is very handy.

title: Great Headset
review: Dont fall out of ear, great sound,well worth it. Best bluetooth headset I have owned.

title: Bad phone call quality
review:
Tried making test calls with Pixel 3aXL + TOZO T10, the voice fades in and out so bad it's totally inaudible. Then I switched to Pixel 3aXL + Bose Quiet Comfort, I was able to hear every word. Finally I call tested using the speaker on Pixel3aXL, the speaker quality is much better than TOZO T10.

If you are buying this headset to listen to podcase or audio books, it's light weight and comfortable. For music, the bigger ear tip you use the better bass you get, small ear tips = no bass. If you are planning on using these earbuds for phone calls, you'd be very disappointed.

title: Hurt my ears after a while
review: This is the first BT headset that I am able to use for business calls and no one complaint about call quality.  The battery lasts forever and I feel great not having something in or over ear(s) to muffle the external sound. I do back to back conference calls for hours each day and these are the BEST headsets ever.  The only downfall is the loops over my ears do hurt after a few hours.

title: So cute and really good sound
review: My daughter never could keep any headset on for more than 10 minutes, but because this is so cute, she wears it all day and I can work without interruption.  I tried this headset and the sound is better than the set I got for myself.

title: Great battery life but noise reduction does not work
review:
Great battery life but the noise filter function does not work right. If I am in a noisy environment (driving, cooking, doing dishes or bathrom), either people can tell right away where I am or the noise filter cancels my voice out and the other end can only hear every other word I say. I think the BEST noise assassin BT headset is Jawbone, too bad they are no longer making BT headsets. Plantronics (or any other manufacturer) should get the technology behind Jawbone's noise assassin. I don't mind paying a few $ more if the headset has great battery life and great noise cancellation.

I tested this headset (and Plantronis Voyager Legend) by calling and mute call on home phone. The microphone is very sensitive and I can hear myself clearly even if I whisper. However, if I speak loudly my voice became distorted, the louder I speak the worse sound. Just a reference for people who has problem with sound quality, maybe try to speak softer will help.

title: Does not work with Wireless LAN IEEE802.11b/g
review:
Great sound quality, BUT...

Tried to use SRS-BTM30 with my Toshiba Portege G810 (which does not have a standard 3.5mm output jack for speakers/headset) for video streaming via home WIFI, the video/sound cuts out frequently. Then I found on page 16 of the manual: this speaker uses the same frequency as Wireless LAN IEEE802.11b/g. So if you are trying to stream media from internet with wireless LAN, SRS-BTM30 does not work well. If you are looking for Bluetooth speaker that does not conflict with WIFI I recommend Jabra BT3030, you just need to buy a pair of regular speaker with it.

title: So far so good
review: Using mainly to make my awesome older Bose headset wireless. Easy to pair, sounds fine, inexpensive. Battery life not so long but hey, $7. Will update if this changes.

title: So far, so good
review: Using to connect my Bose qc15 headphones, which have no volume control and are wired, to a Bluetooth receiver that also has no volume control. Worked immediately right out of the mailer, and the low end of volume is even low enough for watching tv in bed while partner is sleeping , with other headphones (original Beats).

title: It works!
review: Adult(ish) child reports success on Bose QC 25 headphones- quite difficult to find for us!  Bought 2 sets so when these get twisted & break or a kitten chews them (it happens), we'll have backup.

title: Easy on, so far so good (at one week)
review: Bought for my kid's Bose qc25 headset. She was able to install without incident and says they're pretty comfortable. Bought 2 sets just in case- no telli g about durability after a week, but the originals lasted 3 1/2 years.

title: Great way to refresh your headphones
review:
I LOVE my Bose QC45 headphones and have used them extensively over the past several years. They need refreshed. This set was an easy way to quickly make your headphones more like new. Simply pull off the ear cups, and assorted pieces and reinstall. Takes about 5 minutes.

Putting them on takes a bit of practice as you have to make them snap into place, but once you get the hang of it, it's quite easy.

title: Not as good as I would have liked
review: Decent headphones, but not as good as I personally would have liked. I had trouble keeping them sufficiently in my ear to make use of the noise canceling.  Easy to pair, decent battery life.

title: Great way to still use old components
review: Good way to use old componenets.  Connect old wired earphones or wired devices such as speakers to a Bluetooth only phone.  High quality. Fits snugly. Feels well made, and with good sound quality.

title: i wanted to like these
review: I really wanted to like these earbuds.  The sound wasn't bad.  The noise canceling was very good.  They were pretty comfortable but when I took them out the squishy part that molds to your ear kept popping off and would get stuck in my ear.  Several times I have to ask a coworker to fish it out of my ear.

title: so far so good
review: These headphones are comfortable.  Have great sound and the noise cancellation is spot on!  Setup is easy and there is very good base response and the headphones seem to shake your whole head! Lots of fun!

title: Good phones. Good bass
review: Good comfortable headphones with loud volume no noise cancelling as far as I can tell the over-the-ear design allows you to muffle out most annoying noises for the best sound. These are extra bass headphones and the bass definitely comes through though at the expense of the mid and high range and a lot of sounds sound a little bit muffled in my opinion but overall a pretty good set of headphones

title: Good entry phones for kids
review: These are good entry level earphones for kids. They are smaller, so they fit smaller heads, and the volume limiting feature is good so kids don't hurt their ears.  Seems pretty sturdyily made, and should hold up fairly well.

title: Works, plain and simple Fix your expensive headphones.
review: I love my Bose headphones, and was so sad when I was having trouble with the cable. I lost all sound in the left ear.  This cord replaces the breakaway cord that comes with your Bose headphones and bring it back to life.  Just a simple cable can make me so happy. Installs in seconds, works like a new one.  What not to like?

title: Great good sounding headset.
review:
These are a great set of comfortable on the ear headphones. Note, they fit on top of the ear, not totally over the ear as some do. But they are lightweight and comfortable. They offer great bass response with clear mid and high range. The input cord also can come off, protecting your phones, plus they can be used as cell phone headset as the included cord has a built-in microphone.

Great sound for the money. Great as a primary headset, or as a backup. Either way you'll be happy

title: Great sound and comfort. Sounds great, and inline remote and microphone is a welcome touch.
review:
These ultra comfortable headphones offer clear and loud reproduction of most any sound and music you can imagine. With impressive bass response, and clear mid and high ranges, these pair of headphones will make most any music sound great, from classical, to rock, to punk, and jazz.

They are rather large, but comfortable. The muffs totally cover the year, and though they are not noise cancelling, they may as well be because once you put them on almost all outside noises disappear.

The inline remote and microphone is a great touch allowing you to control volume from the line in while also being able to take phone calls without removing the headphones.

They also fold down for easy storage.

The only drawback is I wish the line was a bit longer. I had this connected to my component system to listen to Vinyl, and a longer cord would have been a bit better, but it is manageable.

Though they may not technically sound as good as the more expensive Bose headphones, these sound good enough that cost to benefit of buying these outweigh the more expensive Bose.

title: Great sound and comfortable. Worth the money!
review: These really are fantastic. I never owned a pair of Bose earphones, and usually only purchased $25 headphones, thinking they would be sufficient. I was wrong. These sound so good, music is rich and full. Bass is deep without sounding overdone, mid and high ranges are great. Full sound, it feels like I'm right there in the room. They are very comfortable too, I wore them for 3 hours straight and didn't mind at all. They are NOT noise cancelling but because of their good sound and superb fit they do filter out a bit of outside noise. So unless you travel on planes a lot, I don't think you'd mind the noise cancelling not being here.

title: Avoid these. Non existent noise cancelling, uncomfortable. Can find better for the money.
review:
Got these at a kiosk before a 5 hour flight. I'm really not a big fan of ear bud earphones, especially for a long flight. Previously had a pair of earphones in the same pricepoint that had decent noise cancelling abilities, and thought these would be ok.

First off, the sound is pretty decent, good bass, and overall good sound. The nice cancelling function is non existent. You may as well not even turn the feature on, it does nothing.

Second, they are not that comfortable. AS they are a bit too small after an hour or so they begin pressing on your ears and it gets uncomfortable. I wish I never bought them

title: Adequate sound/comfort-have to download app
review:
This headset gives adequate sound and comfort. The buds fit comfortably into your ears and they wrap comfortably behind your ears. They stay in, have good bass, midrange. They have a bit too much tinny high range, but still sound very good for their size.

The button allows you to control sound controls, forward, reverse, etc, from the button on the handset. The trouble is you have to go to the Play Market (android market store) or App store to download the app. This allows the controls to work, but it also causes the app to open many times when you have a plug into the port. In my example it opened up when I put my SquareUP reader into the phone, and caused a bit of confusion.

Otherwise it's a nice headphone, great sound, and comfort, the only drawback being you have to install an app for it to work to 100%.

title: Great sound and exceptional comfort
review:
These are perhaps the best in ear earphones I've ever used. They are lightweight, comfortable, stay in your ear, and offer great sound.

I've long ago ditched most earbud style earphones. They offer horrible sound, are uncomfortable, and never stay in your ear. These earphones address those issues with style, comfort, and great sound reproduction.

The mid and high range reproduction is crisp and clean without any noticeable distortion. Low range is somewhat lacking but is proberly above what most small earbud style headphones are.

They feature many great design features such as replaceable buds for the earpiece. There is small, medium, and large. There is also a set of memory foam that you can choose. This is good because as everyone's ears are different, most earpieces are not. This allows you to choose the fit of the earbuds to suit your own needs.

The part of the cable that plugs into your walkman, diskman, iPod or whatever is steel reinforced, which is nice as that is what usually breaks first on headphones. They also come with a steel carrying case to protect your headphones when not in use. They also have a cleaning tool to clean any nasty bits that may get into the canal of the phones.

All-in-all a great set of phones for the audiophile. They are lightweight, sound great, and most importantly, stay in your ear and are comfortable.

title: Great for your 2nd Gen iPod Nano
review:
This is a pretty good item to have for your iPod Nano, 2nd generation. If you walk, do chores, or any other physical activity while you listen to your iPod this is for you.

Lanyard snaps securely into the iPod's dock and earphone connector and the adjustable strap goes around your neck. The all-in-one design includes the apple ear buds. I use it frequently when I do light chores around my Christmas tree farm.

My only complaint is really against the Apple earbuds themselves. They really have only adequate sound and they don't fit into your ears well. I would have given it 5 stars if you could use your own earphones with the lanyard or if Apple improved their earbud design and sound quality.

title: Longevity
review: I bought a pair in 2019 when I needed to replace one of my Beats Solo ear cushions. I just used the second one on the same set of headphones. You can not tell the difference between the one that has been in the pack for 2 years or the one in daily and overnight use.

title: Finally found a case where my large headphones (Senn HD ...
review: Finally found a case where my large headphones (Senn HD 600, HiFiMan HE 400i) would fit without me having to worry about them being compressed.  Plus, I can include my mp3 player, amp, and cables inside with no problem. Plus, I can store the Senn HD 600 in it without having the unplug its cable.

title: Great price for an equally great pair of cans
review: Love my ATH-M50.  Excellent sonics for such a good price.  I'm glad I bought this instead of the far more expensive headphones available.  I don't regret the purchase at all.

title: You do get what you pay for
review: Funny that this headset can be bought in many brands.  Must be the result of mass production from which electronic companies buy by the bulk and stamp their own brand names and logos on them.  I bought the Britelink in particular because of the relatively cheaper price, considering that they all looked the same across the board.  It does get the audio across, but does not deliver a superlative performance sonics-wise.  Don't expect to listen to Bach or Brahms on these creatures.  But they may be worth it for watching a late night video when you don't want to bother anybody else in the house with the noise/sound.  Construction is quite flimsy.  How long will they last?  Anybody's guess.

title: Tough and well-made
review: Offers great protection for your cans.  I bought the extra-large size because, as per my research on the Net, this was what was recommended for the Audio Technica ATH-M50.  Found it to be a little large for the phones, but nevertheless still provided ample protection.  Makes me wonder if the large size CASEBUDi was more suitable rather than this extra-large.  But don't get me wrong, it still does what it's supposed to do for my beloved headphones.

title: Don’t buy or buy with great caution ⚠️
review: Ad/write up/description “implies” purchase of the piece is what you need to connect something via Bluetooth for a TV, headphones, earbuds. It contains only PART of what is needed for set-up. THEN when I returned the item almost immediately, I was only given a partial refund. I wouldn’t buy anything from this seller if I needed it for a junk-pile! I tried to contact and didn’t receive a response. Hold onto your cash my friend and read the ads carefully!

title: A lesson in customer service above and beyond
review:
Love the sound. Love the concept but after 2 days of use the earpiece on the left would not release, kept retracting. However, the company was super responsive and is sending me a replacement. I look forward to the new one. If the new one behaves as it should and I expect no less I will add a star.
UPDATE:
New product arrived as promised. No problems. Love the long battery life too. It tells you how much is left in the battery which is a nice feature. No more fumbling around in backpacks to find headphones. The ridged design makes it easy to find. Highly recommend.

title: Love these earbuds!
review: These are the best earbuds I've purchased. The volume is a bit low, but I think that its a good thing to protect my hearing. The sounds is still really good, they are comfortable and the battery life is excellent. I think the longest I've used them is about 3 hours, so I'm not sure what the maximum battery life is. Calls are easy to answer and very clear.

title: Still a great pair of
review: 6 month update Im not sure what went wrong but the side with the remote suddenly reduced its volume so the the left side is mich lower than the right. Still a great pair of headphones

title: Pretty good
review: I don’t have much to complain about this headphone except that it wouldn't connect to the usb receiver for a day which was very frustrating as I use it for work to all my conference calls. However, it has great signal (when it connects) and is comfortable.

title: Great battery life
review:
I find that the best price to performance is in the $30 range for Bluetooth headphones, and they keep getting better and better. I have several pairs that I use for the gym, general listening to music, watching movies, and playing poker. I like to have other charged ones ready to go if a pair gets low.

These were rated very well, so I decided to give them a shot. They are super comfortable and they stay in place at the gym. I am not an audiophile, but these are well balanced and have better sound quality than my other pairs.

The greatest thing about these is the battery life- I used them for about 11 hours, and there was still 50% battery life left. With all my other pairs the battery life is a real problem, and it does not improve as they age. The charging case is also nice and there is a display for remaining battery life of the case. Remaining battery life of the headphones is displayed on the mobile device.

The BT connection is also super reliable. I have not experienced any disconnects or interference.

In summary, I highly recommend these. They are comfortable, they stay in place, they stay connected to my device, and they sound great. Probably the biggest Pro is the battery life. I purchased these to use as a backup for my other pairs, but it turns out that these will be my main headphones.

title: Better than the original
review: The cord that came with the original headset had a slightly too large micro USB head needing it to be forced into the charge slot. This one worked correctly. I was sent one as a replacement. I would not buy one otherwise, since the original should have fit correctly.

title: A worthwhile replacement for my previous one.
review:
I bought this to replace the non-thin version I originally bought because this one was supposed to be thin enough to work with a qi wireless charger. Thankfully it does that just fine. I miss the texture of the original one but have gotten used to this, which is smoother and harder. My other one also started to not hold the folds very well and would often fall over when I would touch the screen. It was only a year and a half old when it started behaving that way, but it was annoying. So, now I'm back to a stable fold and not worrying so much about it falling over.
My biggest complaint is that the opening for the headphones is snug enough that my shure 215 ear buds do not fit. I have to lift the corner off to be able to have them reliably stay put. I haven't tried to cut the opening bigger, but I imagine I'll eventually be bothered enough to have to do it.
I got the purple one, as before, and this purple as nice as the other one. This is minor, but it's still a thing.

Bottom line, it does the job well, looks and feel good enough and I'd likely replace it with the same (or newer) if this one somehow got lost - which is unlikely because the fit is snug/great.

title: which is fantastic as far as I'm concerned
review: Ordered for girlfriend; they lasted a few months for her, which is fantastic as far as I'm concerned. I normally don't buy skull candies since they tend to be fragile, and my girlfriend and I go through headphones very quickly. These lasted a while though.

title: Nice for the price and good sound quality.
review: I have a big head and these fit me well. They are large (I don't like earbuds) and the sound quality is good - however you'll get some sound bleed so I wouldn't recommend them in cubicles or public spaces

title: Good utilitarian headphones.
review:
This is my second pair and they're simple, efficient and easy to wear. These are my workplace headphones. They're not sound isolating (I can hear people when they knock on my door, etc.)

I can't wear in-ear headphones (they bug me and fall out of my ears) so this was my other option.

Overall if you need a pair of simple, decent quality, sturdy headphones and aren't a hardcore audiophile, these fit the bill.

title: ... - they are no frills but they are really nice - I like that they swivel flat
review: A basic pair of decent headphones is what I needed for my workplace - they are no frills but they are really nice - I like that they swivel flat.

title: Mic stops working
review:
The sound quality is great, and function keys are simple to use. I can hear easily with the headphones. Noise cancelation is not something I can comment on because I do not secure them in my ears, only rest them in place. I like to hear what us going on around me.
I have been using headsets similar to this model for at least a decade. This particular model made a very unfortunate event for me when the mic stopped working. It is sudden, with no indition it will happen. The battery charge was at 80%. I was speaking with my Octogenarian parents when it happened. At first, they and I thought something had happened to their land line. I could hear them, but they could not hear me on their wireless. When they also could not hear me on a wired landline, I tapped the speaker on my phone, cutting off the headset, and they could hear me. They were very upset. I was furious that a headset that is only 35 days old is having microphone failure.
Returning products that should be thrown in the trash is something I detest because of the waste of the trip to my rural home, or me being forced to make an unnecessary trip to a drop off center.
Conclusion: do not buy if you need the microphone feature. It is not reliable.

I will use these to listen to books. I would love a refund, but that is not the way with Amazon.

title: No labeling for soldering points
review: These jacks are sturdy, and made to last. What makes want to give them such a low mark is that they were shipped with no labeling as to where the L, R, Mic, and ground should be soldered. You will have to test them. No tip is standard...you think they would be, and that the headphones you are replacing would have universal color coded wiring. Not true. Be sure to have a way to test where the power will go. I would have given these a one star for lack of labeling,  but they are of solid materials.

title: Bought for wife
review: Wife has small ears and hasn't found earbuds that will stay in place. Got these and she loves them. So win win for hubby.

title: Durable
review: After my first two pair lasted me 7 years, my grandson usurped them and have lasted him another 2. Some earbuds fail to endure a week of his Autism enhanced usage.

title: Five Stars
review: BEST earbuds ever..they stay in, are comfortable, and help me concentrate when there's chaos around me.

title: Amazon basics are better.
review: The right side earbud stopped working on both pairs after a few months. Amazon basics are better.

title: Nice, simple headphones
