title: Nice budget headset
review:
Great value for the price. Lightweight with a flip up to mute mic. I recommend these for kiddos as they aren't the end of the world if they break, plus they adjust down far enough to fit a smaller head. While not technically an open back they aren't super sealed either so they can still hear you if you need their attention. Plus, they do not do that annoying negative pressure thing that noise-cancelling headphones create. Many kids and some adults (me) can't stand that pressure feeling on the ear drum.

Are these super steller sounding and amazing, no. But they aren't bad for entry level. Great for $40.

title: Not bad a bit pricey for the durability though
review: Not bad for a beginning gamer headset. Love the flip up mic to mute, this should just be how all mics work if you ask me. I did ding a star for the price. These do not have a $60 build quality. They are plastic and cheap feeling, they sound fine but we are on our third pair as they just don't have the durability. The cord isn't even braided. If you can find them for under $40 it would be a better price point.

title: Worked with PC, but not Yamaha receiver
review:
I could not get this to work with our Yamaha receiver. I googled till I could google no more (there are no included instructions with the transmitter). I found a couple of helpful sites, but none of it helped. The device just wouldn't work. It did pair with my skullcandy headphones but only with my computer not the receiver, and my headphones sounded better paired with my phone and not using the transmitter than they did paired with the PC via the transmitter.

Not what I needed, I wanted these for the living room, not sure how to rate it other than maybe it will work for you maybe it will not.

title: Great if you can get a solid fit
review:
Hubby had better luck with these than I did. He said they were super comfortable and stayed in place at the gym just fine even on the tread mill. I for the life of me couldn't get a comfortable position but I'm also a bit smaller than him. He liked the noise cancelling and I found it annoying especially since there is no passthrough/talk through feature on these. I ended up yelling at everyone not realizing how loud I was being lol.

Just sitting still and listening to music these have impressive sound quality. They can't match my true over the ear Sennheisers but as far as earbuds go these are some of the best I've heard.

For me they were 3 stars because I didn't like the fit and didn't function well with them, hubby said a solid 5 stars he loves them and has claimed them as his own for the gym. So averaged out to 4 stars between us.

title: Pretty good with a couple issues
review: I loved the idea of sleep headphones because I kept losing my AirPods in my sheets at night. This one by MMUSS paired easily with my iPhone and the battery time is really good. I like how you can maneuver the headphones inside the cloth to fit your head shape. What I didn’t like is that the band itself was uncomfortably tight. I don’t have a large head either. I think I might be able to stretch it out a bit hopefully as I wear it. Also these didn’t get incredibly loud, which was fine for nighttime music, but listening to ASMR wasn’t quite loud enough. They’re a 3.5 for me.

title: Great Sound
review: I needed a quick and inexpensive replacement for my headphones after dropping my old AirPods in a sink full of water. After that incident I was happy to notice that these are water resistant. I’m not going to test it out by submerging them or anything. But from the looks of it they can handle the occasional splash or two—just in case of mishaps. These headphones paired easily with my iPhone X and the sound quality was just as good as my older style of AirPods. I’m very happy with these. Good value!

title: Good quality
review: It's sturdy. It fits the headphones well and protects them well. It's a beautiful case.

title: My favorite headset
review: This headset lasted until the foam over the earpieces rotted off, and I wish I could have replaced those because this is by far my favorite headset. They are super comfortable, especailly for long gaming sessions or long meetings, and I used them for both.  They're lightwight. The sound quality is increadible. The mike is fantasic. They're perfect.

title: Good for kids as well as adults
review:
This have excellent pickup on the mike. They're great for online gaming. I have to admit, I use them as much with the PS4 as with the Nintendo Switch and they work just fine for both. They'll work on anything that has a standard audio port.

They can size a little smaller than most headphones I see, which makes them great for kids. They can size up for adults as well, but few go small enough to be kid friendly.

The sound quality is on point, exactly as you would expect from Turtle Beach. They are one of the most, if not the most, respect name in gaming headsets. The wire is long enough even for an adult to use comfortably.

I love them.

title: They're great for the gym
review:
I'm in love with these for the gym.

I don't find earbuds comfortable in general, but these are somewhat better than average, so for people who don't have issues usually, they'll be great.

I do audio classes from Aaptiv. Some involve a lot of jumping and bouncing. Some, like yoga, involve putting the headphones in an unusual position (think downward dog and the headphones sort of danging). They stay. No matte what, they stay. I run. They stay in. I do cat-cows. They stay in. I love not having to keep adjusting them.

The sound quality is excellent.

title: Meh sound; Great comfort
review:
Given the price point, the sound quality is sorely lacking on these. They perform about as well as the cheap ones available at the chain drug store.

Where they excel is comfort. I don't like wearing headphones for long, and I can tolerate these much longer than average. I'm quite pleased at the easy fit and how they don't annoy my ears. I'll use them regularly for that alone.

title: Really good battery life
review:
This took a bit of getting used to, adjusting the ear cups and all. If there is a volume adjuster on the earphones, I've yet to find it, but I have it paired with an iPhone, and the Apple watch can set the volume just fine.

The sound quality is about what you'd expect in this price range. I use it for audiobooks and podcasts, and I think it's perfect for that.

The battery life is extraordinary. I accidentally left it playing an audiobook all weekend. I had started on leaving the office on Friday. I thought I stopped it when I got home, but come Monday morning it was still playing. The battery was half-drained. So if you need longevity, these are the headphones you want.

They don't fold and they are a bit of a pain to carry around. That's about the worst I can say for them.

title: Fit well, good sound quality, survived dedicated feline assault
review:
These are really secure. I paired them with my phone, and then with my [[ASIN:B06XCWLL12 All-New Kindle Oasis E-reader - 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers]] I then lost the Kindle (it's in the house - I see it on my WiFi network, just not with my eyes) and paired it with yet another Kindle. So it can handle three paired devices no issue.

The point of pairing sports earphones with a Kindle was to listen to an audiobook while running on the treadmill. I'm a sort of "bouncy" runner. It's a problem I'm working on. But I usually use headphones rather than earbuds, because of that, and because, even when I'm not bouncing, I'm pretty hit or miss with ear buds. I have more problems with them falling out than most of my friends do. I just kind of suck with them for some reason. Anyway, these don't fall out, even with the bouncing.

They sound great for audiobooks, for GraphicAudio novels (which are kind of a blend between audio book and old style radio drama) and for music. They don't get tinny at the extremes of pitch.

The only thing I dislike about these is that the control is so high near the ear it's hard to use without taking the earbud out. That and my cat keeps trying to run off with them, but that's another story. I should point out, they have survived multiple cat attacks.

title: Comfortable and long lasting
review:
They were a little tricky to pair with an ipad. I don't see the app as particularly helpful for these.

The best feature is one of the swap on ear pads. It looks a little more matte than the others with a visible tiny circle in it. Those crush up like earplugs, and then exactly like earplugs expand to keep the earbud in place. Those are also the most noise reducing. I can't say noise cancelling. These aren't that. But it does help keep of the ambient noise down. My main concern was one falling out, but with that pad, that hasn't been a problem and I doubt it will be.

I had no problem with ear buds disconnecting from each other. Once they got started, they were rock solid. I got about two hours worth of use out of one charge, and then ran out of time to listen. I think for me they will last long enough, and the case holds a charge for powering up on the go. It uses a standard USB cable. I like things that follow an industry standard.

title: Very lightweight
review:
I have been using this one and [[ASIN:B01N4DHGN2 Sport headset, Dylan Bluetooth 4.1 Stereo Headset Wireless Neckband Design with Retractable Earbud for iPhone, Android, Other Bluetooth Enabled Devices-White]] back and forth, and I think they both have such different strengths and weaknesses, it serves best to compare them.

If you are only interested in sound quality they are identical (tested on the iPhone 6).

If you are interested in comfort, things change. This one is substantially lighter, which is both its advantage and its disadvantage. If you want to listen in a relatively stationary or low movement situation (lying in bed, riding on the bus, going for a walk) the light weight of this one serves it well. I prefer it in those situations. If you want to listen in a high activity situation (going for a run, working out, doing housework, bending and picking up a lot of stuff) then the heavier weight of the Dylan grants it a stability advantage. This one keeps leaning off to the side when I run with it.

It pairs with two devices. It pairs easily. It looks elegant. It sounds great. It charges quickly. I use it every day and adore it.

The only minor thing that bothered me was the sides are not marked L and R and it takes a bit of getting used to in terms of figuring out which is which.

title: Great sound, kind of uncomfortable
review: The sound quality is excellent, and be warned they can get pretty loud depending on the source.  They stay in the ear very well.  They are pretty sturdy.  I just find that they become uncomfortable after the first hour or so.  I have sensitive ears, so that might be part of the issue, but I generally don't have trouble with most earbuds.  These just felt uncomfortable, no matter which tip I used, and the tips are fairly atypically shaped.  That may contribute to why they are uncomfortable and why they stay put so well.  They really do a great job of not falling out.  It's impressive.  The sound clarity and range are both remarkable, and what I would expect from a much more expensive pair of headphones.  The high range is undistorted.  The bass is deep and beautiful.

title: Comfortable, great sound
review:
These are very comfortable. I must have small ears, because most in-ear headphones are way too big for me. With the smallest tips these are perfect. They come with three sets of tips, across a decent range. The cord is on the long side, which means I can plug them into the desktop I have sitting on the floor and listen comfortably, not something I can do with my old pair. Even so, they are able to sit in my purse and not bet themselves tangled or wrapped around everything -- which is not a common feature in headphones. I think I must have extra chaos in my purse, because anything that can get tangled, generally does get tangled. Still, it would have been nice had they came with a carry pouch the way the better headphones in the line do.

The sound quality is excellent for the price category. I am very pleased with these.

title: Excellent quality
review:
These are amazing. They are substantially thicker than the cables the come attached to most headphones--more serious stereo equipment--and I was concerned they would not fit in my Nintendo 3DS (which is what I bought them for). No problem. They fit perfectly. I put them in my SteelSeries headphones and the sound quality is great.

SteelSeries comes with this type of cable--only Aiko chewed through them (I have it on good authority that cats don't normally do that, but she won't believe me). Anyway, I tried this on the PS4, which is what I had been using it, with its original cable, for in the first place. The sound quality improved substantially in terms of quality and range. That is, the base was a little deeper with the new cable.

I am very happy with this cable.

title: Extreme noise cancelling; high quality sound
review:
It's set up differently, depending on which console you want to use it with. For PS3, you plug both the AV and USB cables into the base, and then. You need to go into the settings menu on the PS3 to activate the headset.

For XBox 360, you plug both the AV and USB cables into the base, and the small audio cable into the controller.

For the PS4 or Wii U, you plug the standard audio cable into the controller. That means if you are going to use it for the PS4 or Wii U, you do not need to set up the base, except as a battery charging station. This setup is also used for any portable electronic device that uses a standard headset or standard headphones. Vita, 3DS, MP3 player, Kindle whatever.

For the PC, you plug the USB cable into the base.

I have my base connected to the PC, and often plug the headset into the PS4. It swaps between those two setups dynammically.

The audio quality is exceptional. These are excellent noise cancelling headphones. A yeshiva two blocks away from my house is using an old air raid siren as a shabbos alarm. Imagine how loud that is. When I have these on, and have my game set to a comfortable volume (I do not like it too loud) I can easily hear the game over the air raid siren.

title: Beautiful monitor
review:
The base is smaller than I expected, so I can seat it further back on my desk, and it takes up less space. The height isn't adjustable, but seems perfect to me. The center lines up at just below eye level. The display is crisp, no dead pixels, and presents clear, crisp images.

I plugged it into an Ubuntu machine, via HDMI, and there was no problem. The monitor was recognized immediately. I needed to reset the screen size on the settings in Ubuntu, but that's very common.

I played some PC games with it, and it's very good, and very comfortable for that.

It's easy to access the ports to plug in headphones or other audio equipment, or to switch out things in the second HDMI port. The menu buttons on the bottom right swap the input feed quickly and easily.

The default brightness setting is "burn a hole in your retinas", which can be a nightmare if you suffer migraines and leave it on that setting. If you change it to "standard", it becomes a beautiful, comfortable, fabulous monitor.

title: Perfect sound, hookup is a little complex
review:
The 7.1 sound is shockingly good. I have a standard 7.1 surround system, and I didn't think the headphones would emulate that with any degree of quality, but I was wrong. They're excellent. Two things to keep in mind. One, your sound card needs to support 7.1. Some laptops don't. Two, you may need to go into your sound options and turn on 7.1. Otherwise, you just get stereo. For the game systems (XBox or PS3) no configuration is required. Just be aware that running the headset might not mute the tv, depending on your setup.

The microphone is crisp and picks up what you say, not your breathing, which is an annoyance with some other headsets.

The cord is long enough, you won't mind that it's wired. It's easy to sit a comfortable distance away from the TV and have ample slack left on the cord. It's a thick cord, and oddly, doesn't seem prone to tangling.

The only downside is the complexity. By being a headset that supports everything, it has a lot of permutations. If you have an XBox with composite cables, set it up this way. If you have an XBox with HDMI, set it up that way, if you have a PS3 with... You get the idea. But once you have it configured in your environment, you'll love it.

title: good quality product
review: Let me start out by saying the noise cancelling portion is super excellent.  My husband puts these on and he cannot hear anything but the TV or his music.  He cannot even hear a muffled version of me.  Good?  Bad?  You decide, but as far as noise cancelling it is well above average.  Hooks up wirelessly easily.  Charge lasts a long time.  Comfortable.  to wear all day long binge watching or listening.  We have a couple of other pairs of headphones ... MPOW and Panasonics.  Both good in their own rite.  But these are hubs favorites now and he uses them most often.  Overall ... no regrets at all.

title: good simple headphones
review:
These were the first pair of headphones I ever purchased on Amazon back in 2010. I really loved them as a pair of simple headphones. I have had good success with the Creative Brand. These had good tone and good bass. They stayed in my ears fine and for the price, I believe they were worth what I paid. Unfortunately, my cat chewed my cord in half a few years after owning them, so they lasted a few years, but I cannot speak for the longevity of them beyond that.

I would purchase creative headphones again and recommend the brand easily.

title: Lots of Bang for the Buck
review:
I thought this was such a nifty little TV that I bought two, one to keep and one as a gift.
The picture is crisp and clear in television mode, as long as you're someplace where reception is good. If you aren't getting good reception, use the included cable to connect to a better antenna than the included ones.
It was able to pick up all my local channels. When on the go, just do a scan, and it will pick up all the stations in your new location.
But it can be used for more than local TV.
With a standard cable connection, SD and USB ports, you can play music and video from other devices. Plug headphones or external speakers in. For me, the external speaker really helped...old ears here! Any TV this size and price is going to be lacking in sound if you aren't right next to it.

This is going to be terrific in the RV when summer comes.

Low price, clear picture, multi-use...all translate into a 5 star product. Hopefully it will last a few years.

title: Super Spy
review:
It looks like some reviewers received defective products, but the pair I received do everything they are supposed to.
The great thing about these is that they are a true 'all in one' product.
They are a hands free Bluetooth device with calling capabilities (more on that later), a video recorder, headphones, sunglasses, what more can you ask for at this price?
Ok, the calling features aren't that good, and audio can be dicey, but I often find that to be the case on Bluetooth devices.
And they look good on.

Product received to test with the option to review. No financial compensation is EVER accepted, and vendor may request that item be returned. Views and opinions are my own.

title: Travel Companion
review:
Nothing is worse than being on a flight with screaming kids on board.
I never complain or ask to be seated elsewhere (as if there are extra seats on flights anyway), because as much as I did like it, I feel worse for the parent or guardian.

Good headphones are a must.
I don't like buds because they get uncomfortable after a while, but I wind up using them because they take up so little room, unlike over the ear types.

These are the perfect solution.
They are the on ear type. A super soft perforated cover makes them incredibly comfortable, and of course the head band adjusts.

As you would expect, if you aren't plugged in and listening to something they aren't totally soundproof, but once you start playing music or video, you hear almost nothing else.
And the sound quality is great! I'm using them more for video than music, but when playing music the bass is very good, and all the bright notes shine.

They have a modern sleek look. I've been drooling over the new Bang and Olufsen BeoPlay H8, but investing that much isn't likely. After testing these I'm drooling less.

They come with a velvet bag that will be in my purse for my next flight!

title: Great Sound for Careful Users
review:
While these will need to be handled with kid gloves, the sound outweighs any inconvenience. If you tend to toss stuff around, these are more delicate than sturdy. But on to the headphones themselves...
First off, set-up is easy.
After a 2 hour charge, expect about 5 hours of play, which isn't bad. Range is about 50 feet.
If you get a phone call, press the power button to answer, press it again to hang up. Press twice to ignore and continue with your music.

DISCLOSURE: I received a test unit with the option to review. Financial compensation is NEVER accepted, views and opinions are my own

title: Your Kid Wants These, You NEED These!
review:
[[VIDEOID:e00c599341d8bb572c8903e18b05e0ce]] With all of the sound quality of 'adult' headphones, KidJamz keep your ears safe by limiting the decibel level.

This is a company that is passionate about delivering great sound in a sharp product. I have some spectacular headphones from MEE, and with mine as well as this child's set, the design team was clearly working overtime.
These are easy grip, and look to be practically indestructible due to the flexibility of the crown.

Color is bright and kid-friendly.
All the kids liked them.

And let's face it, we're talking about kids. I love that they are easy to keep clean and sanitary. The plastic is safe and the ear foam is hypoallergenic.

I would also say that the age range could be extended. They were comfortable on my small/medium adult head.
Speaking of adults...as a grownup, trust me, you want to buy these for your OWN comfort. How many times has your child given you 'the look' when you're at a restaurant wanting to have some conversation with another adult, and you tell the child to turn off the sound on the game they are engrossed in?
Oh that look!

Protect their ears, and protect yourself from escalating stress!

Lastly, they are a terrific value for high quality, durable kid's headphones. At this price point, they are a downright bargain. Of course, you can't put a price on a child's health.

Sample provided to test and review

title: So far, so good, Nice looks and sound
review:
This snappy set of headphones have a sporty look and feel, and are pretty comfortable.
Multiple earbuds assure a good fit as well as giving the best possible listening experience be it on land or water.
Easy to set up and get going.
I wore them in the pool, and for me they worked just fine, although from peeking at other reviews, not everyone has been so lucky. Because of this, I'll continue to give them a good workout (as well as myself, lol!) so that I can update with any issues, as other users have done. Please feel free to comment if I can help you with a question not already addressed by others, or if you need some photos.

Product sample provided by manufacturer

title: Was there a bad batch?
review:
As a repeat buyer of MEE I was surprised to see the recent negative reviews.
All I can think of is that somehow a few wonkies got out, or people are having problems with the shape.
Personally, I find the shape gives me a custom fit. So long as I have the proper tip on, and work it to fit the natural shape of my ear, the fit is superb, therefore the noise isolation is superb.

Ok, this may be waaaay too much information for some, so stop here if body fluids flip you out.

For whatever reason, periodically my ear canal is pretty damp, other times it's dry. I have no idea if everyone is this way, it isn't exactly cocktail conversation.
Sometimes, although rarely, it's at the point where I change the tip size. Or I need to clean the tip more often. Never had an issue with them when sweating.*

You might also be tempted to use a tip that's too big for your ear, and after it gets stuffed in there in order to be noise cancelling, well, that can be an issue.
While no one product is perfect for everyone, and in every situation, I love these headphones. They stay in place, and you get the full, rich bass, and crisp upper tones.

* Sweating? My mother would be so disappointed that I said I was sweating. Always the lady, I learned the following from her..."Shannon, horses sweat. Men perspire. But a Lady, my dear, a Lady 'feels the heat'"
Love you, Mom.

title: Polk delivers the goods in this product!
review:
Years ago, as a voice-over artist, I loved over-the-ear headphones from the start. While I use both, I actually prefer them to in ear types.
These are adjustable and comfortable, nice looking.
The name Polk speaks for itself, but as far as home use I've had a Polk surround sound as well as a car system, both excellent.
These headphones do not disappoint, and they are downright spectacular in one area, that of voice recognition.

I've fallen in love with my iPhone all over again! Siri catches every word now, and no more dictation typos.
Great headphones for a variety of applications

title: Easy to pair with a Samsung Galaxy Note 2 UPDATED! Battery bad....
review:
Now that I've been using this for a while, I honestly don't understand the poor reviews, unless certain phones are having a hard time pairing, be it brand or age.

SUPER Easy to pair with a Samsung Galaxy Note2. I just set the phone to bluetooth, it searches for the device, hold the powerbutton in, and it goes to 'broadcast'.

It feels comfortable, sounds good. It even performed well during a conference call, and to me, that is make-or-break of a bluetooth headset.
This is a slick looking product, start to finish. Even the charger looks good, and unlike some other devices, it fits perfectly in the charger, no jiggle or push.
Very pleased.

EDIT: I am wondering if perhaps a 'bad batch' went out, it is odd that something that disappointed so many is working perfectly for me. I invite Jabra or any consumer to contact me. If I can help in any way or if you have a question, feel free to comment.

Update: HOURS after posting I put it on for a call, and even though it had been on the charger, it indicated it had only 30 min of talk time. Thinking it must be a mistake, I made my call, and sure enough....'low battery'.
I'll be calling in the AM

title: Love it for Skype
review: I use skype quite a bit, and have tried numerous headphones and mics. This was my first venture into Skyping wireless, and I love it. Setup consisted of charging the unit, and plugging the other component into a usb port. My account recognized it right away, and I was talking immediately. The sound quality was great, and it was comfortable on my ear. The other party told me I sounded fine. I would recommend this for anyone who Skypes. It's a small investment when you consider that it 'upgrades' all your free Skype calls.

title: Reliable and Functional
review:
I use a headset during my run at least four times a week. I have used many different types - always blue tooth, but I have used headphones with independent ear pieces (no cord connecting them) and also ones (similar to these) that uses a cord to connect the right and left ear pieces.

Although I have liked using cordless headphones, in my experience, they are not as reliable. Sometimes, the left headpiece would work and not the right. Other times, both ear pieces wouldn't connect. Although these have a cord, it makes them much more reliable. I replaced a previous pair (different brand) with these.

So far, so good. I have used them for a couple of months and so far they work great. I use the button on the right ear piece to start and stop music and have also used the volume control on the ear piece. It is very helpful so I don't need to worry about handling my mobile device. I also have used these multiple days in a row without charging with no issues. It was a great price point and work great.

title: Sound isn't great
review: I was excited to receive these headphones as I like the over the ear design and they are cordless. The headphones are fine, but a little bulky if you are used to ear buds. I was hoping the sound quality would be better. If the song has a lot of base, it comes across all scratchy with static. It charges in its case fine. The case protects the headphones, but if you drop it, the case doesn't lock shut so the headphone will fall out. I haven't had any issues with charging (which I have with other headphones that have this type of charging).  Overall, they are average, but I wish the sound quality was better.

title: Exactly as expected and does the job!
review:
I needed a platform to elevate my monitor for video calls and this worked absolutely perfectly.

The installation was a piece of cake. The legs went onto the stand easily. The are 4 USB ports are on the left side of the platform where I plug in my headset and camera. It does not provide enough power to charge a phone. I do highly recommend this product!

title: Good Sound Quality and Sturdy
review:
With working at home more and competing with some family noise in the background, I decided to get a pair of dedicated headphones to use with computer for video conferences. I decided to get a more reputable brand since it was important to make sure the sound quality was good (both the sound received and sent). I also wanted to use something a little more concealed so this was a good pick.

It connected to my computer with no issues. I have already used it on multiple calls and the quality has been great. I also love the case that it comes in - very compact and sturdy.

My only gripe is that it doesn't use a typical mini USB connection; it uses the USB-C connection, which is similar to what is used on the newer Macs. It came with its own charger so not a huge deal, but I like to be able to cross utilize my existing chargers for ease.

title: Great Bass & Comfort
review:
These headphones are AWESOME!

They easily connect to your device wirelessly with bluetooth. When I first connected it, I put on some tunes and found the button on the bottom of the headset that controlled the bass. You can crank up the bass and it really reverberates. I had never had a pair of headphones that have had so much bass. They are quite big and provide a really comfortable fit. Once on, you can really tune out the rest of the world.

I didn't realize it at first, but they also have a built in microphone so you can use them to talk on the phone. I tried it out and the person on the other side of the phone call said they heard me loud and clear.

The only cons I would mention is its size. It is definitely not compact. I was also surprised that headphones at this price point didn't come with a case, whether fabric or otherwise.

Bottom line, awesome sound quality and great bass. Highly recommend.

title: Amazing!
review: Truly the best headset I've owned. First off the battery seems to last long, I charge at night and they last thru a full work day with some juice to spare. Sound wise perfect. When I'm outside I can't hear my rooster crow with the music playing.

title: Good distance
review: Using these for work so I'm not tethered to my phone. The distance works great, I work in a smaller office and seems to reach through the walls. My favorite headphones so far.

title: Tone quality disappointment
review:
Easy plug-and-play compatible. Near instant Blue-tooth connection. Simple, accessible push button operation on the phones.

I've been using bone-conduction headphones for routine computer work for several years. I've found that it's not for everyone. However, the convenience and utility are worth a try. The bone conduction sound experience isn't hi-fi. Mental sound focus is situational and auditory input interchangeable and/or simultaneous between room ambient and machine.

The tone setting here is too treble IMO. Or, maybe, it's just different and I'll get used to it. The tone is not independently adjustable. These would be excellent out of the box if the tone was independently adjustable.

The rechargeable battery in the phones I've been using for 2 years died. This next-generation Blue-tooth upgrade for connectivity is noticeably improved.

60-day Update: I've been using these nearly daily. I've gotten used to the tone. The battery is lasting a week. I have a wandering range with this Bluetooth edition of say 75'. The fastest connection and link speed of any I've had. Quite happy.

title: Fits my ears
review:
Fit is the primary feature I look for in an earbud. These are an excellent fit. That makes them good by me.

The sound quality is better than average. Battery life is good. I can predict with 100% certainty that I'll lose them somewhere.

Priced right.

title: Second or third buy
review:
I love these quick connections!

Early versions had male to devise interfaces that were interference fit in some appliances. I may have destroyed a wireless earbud connector with them. But, time has improved the male device interface. This kit has the best fitting connectors yet.

Nice cord length. Excellent fittings.

title: As advertised
review:
If I get 6 months out of earbuds, I'm happy. Nice comfort. The battery here is longer life so far. The sound is good. Jabra's a name brand.

As expected.

title: Fantastic!
review:
Best buds I've had, and man-o-man, I've gone through a lot. Second, I have no idea what 'Gaming Earbuds' operationally means. I just use them for music.

The sound quality, fidelity, batt life, range, and cancellation are a step-function improvement. I've probably bought half a dozen buds in this price range or more and dozens at a half to a third the price. I've decided wi-fi earbuds are just a basic living cost.

So the real test is how long they can continue to operate at this performance, and I can't answer that. These Hecate GX07 are really excellent for now. I'd definitely re-buy.

title: Value
review:
RIENOK True Wireless Earbuds delivers on the advertised performance. Quality sound. Good bass. Easy Bluetooth pairing, As advertised battery life.

Very cool 'micro-carry package.' Value for money.

title: Impressive
review:
Bluetooth 5 makes these a snappy, instant connection after set-up. Bluetooth 5 seems to solve legacy problems. Excellent range. Better fidelity than expected. Comfortable ear fit. These are my Kindle Amazon Prime movies in bed headphones.

I've gone through more of these from triple-digit priced to quick buying inexpensive 'disposable' varieties over the years. These are a noticeable improvement.

Better than advertised. Remarkable for the price.

title: Multicharger friendly, powered USB ports
review:
2.5 critical ideas are incorporated that other power strips have chronically overlooked.

A 6-banger power strip will typically hold 3 chargers max due to tight outlet spacing. That's not a problem here. Six typical accessory chargers can fit in the outlet spacing ... if you have a male plug 'brick' size charger, check the powerstrip dimensions.

Second, the power strip incorporates 2 powered USB-C charge ports. Earbuds, iPhone, most any small USB recharge accessory is adequately supported.

Third, the power cord to the power strip is sized for limited space in the wall outlet. It leaves room to plug yet another charger in the same wall outlet! The power-on LED is pleasant.

By comparison, this is one of the very best I've seen. Better than expected.

title: Excellent
review:
Very comfortable. Easy sync. Great sound. 6-hour battery life. Sophisticated independent recharge case with a 5-minute fast charge from the built-in battery adds an hour and longer with more time. USB connected fast recharge.

Well worth the price. Best of the earbud lot to date. Gets better with use.

title: Worked great, then turned to crap
review:
Worked great for 3 months then slowly then completely came undone. Bluetooth connectivity became iffy, then lost. Headphones pipe the cosmos big bang reflection at max db into your ears. I think I'm hearing aliens!

Something is very wrong here.

title: Very cool, better than expected
review:
I was looking for a better sound solution for working on the laptop sitting in my Barco-lounger. Laptop speakers are, of course, marginal at best. Headphones are a hassle because they sit around till I put them in a drawer.

For the price, the Sphere sound is extraordinary across the audio spectrum ... better than expectations. The Sphere headphones are great. The speaker and headphone pair up and operate as advertised. The Sphere enforces unitary recharge and housekeeping for the headphones. Great idea.

I'm liking it more and more.

5/2018 update ... Worked great, then turned to crap. Slowly than quickly lost blue tooth connectivity. Something's very wrong here

update 2/9/2018: Okay ... the Sphere is now a primary tool. I don't know I got along without it.

title: Solves an irksome problem
review: Airplane flight. Two Bose headphones viewers want to hear one movie on the laptop. The laptop has one 3.55mm audio output. Movie enjoyment for 2 problem resolved.

title: Delightfully unexpected
review: These arrived as a pleasant surprise fitting better than any others right out of the box You get plenty of ear fit accessories to experiment with for the right hold and fit. Finding the right headphone fit for the hard cardio workout has been  continuous search. These are superb. Sound quality is excellent.

title: The search will continue.
review: Inventing an earbud that stays in your ear during a workout must be a technology challenge approaching the scale of a landing on the moon. It's the default chat of the gym ... why can't it be done? You can't find the right one because you can't try them before buying. These aren't the ones that work. The search will continue.

title: 'Wow' factor fidelity and bass! Too big for active wear
review:
First, getting the ear fit right is awkward. None of the earfits really secure them well. These are bigger than ‘buds’. When you have them fitted to your ear in a least worse choice sort of way, the fidelity and most especially the bass is fantastic … as good as I’ve ever heard from such a compact package. But … they are too big/heavy for use on the treadmill. I can’t keep them in my skull.

For non-workout use, these are likely the best full fidelity you’ll find. The ‘earbud for workout’ application just isn’t working for me. If you’re not looking for active wear, these are really superb commuter 'super-buds'

title: Great value for money!
review: I'm not sure how you can get a better sound out of set earbuds. These are used on iPhone 5. Compared to the Apple buds, there is simply not a comparability in comfort and sound quality.

title: Better than most brands, but suggest upgrading to a better Jabra model like Elite 7
review:
Unboxing was less interesting than the last pair of Jabra earbuds I tried. There's a quick start insert. It suggests downloading their app. Could use a QR code instead of making us go search. Paper packaging is minimalist, but well designed to protect the product in transport.

I've tried most of the major brands of earbuds, sometimes several of each. One of the Jabra earbuds is my go-to, the Jabra Elite 7. Unfortunately, these feel like a big step down from some of their more premium products. They feel more like earbuds from half a decade ago, when they were more like earplugs without a lot of features. It does come with some alternate fittings for different size preferences, and the design is still above average. I still suggest going up a model in the same brand.

title: Great for when the other earbuds make my ears sore
review:
I have quite an assortment of earbuds, and like them for different reasons. My normal fave are a Bose set that has kind of a bigger capsule shaped part and then they fit right into your ear. But, for those of us with small ears, even a well designed set like those can begin to make my ears feel tired after a couple hours.

When those make my ears tired and I still want to be listening, I pop these on. The fit is SO different from any other earbuds I own that they are a perfect alternative for when traditional buds make my ears tired. They are interesting to get on the first time, but kind of brilliant after you get the hang of it. By the time these begin to get uncomfortable, the others feel good again.

The sound quality is not as good as my other Bose buds, but is still better than most brands by a long shot.

I appreciate the innovation a lot. They fit well and stay on.

title: Above average offering, but don't care for the design of them or the gesture controls
review:
This product feels different to me than other Sony stuff I've gotten. It's like they've gone out of their way to make everything feel like cardboard. The packaging was like egg carton, and the earbuds and their charging station are a rough lightweight material in a drab color. The earbuds themselves are customizable, but bulky compared to the competition. I find them hard to get out of the container, hard to hold onto, and hard to wear. The noise cancellation and sound are both above average though. I like the charging light on the container. It communicates with color and flashes what the status of the product is, and isn't bright or hard to locate.

USB-C charging makes the base station charge up nice and fast. It holds the earbuds securely, and doesn't rattle or fall open. It's also a nice pocketable size and shape with no sharp corners, making the whole product especially portable. Controls are gesture, rather than button. I'm not a fan of this because I end up doing a lot of swiping and hoping. A click button interface, I can just click it the number of times I know will do what I need, and move on.

I've got a few Sony audio products that I use every day and am very happy with, but with earbuds, I'm sticking with jabra for now. It's a competitive market right now for earbuds. Lots of companies putting out new designs.

title: No instructions, have to use the app, sound quality only okay
review:
These are overall perfectly okay earbuds, but they certainly don't outcompete some of the similar ones on the market.

I have a set of Bose earbuds, and a Jabra set that I like better.

When I think about beats studio buds, I think about sound quality, and particularly I think about Dr. Dre, and playing some music with a thumping beat. Well, the sound quality on this was not great for listening to music. It's perfectly fine for a podcast, but music felt muted and unexciting through these.

The noise cancellation did work well, so I was impressed with that. And they are very comfortable to wear.

But another thing he didn't really care for with these was that there is no instructions, and there's no way to pair these with my phone without downloading their app. I really don't always want to be forced into using their dedicated app. I appreciate that the app has some settings that are very useful, but I would prefer that be an option rather than a requirement.

title: An excellent complete package - quality on all fronts
review:
They did a quality job on these. Luxury without excess. Packaging is acceptable. The case feels great, the zipper is awesome. The headphones fit in very easily, and there is a mesh pouch inside for accessories.

The headphones have a giant L and R printed on the interior foam, which is convenient to figure out which way to put them on, but isn't visible once they are. The buttons are easy to access, labeled, and simple enough to remember.

Bluetooth was easy to connect and had audio cues.

I'm usually not a fan of gesture controls, but they work really smoothly and intuitively here.

The product itself feels high quality, and they're very comfortable and secure. Noise cancellation is fine, and a nice addition, but I don't find it notable. What was more impressive to me was just how little I noticed the usual irritations of wearing headphones. They don't have a background noise at all, they don't feel like they're going to fall off if I bend over or make a sudden move, they don't press uncomfortably, and they don't make noise when I turn my head.

I've tried a few modern wireless noise cancelling headphones, and I'd say some of the others win in one feature or another, but these are an excellent complete package.

title: Sound quality is pretty good, noise cancellation mediocre, fits medium-size ears
review:
Recently I have tried out about five different brands of noise canceling and other earbuds, and have been annoyed to find that the ones that I like, often feel too big for my ears. My favorites for sound quality and noise cancellation are the ones from Bose, but they definitely make my ears sore after an hour of use.

These from LG have really mediocre noise cancellation to where if you are listening to something noisy like music, the noise cancellation works pretty well, but if you are listening to something peaceful or a podcast or even nothing at all, the noise cancellation doesn't really do much.

I do like the comfort level and shape of these, which fit in my ears a lot better than some of the other brands.

The sound quality is pretty good, nothing to complain about, but not reaching any incredible heights of clarity or bass.

Overall, these are a pretty middle-of-the-road option. They weren't my favorite or my husband's very favorite, and the noise cancellation doesn't work that well, but they are comfortable and have reasonably good sound quality.

title: Incredibly impressed with this awesome speaker, great bass for music
review:
I really love this speaker. I already have two sets of Bose earbuds, so I already had the Bose app downloaded to my phone. It was easy to pair and didn't have any issues getting set up. I don't control it through the app, I just control it through the buttons on the speaker itself or just by turning the music on my phone on or off.

I wanted a simple speaker that I didn't need to worry too much about so that I could listen to podcasts and music in the shower, or when working in my vegetable greenhouse this summer. So far it's been great! The battery life has been longer than expected, the sound quality is absolutely amazing for listening to music and has great bass, not any kind of tinny sound at all, and the unit itself seems thoughtfully designed and built to last. It's got a nice weight to it and doesn't want to tip over.

I really appreciate after having a bunch of Chinese made brands in the past, that this one is just straight up quality, everything works, it's easy to deal with, etc.

I haven't truly tested the water resistant capability of it, but after two weeks of showering with it just outside the shower and bringing it into the sometimes drippy or humid greenhouse, it still doing great.

Overall the Bose quality shines through in this item and I've been really thrilled with it for my purposes.

title: Okay, but not outperforming the competitors at similar price points
review:
These are definitely a quality product. I don't think they outperform some of the competitors. They feel really solid. Range is decent. A bit large and heavy. The noise cancelling is just barely worth turning on.

They come with several options for improving fit. I settled on some of the bigger flappy looking parts as being very comfortable. Unfortunately, after wrestling them onto the earbuds, I found that the lid is no longer even close to closing on the charging case. I'd call it an inexcusable design oversight. Lots of tuning options in the app.

Compared to other earbuds I've tried, they sound better and are much heavier than much less expensive brands, but I'm not sure it's worth it. At similar price points, I've tried two other brands. One was even bigger, but sounded amazing (Bose), and the other I found to be superior in nearly every way.

title: Great quality earbuds in a really cute color
review: I wanted to listen to some music and audiobooks from my cell phone, and while the included Samsung earbuds were okay, I was hoping for a mild upgrade in both sound quality and style, and these Panasonic ones are great. I have the metallic violet Samsung S9, so this set of earbuds is a similar color tone but a little bit darker, which is great. I like how it color-coordinated, the sound quality is great for listening to pop, dance and rap music, and my audiobooks sound crisp. The earbuds are comfortable and fit well.

title: Cute little earbuds that work exactly as expected
review: These cute little earbuds fit my ears just right, and were perfect for listening to some hip-hop music and then listening to an audiobook from my cell phone. The little microphone picked up a little wind noise, but seemed extremely comparable to the Samsung earbuds that came with my phone in that regard. Everything worked just fine, and pretty much exactly as expected given the price and form factor. This is a nice quality little set of earbuds that is cute and stylish, fits as expected, and has decent sound quality both on the input and the output.

title: Works exactly as expected and fit comfortably
review:
This little set of earphones fits comfortably in my ears and came with a few of the little differently sized cushions so that I could customize my fit. The included microphone worked fine and I didn't hear any complaints from the people I was talking to. And the earbuds themselves had perfectly good quality for listening to some pop music as well as listening to an audiobook.

Overall there were no surprises with these simple wired earbuds. They work great!

title: Works great but hurts my ears after a couple hours
review:
I got this headset to practice working with speech recognition software such as Dragon NaturallySpeaking. Overall, I've been surprised and incredibly impressed with the performance. The recognition is better than with the standard headset that came with the software, and the headset does everything I had hoped.

There's a volume control button on the cord, and the USB cord is about 8 feet long, which is plenty generous for connecting to my computer and doing speech recognition.

The only problem with this headset is that I want to use it for hours on end while narrating articles. I'm a freelance writer, and sometimes I either just don't feel like typing, have a sore wrist or fingers, or feel like I can narrate my thoughts faster than I can type them. After about two hours of using this headset, my ears start to ache. I haven't figured out any way of changing the tension on this headset so it doesn't press so hard on my ears.

While I would definitely recommend this headset as a low-budget alternative to higher end products, and for people who would like to use a headset for just an hour or so at a time, I would not recommend it for people who want to use the headset for any kind of professional or serious hobby endeavor. I can see from other reviews that I'm not alone in having my ears hurt, and since I have a small size head, and ears that do not stick out very far, I can only think the problem would be worse for most people than it is for me.

title: Great for Running
review: I needed ear buds for running and these are it!  I was super excited to receive the Latest 2020 Bluetooth 5.0 Headphones w/12+ Hours – QCC3003 Chipset because the last earbud set I received kept falling out and hitting the payment every two steps.  Because these have an over ear "holder" if they fall out they will not fall to the ground and you can keep going.  These are not the best headphones I've ever had, but they are not the worst.  Pairing them up with my Bluetooth on my phone was easy.  Mine were red and I don't really care about the color because they work.  I have good ear buds for when I am working at my desk and now I have a decent ear buds for when I'm out running or walking around the neighborhood.  These are good choice for that.

title: Nice Bluetooth Earbuds, but Don't Use While Running
review: Asimom True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth V5.0, TWS Bluetooth Earphones Auto-Pair Wireless Headphones are really nice earbuds and easy to use.  They paired easily and quickly with my iPhone 5.  They come in a case that charges them and they are already charged when I received them.  They come with a USB charging cord for the case and with extra earbuds depending on the size of your ear.  You just tap with on and tap to play or play.  It's pretty tricky at first.  I'm still getting the hang of it.  The sound quality is really decent.  The downside is that these do not stay in my ear and dropped out an onto the ground while I was out for a walk.  So, I'll only use these at work since if they fall onto the carpet they won't get scratched up.  Not as good as a product as the Asimom Bluetooth Speaker, which I also received, but still a decent product.  If you don't have issues with earbuds falling out your ears like I do, then this is great for you.

title: 10Xs Better Than My Sony Earbuds!
review:
After buying some horrible Sony earbuds I decided "That Was It!, I just wasn't an ear bud person". Between the bad sound, constant crackling and continually popping out of my ear, I was done!

Shock set in when I put these Spirit X Soundcores on.
The audio quality is amazing!
No Crackling or Popping. Just
Full crisp clear sound, no outside interference or noise.

Plus These stay in place! Period.
No endless fiddling or crawling around the floor looking for a ear bud that rolled half way across the room.

The hooks go over your ears and do a great job of holding these in place.
Super Easy to use and easy to set-up. Easy to take or make a call, Easy to control the volume without having to find and push just the right spot.

These are just plain easy.
These even come with a size assortment of ear tips and ear wings and a great little case to keep everything in.

title: Great Sound, Long USB Cord, Quality Mic, So So Comfort.
review:
First, this Pro USB Mono headset is only fairly comfortable! Anyone who wears these headsets knows that comfort and sound are the 2 most important factors. The head piece is adjustable and the ear piece is very well padded but the left side is not.
Like I mentioned, the other important factor is the sound quality which is clear with no static. I also like the mic, it moves easily but stays in place when you need it to and feels like it's well made and won't break.
This headset plugs right into any USB on a computer, so your wired but it's long, over 6 ft.
The Cons:
It's alittle heavier on the right side and I have alot of hair and it keeps slipping out of place from time to time.
After wearing it for an hour the left side of my head starting hurting.

title: I Like These Better Than My Sony Earbuds
review:
These were super easy to connect and they sound GREAT. I have Sony earbuds and they constantly run out of batteries which drives me nuts ( it wasn't a long trip)..
These came ready to go with some charge and to recharge the earbuds only takes an hour of putting them back in the case and they last all day. The case charges super fast too and the lights on the back tell you if they're done.
I also love how small they are, they came with medium sized ear pieces on but they come with small and large also.

title: Good Sound But Hard To Use & The Battery Doesn't Last As Long As I Would Like
review:
The Sony WI-C600N earphones are not as easy to use as I would've liked and the Noise Cancelling feature an DC battery life aren't the greatest.
The last photos shows the controls and how they are all matte black and not raised or buttons which makes them very hard to use when the headset is on. They all feel alike and theres nothing to differentiate them when you first start wearing them or if you only wear them once in awhile, it's hard to tell the controls apart.
I also don't like that I can hear background noise from my surroundings.
On the plus side they are comfortable and lightweight. The band is rubber and very flexible when you move.
At this pricepoint these should be much easier to use not to mention the battery doesn't last all day.

title: I Don’t Know How I Ever Lived Without A 10 Foot Charging Wire! Look How Far I Can Go..
review:
10 Feet is Really far in Cord land. So many things are wireless now that when your stuck on a 3 ft charging cord it leaves no room to move and you feel like your in jail. I LOVE the freedom a 10 ft cord gives. Then when you consider al the things you can charge, it keeps getting better. Phones, headphones, vapes, ear bud cases, the list goes on.
Some 10 foot chargers say they’re fast charging, NO! They aren’t. I find these chargers are much faster and at an excellent price.

title: Excellent Quality Headphones! Made For Smaller Heads..
review:
My daughter loves these PuroQuiet headphones for listening to music and also for using at school. They are very good at noise canceling and easy to sync. The buttons are easy to reach and control plus they’re very well padded and comfortable to wear for long periods of time.
These can be used wired or blu tooth and hold a charge for over 16-22 HOURS.
They say “for kids” and they’re a little smaller but still fit adult normal to smaller size heads...

title: I actually wear these while I’m working to have some peace and quiet!
review:
I hate background noise and I’m easily distracted, so when I don’t feel like being bothered, I run around the house in these since they’re noise canceling. They Work!
Dogs Barking - NO PROBLEM!
Husband Talking - NO PROBLEM!
Kids Screaming - NO PROBLEM!
The headphones are smaller and less bulky than a lot of styles and everywhere that touches you is padded. Synced to my IPhoneX in 5 seconds.

title: easy installation; no instructions included (I typed instructions below :-)
review: I’m the type of person who doesn’t really read instructions anyway, so it wasn’t an issue for me, but for those who like instructions, these didn’t come with any.  The little guitar pick looking thing helps pry off the old headphones from the inside, and from there, you rip out the old lining and replace it with the new one (keep track of Left and Right so you don’t mix them up). The liner thing attached with the adhesive backing, so you just peel off the cover to reveal the sticker part. Once you do that, the new pads click right in fairly easily. I recommend saving the longer side for last, because rearranging and pushing it around to get it to click is easier from the long side than from the top or bottom. Pretty straightforward, turned out great, nice and comfortable!

title: Decent noise cancelling, great sound quality, good buds!
review:
These low-profile, lightweight earbuds have some decent active noise canceling that helps drown out white noise like air conditioners, fans, airplane engines, etc. There are 3 options for the rubber buds at the end, with the smallest working ok for a decent fit. (The others were HUGE)
As for sound quality, these are a solid choice, especially considering the price point. The treble is crisp and not tinny, unlike many earbuds, and the bass is strong and pretty powerful. Good sound definition and clarity, plus a transparent mode to be able to hear your surroundings.
Overall: solid in all categories, and reasonably priced for good quality Bluetooth earbuds!

title: Excellent noise cancelling, good definition, nice case, comfortable
review:
These headphones are a solid value for what you get. Below are highlights of various features and drawbacks:
Excellent:
-active noise cancelling
-clarity/definition of sound
-carrying case comfort
Very good:
-audio for podcasts and tv
Ok:
-treble is a *little on the tinny side
-bass isn’t as deep or powerful as I’d like

title: No more falling off!
review: I was having a hard time keeping these ear hooks in my head, especially while dancing or moving around or doing activities. These ear hooks completely solved the problem, allowing these to stay in place regardless of what I’m doing. The only downside is the hassle of having to take it off and put it back on each time I have to put these on in the case, which is why I prefer other earbuds entirely. If you’re using the Apple ones, however, this is a great accessory. Includes a little carrying pouch keychain thing.

title: ok sound, but high pitch sound in background
review:
If these were in a lower price point, they’d have more stars, but for the current price of ~$80, there’s a problem that really should not be there: a very high pitch whine in the background. It’s noticeable most when you have noise cancelling on with silence in the background, or in sections of music or voice that are quiet. It’s not terribly loud, but I can pick it up from time to time.
Other than that, the noise cancelling is pretty good, and the sound has good clarity and power. The treble isn’t super tinny the way some headphones are—EXCEPT when you bring the volume up. THEN, it does get tinny, and the bass doesn’t have quite the power you might like. You can hear subtle details in most music, which I appreciate, and pairing is easy.
As for comfort, the ear cups are a bit small and have a somewhat awkward fit, though they are lightweight and reasonably comfortable.
All in all, these would be Great headphones if they were in the $40-$50 range. In the $80 range, they’re just ok.

title: Great for school
review: This little recorder has been perfect for school. I can record lectures and easily upload them to my computer or listen to them in the car or with little earbuds. Compact, inexpensive, and it really does get the job done!

title: Not as good as other Bose speakers
review: I don’t really use the Alexa feature, so I can’t speak to that, but Bluetooth speakers are always much appreciated in our household. I’ve use several Bose products, from headphones to small speakers, and for some reason, this one struck me as just OK compared to the others. The sound wasn’t as rich and didn’t fill as much space as some others I’ve used in the past. Is it still great? Absolutely. But it’s not quite at the level Bose usually is. Better than most brands in terms of power, bass, treble, and clarity of sound, but a little less across-the-board then some higher end Bose products.

title: Easy setup, nice sound
review: I’m used to a more clear button system, so I worried when I put these on that my phone wouldn’t find them, yet they did! It paired quickly and easily without any problems, and the sound had surprisingly good definition, allowing subtle sounds to come through. Even so, the treble could have been a little less tinny and the bass a bit stronger. Likewise, there was some slight distortion for some volumes and sounds. It wasn’t often, but it happened with enough songs that I had to remark on it. These are good, not great headphones. Now taking price into account, they are Way better than expected! For under $30, these are pretty great Bluetooth headphones.

title: No noise cancelling on this...
review: I’m not sure they sent the right item, but there was no noise cancelling feature/button anywhere. If what they mean is that it blocks sound physically with the ear covers, then a) that's not "sound cancelling", and b) it doesn't accomplish this either way. The sound quality is fine—pretty good actually, though the bass could be a bit more powerful. The headphones are lightweight and comfortable, though they do not fold compactly, making them minimally portable and bad for travel (also no carrying case). For the price, these are pretty great, but in no way do they cancel noise.

title: Nice value version of high end headphones
review:
Always taking price points into account and comparing within the range (as well as referring to the high end products for where the relevant technology currently is), these are pretty great!
Note that many headphones say “noise cancelling” and actually mean that they insulate against outside sounds through earplugs or other physical barriers muffling outside noise, as opposed to actively using other sound waves to sort of cancel out many frequencies, which is a powered process requiring technology that can listen, identify, and then send appropriate sounds at all times to create this quieting effect.
Ok, so knowing that ACTIVE noise cancelling is usually a high end thing found in Bose and similar products for $300-$500, seeing a $50~ product offer this is pretty neat!
And for the price, it’s pretty good, and so is the sound! While slightly canned and tinny on the treble, a common problem on mid or lower end headphones, it is still great for the price and has nice features!
Good!

title: terrible sound quality, great thermos
review:
If you take the insulated thermos/bottle, detach it from the speaker, and throw the speaker out, you'd have a great product at an insanely high price. And that's basically where you are with this: the bottle does its job perfectly, offering a drink that stays hot or cold for hours, with a loop at the top to hang it or carry it conveniently with a carabiner. Everything in that department is fine, until you add the speaker.

Ease of use: great for both halves. Fits most standard cup holders, has the loop, unscrews from speaker to make it washable and versatile for when you don't want horrible sound shooting out the bottom half.

Appearance: really cool! It's a great concept, and you're probably less likely to have this speaker stolen because it looks like a regular drinking bottle from afar. Nice for the beach (partly because ambient noise makes the sound quality tolerable).

Sound quality: the worst. It's like $5 earbuds, but much louder. It is extremely tinny, whether attached or detached from the bottle, with incredibly weak bass that is almost inaudible, and shrill treble. The low and high ends come together to create a perfect cacophony of undefined sounds making every genre of music sound awful. Like iTunes played on your speaker phone, your music will sound the same but louder.

Value: I'd pay $15-$20 max for this. The sound quality really ruins what was a cool concept.

title: Immersive sound experience
review:
Between the perfect fit of the earbuds and the detailed full-range sound, these headphones create an immersive sound experience.
The bass is deep and powerful, and the treble is crisp and clear—not tinny like many headphones. The sound is detailed and clear enough to allow the listener to hear ambient sounds in the recording like breath or clothing (depending on the particular track, of course), so one can pick up fairly subtle elements and enjoy music with both very quiet and quite loud parts. Likewise, it’s great for radio and podcasts because voices and words sound defined.

And the setup?
Well, it passed my “can I make this happen without a manual or instructions” test. I didn’t open the booklet, and that was fine! Turn on Bluetooth, press the button between the volume buttons for a bit, it shows up, and bam. You’re ready to go. So far, I haven’t needed to read anything—it works and is straightforward.

Phone calls?
Fine! Just like the wired headphones but wireless—no issues!

title: The incomparable Bose does it again!
review:
Bose has been and remains the best headphone maker. I’ve tried at least a dozen different products on amazon, with perhaps a dozen more in my life, and in all those experiences, the Bose name always stood far ahead of the crowd.

First, their noise cancelling technology remains the best. Eerily effective, especially on airplanes and in cars, trains, or buses, you put them on, and the world becomes quieter, making you realize how terrible the ambient noise was! These have the added benefit of adjustable noise cancellation, unlike previous models.

In comfort, these are built for long-term use, remaining wearable for hours. Most other headphones I’ve tried tend to make your ears sore, but not these! They feel soft and lovely everywhere they land on your head.

With or without Bluetooth, these offer exceptional clarity of sound, powerful bass, and clear crisp treble, none of which turn to distorted noise, even at high volumes. Yes, these are very powerful! And they offer the option for wireless battery-operated use or plug-in use. They sound equally good in either setting. As for battery life, these won’t let you down. They last hours and hours without needing a charge.

My partner has the QuietComfort 30, I believe, and I always loved borrowing those, so it’s great having a pair of my own (in an even better version, no less!)

Fantastic! No product compares to Bose.

title: Bad app, good headsets
review:
There’s a lot that’s great about these headsets, and only one kind of annoying thing.

The annoying thing is the app.
You need Spotify for the app to do anything. Once you have it, it seems to only work by leaving the Jaybird website, where it re-routes you to the internet, which then tells you to go to the Spotify app. I tried it a few times after setting up a Spotify account, and at no point did the pretty and cool-looking Jaybird interface work. Instead, I went through the ridiculous Jaybird to safari internet to Spotify loop. Annoying fail.
It also lets you make minor adjustments to the sound levels, with both pre-set stuff and manual stuff. I didn’t see a huge difference.

Aside from that nonsense, the sound is fine. Not great, but very good. The earbuds last about 4 hours, and with only 5 minutes in the little box (if fully charged), you get an additional hour-long charge worth of usage! That’s pretty cool! In total, the fully charged box can provide an additional 8 hours, giving you a total of 12 hours. Very nice.

They have a certain amount of inadvertent noise canceling, which is great if you want that, but not so much if you’re driving or doing something else that requires partial attention.

Good product with many nice qualities—not the best version of this, but still excellent!

title: Ok; A little canned and lacking in detail
review:
Unfortunately, the sound on these isn't great, which is unfortunate given the eco-friendly approach in the packaging and product. The mid range is ok, though the treble and bass leave quite a bit to be desired. The bass lacks strength and intensity, while the treble and mid feel a bit canned, and there's an overall lack of definition.

Are these bad? No. They're better than many headphones, and are ok for the price. But for a little more money, you can do much better. Still, if this is the price range you want, and the environment is a priority for you, as well as supporting businesses that try to be responsible, it is worth considering these.

title: adjust the sounds of the world around you, take calls, and listen to your music/audio!
review:
There are some pretty neat features with these headphones that make them uniquely better for some people. For example, if you are slightly hard of hearing (but do not use/need a hearing aid), these can actually turn the world around you up, making it a bit louder to better hear conversations. Likewise, you can turn the world down and make things more quiet!

The charging and holding case is also pretty awesome! They live and charge in this neat little box that indicates when it is charging or ready to pair, a process that was relatively easy, but sometimes buggy when putting on and taking off.

For music, you get a nice amount of detail in the sound. I always test it with orchestral music to see if you can pick up on the gentle rustle of clothing. Yes, you can hear that! At the same time, however, the sound can be a *little* tinny and lack richness among the treble notes. Overall, the quality for music is good. Not amazing, not mediocre or bad. Just a solid good.

For audio, it is excellent--crisp, clearly-defined sound!

And yes, you can make phone calls with these!

They take a little troubleshooting to figure out, but they're well worth the effort for their many interesting features. Cool technology!

title: good headphones with sharing options for others of the same kind
review:
These super comfortable headphones have special cushioning that helps block out extraneous noise, so while they may not be noise-cancelling, they do a great job making the outside world fade away. (It is not the standard cup-type design with a hollowed out section with a puffy circular exterior--the whole thing is cushioned, kind of like an extra-squishy ear ottoman!)

The sound itself is good. Not amazing, but very good. (There is a hint of tinny quality to treble, and the bass notes are not super super intense.) But I am a musician and dancer, so I am more critical than most on this. For regular usage, for people not super invested in extreme detail or the highest quality, these are awesome.

Note: I was not able to activate sharing between other bluetooth brands and these. I am pretty sure you need more than one of this exact brand for the sharing feature to work. That's another thing to consider, along with the fact you would have to double your investment (current price is $199, so not particularly cheap).

Great headphones with a cool sharing feature, if your other pair is of the same kind.

title: Strong bass, somewhat tinny treble; great fit
review:
4.5 stars
While the treble may leave something to be desired, with a rather tinny quality and slight general lack of detail in overall sound, these headphones are decent! The bass is strong and doesn't distort, and best of all, the fit is excellent. It holds well and is very comfortable, both on its own, as well as in comparison to other similar products.
Easy setup and pairing, too! Nice headphones, especially for modern music that emphasizes bass sounds. Solid workout option!

title: Exemplary fit and sound
review:
The main issue I have with headphones is usually the fit, then secondly, the tendency for the sound to be tinny. But this is Bose.

Known for innovative and exemplary sound quality, Boss speakers and headphones are consistently top-of-the-line, and these are no exception to that expectation. The high and low ends remain clear, crisp, and defined, free of distortion of echo, maintaining detail in whatever you are listening to, whether orchestral or spoken word, hip hop or show tunes. Everything sounds great!

As for fit, that is also great! They stay in perfectly and block out noise quite well, and I can dance with them without problems for the most part. That's a first!

These are excellent. But if you've heard of Bose, this won't be a surprise.

title: less mess with cords; a little slower
review: This cord charges and synchronizes without issues, though it seemed a little slower to charge than my official and overpriced Apple cord (not by a lot, but noticeable). The benefit of a twist cord is that you get some extra length without as much of a mess. Saving on all that extra winding cord is nice--the headphone situation alone is bad enough, so it's good to not have an additional thing making knots of itself. Good!

title: best kids' headphones I've seen! Great sound and durability!
review:
These had FAR better sound quality than I would have expected. Usually, kids' headphones (from what I've experienced) don't bother with making sure the music has detail, decent treble and bass, etc. While these have a volume limiter, which is great for protecting their ears, the headphones still pick up everything a pretty good quality set would.

Likewise, we put them to the test and sat on them, bent them, dropped them--they survived! These guys are TOUGH. The added padding that is removable is a nice touch--they can grow with your little one by letting them adjust the fit for the size of their head.

Great product--best I've seen so far!

title: comfortable uni-taskers (no output) with ok sound quality
review:
While they are ok for the price in terms of sound quality, fit, and durability, they lack a fundamental function for what Many people use to play their music: the ability to receive and make phone calls. If you are using a smartphone, these are only headphones, not headphones with a function button (like the kind that come with an iPhone, for example), and not ones that have an output through which you can speak or take dictation.
That aside, the sound quality was ok, with a somewhat tinny, canned quality and poor capability in processing deep bass or treble. If changing the levels to decrease treble, you'll see some improvement in the sound. For anything spoken word like podcasts, these are fine.
The fit is not bad. Usually, these things are big on me (female with apparently small ear-holes, if you would judge by most headphones), but these were comfortable. The three sizes of rubbery earplugs always help and are generally standard, and the ear hooks also aide in keeping them in place.

Summary:
For the price, you get decent headphones that do not have an output function.

title: Poor sound quality--not suited for music
review:
While the pairing process was simple, and the ability to make calls went smoothly, the sound quality was sub-par. One might expect this level of quality in a $10 headphone.
Here's why:
-The volume tops out at somewhere in the 80 decibel range, which is not a lot. It would be fine for background listening in a quiet environment, but if you want to listen to music loudly, which many people might, or if you are dealing with lots of background noise, then it's not even remotely adequate.
-Does nothing for treble or bass. Everything sounds right around the middle, flattening out most music.
-Lacks detail. You don't hear the quieter elements in music, and it does not pick up on individual parts. Fuzzy.

I wouldn't buy these. Bluetooth headsets can be very hit or miss. While it was user-friendly, this was mostly a miss.

title: Ok sound quality--not what I'd expect for the price
review: Oddly, I got better sound quality from several cheaper headphones I own, but bluetooth has always been a bit hit or miss for me. Pairing was very easy (thankfully! some can be a pain), but the range isn't great. It's fine if you plan on putting your phone in your pocket, but if you are working out and want to set your phone aside, you only have about 10-15 feet, if that. Mid-range sounds are fine, but on the high trebles and low bass, it starts to sound a little distorted. The fit was ok, but I have very small ears and ear canals, so even the small inserts were slightly uncomfortable after a while. They stayed in place fine, but I used it for dancing, so the range and quality were not great for that. Still a pretty good product, though--just not as good as one might hope for the price.

title: excellent fit for my small ears, decent sound--great product!
review:
Contrary to some other reviews, I found these to be excellent earhook headphones! My favorite part was the fact they actually fit!! Other earhooks won't stay on my ears for more than two seconds, but these have two features that make them perfect for workouts and movement:
-rubberized earbuds that go into the ear canal (with three size options)
-a special rubber adjustment on the earhook itself. You slide the red bump on the side of the earbuds down to change the shape of the hook and lower the arc. For women, this is essential, as I am pretty sure other earhooks don't take us into account
