review: These were flimsy and broke within a week, but I can't say it is the headphones fault.  My son is rough with things and I didn't expect them to last long, which is why I only spent five bucks on them.

title: YAY!!!!
review:
So glad these are available! They don't come with directions and so I found some videos online and it was super easy to remove them with fear of damaging the headphones while doing it. They popped off with very little effort.
I was able to get the 1st replacement pad to click onto the phones without any issues though the 2nd was less cooperative. I eventually got it on but it fell off when I knocked it off of my nightstand onto the carpet - not a big fall. I had my husband try and it took him a while (and a lot off pressure) to get it to stay but it's super solid now. They're very comfortable and have the same sound quality.
I think I got one that was a little off but I still highly recommend them.

title: does exactly what you need with no issues
review: sometimes things are as simple as--does it work without screwing things up? And this is that sort of product.  It needs to connect your jack-less phone to your corded earbuds.  It fits perfectly with both, no degradation of sound quality, no lag time. Your music just plays and you don't notice.  And it's small enough that you really almost don't notice it.  Saves the old buds from being obsolete (especially if you plunked down some money for them), saves you when you forgot to charge the wireless ones. Excellent product

title: had a hard time getting them to work
review: I can't really write a fair review of these as I don't think I received a working pair. The right bud never seemed to charge in its case.  I thought I'd figured out that it wasn't being pushed down far enough to make contact and so jury-rigged something that would allow that to happen which seemed to get some sort of charge in it. But I was never able to easily pair with my iPhone, and when I could either the right one died within a few minutes or they disconnected and then wouldn't re-pair.  Best I can say therefore is a) they were comfortable  b) the few minutes of sound I had on scattered attempts sounded better than some of my earbuds but not as good as my PowerBeats 3 or Jabra Elite.

title: (Disclosure - not an audio expert) Everything sounds good but the biggest difference between this and my cheap ...
review:
A+ comfort
A+ sound. (Disclosure - not an audio expert) Everything sounds good but the biggest difference between this and my cheap wired headphones is the bass. I didn't fully appreciate how obnoxious the bass is on pop songs until I got these.

Negatives:

The sound will drop out for a fraction of a second occasionally. I expect this is because I live in an apartment building with tons of wireless signals everywhere.

The charging system is kind of awkward. You want the base to be hidden out of the way somewhere but you need it someplace handy for easy charging. But I can't think of much of a better way they could have done it.

title: Comfortable, good sound
review: I am not an audiophile but I can tell you these headphones are comfortable and sound good to me.  I bought these headphones so I could listen to music or videos late at night and be sure not to disturb my neighbors and for car rides.  For these purposes these work great.

title: Worst sounding headphones I ever bought.
review: They just sound horrible, period! No bass whatsoever, none! The midtones are flat. I had my share of cheap headphones, but, these are by far the worst sounding ones. Can't really comment on the comfort because it was painful enough to just listen to these..

title: Great headphones.  Give them a trial.
review: These headphones are the greatest and I am a music lover who needs music all the time.

title: Wow
review:
Some consider it BS, but if you have a resolving system and a decent ear, you will absolutely hear the difference between power cables. I started out as a cable nonbeliever, but I simply can't deny what I hear. I bought some of the 10 awg Chinese ones, and definitely prefer these to those. With those, everything is very in your face - detailed, but almost harsh sounding.

These on the other hand seem to open things up, and sound a lot more smooth. I would take a blind test if possible, because it's very obvious. I also confirmed with Pangea that if you're using a headphone amp, you likely will not need the increased gauge of the AC-9. Regardless, I really want the AC-14SE's after using these.

title: Excellent, highly recommended
review: Superb, wide soundstage. Ridiculously good build quality that is better than a majority of headphones. High quality, braided 3.5mm detachable cable. Sound is very refined with great clarity, a bit warm with the entire spectrum seemingly emphasized. Excellent bass that doesn't muddy up the mids. Mids are not recessed and are also excellent. Treble also sounds great, but it can be a SLIGHTLY bit sibilant/harsh if you're treble-sensitive like I am. However this isn't a problem on most songs, and if you are really concerned about it you can bring it down by 2-3 dB with EQ (10kHz region). Most people aren't going to have this problem however, and I'm pretty sure it will tame over time (I have a pair of Grados that are notorious for their piercing highs, and after 5 years of use I have zero problems with the highs. Burn in must be real to some extent.). Overall, with their solid bass, great soundstage, and a frequency response that leaves no area recessed, movies, games, and music are superbly presented. Highly recommended

title: Neutral, detailed sound - performs way above the pricepoint
review: Keep in mind I'm talking about the A151P 2ND GENERATION - they're excellent. Neutral, very detailed, amazing soundstage for monitors. Just make sure you put them in correctly, I went back and forth through all the sizes and found that I had to use the smallest. Get a deep seal and there will be just the right amount of bass. These rival some of the $200 headphones I own. I'm always thinking about upgrading my current set of headphones, but I don't feel the need to upgrade these. Only downside is the comfort with the default silicon tips when you get a good seal, but it could just that I'm over-sensitive. I might order some foam tips. Regardless, they're just great if you want detailed, neutral sound.

title: Hits all the right marks, excellent...
review:
Excellent. Bass is great and balanced, mids aren't recessed, highs are crystal clear. Sound stage is amazing. Comfort is amazing. Amp isn't required. Looks slick. What the hell else could you want?

Only "downside" is if you want to use it in public / not a closed headphone obviously. I own a 7509HD and a SR125i, the HD 598 is better than both. For $150, even $200 - this is an incredible headphone. I did a tremendous amount of research, and my search ended here. Highly recommended

title: Good for the price
review:
I like these headphones. I have a problem with ear buds in general. They either fall out of my ears or they cause too much ear pressure and I can't wear them because it's too painful.
These mostly stayed in my ears. One fell out of my ear into a sink of soapy water and still worked. Another time one fell to the ground and now the buttons are broken, but they still play.
The sound is pretty good. I mostly listen to audiobooks. No complaints.
The battery seems pretty amazing.
Overall, I know I have a hard time keeping earbuds in my ears. I'm pretty sure it's my ears. They don't cause pressure or pain.
They're cheap enough to buy again when they stop working. Which I hate to say because it's not good for the planet, but it's true.

title: Left earbud is DOA
review:
Right earbud sounds great. Too bad the left earbud doesn’t light up or work.
Quality control seems suspect.
At this price point, I expected better. Sending back for a replacement, I’ll give it one more try.

title: Nice headphones
review: They're nice headphones for a good price. I've enjoyed them and don't have any complaints. They're really good at noise cancellation.

title: Great sound, but...
review:
I was already happy with my AirPods Pro v1. They were the best earbuds I've ever owned. The Black Friday sale prompted my to try the AirPods Pro v2: Wow! They actually do sound better.

Everything looked great until I noticed the case discharging by itself at an alarming rate, as much as 5-10% per day. It looks like the built in "Find Me" feature is to blame, and it cannot be turned off. This is an issue for me because I don't use the AirPods all the time, especially in the winter. Finding dead Airpods when I do decide to use them would really upset me. So one star off.

title: Good for Travel But Bass Isn't Great
review:
These are fairly decent for this price point (you can't expect perfection for something less than $100) but when you turn up the volume, the bass is not great and actually sounds a little muffled the higher you go. However, if you like to listen to classical music and soft rock, it's fine. It works using Bluetooth and syncs up easily. The battery power is fine and the controls are easy to use. My only other quibble is the crudeness of labeling the R and L sides of the headphone in can't-miss big print, as if they're made for older people or those with vision problems. I found this detail gave the headphones a slightly tacky feeling.

I also like the fact that they fold up neatly inside the included travel case and it doesn't take up that much room in my luggage. It's something I would take on a plane or a train - good enough for a trip but I would use Bose or another high quality headphone when I'm at home listening to music.

title: Great for the Pikachu Fan
review: Though not advertised as such, these headphones are clearly inspired by Pikachu, with the black and yellow design. The sound  quality is average, but then these are meant for kids and best suited for gaming. The headphones are tight fitting but not noise cancelling. The best thing is you can plug the cord on either the left or right, so you can avoid tangling up the cord. You can also lengthen it by pulling on it, so it is adjustable. Overall these are great fun headphones for the Pikachu fan.

title: Excellent Sound Quality, Comparable to My $200 Sony Earbuds
review:
These earbuds have an interesting design - instead of the usual black, the wires look exposed because of their copper color - but this is an illusion because they're actually covered with a protective translucent rubber that feels a little slippery to the touch. The earbuds themselves remind me of pencil erasers, because they're slightly gray with copper interiors. The pair come in a zippered black and red case that has a nice mesh pocket on the inside, with an extra set of earbuds that you use to customize the fit.

The sound quality is sharp, crisp and clean. I listened to classical music as well as pop and rock, and the delicate notes came through as well as the thumping bass. To my relief, it didn't have the muffled quality of cheaper earphones and the sound is comparable to the $200 Sony earbuds I bought awhile ago. However, the included earbuds didn't fit perfectly within my ear, so after I customized them with the included set, the noise cancellation feature worked great. It effectively blocked any sounds around me that might interfere with the music.

Overall I'm very pleased with this pair of earbuds. My only question is longevity - my Sony ones lasted almost three years, so if these hold up even half as long, I would consider it a great purchase considering the price point and the sound quality you're getting.

title: Long-Lasting Headphones for Voice Recognition and Cell Phone Use
review:
I've had this headset for a few years now and they still work great. I bought them because I recently installed some voice recognition software that would translate my words into text. In addition, I've been using them as a headset for my cell phone- studies have shown that there is a danger of radiation when you hold your cell too close to your head. I've happy that this headset can be used for this purpose as well.

For the price, this headphone has lasted longer than others that cost more. If you're looking for music headphones, these aren't that good, but for the human voice it's more than sufficient

title: Pretty good for corded buds
review:
Good sound for listening to audiobooks. A little bit flat sounding when used for music. Cord is very easily organized, but as usual, my ears cannot hold on to them when I am active. I lost both my Samsung and my Beats earbuds. They leapt out of my ears, vanishing into shrubbery or diving down run-off drains. These corded buds will be more easily corraled for long term
And cost significantly less.

title: Great headset
review:
I love this headset. You can flip the boom microphone out to turn it on. My only complaint is that unique rings are not transmitted, rather the headset beeps at you to notify that you have a call. I use this all the time with my razr's navigation system in my car and it is fabulous.

Just FYI-The case often hits the side button and causes the battery to drain.

title: It could have been better
review:
I have a couple of problems with the style pack.

First, I have a minor problem with my bluetooth headset... (not Creative). I lose the connection if the player is hanging from my belt, so I want to use the clip. My clip broke after a couple of weeks. No clip - no use for the thing.

Second, the case itself is too thick. As has been mentioned in other reviews, you can't get to the on / off switch through the case. I either need to use a pen tip to dig in, or slide back the case.

I won't replace my broken clip. I'll do better with some velcro and a key chain.

title: Excellent sound quality, secure fit.
review: I have been looking for moderately priced bluetooth headphones for the gym, ones that stayed in place on the treadmill, and offered quality sound. These work so well. Secure fit--the design keeps the headphones in ear without having to constantly re-adjust. Fine sound --rich bass without mush, clear treble without that tinny sound. 3 equalizer modes that allow adjustment- and you can actually hear the difference and choose the one you most enjoy. The controls are easy to use once your fingers know where to press. The call quality through the headphones is very good. The battery life--have used for a few hours over 2-3 weeks and battery life is still "medium" (nice to be told  where the battery life stands each time you turn these on.) Okay, two side comments: they are a bit bulky due to extensive battery life and easy to use controls, but not to the point of hampering fit, and; the memory foam earpieces  did not work that well for me, and when trading them out to try the regular ones, they immediately ripped. No issue, though, cause i preferred the regular earpieces, and had a chance to order more free as well. All in all, a great purchase at a good price.

title: amazing Sound reproduction
review: Truly surprised by the range and quality of sound from these inexpensive earphones. Using them with a computer with beats audio. Clear lows, crisp highs, no distortion. Very pleased. Fit as comfortable and secure as any earbud I have used.

title: I love most everything about these
review: These stick in your ears like they were glued in and they are comfortable. The only thing I didn't like about them is the fact that if I use them with my True Wireless Earbuds the buds won't sit low enough in the charging case to allow them to charge. Perhaps a smaller size (these are the large) will work. I fear losing an earbud while working or riding my bike so the fact that these stick in my ear so well makes them a must have for me. I don't care too much about how they work with phone calls because I don't talk on my phone and the noise cancelling isn't a big deal so the fact that these fit so snugly adds to the isolation. All things considered I give these two thumbs up and I will get more.

title: Nice cable
review: My Philips Fidelio X2-HR headphones came with a nice cable and I’ve no doubt that it would double as an escape device from a second story building but I don’t need a 12’ cable. All the extra mass and weight are a PITA. So I got this 1.5M beauty, great materials and construction and I love the right angle plug. And they are nice heavy duty gold plated plugs. Being an IEM guy I’m a unapologetic “cable slut” and these check all the boxes. Braided silver/copper wire encased in a smooth flexible silicone like clear covering oh-oh-oh. Get one, hell  get two and just stare at it. You won’t be sorry.

title: Good buy, good sound, great warranty
review: I’ve been seeing reviews and recommendations from folks I trust praising these headphones and I needed a pair of lightweight beaters I could take out and about so I figured $30 wasn’t too bad a gamble. The lifetime warranty was a nice touch by Koss too. My main music listening is classic rock and jazz and my go to system is a HiBy R6 with BGVP DMG IEM’s but when I’m out doing yard work or just knocking around I listen to podcasts and audiobooks. For these tasks these are excellent headphones. The fit is a little snug but their weight makes that bearable. They are lacking a bit in the upper frequencies but do have a nice bottom end. Overall it was a good buy and I wouldn’t hesitate to buy them again or gift them to friends.

title: Compact and versatile
review: I bought this to allow me access to USB charging ports that didn’t take up those available on my laptop and were more accessible than those on a typical wall plug charger. I mounted it to the side of my desk and it works great. I can charge my phone, headphones, Garmin Edge, bike lights, etc. without crawling around on the floor.

title: Exactly what I needed
review: This is exactly what I was hoping for. Attached quickly and easily to the underside of my studio desk and holds my headphones securely while still being easy to grab. I love that there are extra cable hooks included as well. The only slight drawback is that the adhesive is so sticky that you have to be absolutely perfect first try because you will not get another chance sort of replacing the whole strip. Luckily I'm not OCD because my installation is currently angled slightly. :-)

title: My Grannie loves to be able to visit online while using a Stopmotion Explosion Pro HD 1080P Webcam with a Microphone
review: Product Includes 1 x Stopmotion Explosion Pro HD 1080P Webcam with a Microphone and 1 x Manual. The webcam works great with my Dell that has windows 10 on it. The Stopmotion Explosion Pro HD Webcam is simple to use. It is plug and play. I connected it to my laptop and it was ready to use. I needed an easy to use no fuss webcam for when my grandmother comes to visit for extended periods of time. If I am not in the room this is one she can operate herself, once I turn on my laptop and get her set up, so she can talk to her kids and other grand-kids. I do have a separate headset that volume is controlled thru a separate mic rather than the one with this camera. Some other webcams are not senior friendly, are just to far advanced and have to many things to fiddle with. For the purpose that I wanted it for it is great. Everyone is just happy to see Grannie on webcam. I received this product at a discount in exchange for a review of my honest and unbiased opinion.

title: Great sound. Easy to use, very comfortable light earphones.
review: Good quality headphones. Very good sound and bass. Very easy to pair. Connects when turned on faster than any Bluetooth headphones I have used.

title: Fine when they worked for a few months but useless warranty and non-existent customer service.
review:
After about 10 months these do not hold a charge very long. The description says there is a one year warranty and when I clicked on info I got
"Please contact the seller directly for warranty information for this product. You may also be able to find warranty information on the manufacturer’s website." I do not see a way to contact Bluedio via an Amazon link. I searched and found a poor web site with a phone number that may be in China but didn't work. No email link. I found them on Facebook and sent a message with no response. I also found them on eBay and sent a message also with no response even allowing for the time difference.

The warranty is useless and the customer service non-existent. I had bought some Nakamichi headphones on Amazon which continue to work although the headband broke.
Update: After posting this review, Bludio contacted me and offered me the T3 which I received quickly. It took a negative review to get results. Having said that, the T3s while a bit heavy and with some background noise have a battery life SO FAR that is a big multiple of the T2s even before the battery wouldn't hold the charge very long. I am upgrading my review based on the company response. I would have given them 5 stars if they responded to my messages not just to the negative review.

title: Good chat headset
review:
I had an old USB headset that was much more expensive. I didn't want to use yet another USB port or get yet another USB hub so I found this headset and based on the reviews bought it to talk via Skype, ICQ, MSN, etc. primarily with people in Russia and Estonia. It attaches to the sound card on your PC.(I did have to disconnect the speakers to attach it so it's one or the other) The first time I used it, I was surprised to find that the sound quality was as good as my internet phone which is as good as, if not better, than a land line. Subsequent conversations were less successful which may have been more a function of bandwidth and packet delivery than the Headset. It is relatively comfortable and easy to use and when I recorded a conversation on Skype, I listened to my own voice and found the quality very good insofar as I can tell how I sound.

The price is right and with Amazon's great free shipping, I bought it from Amazon where because of the free two day shipping plan I have, I buy as much as possible(no. I am not affiliated with Amazon).

title: Watch is great! Don't waste money on the package with ear buds
review:
There was a learning curve. Had to go the youtube university to figure out a couple of settings that were not addressed in the manual or app. Not a big deal, but more time consuming. Loving the watch so far. Great features and comfortable to wear. Haven't worn a watch or anything on my wrist for almost 20 years, so the comfort is a plus.

The earbuds included with the package deal are not great. The brand is Wearable4U and they constantly disconnect, randomly turn off, and sometimes unpair with the phone. Sometime one earbud with just stop working and when you touch, or tap it, the video or call you are in the middle of will stop or hang up. The sound quality is just as bad. Listening with a tin can and a string is just as comparable. I went ahead and spent the money on the Sony WF-1000XM4. Save your money on the package with the Wearable4U earbuds. You will just end up buying something different.

title: Amazing for the price, fun to listen to
review:
I make a living with my ears. I'm currently the Creative Services Director for a national radio network. In previous years, I've served as Chief Engineer for a pro recording studio that I designed and built.
Point is - sound matters to me.

The 1MORE In-Ear headphones are FANTASTIC for the value. For daily wearing (non-studio reference situations) you just can't get much better. They aren't studio cans, they won't replace monitors, but for plugging into your iPhone/iPod, you're gonna love 'em.

The overall tone is cool, not bright. That means the midrange sounds accurate and non-harsh, but not terribly warm. That's okay, I'll take cool over harsh any day.

When you first purchase them, I'd suggest letting them play for a few hours (or overnight) plugged into a sound source, so they break in a bit. I did notice an improvement afterward.

Seriously, for $100, these are great!

title: Works well with a number of headphones
review: I have used this with Sennheiser px210BT headphones, with Creative Labs bt headphones, and with Motorola s9-hd headphones with audio from my home amplifier as well as my mp3 player.  They work, and work well.

title: Hurts ears
review: I was hopeful with these since I wanted small headphones that still had good sound and mike.  The sound is great.  However, after wearing these for about two hours of Zoom meetings (separated by an hour) I find that my ears hurt. I'm female and would say my ears are normal size--not big or small. Love the concept.  But unfortunately ear pieces are just not comfortable.  Also, the over the ear pieces are fine but a bit large.  Will be returning these

title: These earphones are better than skully candy
review: These earbuds are worth the money! I use a iPod mimi and use them faithfully at the gym. they fit comfortable and never fall out while in ride the bike. sound is above average. found them on lightening deal. I bought several and glad I did.

title: So, not so funny story
review: My neighbor in the house next door got STABBED. According to the cop who interviewed us the attacker rang the doorbell, and when the guy answered the attacker forced his way inside and stabbed him. You want to know what the scary part is... I didn't hear a thing thanks to my Sony WH1000XM2 Headphones. Probably the best noise canceling headphones I've ever owned! 10 / 10 would buy again, definitely better than Bose.

title: I didn’t know I needed this  - but I did!!1
review:
We have headphones for our kids but we keep them up on the countertop in the kitchen with the iPads we let them use.
They were starting to take up a lot of space.
I got this hook on a whim and I LOVE IT!
I didn’t even consult my husband on the purchase - he LOVES it too!
It really doesn’t need to slide all the way on to hold. It’s just perfect!

title: High Quality Sound
review:
I’m very impressed with the quality of sound from these headphones!
We got theses for our 6yo - they fit her great!
They also fit me!
The pink on these are so cute!
My daughter couldn’t wait to use them.
The ear pads are very comfortable.
The noise cancelling is very good.
I actually think that the quietest volume is a little loud. It would be nice if the volume went even quieter!
It’s nice that so much can be controlled with these headphones.
If you press the on/off quickly then it pauses/plays music or hangs up/answers a phone call.
You can even hold it down for 2 seconds to talk to Siri on an Apple device.
If you press and hold the + button then it skips the current song and goes to the next one.
If you press and hold the - button then it rewinds the current song/video - this doesn’t work on all song platforms.
I LOVE that this can be used either as Bluetooth or plugged in to an audio port.
Our iPhones don’t have an old style audio port but our iPads do. When we travel our kids get a small iPad and they can use it to watch a movie while in the car or airplane - even if their headphones didn’t get charged!!
These headphones are easy to connect.

title: High quality & reliable cable.
review:
I like to take a multiple tip charging cable with me when I travel.
I charge my iPad, iPhone XR and bluetooth headphones.
This charging cable is sturdy!
The cable has a solid connection between the phone and the usb.
The cable has multiple tips that interconnect - micro, lightening and usbc.
I’ve used this cable on multiple trips and it has provided a solid charge and the charge speed is as expected.
The cable is durable and I haven’t seen any noticeable wear.
The only downside about this cable is that there is always one tip that is hanging off - all 3 tips don’t stack at the same time. The extra tip kind of gets in the way.

title: Too big even for an adult.
review:
The first thing I noticed when putting the headphones on my 6 year old son was that they were too big for him, even on the smallest size.
I put them on myself and the smallest size was slightly big for me but almost the right size. The biggest size is way to big and I’m not sure anyone could fit that size.
I’ve attached photos with my son and myself using the smallest and largest size.
The sound of the headphones is good and they are pretty comfortable.
I think that the highest volume could be too loud for a child so I will make sure that I watch how high the volume is. When the headphones are on the highest volume I can hear what the person is listening too when next to them. This makes it helpful with making sure to have them turn it down. But I would prefer that the volume wouldn’t go that loud as an option.
I’m giving these headphones a lower rating because I bought them for my children and they don’t fit them as well as I hoped.

title: Great headphones. Customize to each ear!
review:
These earbuds are everything I’ve been looking for.
I have an iPhone XS and I wanted a pair of earbuds for traveling that I could leave in my travel bag.
I currently use only bluetooth earbuds and don’t like those for travel because they aren’t ever charged enough, difficult to connect to on an airplane, etc.
These earbuds come with a case - kind of like an old time coin purse - which is easy to use and store in my bag.
My ears are strange. I have a hard time getting things to stay in there. These earbuds have multiple sizes tips and the small actually is small - so they fit!
I also like that the earbuds fins come in 3 different sizes. I’ve found that one ear fits a different fin size than another best.
I like that the earbuds are magnet - it makes putting them away and taking them out of the pouch easy.
The sounds is good and both sides of the lightening cable work - it’s frustrating when only one side works on the non apple brands.
The buttons are easy to use.

title: Quality on a budget
review: Up until recently, I have been using Sony headphones that I buy here on Amazon. I decided to give these a try, and boy am I glad that I did! These are awesome headphones that have just the right amount of base. Even my husband likes them, and he's quite picky. You can't beat them for the price! As other reviewers mention, they are perfect for everyday average listening. Music sounds great!

title: and they are good to go the next day
review: After years of replacing earphones as one channel dies, these have taken a beating on keep on ticking in each ear.  I coil the cord, drop them into pocket, and they are good to go the next day.

title: I'm impressed
review:
After I looked around a bit. It turns out that a (headphone amplifier) of any good quality, is way expensive. Ok, that is the first strike on other people. Then, those other people are not powered by the usb. I've got enough wires around my desktop, the usb powered of this little gem, was the deal maker for me.
Then the next step. I got this. And I'm already loving this on paper. Then I use it and it's nice. I just got a set of 600 ohm headphones. And a motherboard cannot drive those very good. So this little powerhouse, make the volume come back. And if I like the volume on my 600 ohm cans. Most people use 32 or 80 ohm. I have to think this is way to loud of an amp. Those people will never go full throttle.
There has to be some bad. What is it, Mike? I've been using this for about 12 hours. And I'm impressed. But then. A cracking, and a hissing. Maybe it is just on that one video, I am hoping. Nope. It's for real. So I switch out the usb wire they shipped with. For a usb 3.0 one. And yea. I know this product is only rated 2.0. But 3.0 is backward compatible. And the cracking and hissing is gone. I didn't want to lose this. And now, I won't.
So, takeaways from my experience. Save yourself the time and just buy a 3.0 wire now. I read a couple other reviews that had this problem. I never saw that anybody "fixed" their issue. I was determined. I wanted this to be true. It is great after all. A good wire is like $10 for 3 feet.

title: nice & soft & an easy change.
review:
These ear-cup were so easy to change. Take a little screwdriver, or a butter knife. And there is a ring that holds the ear cup to the headphone. pop that ring off and put it into the new ear cup. then snap it back on where it came from. It is like a 5 minute operation for both sides together.
The leather is so very soft. I was considering velvet or leather. I have had both, and this leather feels fetter. At least where I live (West Virginia). If you are in the garage in a hot environment. I guess that sweat would play into that decision. And I could not help there. But, I am glad with the decision I made. Oh, and the memory foam part. Because these are memory foam. And not just regular foam. They don't really crush down much. So my ears don't really touch the back of the ear hole as much as the last pair did. It is not perfect. But that is the earphone design fault. These are a good ear-cup.

title: These are the ones
review: I had been trying for a good set of headphones for a year when I found these.  I had been through 4 pair of headphond that cost over $100 each.  But none of them were any good.  I was able to return them all, except for the last ones, so I did not waste too much money.  I was, OK, with the Beats I had last.  For about 6 months I was satisfied.  But then they quit working altogether.  And I could not return them after so long.  That cost me $180.  So I was back to the shopping again.  But then I found these.  These make me happy.  So much that I feel every body needs to feel this awesome over head design.  So very well designed and also very well manufactured.  For anybody wanting to spend less than $1000 for a set of headphones.  These are the ones.  I think that STUDIO quality headphones are probably a different set of standards.  And 'Blue' might make a STUDIO style also.

title: This works well for me.
review:
Expected a small earphone based on reviews but was still surprised at it's tiny size when first looking at it up close.

Medium ear "hook" worked for me - suggest playing with this (removing the rubber hook and adjusting it on the ear piece) until getting right fit - the bud goes in ear and added loop of rubber is supposed to counter against the curve in another part of your outer ear - genius design imho and when this thing is in, even jumping up and down or shaking your head or tapping your head (yes tried that too, silly I know...) will not dislodge this.

Paired easily with a samsung ach930, sound is great and the other side of the call is also impressed, no complaints of echo or static.
Have a plantronics 510 which is good, this wep200 is smaller yet compares in quality to the plantronics.

title: Didn't work after 4 months of use
review: After 4 months of careful use, only one speaker works. Apparently the connection of the cord to the headset is flimsy and there was static from day one. But now only one speaker works and that is very irritating.

title: Works Great -
review: This little amp is just what I wanted for my headphones when I do the treadmill. The sound quality is fine. It plugs in so there is no nuisance with changing batteries. Basically, it's perfect.

title: Very nice headphones w/convenient travelling case
review: These headphones work very well, are about 1/3 of the price of the Bose, and come in a very convenient travelling case.  Independent reviews indicate the Bose headphones do a better job of noise cancellation and I do notice that it doesn't always block out a loud TV, for instance.  I have no regrets on the purchase though and am very satisfied that I am getting my money's worth from them.

title: Pads on my MDR-7506 were shot...
review: Fit great, made my headphones new again. I had been thinking of getting new ones but this is way better.

title: Old headset becomes new again...
review:
These were the first wireless headphones I ever purchased. Although I bought them via Amazon, they're not coming up in my old orders - no surprise, I suppose, considering it was sometime in 2009 or 2010. The reason I'm reviewing them now is because I recently needed to use them when a cheap pair of Kotion wireless headsets died on me and my old ASUS was waiting in a drawer to try them out again. When I first got them, they were nothing but trouble. Wouldn't connect reliably, wouldn't hold a charge.

Strangely, almost 10 years later, after I charged them briefly and plugged the dongle in... they work great! Sound good, holding a charge, connecting easily to my PC for use. I'm guessing that wireless drivers have come a long way in the intervenining years, as there's no problem in using them with my PC now. The only problem is that the foam they used in the earpads completely disintegrated, but those are easily enough replaced with spare foam pads available here on Amazon (I've ordered the "Zotech 4 Pairs 2.5'' (60mm) Foam Pad Ear Cover for Philips Sony Headphones" which I believe will fit fine).

All in all, they've become my backup wireless headphones. Not bad for a 9 year old wireless device that's been sitting my in drawer doing nothing!

title: These are awful earbuds.
review: I purchased these earbuds at a store -  luckily for only $4.99, so at least I didn't waste more money than that. They are the worst sounding earbuds I've had the mispleasure to use.

title: A great gift!
review:
I got this wonderful little player/recorder for Christmas this year, and have had a great time with it since.
Pros: The sound quality is great! The size is nice. It's easy to get files on and off the device using the software (note: go to the PoGo webpage for updated software). The fact that I can plug it in to anything that has an earphone jack and directly record MP3s is wonderful - I have a lot of cassettes that need to be digitally recorded, and this is the first time that it hasn't looked like an impossible task.
Cons: It was a bit difficult to get the software and drivers to install (I'm using Win 2000), and the manual was obviously written by people who didn't have English as a primary language.
Summary: I love it! Once past the installation difficulties, it's well-worth having and I'll be happily using it for a long time. :)

title: Yay!
review: These headphones are amazing! I have trouble finding earphones that will work with my ancient iPod so I was very pleased that these worked out. I listen to a lot of my music in bed and sometimes fall asleep listening to music. These are SO comfortable and cords don't tangle . Very happy with purchase.

title: Amazing for the cost
review: OK, these are NOT high end headphones, but for the $10 I paid they sound great. Comfortable to wear. Cord is the right length. If I lose them or trash the plug on an airplane seat (OK, this is my second pair) I've lost next to nothing and I still have really good sound for average use.

title: Amazing for the cost
review: Just got these as throw-away headphones and I'm surprised at how good the sound is. Now to see how long they last...

title: Comfortable and Durable
review: I bought 3 pairs for my young boys and wife to use.  My boys are not gentle with them (nor is my wife).  They so far have lasted a solid month with no problems and not breaking.  For an adult, they are "good" over-the-ear headphones.  They are comfortable and do their job.  They certainly are not to be compared to something in the $50+ price range, but for my boys they are awesome and lasted.  I previously purchased 2 pairs of $6.99 headphones off Amazon and was disappointed because they hardly lasted a week - they were garbage.  I had low expectations for these since they were only $3 more, but these have exceeded my expectations.

title: Don't be a cheapskate like I was - buy something else - all the negative reviews are true
review: Bought qty 2 for my children.  The headphones were not abused and taken care of.  One of the two sets of headphones simply stopped working while they were being used on day #6.

title: Just what I needed
review: This is a nice looking sturdy case to carry my earbuds in. I hook it to my work bag and off I go. I always know where my earbuds are and they are very well protected. Nice little case for the money.

title: Four Stars
review: These are really nice headphones for the money. The sound is quite nice, seriously. Easy to use and stay charged for a long time. They are comfortable to wear. I am happy with these. No complaints at all. I'm a satisfied customer.

title: Only thing the speaker is poor so replaced it with the Koss KSC75 speakers and ...
review: Just what I was looking for. The headband that is. I wanted lightweight durable headset. Something I would barely notice sitting on my head. This fits the purpose marvelously. Only thing the phones are poor so replaced it with the Koss KSC75 phones and now I have some marvelous lightweight great sounding headphones. I'm amazed nobody has made a better set of these lightweight babies. Too bad you have to buy two different sets to make one good one.

title: Great replacement eartips
review:
Received 2 pairs each (small, medium, large) replacement earbuds.
This works exactly the same as the OEM and really cannot tell the different in physical appearance between the two. The comfort is the same too. Great product at a low replacement cost!

title: Five Stars
review: great solid case with great soft protection. headphone wire does not fit due to design.

title: great price and quality sound comparable to $100 headphones
review:
these meet my minimum quality expectations for headphones that should cost over $100 judging by the sound.
great quality headphones! great price and value. better than my other ausdom m04 and m05 headphones.

title: great sounding
review:
these headphones are comparable to headphones costing 100 to 300 range.
they last over 22 plus hours of usage.
amazing value! sounds better and cost less than my other value ausdom m04 and m05 headphones

title: Well made!
review:
This review is for the Adaptor 45. It seems to be a very well made backpack. I was able to fit in three Canon 4-5 inch long lenses, the Canon DSLR camera body and a GoPro with charger in the main lower storage area. There was some space remaining which I used for headphones and other misc equipment. In the top storage area I fit in a headlight, two compact led flashlights, a half dozen camera batteries, charging cables, memory cards, two iPhone waterproof cases and more chargers. With all this gear the bag came to 9.4 pounds.
I adjusted the straps and walked around for 30 minutes. The bag was comfortable on my 6’1” frame. It stands upright on its own when placed on the floor. It qualifies for under seat placement on average sized or large jet aircraft.
I am happy with my purchase. Will do a follow up after I put it through it’s paces on an upcoming three week 6,500 mile multi-country photo safari.
Followup: This pack worked great! Cameras and lenses safe and secure. Even when dropped by porters and bus drivers a couple of times. My weight with gear was 9 pounds which made wearing easy. I strongly recommend this camera backpack!!

title: Despite much abuse, lasted for years
review: I am notorious for destroying headphones. I think they last me an average of 3 months before I have to replace them, regardless of quality. I thought these ones were done for when I dropped one of the earbuds in an old cup noodle, yet they still functioned perfectly. Later, I thought they must be dead after I dropped one of the earbuds in coffee and failed to notice for 5-10 minutes. They remained perfectly functional, somehow. Finally, I dropped my phone while they were plugged in, straight down onto the earphone jack and bent it. They still worked! They finally gave out months later after being violently pulled from my phone by a large dog. As you can see from the photo, the earphone jack came loose from the attachment. In the 2 1/2 years that I tortured these headphones, the sound quality never suffered. RIP. Best headphones I have ever owned. I am buying another pair.

title: Decent sound, great price!
review:
I purchased this for my teenage daughter after her stock apple earbuds broke. I compared these buds with a Klipsch S5i which I have been using for the past 3 years - a great sounding set that I had purchased for $100+.
The good news is that the Pansonics sound great - a wee bit muddier, and lower dynamic range, but these are the best sounding earbuds I seen for under 30 bucks. Way better than the crappy throwaway sets you typically find at gyms, grocery stores or the discount bin at the Big Box store. In fact, I would say they sound about 80% as good as the Klipsches - and a tenth of the price!
Let's see how long they last. If they last 6 months with my daughter, I will bump this to a 5!

title: Great sound and fit
review:
I had the older black and white version for a couple of years - which unfortunately found its way to a washing machine, and came out ripped. This one feels fairly similar, so I not sure if there really is much of difference, other than styling details.

I really like the Bose bearbud design - the 'slightly loose' fit is in my opinion a super-feature if you use your phone for telephone calls. The really snug fiitting ones (e.g. Klipsch) work great for music, but make it hard to hear yourself on phone calls (Leading to you speaking louder than necessary)

One issue I have is that this earbud comes with a monstrous amount of packaging, as well as a storage case which is really not needed. And a fairly thick user manual - really? I would rather have Bose eliminate the extra cord, case, fancy packaging & manual, and reduce the price by 30 bucks or so.

The only other gripe is that the cord gets tangled fairly easily. Other than these 2 minor issues, this is a great sounding unit.

title: Good,  not great
review:
I needed a quality headset at work, and at the gym. I have been using the $ 10 Sony 'over the ear' clips - these are cheap, better than apple's default buds, but the sound quality leaves a bit to be desired. I also needed something with a microphone for the occasional call.

First, the good - these Klipsh do appear to have great build quality, are very comfortable, and provide great sound isolation. (I had comfort issues in the past with a $200 Shure 'in-ear' set that I enjoyed listening to, until they unfortunately found their way into the washing machine).

However, the sound is just marginally better than the $10 Sony. Also, they are a pain to use in the gym, especially if you are on a treadmill. While they do a great job of cutting out he ambient noise, there is the constant 'thump thump' of your movement being transmitted back to your ear.

Update: My wife purchased the Bose Mie2i a few days ago. Although a bit more expensive than the Klipsh, these sound much much better (especially vocals), although they do not have the sound isolation of the Klipsh.

Bottom line: These Klipsh sets are good, but not worth the price premium. (If I were to do this again, I would go with the Bose)

Waiting for someone to now combine the best of these 2 headsets!

title: The best bluetooth headphones out there
review: This is my 2nd pair of LG bluetooth headphones. I bought these as a refurb and they work perfectly. I love the retractable chord for the earplugs. Quality product, def spend the money for a solid pair like this as opposed to the cheap knockoffs I bought on here for $15 that broke in a week.

title: Fabulous, except one small fixable problem
review:
These headphones worked perfectly out of the box. After their initial 1-day battery charge, I plugged them into the TV, turned them on, and was blown away by their quality. Great sound reproduction and lightweight. I can hear them in any room in my apartment. I can even stand out on the deck, close the door, and still hear them perfectly without any hiss. Easy to recharge becaue they just lay across the top of the charger cradle.

My only complaint: they fall forward if you tip your head down for an extended time. This didn't affect my 5-star rating, though. I just attached an eyeglasses strap (crokie) around each side. I place the strap around the back of my head, and cinch it up when I need to. Then I can cook or whatever without them falling into the frying pan. Not too ugly because my hair covers it up. Great headphones at a good price. Amazon delivered them quickly, too.

title: Great product
review: I bought these headphones for my 12-year-old daughter who loves to listen to music. They were super easy to pair with her phone. Battery life seems good so far. The sound quality is great. She is very pleased with them. I love that they are open-ear headphones so that she can actually hear me when I call her. She can still enjoy her music while not being taken out of the environment and oblivious to everything that is going on around her. Plus, a bonus is that they are pink, her favorite color!

title: It still works great. I give it heavy use as a telecommuter
review: I bought this headset in August, 2012.  It still works great.  I give it heavy use as a telecommuter.  It's comfortable for multi-hour use such as 5 or 6 hours at a time.  Lightweight.  My voice quality is great on the other end.  I have received a few compliments and inquiries about what I'm using.  I'm happy with this product.  It works well.  And the price is amazing for what it delivers.

title: Five Stars
review: These headphones are extremely comfortable and they sound great! Also you can't beat the price.

title: Great sound. Be sure to use the correct size ...
review: Great sound. Be sure to use the correct size tips for your ears. If you do not, these In-Ear Headphones will sound absolutely awful. I actually initiated a return to Amazon for this item. Before taking them to UPS I decided to check the reviews where I found info on the correct sizing procedure. The difference in sound quality was like night and day.

title: Sound = Good.  Stability in ear = Good.  Battery Life = Fair-
review: The earbuds only show 90% charged when I connect to my phone, even though they show fully charged on the case.  I had them on today for 3 hours and they registered 40% remaining charge.  The earbuds that don't have the extension (similar to Apple Airbuds) just don't stay in my ear, no matter what I do.  These stay in my ear at least.

title: It's Sennheiser..........Need I Say More
review: When I realized that I needed a second set of headphones so I could listen to my vinyl, without bothering anyone else in the house, I looked at Sennheiser first. I had just sold my long time  Sennheiser HD-600 and I missed that laid back sound.

title: Great way to display my headphones
review: I used to keep my headphones in my audio/video closet until I needed them, but no more. The less I have to carry these around, is a better chance I don't step on the cord.

title: These are some very nice headphones. When I look for earphones I always ...
review:
These are some very nice headphones. When I look for earphones I always look at the cord if it is not twisted or braided I know they are not going to hold up to my roughness while using these. These are a rubber based cord that is twisted. Just what I prefer. These cords do not tangle and this cord seems to be very durable.
The earphones fit my ears nicely and I love the slim design and it helps the weight in my ear so they do not slip out.
The sound coming out of these earphones are great, they do not crackle and the sound is of excellent quality. I like that they come with extra ear pieces so those with smaller ear canals can adjust the ear piece accordingly. I like the velvet carry case this comes with.
Overall I am very happy with these headphones They have met my needs and exceeded them.
I received these headphones for free for testing and reviewing purposes. This is my honest unbiased opinion and have come to it by wearing the headphones myself.

title: This is a great set of headphones
review:
This is a great set of headphones, They fold up for easy storage and packing. The sound is great, clear, crisp and has quite a bit of bass. love the braided cord. They last longer than the rubber cords. Great padding on the ear pieces, Was able to wear for some time and my ears never got sore, Just hot. These are easy to adjust just pull on the ear piece and they extend for larger heads or push back in for smaller heads. These were able to fit my head and also my daughters head. Great headphones, I have nothing negative to say about these headphones.
I received these headphones at a discount for testing and reviewing purposes. This is my honest unbiased opinion and have come to it by using the headphones myself.

title: My kid loved this headset
review:
My kid loved this headset, it fit his head nicely and on his ears was padded but also helped cancel noise, worked well with all devices, we have not had any issues out of it at all. Very heavy and you can tell the material is better quality than most. Sound is amazing with all devices, Fast shipping and product came very seccure in the package to ensure no damage to it or other things.
I received a discount to write my honest and unbiased opinion

title: WOW
review: Very great buy for the buck. My wife has the Apple Earbuds. I see no sound quality deafferents.

title: Do Not Compare
review: Hard to rate this headset. For the $30 ....yes, they are 4 or 5 stars. My problem is that one of the ear pads fell off my $300 Bose headset. I was mad, so I purchased these. When I put them on, all I could say was OMG. The sound quality was so terrible. My advice do not compare them. You will be very disappointed. But remember for the price they are five stars.

title: Good sound, good noise cancelling. Terrible Bluetooth Connection
review:
I got it on prime day deal, was very happy about the value. Sound was good, noise cancelling was good. In NYC subway platform, I only need 50% volume, and hear clearly, as opposed to previous small earplug headphones, I crank it up to 100%, still would miss things.
BUT the Bluetooth connection is TERRIBLE in the subway. As the train moves, I could lose connection 5 times on average in a normal an hour train ride. I guess it's because of interference? But I never had this issue with any other bluetooth headsets.

title: As my buddy used to say, "Nearly perfect..."
review:
I was originally looking for noise cancelling headphones. What I didn't realize is that "CVC 6.0 Noise Cancellation for Hands-Free Call" meant noise cancelling only for phone calls. Otherwise, these are solid, comfortable headphones that block most outside sound and sound pretty darned good. I kept them for home use, and my kids pair them with their phones and Chromebooks and am going to have to get a 2nd pair to keep them happy! My workplace requires noise-cancelling headsets or earplugs so, I had to get something different. But, overall, these are super nice!

Tribit, make these a full-on noise-cancelling headset, and they'd be perfect! :-)

title: Expect what you paid for and you will not be disappointed.
review: If you have $200 headphones in mind, these are not the product for you, but if you want wallet friendly headphones that work and are prepared for $20 materials, you will be quite happy with these.  The other reviews are pretty spot on.  These headphones have good sound, work as advertised, and super inexpensive.  They're leaky, but that's actually a plus for me because I need some environmental awareness in a busy home, even during headphones time.  They feel like they cost $20, though, so don't drop them.

title: DO NOT BUY!!!  They Lie!!! Very Dishonest Company
review:
Update: 5/2021-
Still no Onemesh firmware as promised. They listed this product as "planned" then removed it. Has a known bug with slowdown and has to be rebooted a couple times a week but has never been fixed. I wish I had returned it.

I bought a AX1500 OneMesh extender and a AX1500 router from TP-Link and figured they would work together....Well, NO!!! After talking to tp-link (Took almost 2 hours getting kicked out of the queue twice) they could not tell me when if ever this router would get OneMesh. I returned this router and got a AX1800/AX20. It is planned to support OneMesh.

I also had problems with my Oculus Quest 2 stuttering. Some folks say the AX20 is better with a stronger processor.

To Recap: Bad customer Service/Support. Problems with VR Headset.

UPDATE: Received my AX20 in 8 days Even with Prime...Bad Amazon. It got lost in Il somewhere.
The AX20 v2 does not have OneMesh...Yet but they claim it is coming soon. TP-Link has till mid January then the router and Onemesh extender is going back.

title: Good for my podcasts
review:
Having lost an expensive Jabra ear pod this was just what I was looking for. I use them for listening to podcasts when out walking. They stay in the ear, can not get lost (being tied together) and reproduce the mid-range of voices very well. The battery lasts a long time and I charge it once a week. (if the charge gets low, it has a bell like tone that annoyingly repeats every minute). It can do music but the sound quality is nothing like the Jabra that cost five times a much.
Update July 2022. After 2 1/2 years I had to dispose of headphones. Although they were working the same as always, a little tab used to lift up the cover on the charging port broke off and I was unable to pry off the cover.

title: Disappointing quality.
review: I purchased this product to connect headphones to a TV. The sound from one ear was great. In the other ear the  sound was muted and of poor quality. Unplugging and replugging multiple times did not improve the sound. I ended up going to the local guitar store, paying $12.99 for a connector that worked flawlessly. This set of connectors went directly into the trash where they belong. Sorry but just not worth the money.

title: Works great with Bose
review: I purchased this as a replacement for Bose headphones. The cable works fantastic. Get it!

title: These work great, I like them. A good investment.
review:
These work fine for me. I have not had any problems with them yet. Usually, electronics that are cheap in cost are cheap in quality too, but these are holding their own. The only problem I've found is that if you plug them in with the included cable, that one side tends not to have sound. You have to fidget with it to get the sound to come out of both sides. If you are using the bluetooth connection, then you won't have that problem.

I'm not really a fan of the blue color, but that's just personal preference. Apparently they are the royal blue color, but to me it's just flat and dull. I like the deeper, cosmic blue color... (not quite midnight blue or navy blue, a little bit lighter than that)... which I thought was royal blue, but I guess I was wrong. I have a royal blue colored Apple Watch Band that I like, but when I put it next to the headphones, they are the exact same shade of blue. I like the way the band looks, but not the way the headphones look. Just thought I would point that out incase color is important to you.

title: I have no complaints about this product
review: I've been using it for about 2 months now, and it works pretty good. I like it. My old headset had a hum on the line that the headset people (of that particular headset's website) and the phone company couldn't figure out what was wrong. Then someone turned me on to headsets dot com and I got this product. The hum is no longer there, but I would advise getting a really good phone to use with this, because the cheaper phones (I'm using a $20.00 phone currently) aren't completely compatible with this headset. It's hard for people on the other line to hear me sometimes -- true, it could be do to a bad connection or whatever, but I think it's because of a cheap, crappy phone.

title: Works as expected
review: Great replacement for original cord of Bose headphones that frayed.  Seems as if it should hold up well.  Easy to connect and disconnect.  No apparent loss of sound quality.  Good length

title: Cute color, great for daith piercing
review: Great setup and sound quality.  I have an inner ear piercing so I don't like earbuds that rely solely on staying in from pressure, it hurts. The ear hooks are great.

title: I wrap mine and they unravel as easily as the OEM cables
review: I have find them to be very open & transparent through my Onkyo DP-S1.  A huge improvement from the two cables that come with it.  While tangles seem to be an issue here I feel that comes with the cable being that much thinner and nothing specific to the cable itself.  Just need to take care to wrap prior to stuffing in a pocket or loose.  I wrap mine and they unravel as easily as the OEM cables.  I also had concerns about fragility connector & attaching to the cable but I have seen videos on the Linum site showing the connectors being pulled loose from the headphone by the cables only.  Not going to try it but it is there for the viewing.  Overall I hope they continue with the top end Linum BAX cables and let's see/hear how much detail & music is really there in the player hiding in lessor cables.

title: Audio quality poor, no mid on high range.
review: Sound Quality Poor Disappointed there is no mid range or high range low only also the microphone is too close to the headset and causes an echo when you use it for a telephone call. Suggest you make another selection.  Consult a specialist before purchasing tech gear.

title: Make sure your lady friend has big ear holes. (You too, ladies.)
review:
Might be wonderful, but I’ll never know. Earbud tips are way too big to fit my ears, and according to Grado, these are the only ones they’ve got. It means that even if you can mash the eartips into your ears, they deform over the speakers and muffle the sound (and hurt your ears). Disappointed in the purchase and also in Grado, whose headphones and cartridges I’ve been buying for decades. When I wrote to complain, I got...well, I got a response that women working in male-dominated industries are familiar with. Defensiveness, mostly. Nobody’s complained before, much respect for women in the family, you can’t please everyone. I believe he genuinely meant well and was surprised and confused by the criticism, but that doesn’t change the fact that if you’re a woman, these phones are less likely to work for you than if you’re a man.

Am I annoyed? Sure. Same as I am when techbros make their products for themselves, essentially, because their default human is a man their size, and when medicine’s made for 180-lb 25-year-old men, and when women who’ve done the work to become astronauts can’t manage to do a spacewalk because the male engineers kind of didn’t figure on women’s being up in space and didn’t make enough space suits to fit women.

Not recommended as a gift for a lot of people, unfortunately. I hope Grado rethinks tip design and also market approach. Meanwhile, I’ll be returning these.

title: These work great for Kindle Paperwhite!
review: Old type stylus models with black rubber tip just don't work on the Paperwhite screen.  Boxwave has figured it out and this stylus is superior!  My wife uses it on her Paperwhite Kindle and I use mine on an older Kindle Touch.  In both cases the sensitivity and resolution is far better than anything we have experienced before with a stylus.  Buy this and you won't  be disappointed.  Well worth the money.  I also like the feature that allows you to plug the retaining cord into the earphone output on the Kindle Touch.  Not likely to lose it.  Boxwave also was very responsive to a pre-sales question regarding suitability.  I will find other things to purchase from the.  A good company.

title: Poor Quality/Decent Sound
review: I have gone through three pairs of these earbuds in a little over 8 months. I bought two pair because the price was right and some folks had very good things to say about them. My initial impression was very favorable. After about 40-50 hours of use, the first pair went down. One earbud stopped working. Though I was beyond the usual warranty period for Amazon, they replaced them. The second pair experienced the same problem, and now my replacement pair has died the same way. I can sometimes get the dead earbud to work by tapping it. Either I am really, really unlucky - three deaths in 8 months - or else the quality of these buds is very poor. I'm going with the latter. If you purchase these, send in your warranty right away. You may need it in no time at all. They were very disappointing.

title: Switch and breathability Issues
review:
I'm on my second pair of these. The sound and noise cancellation is fantastic, although you can hear a white noise hiss when all is quiet.
There are two problems with this headset. The first is that the on/off switch is cheap. It broke on my first pair, and now the second pair is ready to break as well. The second problem is how hot your ears get wearing them. My ears are practically sweating and I have to hold them open to get fresh air under the cups. I'm sure it's because they need a seal to do the noise cancellation so well. But it means they are not comfortable for wearing over an hour.

title: Bohm Wireless Headphones
review: I find that the sound quality is excellent and the operation of these headphones to be reasonably well organized. I am quite satisfied with these headphones.

title: ear buds will not stay in my ears
review: I've tried 3 different sizes of earbuds and none stay in my ears very well.  When I do get them in they are not comfortable.  Will not be using very often.

title: Likeable except for sound
review: The name suggests it’s from Japan; not so, made in China.  IMO, the quality falls short of expectations despite being a very user friendly unit with good features.  HDMI allows for an easy connect to homeTV, not generally found on most DVD players.  Cable not included.  At this price the sound is too tinny.  Maybe earbuds improves it?  I would recommend it if you don’t mind average, e.g. Chevrolet quality but if you want Japanese or BMW fit and finish level look elsewhere.

title: Worth the Price?
review:
I tried low end earbuds ~$40 and I wasn’t happy with the muffled sound. However, the thought paying $200+ for earbuds too much. So, I bought Creative’s mid range units at $80. I’ve kept these as they were a big improvement over the cheap ones. They are hard to connect to my iPads and I didn’t think I was hearing all the jazz I was listening to.

I finally gave in after reading all the rave reviews of Apples top AirPods. Well, they’re great, by a large factor. I can hear the umph in the music as well as background brush strokes on the symbols. I still wonder about Apple’s other, mid-level units which got high reviews...?

However, these connect effortlessly to any Apple device they’re next to, AND without reading a manual. Further, the controls are minimal and you learn them automatically, on screen when you first connect. Overall, I like them well enough to keep even though I cringe at the price of these little used accessories =&

title: Surprisingly bad with a twist
review:
I don't know what to think of these headphones. The sound out of the box is terrible, just abysmal. I've never heard a more unbalanced headphone anywhere. If you can't use an eq with these headphones, stop reading and look elsewhere.

If you can use an eq in your application, you might find these headphones surprising. Once the shrill high-end is toned down and the bass and mids bumped up, you will find the sound is pretty good for a ~$60/pair. The soundstage is small, but clear and the instrument separation surpasses what I was expecting. However, boost the bass too much and you will get distortion.

A couple of weeks before buying these I heard the quad-driver version and they were simply amazing. It was like I was sitting in my own living room listening to a full surround sound setup. I've never heard spacial definition or as big a soundstage in a headphone as I did with the quad-drivers, especially IEMs. The quad-drivers are on par with $600/pair HiFiMan planars. That's why I took a chance on this much cheaper bluetooth version of a single driver.

If you don't mind playing with the eq and don't want to buy cheap knock-offs from china (these are made in china, but by the company that designed them), take a chance on these. If you just want to plug and play, buy something else. I'm still on the fence on returning them myself.

title: Great for blocking out sound and keeping the ear buds ...
review: Great for blocking out sound and keeping the ear buds in, for me this is the only earbuds to buy.

title: but I ended up throwing them out and buying something better. The material is thin
review: They work, but I ended up throwing them out and buying something better. The material is thin, unlike the image, and probably seems like other headphones I had that would flake bits off over time. Also what you can see in the image is there is no o-ring of cushion on the back. The little ring of foam you can find on the OEM or other 3rd party pads helps your ear from touching the hard plastic inside the cup (the thin material doesn't do anything for comfort). If you look in the image You'll see a new pair of OEM, the old pair I'm replacing (they were still good, but they were a bit flat, which ended up with a lot more of my ear in contact with the headphones) and these pair of Tinksky, which you can see the material is a lot thinner and the cup is smaller. And in the 2nd image you'll see how it lacks the padding on the backside that keeps your ear off the hard plastic. Some people may not care about it lacking these parts. But I wear them for 6 to 12 hours a day, so it's very important to me.

title: Awesome! everyone needs one of these
review: Awesome! everyone needs one of these. It puts my headphones right where I want it and it hasn't fallen off for 6 months. Great product!

title: They Work Well
review:
I bought these headphones for a few reasons:

1. I do not need or want expensive headphones for running or working out in. I am hard on my stuff and they just get thrown in my gym bag, the center console of my truck or the counter in the kitchen, when I am done lifting or running. At $40, they are not too expensive.

2. I wanted JVC again, because the last pair of JVC BT headphones I had lasted for a long time and they sound decent. If I want to put headphones on listen for sound quality or noise canceling, I have much more expensive over the ear headphones for that.

3. I wanted this style of BT headphones because for me, they fit better and stay put better than earbuds. I have tried several different types of earbuds and they do not stay in my ears as snugly as these do, which makes me uncomfortable, particularly when I am running. These stay put and feel more comfortable to me.

The cost is good, the sound quality is good, the fit is good and the battery life is good. To me these are 5 star set of $40 BT headphones.

title: Great Price!
review: My grandchildren go through ear buds. Finding a cheap but good quality earbud hasn't been easy. These are good ones for a great price!

title: A good backup set of headphones
review: These aren't anywhere near the higher-quality headphones I have, but they aren't too bad for this price point. The case is an awesome plus, especially because I think these are good to keep as a backup pair of headphones just in case or when you want a fairly good sound quality without worrying so much about losing your better-quality headphones.

title: Not convenient
review: Not convenient. I use my head phones for work so I put them on and take off probably 60-80 times a day. With this design, each time I remove my headphones, It takes a little time to get the headphones on. If I ordered a regular stand, I would quickly hook the headphones on the stand and be done. If you use your headphones occasionally, this will not be a problem.

title: Just right
review:
Perfect pieces for the headphone I currently have.
Works great
Thank you

title: Disappointed.
review: At first these rocked! Then suddenly the buttons on the cups would not work. They turned into dumb bluetooth headphones. After about an hour of wear the top of my head would start hurting. The noise canceling is ok - works best when music is fairly loud. Sound quality is great. Doesn't do highs too well, bass was excellent. All in all, I ended up returning these. I am looking for something just a bit more... perfected.

title: Folds for book reading!
review:
This is the only case I could find that lets me stand my kindle in portrait position to read a book! It doesn't make sense why other case makers would make Kindle cases to stand only in a horizontal viewing position.

The only think I find wrong with it, is it needs an elastic band or velcro strap to hold some earbuds.

I have had the navy leather look case and didn't care for it so I bought the light blue one that looks and feels a little like denim. I like both the looks and feel of it.

title: Good voice quality, bad design
review: For the price this is a great little headset with good voice quality on both ends.  The negative is that it won't stay in the ear and the ear hook is too flimsy to do any good with hanging it on the ear.

title: Good size, good sound
review: These work great for my sensitive 9 year old who doesn't like her whole ear covered, but can't handle earbuds. These fit softly over the ears, but don't wrap around the whole ear.

title: Needed quick quality with little fuss and got a lot more for my money.
review:
I certainly didn't expect anything of audiophile quality or anything astounding. Knowing how much I'm spending is the context for the review.

It's a good pair of headphones.

They're lightweight, comfortable, the earpads stay reasonably cool, the cord is just long enough to listen to at a desk (and that's a good thing), and they sound awfully good for what I paid. They also look pretty okay. The fact that they fold flat is a nice little bonus but for a pair of utility headphones, I think these are a home run.

So as a sound engineer and a musician I would put it this way. They're not high fidelity headphones, nor do they work for performance. They won't work for reference/studio work at all. They're too flimsy to call a solid pair, but for casually listening to music while multi-tasking at home or for watching a streaming video, these do just great. I think there are a number of good headphones like this one you can get for less than $20 or so. This one is up there and I would buy it again if I needed another.

title: Yes yes and yes, they're perfect.
review:
So this is what I experience everyday. The bluetooth connection is fast and solid. The sound clarity and mic clarity are excellent. The battery life I'd say is fairly average but also as advertised. Once you get used to the buttons this headset is very easy to operate and the earpieces are comfortable for hours. The on/off sound+vibrate are cool sounding and the headset tells you the battery level when you either power up or hit a volume button. You can also switch between Active Noise Reduction On, Active Noise Reduction Off, and Passthrough modes all of which are useful in different situations.

Whereas I normally use a $300 pair of active noise reducing on ear headphones for travel, I took these to London and Paris and they were flawless on every flight. There are cheaper options out there but get these!

title: Quality Studio Headphones
review:
These are studio-quality headphones. They aren’t meant to be the typical Bose-style noise cancelling headphones. Not are they for reaching super-bass low end tones.

They are high quality full-range studio headphones.

title: Perfect size!!
review: We travel every week and need so much cords including phone chargers, iPad chargers, car plug in cords and so much more. It also holds our headphones and battery packs all in 1 place. We know we have everything we need each time we travel having this organizer. It’s also very durable and heavy duty. Absolutely love it!!

title: These are every bit as good as the Beats headphones we were given with our ...
review: These are every bit as good as the Beats headphones we were given with our new phones. They work as ear plugs too. Once they're in I can't really hear anything else.

title: Great gift item for my 8 yr old boy. Easy to setup and operate.
review: This was a gift for my 8 year old. He has been asking for an mp3 player and this was a great choice. It comes with a decent battery charge out of the box and the setup was a breeze. We got it connected to the Bluetooth headphones and added songs to it right away. The time it took most to get it playing was the adding of the songs. Very user friendly and the touch response is fast. It fits his hand well, too (see photos). He is very happy and the clip was an added bonus. He loves to ride his bike and have it with him. We are kow getting ready to order an SD card to add memory to the device.

title: Great value
review: For the price i would say these are basically unbeatable.  Good sound quality, great bass response, and very comfortable.  To clarify, some reviewers said the volume control on the headphones doesn’t control the phone volumes and works independently, that is incorrect.  The headphone volume does control the master volume on the phone.

title: Don't hold a charge, keep disconnecting, fairly uncomfortable
review: I received these as a gift, and at first I thought these headphones were great- they connected to my computer right away, no hassle, sound quality was great. They seemed fairly uncomfortable but came with many different sized silicone earpieces which helped a bit. Less than a month later, half the time they don't hold their charge more than half and hour, sound has become muffled, they are still falling out of my ears, and they repeatedly disconnect from my computer. Not sure if they broke or if they all degrade this quickly.

title: Stopped working after 3 weeks
review: To start with, only one of the headphone inputs worked, and that one diesd after just 3 weeks of use. Big waste of time and money.

title: The Apex of Affordable and Quality
review: I got these during a Prime Day sale event for about 14$(usually they’re 20$). They are Apple quality wired so, naturally the sound is great and devoid of bluetooth-related losses. They are great and at least last like a year before you might consider replacing them. There’s better out there, but these don’t leave to much for one to desire for wired earbuds(unless maybe, if your not a IPhone user).

title: One Month in and design reminds me of Apple!
review: It’s rating sees to support about 20-25w fast charging. For me, that’s just enough for my Switch, headphones, and Iphone. It’s probably not gonna cut for like a Macbook but I caught this on sale anyways lol! It’s definitely more robust than Five Below’s options so, for a dollar or two more it’s definitely worth it. Can’t speak on quality control though, maybe I got lucky?

title: fantastic for transcribers
review:
Bought this for transcribing audio interviews with a lot of background noise and I wanted headphones that wouldn't alter the sound and helped with clarity. I'm really impressed with how much these headphones helped me understand each word spoken in the recordings. They're also very comfortable to wear and sort of seal your ear.
This morning also plugged them into my iPhone to get better sound during a phone conference (iPhones tend to have terrible sound for phone conferencing) and they were so awesome. Could hear everything so clearly and with half the volume!
