title: A great replacement for my old Plantronics Voyager Legend
review:
My old Plantronics Voyager Legend finally bit the dust and I started looking for a replacement. After reading all the reviews and talking to a number of my tech smart friends I decided to try the newer Voyager 5200 model.

The new model is just as comfortable as the one it replaced. Controls, especially the volume up & volume down buttons, are better on the new model. Pairing is easier on the new model because of the flashing lights that the old model lacked.

I watched the Plantronics video and there are many many features on this model that I will never take the time to learn to use. But they are there for the person that needs them so it is a much more versatile unit than the older one.

With the older model the headset had to be placed entirely inside the case to charge but the new model allows sitting the headset onto the end of the case to perform a charge (as well as inside the case).

All in all it’s a very nice improvement and well worth the money. Highly recommend.

title: Cannot Connect Devices and Unreliable
review: This device can “Pair” my Bluetooth headphones, but after realizing there was no sound coming out, I saw an option to “Connect” and it kept failing. This dongle is completely unreliable with Xbox One controllers, too.

title: Something isn’t right.
review: This cable will not fit properly in the back of my tv and will not lock in. It fits in the back of the wireless headphones transmitter. It will not fit in the back of my 55 inch Samsung either. Either end doesn’t fit. The shorter cable that comes with the headset fits perfectly and locks in both tvs.  I needed this longer cable to run thru the wall to the tv hung on the wall.

title: Better that Beats Solo
review:
I bought these for my 10 year old. Myself and three other family members did a side by side blind comparison on Christmas day of Beats Solo ($149), Bose Quiet Comfort Gen 1 ($299), Harman Kardon BT ($199.00) and the Sony ZX600 ($58). We rated for comfort and depth. We tested various types of music. I was very surprised by the results.....

Tester #1 (a frequent headphone user)
1. - Bose Quiet Comfort
2. - H/K BT
3. - Sony Zx600
4. - Beats Solo

Tester 2 & 3 (ear bud users)
1. - Bose Quiet Comfort
2. - Sony Zx600
3. - Beats Solo
4. - H/K BT

Tester 4 (Me)
1. - Bose Quiet Comfort
2. - Sony Zx600
3. - H/K BT
4. - Beats Solo

All of us agreed that the Bose were the best. Everyone was very surprised at the quality of the Sony for the price. We all agreed that the Beats were nice looking but not very comfortable, not a lot of depth (mostly all bass) and too expensive.

Bottom line ... If you are looking for a very good set of headphones for a very good price, go with the Sony

title: Right choice for me
review: This headset is made to work with a variety of devices, which is exactly what I need. I can use it on my phone, cell or laptop, making remote meetings easy wherever I am. I didn't need it to be wireless - wasn't worth the expense to me. Wired is fine and this works exactly as I hoped. Good sound and comfortable to wear for long meetings. I would recommend.

title: Quality sound!
review: I go through a lot of earbuds because I'm on my phone & laptop throughout the day for work. These work really well with my iPhone and Dell laptop - sound quality is excellent and I love that it comes with multiple sizes and types of earbud covers to fit different ear types. Very happy with this product purchase and highly recommend!

title: Comfort and great audio
review: Comfort and great audio. I really love these earbuds, however I wish the battery life would be longer.

title: Cheap price, cheap quality
review:
You want cheap, you get cheap, and these are cheap. They're flimsy as can be. I do like how the ears rotate and swivel, but I feel like they're going to break every time I swivel them. The sound is ok...when it works. The wire and connector are super cheap, so when either moves even slightly, the sound crackles. It makes these headphones useless to wear when you're on the move. When you're sitting still, though, they sound ok.

Honestly, spend a little more money and get a nicer pair of headphones. There are plenty of good options for just a few bucks more.

title: Panasonic Bluetooth earbuds
review:
Pros:
Connects easily to phone, surprisingly clear phone call volume, very light weight, easy to charge once you find the "port"

Cons:
Probably the most awkward fitting earpieces I've ever worn, hard plastic components...including the inner ear plugs

As most of the other reviews have stated already the earpieces fit awkwardly on the ear. Almost like it's gonna fall off! I'm not a runner (unless the coffee is ready) so I can't tell you if it would work well for someone who runs and is looking for that in this particular item. I did connect it to my phone and placed some calls and it was pretty clear both ends. Course I was in a home with minimal background noise. My biggest concern would be actually putting these on or off my ear. Because of the style and hard plastic I needed two hands to put it on my ear. Seemed like it would've been more pliable. So overall if you need Bluetooth earbuds and these were on sale cheap....it would be a good buy. I expect more out of Panasonic.

title: Sennheiser Urbanite Headphones
review: I also never owned an expensive pair of headphones.  In fact, I usually used the ear buds and have for years.  These headphones are pretty impressive.  The sound is crisp and clear and very comfortable to wear.  I am a bit worried however that when I would use them the most (while on a long walk exercising) that they might get funky.  Only time will tell I suppose....but in the meantime I'm gonna enjoy the tunes.  There seems to be a microphone included.  I haven't tried it out yet to see how well it works.  I will try to update my review after trying it out like that.

title: Works great!
review: My daughter is attending virtual schooling which requires listening to classes online and completing studies online.  These work great.  She wears them almost every day at the computer and they fit her perfectly (she's 10) so they can be adjusted down to fit a child's head. She has claimed them as hers so I haven't been able to use them myself.  I also like the fact that they microphone arm is rigid without the foam covered mic at the end.  I have a headphone/mic that came with the Rosetta Stone program that is bendable with the mic with foam cover.  It seems I could never get the mic far away from my mouth...to the point where it seemed it was pressing against my lips.  Needless to say, that is aggravating.  This headset also has a volume control on the headphones which is a nice extra.  The mic also can turn either way if you would prefer having it on the left side or right.  All in all I think they are pretty nice headphones and work perfect for online schooling.

title: Decent quality headphones at this price-point ...
review: Good-quality, solid headphones.  Not the most amazing sound quality, but definitely not the worst either.  A decent quality you would expect at this price point.  I used these for running, I always prefer behind-the-head style headphones for running.  These stay on securely when I run.

title: Cheap price, great quality
review: These headphones produce a crisp, full sound and are well worth the price.  I accidentally cracked a pair while they were in a bag I was shoving underneath an airplane seat, and replaced them as soon as I could.  It was great knowing that I wouldn't have to spend a small fortune to get another pair of good quality everyday-use headphones.

title: Great headphones. Could be a little more comfortable (they ...
review: Great headphones.  Could be a little more comfortable (they pinch).  You'll need an external DAC to really appreciate them with a smart phone or non-apple laptop.

title: It sounds even better than the DAC on my macbook pro
review: I was a little hesitant about buying this because I have the audio technica ATH-M50s, which are low impedance headphones (i.e. you don't need an amp to power them).  However, the improved sound quality alone on my Nexus 5 make the price worth it.  The Nexus 5 has a mediocre DAC, and the difference with the FiiO E10K is night and day.  It sounds even better than the DAC on my macbook pro.  3 stars because the mini usb connection is flakey, and I frequently have to adjust the cable to get it to work.  This is a problem to the point where I'm considering returning it.

title: Worth the splurge
review:
Best purchase! I own an older version of Bose on-ear noise cancelling headphone they work great! bought a cheap Bluetooth headphones and enjoyed the wireless functionality, until 3 months later the on/off button stopped working :( So I decided to go to the Bose store and check these out... OMG soft, comfortable, easy, and they block so much external sound that you won't know they aren't noise cancelling headphones! works SEAMLESSLY with all my Bluetooth devices (samsungs & ipod touch). GREAT on calls most people don't even know I'm on a headset. Getting ready to travel in a few weeks on a 22 hr flights looking forward to using these seeing how these work in that environment for listening to audio books & movies.

Most negative thing I can say is I am disappointed that the audio plug on the headset is a non-standard size.

title: Didn't work with my headset
review: Didn't work with my headset.  I think in addition to the physical size of the connectors, you need to pay attention to the number of conductors

title: Worked Better than Required
review: Bought these to listen to a scanner at the Indy 500. These buds are great. They are comfortable and block a majority of the noise without compromising the experience.  We were able to hear the roar of the engines and able to hear the scanner  They also work great for yard work.  Highly recommend these earbuds

title: Dope
review: I love these. Bought them a second time. Inexpensive as eff. Sound is very very good. Not amazing, but better than the majority of earphones I have purchased. I use them for working out and the sweat never affects them. There’s a cord that connects them that I don’t like. I also don’t like the fact that the only indicator that you need to charge is that it all of a sudden announces battery low every 30 seconds until they shut off. Oh well. They were inexpensive and they come with chargers and a case so that was nice. My first pair lasted 2 years of daily use and my new ones will probably last longer. The first pair just broke because I let the second earbud dangle all the time so the connector stopped working. Basically it was my fault.

title: Great sound, customizable and easy to use. What is there not to like
review: These Beats earbuds provide wonderful sound for an ear bud. The sound is full and seems unlimited, other earbuds I have used seem to die off in areas of songs where the sounds reach towards the limits. These are easy to fit and use, it does take getting used to the one button operation, but it is not a factor really. You will also get an app to control and customize your ear buds, handy in setting up these for exactly how you want them to work. In all a really good set of ear buds, you cannot go wrong with these.

title: Byron Statics Record Player/Turntable is a throwback to my youth listening to music on vinyl
review:
Byron statics record player/turntable lets me play my old vinyl records I have kept over the years. First of all this record player is easy to use for those who have never seen a record player before. The instructions are clear and easy to follow, for those of us who had a turntable in your youth this is a bit like riding a bicycle, the controls are just like my last turntable (from the early 80's).
Sound quality is better than my 80's turntable though, and this has the option for adding headphones to add to the experience. Gone is the always background hiss that was constant in the old turntables. Also included is a RCA connector if you want to hook this up to a surround sound system. I connected this to a JBL speaker and the internal speaker is close to the JBL speaker.
I can now listen to my old records that I have stored for years, hello Jefferson Starship. A really fun way to bring back my ability to play vinyl records.

title: JVC Headphones as good as it gets for wireless headphones
review:
First off the sound quality on these is amazing for a wireless headphone. Everything is crisp and clear - the power to drive the sound is here. These headphones have good base boost, and volume levels to make these great for those who fly. With the added assist of noise cancelling, these are headphones I like to keep in my travel bag. i am not sure if I would get 17 hours out of a charge, but these can go a full day of travel without requiring a recharge.

These are comfortable for long lengths of time both in weight and the over the ear fit. I will continue using these as my go to when traveling.

title: These Lasmex headphones are top notch, great sound quality and comfortable
review:
My husband cannot say enough about these headphones and their great sound quality. He has found them to be better than his really expensive sound cancelling headphones from a well-known brand. There is great Bass, and the range of the volume is good for headphones. He is required to travel for his job occasionally and uses headphones on the plane to make the trips more bearable. Charging was around 90 minutes and a charge lasted him through two 3 hour flights without requiring a recharge.

Build quality is as good or better than the other manufactures out there. These connected right away with the Bluetooth network on the first attempt. These come with a nice travel case also to protect the headphones. These are a great option for those looking for a really nice set of headphones.

title: iHome iB82BC is a Good Bluetooth headphones for those on the go.
review:
The Ihome iB832BC headphones synced right up to my android phone and have worked consistently since being synced. I got these for when I was walking my dog and general activities where a mobile earbud set would be of great convenience. The sound volume is quite sufficient for everyone to use in most activities. Sound quality is not terrific but that is to be expected with bluetooth/digital music combos (even my husband's Bose headset has average sound quality (he says it is due to the digital music limitations).
Using this as a phone headset is average, it works but has its limitations. I always feel the limitations there is the microphones in these units are not the best quality and are the weak link in these systems.
Battery life is good, I average around 6 hours between charges which is good for most uses, but not the highest I have seen on these type of headphones.

title: Panasonic head phones are lightweight, easy to use, and provide good sound quality. Everything I would expect from Panasonic
review:
These Panasonic head phones are lightweight, easy to use, and provide good sound quality, and are also a great value. Linking these to a device via Bluetooth was easy and straightforward, I had the headphones attached and working within a few minutes so no surprises there.
I also like that these fold up to be pretty compact, so it makes them easy to bring in a carry on or computer case when traveling. The unit comes with a standard micro USB cable for charging, and out of the box charging the headphones took less than an hour to a full charge.

title: Fantastic Earbuds for Smartphones
review:
I am very happy with the iLuv earbuds. I've used them with a Android smartphone and they work wonderfully. The sound is well-balanced for listening to music, but I've used them mostly for phone calls. I can hear the calls better with less interference from outside sounds and the mic works well when talking.

Added features which make these earbuds so great are the pouch for storage and for carrying, the no-tangle cord, and the different sizes of ear pieces for a good fit. They've made handling phone calls while on the go so much easier.

title: Well-made earbuds with great features, but weak bass
review:
Item description does a great job of listing all of the features of the product. Of all the special features of the earbuds, these are my favorite:

* 3 sizes for a better, more comfortable fit
* Magnets on the split portion of the cord to keep them from getting tangled up
* Controls to allow easy handling of music and calls
* Small storage bag to hold the earbuds when not being used

In addition to these features, I am impressed at how well the earbuds are made. The cord is really sturdy and seems it will hold up to regular use. It has so far! The sound quality is good. It is worlds away from the standard earbuds that come with a product, but somewhat disappointing. The bass is weak, which was a let down considering the price range of the product. So while I love all the extra features of these earbuds, I couldn't quite give them 5 stars based on the quality of sound, which is the whole point of upgrading to a premium earbud.

title: Nice basic mp3 player with a few extras
review:
I like the GoGear Muse - it's a nice basic MP3 player with a few extras that make it stand out from a comparable model of an iPod. Below are a summary of the top features:

* Small and compact, which makes it very portable.
* Comes with a lightweight case that protects the front of the player and has openings for the various ports, which makes it convenient to charge.
* Headphones have an attachment that clip behind your ear. They have avearge sound quality.
* MP3 player also has an FM radio that works well
* Comes with an arm band to use for exercise, walking, etc. The size is large enough for an average-sized man to wear comfortably
* Can be used with Philips Songbird, but is also compatable with iTunes. (For best results, set up a separate playlist just for the GoGear)

Overall, it's a nice MP3 player to use when exercising, sitting by the pool, or walking. I appreciated the extras like the case and the armband that were included with MP3 player.

title: Grandma Approved
review:
I bought these for my grandmother. She can not hear her tv and doesn’t want to disturb her neighbors in her apartment complex.

She LOVES the headphones. She said they are comfortable and easy to use. The sound is amazing and she can still control the volume with the remote.

*Make sure the tv is Bluetooth compatible. If you don’t know, Google the model number.*

title: Died within two weeks
review: Purchased these because my bluetooth headphones always die quickly, and these were a little more expensive than other options, so I thought they were a bit higher quality.  I was wrong!  From the very beginning, the earbuds would randomly go in and out.  After two weeks, the right earbud completely died.  Returned them because I had them for only a few weeks.

title: Works great
review: My desktop computer is on the floor during my covid "work from home year" and this extension works great. It allows my iPhone headphones (the original style) to do audio and mic for zoom meetings and works with my recording mic for narrating videos. The length is nice and long so I don't have to worry about disconnecting my mics. Excellent value for the money.

title: Best for travel.
review: Such a great value for a low price. Ordered as a back up for my cordless earbuds while traveling and ended up only using the corded. Was great to plug in on the flight a great sound quality. Kind to my ears roo. Some earbuds hurt but not these.

title: Works for my Apple earbuds
review: I have wired Apple earbuds with a rectangular piece for controlling volume, phone calls, etc. The earbud stems fit perfectly and I was able to easily wind up the cord including the rectangular piece. I don't understand why another person wrote a negative review because of the rectangular piece.

title: Very comfortable.
review: I have Sony headphones and wasn't sure if these would fit. It took me about 5 minutes to get them on but once on, they stay on. I like to walk and listen to music or stories and these headphones do not distort the sound and are very comfortable. The bonus is that they are not esxpensive!

title: Pretty good for the value
review: These headphones, in general, a pretty decent for the price. They don't fit too terribly on the head, in fact they might be a little loose on you depending on how wide your head is. I wish there was some adjustability to these. Overall pretty decent value and quality.

title: Love it.
review: Love that I can update my old Alienware desktop to the new usbc to use my oculus virtual reality headset also got the EZDIY-FAB 5.25in 10Gbps USB 3.1 Gen2 Hub and Type-C Port,Front Panel USB Hub with QC 3.0 Quick Charging .

title: Love it!
review: This stand is perfect— it’s sturdy and has a sleek design.  Looks great on the desk and I don’t neee to worry about my headphones getting knocked on the floor by accident.

title: Great extension for a Nintendo Switch
review: Works great to extend our headset on a Switch. A+ Price and the quality is great.

title: These have help up decently with every day use, ...
review: These have help up decently with every day use, but they're already losing sound in one of the ears.  May be time to invest in a decent pair of headphones for my son.

title: Phenomenal Earbuds but I may have gotten a dud
review: I freaking loved these headphones. They are amazong. Great sound quality, convenient, hold a wicked long charge. But the left earbud stopped charging today. I bought a protection plan but they said I should still be covered under warranty.. not sure how to contact manufacturer. I really love these and I'm hoping I just got a dud because these have been so great for me because I listen to podcasts all day and can be charging one while listening to the other.

title: :-( I just got these and....
review: These headphones don’t have good sound at all, unfortunately. I usually buy cheaper Bluetooth headphones because they don’t seem to last long at all for me(prob because I use them all day everyday to listen to audiobooks, listen to music and YouTube even movies while I work or take a break.)  I have to say, these have the worst sound quality I’ve ever heard in a pair of earphones. Very tinny and I can hear things around me more than I can hear what’s playing in my ears. Also, the volume doesn’t go very loud at all. I’ve never bought Anker before but with the reviews online I was excited to think the quality of sound would be at least fair but OH! was I so wrong!! I haven’t decided if these are going back or not? I will say that the magnet feature is really great(that is all I can find good about this product so far. I’m going to see how long the battery last before I make my decision. What happened Anker? How did these even get a 4 star review on here???

title: These headPhones steal data and information from your phone
review: DO NOT BUY.  these WIRED headphone need to be connected via bluetooth to use.  Major Scam!!!!!

title: HORRIBLE headset - don't waste your money
review: These headphones are the worst sound I've ever experienced in a headset.  NO noise cancellation (not even a little bit!), my office is two rooms away and down the hall from my living room and the headset still picked up TV noise.  Sound quality is tinny, like you're listening to someone talking to you inside in a metal tunnel.  Co-workers said I sounded terrible on Teams calls. Volume button is teeny tiny and hard to use, if you have large hands or fingers (which I don't) I can't imagine how you'd fare trying to turn volume up or down.  HARD PASS on these, returning them immediately.  You get what you pay for I guess...I invested in slightly more expensive gaming headphones and they are awesome!

title: Be sure your device is Bluetooth 5.0
review:
I'm really pleased with these headphones except for one thing: The Macbook Pro I bought these to use with is only Bluetooth 4.0, and apparently this causes some conflict because I have to remove and rescan for the headphones every time I use them. I really do think this is the culprit, not the headphones themselves, because the instructions clearly state they should be used with the same version of Bluetooth on the device.

I bought the headphones because my soundcard has gone grouchy and screechy, and I was trying to avoid getting it replaced. Considering this is an early 2013 MacBook Pro, however, maybe it's time for me to think about upgrading....

The headphones themselves fit my small head well, and they stay connected throughout our 1200 square foot house. It's only when I try to go outside that the connection is lost.

title: I am very pleased with this case
review:
I was sent a free blue case for a 15" MacBook Pro in exchange for my honest review. This is it.

I love the case! It's plenty big for my 15" MacBook Pro Retina, and it's wonderfully padded and protective. The inner sleeve is a very velvety soft fabric, and the external fabric is a satiny cushioned material. There is also a soft kind of rubbery bumper around the edges that helps keep the case from sliding inside a briefcase or when stacked on its end anywhere. The whole case just feels very elegant, which I wasn't expecting.

My case came with a tough foam-plastic insert to help it keep its shape in shipping, but I find that I can use it for some additional padding and my laptop still fits well without being too snugly stuffed. There is room for a USB cable and small pair of headphones, and you could put a legal pad or some papers into it too.

I like that the case itself can actually be used as a laptop tray of sorts, so you can sit your laptop on top of it when surfing in bed or a chair. It's not stiff enough not to bend, but it extends about an inch all the way around underneath and makes a non-slip pad that will help protect your legs from laptop heat if yours is prone to that.

title: Great product. Limits the volume which is a great ...
review: Great product.  Limits the volume which is a great idea.  Too many folks increase the volume too much (e.g., to drown outside noise) which can damage long term hearing.  I bought two for both daughters and they use all the time.  Recommend vs normal headphones for kids.

title: Did not meet my needs
review: There is no noise canceling built into these headphones. Plus the Cable is just too short you have to be sitting directly in front of your computer. I would not buy this again.

title: Size
review: I really love this headset.  But I have a small head and wished I could adjust the size to fit better.  Other then that they are wonderful.

title: Solid product
review: I have a hard time getting headphones to stay in my ears but these work very well and seem to stay put. They cancel noise pretty well and the sound quality is what you would expect for the price. Would buy again.

title: Okay, but not Great
review: These headphones sound great when you are listening to music, but that is it. If you try to watch any Youtube or Netflix with these and you will see that the audio does not sync up with the people talking, and then on other apps and social media, the audio is just terrible. I would say get them if you just want to workout or listen to music to because they are great for that, and they come with a lot of different sized earbuds and wings, as well as a travel case.

title: Great
review: Super comfortable, sound great and very versatile headphones. I like the value for the price!

title: Useless
review: Mic never worked from the get go, headset crackles. Got it for work meetings, cannot use it at all.

title: Good for price
review: Very good headphones for the price.  A little tight on my head so uncomfortable after a long time.  Also they fade in and out with strange sounds depending on what is between the transmitter and the headphones and they pop loudly (hurts the ears) when they shut off.

title: Perfect for sidesleeping; doesn’t hurt ears; last longer than other brands
review: These are some of the most comfortable earbuds for side sleeping. They do not hurt my ear even though I wear them all night, every night. They have helped saved my relationship! I use these to block out his snoring (by playing white noise). I like how they make somewhat of an airtight seal which helps block out more of the outside noise. I then use an app to play white noise so I can’t hear my boyfriend snore at all. These last a lot longer than similar ear buds I have bought on Amazon. I hope they don’t stop making/selling these.

title: Don’t hurt ears for side sleepers!!!
review: These are the only earbuds that do not hurt my ear when I’m sleeping on my side. They have saved my relationship! I use these to block out his snoring. I like how they make somewhat of an airtight seal which helps block out more of the outside noise. I then use an app to play white noise so I can’t hear my boyfriend snore at all. They don’t last long. I have had to buy replacements many times but I don’t mind since they are cheap and are the best for sleeping.

title: Works good
review: The only thing is there is no volume control on the speaker itself only a mute button. You can also plug headphones into it if needed.

title: Most comfortable so far!
review:
I've bought several bluetooth ear buds and these are the MOST comfortable so far. Sound quality is good. A test call to my mom (I've done this with all purchases) and she stated these had the best call quality. No echo, no distance/tunnel sound to the call. I have sensitive inner ears due to having to wear ear plugs every night (snoring husband) and these are awesome. I almost forget they are in.
Pros:
Pausing music, audio books (it's amazing how few earbuds do this
Easy controls for volume, skipping songs, answering calls
Easy charging
Good sound quality - I'm not an audio file though
COMFORTABLE
Can use one bud at a time or both.

Cons-
The distance I can get from my phone before it disconnects is not as far as other buds I've tried but I'm ok with that.

Will update after I've downloaded some music and used them for a while. So far I'm loving these. By the way I'm paired with a Samsung galaxy s8.

title: Can’t figure out buttons
review: These are great if you just want to connect them and listen without using any of the controls. If you want to use the controls, get a different product. The directions are not clear and no matter what/where I press/tap on the earphones, the only thing I can figure out how to do or get to work is 1) noise cancelling and 2) pause/play. Although I did accidentally call someone once somehow (luckily it was my cousin).

title: Fit well and work great
review: Excellent headset that works great. Chord could be a little longer is the only drawback.

title: Perfect
review: Great price for the exact functions I was seeking, doing student video editing and listening to music around the house while doing chores.  Irritating that if there is no signal for a minute or two, static begins, but not a big deal. Comfortable enough and good mileage on the AA batteries required in the headset.

title: Great sound without breaking the bank
review: I was looking for decent, quality headphones for short business trips and the occasional use at home; these are perfect.  There seems to be a gap in the market, people either have cheap/crappy bluetooth headphones that were $20 or they have very expensive/brand bluetooth headphones that are $400.  These are the perfect answer for something looking in between the worst and going crazy, highly recommend.

title: Works as advertised
review: Works fine so far, going to invest in wireless earbuds eventually but this gives me a chance to use the several pairs I already had.

title: Descent Mini Projector
review: Seems well built and easy to use. Not enough experience on all of features it has yet. Hooked right up to WIFI and Bluetooth without issues. There is no lag with earbuds I’m using. The only issue I may have is it’s not quite as bright as I thought it would be. This is supposed to be 150 ANSI Lumens, however I have another mini projector that is only 50 ANSI Lumens but it is brighter. I bought this unit for the Android System and it seems to work good so far. I’ll have to play around with this one more and see if I can brighten it up some. Picture is great but just a little on the dark side.

title: nice little amp
review: I have this amp paired with my iPhone bluetooth and play along with the Chordify app to play all my favorite songs every day. I don't consider it practice, it's more of an enjoyable pass time. If you love playing guitar get this amp along with chordify app and headphones and have fun.

title: not recommended
review: Right channel randomly goes out. Thought I would spend extra bucks to get a nice pair of studio headphones but these are not them. The box was not sealed so who knows if these were a return or not. I sent these back and will try a different brand. Not recommended!!!

title: Fair value for the price
review: I didn’t expect much from these because of the price but thought I’d give them a try. I was surprised with the sound quality. The are super easy to use and stay put in my ear as well. title: Eventually Works To Reprogram Frequencies On Baofeng UV-5R
review:
This USB-to-mic/earphone-connector cable allows your desktop computer running CHIRP to interface with your Baofeng UV-5R so you can download/upload, enter, re-order or edit your frequencies and other features of the UV-5R (like screen colors, notification tones, etc).

I used the cable to match my UV-5R's frequency list to the existing list that came with my Rugged RDM-DB RZR 2-way radio.

To find the list of freqs the RDM-DB uses, search "Setup for Rugged Radio RDM-DB Radio." That list can then be entered into the UV-5R one line at a time using CHIRP. To learn how to use CHIRP, search "How To Use CHIRP Software To Program A Baofeng UV-5R. Using CHIRP for HAM, GMRS, and FRS Radios"

The biggest problem with this cable for me was that my computer running Win10 could not find the driver for the cable. It was supposed to load the driver automatically. It didn't.

Fortunately, the instructions that came with the cable pointed me to where I could download and install the driver manually. That probably took me an hour to figure out -- like all things Windows -- but eventually the driver was installed and the computer recognized the cable.

Works fine now.

One star off for difficulty in driver install.

title: Cord Tangles and Has Right Angle Plug
review:
Cons:
1. The cord is not silicone wire. It tangles easily.
2. Right angle mini-plug puts excess stress on the wire. I expect it to fail. With straight mini plugs, I can install a piece of shrink tubing over the plug to provide increased stress relief where the wire goes into the plug. Can't fit shrink tubing onto a right angle plug.
3. Size is a bit too large for comfortable sleeping. I use earbuds specifically to help me get to sleep by putting a droning podcast on at very low volume. Out like a light in a few minutes. The earbuds also act like earmuffs to mute room noise. These Panasonic buds are just a bit too long and are uncomfortable in the ear that's against the pillow.
4. Audio quality is so-so but adequate for voice.
5. Expensive for what they are. Can find four sets for less $$ elsewhere.

Pros:
1. The buds are angled such that you can see in daylight and feel in the dark which one is left and which is right.

After they break, I won't be buying them again.

title: Does not fit; see attached side by side photo
review:
I bought Neutrik because it's the best, hands down. Usually.

Except these 3.5mm mini plugs, whether this right angle or the straight model (I bought both), simply are too large a diameter. Or there's some other dimension that's just slightly off. Can't really tell.

I cannot fit the Neutrik plug into either my Canon HFS100 camcorder's or my Nikon D800's mic-in and earphone out sockets without undue forcing, which I won't do.

Ironically, an inexpensive molded cable fits fine.

I trust Neutrik for all my XLR and other connections needs. They're the gold standard. It's a mystery to me why this particular stereo mini plug simply won't fit. I've tried side by side comparisons with other plugs

See the attached side-by-side photo comparing the Neutrik right angle mini with a "standard" molded mini plug that works fine in all my devices.

To add insult to injury, we bought a professional audio breakaway cable at work that featured the straight version of this Neutrik connector and it doesn't fit either. They're well built, just not to the "standard" spec.

Cannot recommend them.

title: Accidentally the best earbuds I own
review:
These came with my Zen X-Fi, that was retired when I got my iPod and that was retired when I got my iPhone 4, which is the closest thing to a "one device to carry and do most everything." But Apple earphones are sound leakers, don't fit ears very well and really don't stop ambient audio to leak past them.

These Creative earbuds seal into my ear canals wonderfully. They come with three sets of ear buds in different sizes for different sized ears. They have a full rich sound with good bass. They are very responsive, delivering plenty of volume. I wear them under my ear muffs when doing yard work and can listen to podcasts even when mowing the lawn. They work well on airplane trips.

The cords are silicon and do not easily tangle and come untangled easily.

The strain relief on the plug could use some help. I had to coat it with silicon sealer to reinforce it when the cord frayed and almost broke. Now the plug is ugly, but strong.

I bought some Klipsch S3's thinking they would be better, but no, these little Creatives beat them hands down.

review: I love this MP3 player. I bought this to use when mowing and it works perfect. The original earphones had great sound but the 2nd time I used them, the cord fell out of one earpiece. I found a really good pair to replace them and now I wouldn't take anything for this player. It was a refurbished player but works like a new one. I highly recommend this item but be prepared, you may want to purchase a more durable set of earphones along with it. Still a great bargain for the price.

title: GPU fan is horribly loud, even at low RPMs
review:
A few reviewers have already mentioned it. The GPU fan is EXTREMELY distracting even at low RPMs. It makes a really high pitched whistling noise that drowns out game/music audio, making immersion into a story-driven game or movie impossible without good headphones. I’ve taken the bottom case off to view if anything was obstructing it (dust or what not), everything looks brand new with no signs of dirt/dust.

Read on forums that this is common with this model. Some people taped over the vents in the back to control the whistling, but I’m not going to risk damage from overheating by doing this. This model should be recalled and redesigned.

I’m also running it on an external fan pad on full speed, but the fans still insist on blowing at almost max speeds on games that could run on a potato. I fear that overheating damage is inevitable and imminent with this rig.

As far as running games, it can run the highest settings for any current game out right now, but your fans will be screaming when you launch it, and I just can’t focus on anything with the whistling.

title: Sound Quality
review: Sound quality is great and they feel comfortable in my ears.  Battery life isn't bad either compared to my old wireless earbuds.  I definitely would recommend this product to my family and friends letting them know they work just as good as iPods and more affordable.

title: classic headphones
review:
i've used Koss PRO-4AAs since the 70's in professional applications.

I've seen reviews of the current version saying that the new ones aren't as good as the originals, but i fail to see why people would say this, these are as comfortable and as good-sounding as ever, and cost less.

And still built like tanks. The only reason i don't have my old ones is that they were stolen, i'm quite sure that, barring major misfortune, those headphones are still working for someone, somewhere... so here's to another 30 years of enjoyment.

The passive noise isolation can't quite match modern active-cancellation 'phones, but it is still excellent - hence the 4-star rating.

The only nitpick i would have is that the deep bass frequencies are possibly not quite as "tight" as on earlier headsets, but this is a subjective observation and i've not had a pair for the past 8 years, so i could be wrong. So that's why i gave them four stars for sound quality.

Five stars for comfort, especially considering the solid construction makes them heavier than more modern sets.

title: Staying connected even if I forgot my phone
review: Watch works great wish battery life was better but it is still nice being able to make phone calls on my watch if I leave my phone at home using my Bluetooth headset

title: A good overall product but some comfort issues
review: I had always found the Motorola H700 flip headset to be the best and most convenient bluetooth solution. Its performance was good and  the flip microphone made it easy to carry in a holster. Unfortunately it finally died and they are out of production. So I decided to try this headset and was pleasantly surprised. This actually surpasses the Motorola H700. Voice recognition by my iPhone is improved - presumably because of the better noise reduction of the headset, the calls seem very clear on both ends, and the talking caller ID is a real plus.It can fit in the same holster I used for my H700 - though it is a bit large for it. If I can find a holster with a belt clip, this could be a real winner. The only con is that it isn't extremely comfortable on the earlobe after a few hours. The bar that holds the ear clip to the unit is a bit too long I think and the end poking through tends to be a little irritating. It comes with an additional ear pad and clip but there is not really any more comfort using either of those. I have not tried the "comfort kit" - sold separately for way too much money. When I first saw the "comfort kit" advertised I was amused that a $100 bluetooth headset would need an additional expenditure  to be comfortable. However I may be forced to try it if I can't get  the ear clip adjusted properly. Jabra should be embarrassed by this.

title: Good for the price - needs a volume control
review: I was very surprised at the noise canceling capability of these earphones. The big drawback is that there is no volume control on the earphones so you are dependent on the devices (or worse yet the airline seat control) for volume adjustment. My PDA/MP3 player's volume resolution is very poor so the sound is either too loud or too soft. However as strict noise canceling, at least in airplanes, they seem to work very well.

title: Prevents loss

title: Can't beat these for the price
review: Great headphones for the gym or around the house. Nice quality for one third of the price of Beats or Bose without giving up the sound.

title: Just what I needed
review: I am a recent work-from-home-er, and I needed a headset phone badly.  For the price, this thing is perfect.  Really it's the only thing out there that was affordable that does exactly what I need it to.  The buttons are so very small, and sometimes one gets stuck when I'm dialing out, so I worry about how it's going to hold up over time.  It's also taken some getting used to such a small keypad.  There's a nice little selection of ring tones, and the message light is very convenient.  All in all I am completely pleased with this purchase.

review:

I like them better. It took a few minutes to adjust to the difference between the two but all in all I like these better.

review: My 4'11" wife has very small ear canals and has tried many types of headphones and earbuds over the years without success. Normal sized ear buds are painful and fit poorly, and even her Corwin headphones are heavy and too hot.  These Aftershokz solve all those problems and have become her instant favorites for audiobook listening and listening to the TV in bed at night.  They easily pair with her phone and the TV, so no complaints there. Two thumbs up; I just wish I had found them sooner.

review: Appears to work fine, this is my 2nd set of noise-cancelling headphones, and I can't say these work any better/worse than my older set.  I think the quality is reflected in the price, and I'd recommend these and purchase them again if I needed a third-set :-)  Gordon

title: I love these headphones
review: I bought these to use in my office. It helps to drown out the background noise and distractions so that I can focus on my work. I love these headphones!

title: Dissatisfied
review: I read the reviews and I was excited for these but now I'm disappointed because they are too big for my ears they constantly are falling out and I'm having to push him back in my ear which then shuts off the music or hangs up the phone call, very frustrating. When they are secure in my ear the sound is pretty good. I used to have an LG headset and those would stay in my ear, kind of wish I would have bought that instead.

title: I want to love these, but they're ok.
review:
I was really hopeful these could be a good replacement for the HBS-830, LG Tone ultra.

In fact, they have one key feature that blows most headsets out of the water: They have rewind + fast forward buttons that work (for iPhone at least, which is what I have), if you hold down the next track or previous track buttons for 2 seconds. which I haven't been able to find on any other bluetooth headset besides the older LG models that are no longer being produced

That alone would be worth it. The sound quality and battery life, is not as great as the LG version, which is expected at this price point, however, there was one major drawback.

I can't quite explain it, but there were weird audio bugs when switching between differetn apps. I could only play audio from one app at a time. If i wanted to switch apps, I'd have to disconnect and reconnect the headphones. If the manufactures can iron this out, this could be an amazing LG alternative and the only headet i've found with rewind/fast forward.

Yes, I have the updated firmware on my iphone.

title: Amazing looking, almost-awesome budget headphones
review:
Overall, Looks and feel are amazing, sound quality is so-so, battery life and the charger are what's holding this back from being a 5 star budget headphone

Pros:
-Looks amazing. I get lots of compliments
-Feels great. A very nice feel when you don't want tight/heavy over-the-ear headphones & also don't want earbuds in your ear
-Sound quality... it's decent for the budget price. Not for audiophiles of course

Cons
-Poor battery life. Not expecting much for the price, but I'm getting way less than the advertised 8 hours
- terrible range. As long as you stay close to your device, should be fine. Excellent range is not expected for the price, but these headphones don't just lose connection, they have a very loud distorted screech
- Annoying to charge. Not mentioned in the Q&A section, but the micro-USB port is in a hard to reach spot. It's hard to describe, but not all micro usb cords will fit, it has to be ones with slim heads and long metal plugs. So if you lose the provided cord you're out of luck unless you happen to have a slim one. Again, for the budget price+the slimness of the headphones, I understand it's difficult, but there has to be a better solution.

title: Great quality for the price. Decent Sound quality; great for insane bass. It's a tight fit.
review:
Who is this for? If you're looking for a stylish budget headset; you're not an audiophile and want crazy bass and good battery life and you don't want to pay extra for noise cancelling. Also better for smaller heads, as it's a really tight fit.

Pros -
Very stylish, I got the white and get a lot of compliments at work
Great Battery - I'll use it non stop for two to three 8 hour shifts without a charge
Good Range
Decent sound quality especially for the price
Insane base, although it gets distorted at max bass levels, it's good if you're just looking to really bass-out

Cons
-This headset is REALLY tight. my head is a size 7 3/4 in baseball cap sizes (a little on the big side) and these earphones get painful after about 30 minutes of wearing so i need to take breaks. I've been stretching them overnight for months but little effect. Kind of a bummer but worth it for now. This is the only reason i'll eventually upgrade.
-kind of the opposite of noise cancelling. If you go to medium volume levels people in the same room can hear. When I'm really rocking out in silence, my headphones can be heard in different rooms.

The call answer/end button doesn't work with my phone (a Sanyo model).  I like that you only need one ear gel because it's reversible.  My old headset had left and right ear gels, so if you lost one (which I did) then you're stuck with only being able to use it in one ear. This product doesn't have that shortcoming.

title: Bad Charge Fails Tile Fails Do Not Buy
review: I would have returned these for a refund but my puppy ate the packaging so I guess I am stuck with them. I wanted to review about my problems with these earlier but Amazon blocked new reviews for a while saying they thought the negative reviews were all scammers. Way to be really sus amazon. so here's what I think: they are nice when they work but they don't work reliability at all. I got them brand new and they were not working. title: Sure glad I switched to these.
review: Has not failed. Love these. I returned an expensive, new-on-the-market brand promising all sorts of action and features, for my Panasonic cheaper earphones. I'm sure glad I did. Expensive does NOT always mean better.

title: Too many issues with the headset.
review:
I'm sorry but I really really really tried very hard to like these headphones because I spent so much money on them that I thought "they must be good". They are a little uncomfortable in that they fall out my ears, and I often struggle to shove/push back in. I've even tried the extra attachments and ALL sizes/all ear pieces.I push them in hard because I get some "air" /outside noises. I thought maybe that exta lengthy shaft between the earplug and the base, is what's causing the base not to rest in my ear properly.
For me, these may be worth $25 to $30 but not $49.

title: Nice quality for the money. IF it shorts in wiring I wouldn't have wasted a lot.
review:
I did look at the many other supposedly higher quality models by the same brand name but it all boiled down to the wiring. After long use and motion most headsets short-out in the wiring, making them only audible in one ear, or not at all audible. No matter how much you pay for a headset, there is a high possibility that it will short-out in the wiring. The price is great for this good quality item. Sound is ok, bass is not the greatest but it does a job that is likable.
It hasn't yet, but if it does, short-out in the wiring I won't be so upset. I think I would hate myself more if I did pay $50+ for headphones, and then shorts out in the wiring.

title: Design falls short of previous earbud designs
review: I purchased these earphones for use with my new 3G iPod Shuffle because I was very happy with the Sony earbuds I used with the 2G iPod Shuffle. While the sound quality is comparable, the Y-style design of the cord is terrible because this little thing called gravity gets in the way. The super-long cord is also not fun because I find myself constantly managing it to ensure it doesn't get tangled. In contrast, Sony's over-the-should "OFC neckchain" design in the previous version coupled with the modular approach they took to the cord - approx. 1 foot with an optional 3 foot extension - meant that I could clip the previous iPod on the inside of my coat and be unconstrained by a long cord. Ultimately, the whole idea of a remote that is integrated into the cord feels like a misfire to me. The 2G generation iPod Shuffle plus the older generation of Sony earbuds are far more functional and I'm going back for as long as my old Shuffle will hold out.

title: Comfortable fit perfect
review: Very easy to install Just like the originals. The only thing is around the USB port where you charge your headphones like the original beats there's a little bump or rise in the earbuds that accommodate that little USB port bump. But there's no problems in it It adheres and holds extremely well. when the pads wear out on the earbuds these are a perfect choice and for the price you can't go wrong. Just make sure you line up the two little nipples that stick up with the holes on the new pads.

title: They they fit your ear perfect they don't fall out good battery life good bang for buck
review: I bought these for worth. I normally wear over the ear headphones. But as summer comes it's too hot for that. The fit might you're well they come with many different pieces to fits your ear properly. Sound quality is pretty good for what you get for the price I am happy. They don't fall out.
