The sound quality is find. . . again for meetings. But if you’re wanting to listen to music on the go, then earbuds / headphones are certainly the way to go. I have some nice Sony headphones with active noise cancellation I really love.

The part around the back of the neck has some flex to it. But it’s not what I would call “adjustable”. The side parts are rigid. It’s fairly comfortable.

Very easy to operate. Easy to pair. Can pair to multiple devices.

Made in China.

title: Made in China.  Not a lot of "noise cancelling", but nice sound.
review:
These do to offer true “active noise cancelling” (ANC). Other than simply fitting in your ears to block-out some noise. . .I’m not sure there’s a lot more noise cancelling going on here. I have some “real” noise cancelling headphones which I really like if I’m looking for noise cancelling. Still. . . .I like the overall sound quality of these earbuds. Reasonable base and clear sound. Fit comfortably as well.

These earbuds are Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 60 bucks, they are at least 20 bucks overpriced. . . but. . . overall I like them.

title: Made in China. More features than some other, less expensive, options.
review:
These are not water resistant. . . so. . .If that’s something you need. . . .These will not work for you.

I like these offer one-hand operation. I have others which require two-hands. . . so. . . these are much easier to operate.

These offer 22 channels. Again. . .I have others with 16, so more is better.

They come packaged in two boxes of two walkie-talkies each. They can either be charged using the included charging trays. . or. . .via USB-micro cable (included). Headset is also included, or you can use your own. Wired only. No Bluetooth. Two programmable keys.

The instructions are written really well. Often with Chinese products, the English is not great. . . But this is just fine.

These walkie-talkies are Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 90 bucks, they are a bit more expensive than some other options but they offer more features.

title: Made in China.  MicroSD card is great option.
review:
These headphones are charged with a USB-C cord. A short one is included. It’s great that there is a throttle on the volume. I love that there is the option of using a microSD card, so you don’t have to be connected to anything. (microSD card sold separately) Great for kids without phones. They fit next to the ear, and are quite comfortable.

These headphones are Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of twenty bucks, they are a little overpriced, but overall I like them.

title: Made in China.  "Average" sound quality, at best.
review:
I was expecting more out of these. It does not have the “deep bass” as listed. What it has are a lot of “scratchy highs”. Certainly not a “clear” sound.

The earbuds themselves are ok. . . The case is small and cool. It charges with a micro cord. Short one is included. Wall charger not included.

These earbuds are Made in China. At the price of fifty bucks, they are overpriced for not-so-great quality. Better options, at a lower price, abound.

title: Made in China. Crazy overpriced.
review:
I like that these headphones have a volume throttle. They fit next to the ear and are comfortable. They charge with a USB – C cord. Easy to operate. The sound quality is fine for this sort of headphone.

These headphones are made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 60 bucks they are about 50 bucks overpriced. You can find others between 12 and 15 bucks.

title: Made in China. "Noise isolating" and not "noise canceling". Very pricey.
review:
These are “noise isolating” and not “noise canceling”. There is a big difference. “Noise isolating” is the equivalent of sticking your fingers in your ears. But in this case, instead of your fingers, you are placing earbuds in your ears. The better the earbuds fit… The more noise which will be blocked. Multiple tips are provided so you can get the best fit.

The sound quality of these is decent. Not a lot of bass, but still reasonable.

These earbuds have a very cheap look and feel. They do come with a case, which is nice though.

This item is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 50 bucks they are crazy expensive. A more appropriate price would be no more than 10 bucks.

title: Made in China.  No microSD.  Very nice sound.
review:
On thing these headphones does not offer is a microSD input. But it does offer audio-in. Of course it connects to Bluetooth. . . but. . .if it had microSD (which some other similar headphones offer) then you could listen to music without having to have a phone.

These headphones have really good audio. The volume control is limited, so you can’t make it too loud. But even the bass is nice.

These headphones fit against the ear. They are soft and comfortable.

These headphones are Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. Currently, they are offering a green pair. . under a separate listing. . . which is five bucks less than these.

title: Made in China.  Multiple listening options.  Metallic finish
review:
The ones I have are “Rose Gold”. They have a nice metallic finish, which you can not see in the listing pictures.

I like that these headphones offer multiple listening options. . .Bluetooth. . . microSD (sold separately). . . FM Radio. . . Audio-in.

These headphones fit beside / next to your ears and not around your ears. They are quite comfortable. Nice for younger kids.

These headphones do not offer Noise Cancelling. They sound is quite good. . . especially for the price. Nice bass.

One thing I really don’t like about these headphones is the fact that you can’t read what the buttons are for. Not only that, the on/off switch is not listed at all. . . and it came “on”. . . and I didn’t know that. . .So when I was charging the battery. . . It really did nothing at all and didn’t charge the battery. They are charged by a micro USB cord, and a very short one is included. Wall charger is not included.

These headphones are Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. They are “generic” headphones, so there is no branding on them, and could be sold by any number of different Chinese companies.

title: Made in China.  Issue with "noise cancelling" button.
review:
These headphone fit around your ears. . . depending upon the size of your ears. A little larger / heavier than some, but comfortable.

There isn’t a slot for a microSD card. . . but there is an “audio-in” with cord included. Charging is via USB-C and there is a short cord included. No wall charger.

These headphones come with a nice, hard case with carrying strap.

The bass is ok, but not super great. If you like “thumping” base, then these might not be the headphones for you.

My one “issue” with these headphones is the Noise Cancellation. There is a little sliding tab on the bottom of the right side to turn this feature on/off. With most other headphones I have tried. . . even when there is a similar tab. . . When you turn the headphones on, the noise cancelling is on, as long as the tab is in the on position. When you turn the headphones off. . . then the headphones are off as is (of course) noise cancelling. Not so with these headphones. When you turn the headphones off. . . . noise cancelling is still on. You have to turn that switch off as well. If you neglect to do that. . then noise cancelling stays on, and uses-up battery.

These headphones are Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of eighty bucks. . they are double the price they should be.

title: Made in China.  Nice for the price.  microSD card (sold separately) Nice for kids.
review:
For inexpensive headphones. . .These are really not bad at all. They are especially nice for kids. . .because you can use a microSD card (sold separately) and do not have to have a cell phone. But you can connect via Bluetooth as well.

The box shows “Extra Bass”. I don’t really find that to be the case. It has “nice base”, but I wouldn’t call it “extra”.

Charging is via micro cord. Short one included.

Easy to operate. Comfortable over-the-ear design.

These headphones are Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon.

title: No Noise Cancellation.  Made in China.
review:
First of all. . .These are NOT “Noise Cancelling”. There is nothing in the information about it. . . and other than the fact that you have something in your ears. . . there is no noise cancelling. . . So the listing is incorrect. . .But Chinese companies know that it sells better if they say they have noise cancelling.

There are a lot of earbuds that simply go into your ears, and that’s it. These not only go into your ears. . . but. . .there is a loop that goes behind your ears. I actually like that because they are more secure. They are comfortable.

The sound is very good. . . especially for earbuds in this price range. Nice base too.

Comes with a short USB-C cord. . .Extra earbuds for sizing. . . and short carrying / wrist cord.

These earbuds are Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon.

title: Made in China. Decent but way overpriced.
review:
I have what’s being called “Red”. But as you can see from the listening pictures… It’s really more of a rust or clay color. They look exactly like the listing pictures.

These are not the easiest earbuds to get out of the case. There are plastic strips along the bottom which need to be removed before charging.

Though they offer some “noise canceling”… It’s not that great, but better than nothing.

The sound quality of these is fine. There is reasonable basis. Not too challenging to operate. They are charged using a USB-C cord and a short one is included.

These earbuds are made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 135 bucks they are over double the price they should be. I have some others that were around 35 bucks and work just as well as these.

title: Nice enough ,but not that easy to operate.  Made in China.
review:
Though these earbuds are nice enough. . . The instructions certainly leave something to be desired. They are Chinese on one side and English on the other. They are auto-on when you remove them from the case. If you remove them from your ears. . . they music will stop. The earbuds detect if you’re wearing them or not.

These earbuds indeed offer noise cancelling. Some advertise that they do. . . but in reality they don’t. Not so with these. You can turn the noise cancelling on or off. See the instructions where it shows ANC.

Additional earbuds are included for proper fit.

These earbuds are Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon.

title: Nice for the price. Made in China. Nice overall sound quality.
review:
This listing is for several different items. I have the Red B39 headphones. 430 bucks they are not bad. These headphones fit over the ear and not around the ear. Though they honestly feel a little cheap, and make a “cracking” noise when you open them… This sound is actually quite good. And in the end, I guess that’s what it’s all about… The sound. There is nice base, which is missing from many low-end headphones. I like the fact that you cannot only use this with Bluetooth, but you can also use a microSD card (sold separately) as well.

These headphones are made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon.

title: Made in China. Better than expected. Multiple ways to listen.
review:
These kids’ headphones are actually better than expected. They fit comfortably over the ear, but not around the ear. The headband is adjustable. The ears actually flash multiple colors. The sound quality is actually quite good, even the base, for a kids headset such as this.

I really like the fact that there are multiple options for connecting. You have Bluetooth… 3.5 mm jack… FM Radio…And microSD card. I find the microSD card to be especially nice because you can load lots of music onto it without having to be connected to Bluetooth. So a kid does not have to have their own cell phone to be able to use these headphones. Note that the microSD card is sold separately.

This headset comes with a short micro cord for charging. There is no AC wall charger, so you will need to have that on your own.

This headset is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current cost of 24 bucks I think is a little bit expensive for what it is, but overall I quite like it.

title: Okay for the price. Made in China. Not a lot of base. Not noise canceling.
review:
Other than having something stuck in your ear, these earbuds are not noise canceling. Though they are listed as such. Nothing on the information included with the earbuds shows that they are noise canceling either.

These earbuds charge with a USB – C cord. A short when is included. An AC wall charger is not included. 2 smaller sized earbuds are included. But they are stuck at the bottom of a black box where the charging cord is also located, so make sure you look for them.

The instructions are written and very small almost micro print. They are touch operated.

I guess you could say the sound quality is “reasonable” for earbuds at this price point. But there is not a lot a base.

These earbuds are made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon.

title: Here what's going on around you. Made in China. Great sound.
review:
I think the most important thing to note, right off the bat, is that these are NOT noise canceling earbuds. You are supposed to be able to hear what is going on around you… Car horn… People talking… Bike bell… Siren… And bear growling behind you. ;-)

For this type of earbud, the sound quality is amazing. Sometimes, with earbuds such as this, you don’t get a lot of base. Not so with these. It has very nice base and also treble.

They stay in place very well. They are also very easy to operate.

My only “issue” with them is the fact that the charger and case are not one. You have a nice magnetic case, but the charger is separate. They really should have made it altogether, even if that made the case a little thicker. Also, the charger and USB cord are one. Again, it would’ve been nice if they simply had either a micro cord or a USB – C cord that you could connect to the case and easily charge.

Made in China.

title: Works great on both 4 and 5
review: I had the PS 4. . .then got the 5. . . and these headphones works well on both.  Easy to set-up. . . Great sound. . . fit well over my ears.

title: Steller earbuds, for the price.  Nice base.  . .Snug fit.
review:
These are really quite amazing earbuds. First of all, the sound is really great. There is very nice base. Granted, I think the base is a little bit better on some Sony headphones that I have. . but. .those are headphones, and not earbuds. . .plus . . they are twice the price. So for the sound / base of these earbuds. . . I’m quite happy.

Cool box for charging. USB-C cable (included) to charge.

Fit really well. I’ve never had earbuds quite like these, so I was a bit concerned with one falling-out and losing it. . . but. . they fit snug.

FYI. . . You must use both of them. You can not use only one. My brother is deaf in one ear, so these would not work that great for him, for example.

The noise cancelling is very nice. Also pairing was a breeze. There is an app, if you wish to download it, for more control.

title: Unable to pair with Apple AirPods
review:
I had difficulty pairing this with Apple AirPods. I ended up having to pair it with a different headset to make it work.

I like the compact size, the fact that you can be a passenger in a car and others can’t hear. But better instructions would really help.

If you look around on Amazon, you will see that there are different (Chinese) companies selling this same product. So you might just want to check and see who is offering the best price before purchasing.

title: Great Sound. . . Great Experience
review:
The Jabra Elite 75t has exceptional battery life of 7.5 hours of constant use, which also helps with wireless connectivity. I used these in the gym where I experienced almost no Bluetooth hiccups when I traveled several feet away from my connected phone, which is notoriously difficult on true wireless earbuds. Even though these earbuds do not have active noise cancellation, the sound quality is of high quality. The option of a button press on the left earbud allows you pause the sound to allow someone to talk to you. The Jabra Sound+ App allows you to customize the hearing experience, also has EQ settings that allow you to tweak the sound to your liking.
The snug fit really helps buds stay in your ears securely and also promotes the best sound out of them with improved bass performance. And these do have very good sound quality for true wireless if you can get that tight seal. Having volume controls on the buds is a great option which you can press and hold the button on the left earbud to lower volume and press and hold the button on the right earbud to raise the volume.

Overall, the Jabra 75t is a great earbud with quality sound for the much more reasonable price than the Apple Airpod Pro. I highly recommend these Jabra 75t earbuds.

title: Very Basic.  Short Battery Life.
review:
This almost goes without saying. . .but. . . If you have a laptop without a DVD drive, then you’re much better-off purchasing an external DVD drive (for less money) than this portable DVD player. Having said that. . . If you really want a portable DVD player. . . here’s some information on this one.

The player is lightweight. 2.8#. It measures 10.25” X 7.25” X 1.5”, when closed.

The screen quality is fairly good, but you have to be looking at it straight-on. So it’s really just for one person to watch. The sound quality is not very good, but there is an AV out, so if you have wired headphones or speaker, that will work. There is no Bluetooth.

This portable DVD player does not have “DVD memory”, so it will not start playing where you last stopped.

Basic functions are on the player itself. A lot more functions are on the included remote.

The screen will swivel, which makes it so you can attach it to the headrest of a car (with included strap) if you wish.

There is only a two-hour battery life, so you may not make it through an entire movie, depending upon the movie length. It comes with a car charge, but it’s only 49” long, so it may. . .or may not work in your car.

This unit will not play Blu-Ray DVD’s, but most portable DVD players don’t.

In the end, this is a very cheap, lower-end of the pricing, portable DVD player Made in China.

title: Overall great product.
review: Made in Stockholm Sweden. The first thing I noticed about these sport headphones the packaging. I know the packaging has nothing to do with the performance of the product, but I must say that Adidas has done a superb job with the packaging of the product, both aesthetically and utilitarian. Inside the nice dark gray box you find the headphones wrapped in tissue paper with an Adidas logo’d tape piece holding them to the paper. Underneath the headphones is a tabbed divider that contains the additional sized ear wings, tips, and charging cord. Underneath that divider is the Quick Start booklet. Instructions are simple and straight forward. When I put the earpieces in my ears, they fit comfortably, like a glove, making a very good and perfect seal. This works wonderfully in keeping sweat out of the ears during exercise. The sound was excellent. Playing music was enjoyable. Buttons are easy to use in pausing and adjusting volume. Receiving calls is easy and has great quality sound. They look great, feel great, sound great.

title: Use it on my computer, and it's great!
review:
I have the B450-XT.

I actually use this on my computer, and not my phone. I use Dragon Naturally Speaking software. With other headsets I’ve tried, I was unable to have music playing in the background, because the headset would pick it up, and “confuse” the Dragon software. This doesn’t happen with this headset, and Dragon works great without any “issues”.

I also use this headset for Zoom and Skype calls. All worry-free.

Because of the long battery life, and the standby mode, I can just turn it in and forget about it.

Because I use this with my computer, and not my phone, I don’t use the “Parrot Button”. Having said that, I know that it can be configured for some voice-activated commands.

title: A little pricey, but it works well with Dragon Professional Individual.
review: To be quite honest this headset has a very cheap look and feel. Having said that, it works. I use Dragon Professional Individual, and it works without a problem. It has a USB – 3 connector. The cord is just over 6 feet long. There are no instructions, it is just plug and play. It’s comfortable enough to wear for extended periods. I wish there were some control buttons on the cord. Or on the headset itself. Such as mute. Nonetheless you can do most of this through the software anyway. Though this is marketed specifically for Dragon software, it really can be used as a general headset for all applications.

title: Make sure you download the app.  Not noise cancelling, but still very good sound.
review:
When I first received these, the B&O app was not available for these earphones. Honestly, I was less than impressed with the sound. But after a couple of days it became available on the app, and then I was able to make adjustments to the way I like it. . . and now. .. I’m a happy camper. . . .mostly.

Some things to note:

They are 23” long, end-to-end. Perhaps it’s just my “thick” neck, but I wish they were an inch or so longer. They “pull” sometimes.

The cord looks / feels like nylon. As such, I’m afraid it’s going to get “mucky”, eventually. I wish it were smooth.

The charging cable is a “proprietary” sort of thing, and only it can be used for charging.

There are lots of different earbuds, so you should be able to find some that will work for your ears.

They are not “noise-cancelling”. Nonetheless, they still sound quite good.

There are magnets attached to each end. . . You put them together and it turns them off. Though that’s a nice feature. .. if you think you’re going to wear them around your neck that way with them off. . .I wouldn’t recommend it. The magnet is not that strong, and you could very easily lose them.

title: Simple. . . . Comfortable. . . Great sound quality.  Made in China.
review: I’ll be honest, I don’t know how you could find a nicer, simpler, more comfortable and easy to use headset than this. I’ve owned several bluetooth headsets of various brands and styles and I think I like this one the best. It fit over my ear easier than most and the earpiece that fits inside the ear is so comfortable. It’s nice looking and is extremely simple to pair. Just turn it on, open Bluetooth on the phone and locate the Jabra Talk 25 device, touch it on the screen and you’re connected. The free Jabra Assist app has features that locate the headset if lost and the user manual, which is intuitive and easy to understand, is also located in the app. A quick start guide book comes inside the box and really, if you’ve ever used a Bluetooth headset before, you really don’t need anything else. If you’re completely new to them, the user manual is very simple to understand. The sound quality is excellent.  Made in China.

title: For the price, these are fine.  They stay in place.
review: These come with three different size earbuds. .  .and that’s a good thing, as “one-size-fits-all” usually doesn’t fit me.  They are very easy to change-out, and area made of silicone.  Of course with the over-the-ear hook, they stay in place.  I’ve tried some other “sport” headphones, which didn’t have the over-the-ear hook, but they just didn’t stay in place.  The cord is 45”.  The sound quality is decent for this price point.  They are Made in China.

title: Case not included.  Very nice overall though
review: These earbuds are Made in China.  They come with three different “buds” so you can match them to your ears.  They are 26” long total.  There is a little “loop” that gathers the cord together.  (see the current 4th picture in the listing)  They do not come with a case (wish they did).  The sound quality is very good, for a headset of this type / cost.  Easy to make phone calls, and both I and the person I called could hear just fine.  I love not having the long cord connected to my phone, which always gets in the way.  Very happy with these.

title: Great in oh so many ways. .  .
review: Though I know that this headset can be used for VOIP calls (Skype and such), I don’t use them for that.  I use them as everyday wireless earphones.  They work really well for me.  They were very easy to pair to my phone.  Because they go around the back of your neck, there’s not a cord to hand in your way, especially when working-out.  The noise cancelling is certainly the best part.  It allows me to listing to my music, very nice-and-clear, by the way. . . . without have other “outside interference”.  I’ve also used it for calls and both I and the person I’m talking to can hear the conversation without any problems.

title: As long as you know what you're purchasing. . . "basic" earbuds. . . they are fine
review: This is a pair of Amazon Basics brand in ear headphones with mic. They are a brightly colored hot pink that definitely stand out. If you are looking for a color that sticks out then this would be a good color choice. They come with 3 size buds for your ear. The typical small, medium, and large bulbs that you can attach and detach as needed. They are about 51 inches long from ear buds to the end of the plug. It comes with a mic, but you are able to use them for output audio only if you wish.  Made in China.

title: Comfortable Fit - They stay in my ears!
review: I absolutely love this pair of Bluetooth earphones. The first thing that I love is how they fit. The extra ergonomic sport design with extra tips helps keep the buds in my ears. These are capable of going in my ear and staying in without having to insert the small bulb so far in my ear. Some other brands I have had to put them in so far to keep them to stay it was like inserting an ear plug, which muffles the sound and completely diminishes the quality. These stay in my ear without muffling. Great! The second thing is the distance. It says there is a 10 meter range and I think this is perfect for my needs. I tested them by walking around a two bedroom apartment with two floors, and I was able to hear the music everywhere I walked. Upstairs or downstairs through walls, doors, and the floor. Great! Then I tested them by walking down the hall and I was able to get apartments away before it started to break up. The controls are easy to use and instructions are easy to follow. You should note the English instructions are not on the first page, but they are about a quarter way through. You may be tempted to get some Bluetooth buds that do not have a wire and are completely free, but I would suggest against it. In my opinion these are better and the wire that connects the two are not an issue.  I definitely recommend these.  Made in China.

title: Not really for strenuous exercise
review: The first thing I will comment on is the instructions. They are presented as pictures only. There is more than enough room on each page to include a sentence or two describing the action being taught. I understand they are trying to present directions in a way that anyone can understand regardless of one’s native location and language. However, it is not an outrageous request to have words with pictures. The sound is great, but this depends a lot on how you will have them stay in your ear. For me, even with the smallest size rubber bud, I have to insert them in my ear like I would an earplug to get them to stay in. Therefore, the sound is as you would expect if you had earplugs in while wearing a set of headphones over your ears. If you let them rest in your ear then they are bound to fall out. For my ear, they will not stay in while doing a lot of physical activity. If you are working out at home or in a gym on a stationary bike then this would suffice. If you run outside and pound the concrete then you would be concerned about one falling off and getting lost. Another side note is that the left ear bud will only play when the right bud is in (or very close). I will use them mostly while sitting at my computer listening to music or podcasts.  Made in China.

title: Handy gadget!
review: This 5 way multi headphone splitter is something worth having. Even if you do not use it every day it is likely to come in handy at some point. If you have kids and you travel a lot then this is very useful. You can let them share one iPad or one portable DVD player and they can each plug into the headphones. This means you can let them listed to their own movie or music while you listen to your own. You may never need to have 5 listeners at once, but it is good to know you have the option if needed. Nice product. Made in China.

title: Nice, but you might also consider Plantronics
review:
If you’re one of the few people. . . like me. . . who still has a landline.. . This device can be quite helpful. I work from home, and find a landline best for my needs. But I have several international clients, so being able to talk to them via Skype, without having to change headsets, is really nice. I’ve used a very similar headset with a different system, so I’m used to it. But if you haven’t used something like this before, then it might feel kind of heavy. The one thing that this system is missing is cell phone connection. I’ve used a Plantronics system in the past that I quite liked which has all three. . . landline. . . VoIP. . . and cell phone. . . . It’s slightly more expensive, but if you use all three, then it’s worth the money. Below is a link to one such system. But they offer a couple of different ones.

[[ASIN:B005FSJ6PM Savi W720 (83544-01) Dect Head]]

title: Expected better from Pioneer
review: These earphones were a disappointment in the sound quality and fit.  I thought they were a good value, but you get what you pay for. The earphones that come free with the purchase of a new cell phone has a much clearer tone then these. The over the ear hook works, but I found it bothersome and the buds kept popping out of my ear while I was exercising.  For some strange reason I expected earphones with the name PIONEER on it to sound and function much, much better. I found them to be frustrating and took away from exercising experience rather than enhancing it. Sorry to say they did not work well for me.

title: Awesome!
review: These are the nicest in-ear headphones I have ever seen or used. I listen to my music everyday in one form or another. I go to the gym first thing in the morning, sometimes I listen to music at work, while I clean house, and doing yard work. I have tried a number of in-ear headphones over the years, but have never invested in a quality set. The clarity, design, ergonomic fit of these are so superior to anything that I have ever worn before. I was very surprised at what a difference these would make in my music experience.  This is one of the best music up-grades that I have ever made. As much time as I spend with my in-ear headphones, it makes so much sense to invest in a quality experience. They are packaged so beautifully that I my first thought was these would make a wonderful gift. They come in a black box with a magnetic closure. When you open the box, the in-ear headphones and accessories are on one side and the left side is the unique design drawings of the headphones.(very cool) In addition to the headphones, you get 8 different foam tips so that you get the perfect fit. There is a gorgeous black leather carrying case with red stitching and the "1MORE" logo embossed on the front of the case. There are two other connection devices that I am unfamiliar with in the packaging. The instruction booklet is difficult to follow. Overall these are fantastic headphones and the best in-ear experience that I have ever had. They are awesome!

title: Really nice. . . for the price
review: First of all, you get what you pay for.  Plain-and-simple.  These are very inexpensive earbuds.  Having said that, I think the sound quality, for the price paid, is quite good.  They fit well enough, again for the price, though I would never use them working out, as they tend to come loose with too much moving around.  These are a great option to have for an extra pair. . . or for kids, when you have to replace them more frequently and don’t want to invest in something more costly.  Again, overall, for the price, I think they are quite nice.

title: Great Sound. . . Great Function. . .
review:
Right out of the box the first thing I thought was "Simplicity!" That's a very good thing. Instructions: simple. Headphones themselves: simple. Earpieces: simple. Bose Connect app: simple. Bluetooth pairing: simple. It has a very nice zippered case to carry what few simple items come with it, the device and the charging cord. Really, once you figure out what size earpiece you need, I see no need to carry the others. Now, fit and comfortability. These earpieces are SO comfortable, soft, and easy to fit into the ear. The medium size that where installed out of the box fit me perfectly. The power button on top of the right side was very easy to feel and operate. The right side of the cord houses the function button piece and microphone for calls. Unlike some wireless headphones I've tried, this function piece is very light and doesn't feel "weighty" on that side at all. The sound is very good. When the music goes silent, I did hear a very slight buzzing in the background, but it didn't really detract when listening. The only drawbacks were that the app did not have an equalizer function to adjust the tone. That's a pretty big deal for me, but I have to tell you, I LOVE these headphones!

I'll give them four stars instead of five, only for the lack of eq function.

title: More comfortable than some of a similar style
review: These earphones are fairly easy to put on once you get used to them.  The actual bud that fits into the ear has about a half inch of adjustability up and down within the piece that goes around the ear. Most earbuds I've used, after about a half hour of having them in my ear, make my ear fairly sore. These have proven to be pretty comfortable, even over some extended (1 hour +) use. They do have an excellent sound quality.  I have found the button on the microphone that is used to engage a call when received, has taken a little getting used to, as it's a little harder to push than most ear bud set-ups I've used, but it works fine.

title: Not An Ounce of Bass to be Had.
review: I usually like Philips products. . .  but this one is not one of those.  There is absolutely no bass from these headphones.  None. . . zilch. . . nada. . . . zip.  Never in my life have I ever used headphones that have zero bass.  I’ve used plenty that didn’t have a lot.  But this is the first that has absolutely none.  I like the design. . . I like the feel. . . I like everything about them.. . but without bass, they are really useless to me.

title: GREAT Headphones at a GREAT Price!
review: I LOVE these headphones!  They fit my head / ears perfectly.  Extremely comfortable.  The sound quality is really great.  Plenty of bass, which I really like.  Not a lot of ambient noise with the over-the-ear design.  They are “stylish” without being “crazy odd”.  The included cord is the perfect length for me.  It’s also detachable, which is a nice feature.  At the current price point, they are a very good option.  The in-line mic is a nice feature.  You’re able to answer calls without taking your phone out.

title: WAY too Expensive for “Made in China”…But a GREAT Item to Have.
review:
First of all, the product dimensions listed on Amazon are incorrect. It’s just a hair more than 5” long. About 2.75” tall and a hair over 1.5” wide. It fits easily into a pocket.

When you don’t have cell service. . . . this little gadget could be a lifesaver.

Here’s what the information shows that came with the radio:

DC Power Outlet: 5V, 2.5W maximum output power.
Light: 2 lumens
Radio time after 1-min of cranking: 10-minutes
Radio time after fully charged: 2.5-hours
Please Note: I do not know how long it takes to crank it to “fully charges” but elsewhere in the information it shows that you should not crank it more than 5-minutes if it is still operating, and not more than 10-minutes if it’s completely dead

Also, there is an earphone jack.

The light, though not that bright, is certainly a nice feature. The radio works just fine for what this item is for. . . and emergency. It can be turned-up really loud.

It’s very simple to operate.

Overall it’s a very nice item to have. . . . but. . . . at the current price. . . it’s WAY too expensive for “Made in China”.

title: Great for "Gamers", but not for "general use".
review:
This is not a headset for those looking for something “easy”. If that’s what you’re looking for, then you might be better served with Beats Wireless or other wireless headset.

I think this headset is easiest explained if you compare it to a TV. With a TV you can connect your DVD player to it. . .a TiVo box to it. . .perhaps a Roku device to it. . . and so on. Then you use the input button to switch between them. It’s similar with this headset. There is a “box” which you plug-in to the power. Then you set-up the “box” to work with your computer and game box(es).

The sound quality is fine with plenty of bass. The headset is comfortable to wear. There is a built-in microphone which you can pull-out if desired, which is convenient.

One nice feature is that two batteries are included. One can be in the headset and the other charging in the “box” so you will never run out of power.

You can “share” the audio with someone by connection to the headset, which is kind of cool.

Overall it’s a nice headset, and I’m sure “gamers” will love it. . . but again. . . if you’re simply looking for a headset for “general use”, then this is not the one for you.

title: For use with the Savi 700 series
review: I have a Savi 700 series headset, and after much searching I found that these are the headset accessories for my Plantronics headset.  Though I needed only one of the replacement parts, you receive the entire "collection".  If you happen to work with others using the same headset then perhaps others in your office can use some of the other pieces.  Make 100% sure that these are the ones which will work for your headset before ordering.  A lot of the Plantronics "buds" look alike, but they are "headset specific".

title: Not perfect, but I'm VERY happy...especially for the price.
review:
Very good, for the price. I have a different Bluetooth headset and these put them to shame. They are comfortable, sound "fine" for everyday use and have a long battery life. There's a battery indicator both on the headset, and it also shows on the device it's paired to.

Another thing I really like is that it comes with a hard-shell case. Really great to have this.

If there's a "con" for me, it would be that they don't fit very "tight". Meaning . . If you bend-over, then they are probably going to fall forward. I'm a guy with what I would assume is an "average" head size and this is one thing that kind of gets on my nerves at times, but I deal with it. These are certainly not the type of headset that you would want to use while working-out.

Another "con" is the fact that when you extend them, the "extension" portion is metal. Honestly, I think it would have looked better if it were white plastic. If they are not extended, then they look pretty cool. . . but when you extend them, and the metal is showing. . . not-so-much.

Overall, I'm quite happy with this headset. LOVE Bluetooth, so there are no wires. If you're looking for "exceptional" sound, then you probably want to look elsewhere, but I'm quite happy.

title: Not the most comfortable, but overall very nice
review:
I've been wanting some Bluetooth headphones for a while.. . but they were either too expensive, or didn't have the best reviews. Then along came this item.

Overall, I'm very pleased with them. Honestly, they are not the most comfortable things in the world (which is why I give them 4-stars) and they also feel a bit "cheap". . . but. . . they work. . . and in the end, that's all that matters.

These are certainly not some high-end product with perfect sound. They are an inexpensive item with "acceptable" sound. I've started walking, and I have always hated having a cord when listening to music on my iPod Touch. This item has really fit-the-bill for me, and I enjoy them immensely. Not having to mess with a cord is just SO much better.

I haven an AC charger, which charges very quickly. The "kit" I have is Innergie mMini Combo which allows you to charge two things at once.

[[ASIN:B005SNKTK0 Innergie mMini Combo 15W AC, 10W Auto and Dual USB Duo Travel Charging Kit (TADP-10BE AA)]]

title: Great Price for a Great Product
review:
There is so much to like about this item. First of all, though you can use it anywhere you like, it's really made for car travel. One might say that you can use a laptop. . . . or if you have a "fancy" car it might already come with a DVD player. . . Well. . . This unit is really for the "rest of us". The one I have is the 7" model, though I see now that there are duel-screens and a 9" model. There are two headphones. That could be a problem if you have more than two kids. .. and I don't really see a way to add more.

For the price, I really don't see how you can beat it. If you can afford it, you might want to "splurge" on the duel (2) screen model.

title: Not a huge fan. . .
review:
I wanted a Bluetooth headset for my computer for when I use Skype. I've used several headsets, which fit in the ear, for "regular" land line phones without a problem. I should say that I don't have a cellphone with Bluetooth, nor have I ever used a Bluetooth headset in the past. I see a lot of people with them. . . and most of them look really bad/silly.

Here are my "issues" with this headset. . .

First, it's not comfortable in the ear.

The little metal bar that goes around your ear isn't comfortable either. It's cheap too. Just a piece of wire.

Confusing. .. Press this button this many times this fast to answer a call. . . hang-up. . . etc. . . They really need to make it much simpler to operate.

On the "plus" side, the battery does last a long time. . . and the sound quality is fine. But . . for me. .because it's just not comfortable to wear. .. I'll stick to a headset that I plug into my computer.

title: Good sound quality. Comfortable fit.
review: I’m really impressed with these. My husband drives a concrete mixer and spends a fair amount of time sitting at job sites in his truck waiting for the crew to be ready for him to pour. He uses that time to catch up on podcasts, make calls or just listen to music so he needs a good pair of earbuds to accomplish that. The noise cancellation is excellent. If it can block out the sound of the truck it could probably block out just about anything. Another great feature of these that’s surprisingly difficult to find is the ability to use them individually. Plenty of pairs allow you to use the right one but both of these connect independently so you can use left or right by itself. The sound quality is great and the equalizer in the app really lets you fine tune to your preference. Battery life is excellent. He can use these for several days on one charge, though it’s lengthened a bit since he switches back and forth between the two earbuds. Overall these are really great earbuds.

title: Took a little getting used to but I love them!
review: The first time I put these earbuds in I hated them. They felt weird in my ears and I kept thinking they were going to fall out. These are unlike any buds I’ve ever used and they took some getting used to before I appreciated them for those differences. The main thing that took time was the fit. They take practice to get them in your ears correctly and that is largely dependent on choosing the right size tip. That was my mistake  at first. I always used the smallest tips on other buds so I went straight for them with this pair. Once I switched to a larger size I was good to go. These fit inside your ear with the tip pointing to the canal and I now find them to be very comfortable. These are not earbuds that try to be discreet. When you’re wearing them it’s obvious because they’re fairly large, flat circles sticking out of your ears. I wear them at home 99% of the time so I really don’t care but I really appreciate the surface area of the buds. The controls work super well. I really love being able to swipe up or down for volume control. Sound quality is great and easy to customize in the Surface Audio app, which is user friendly and helpful. I love that you can use just one of these earbuds. I have a toddler and need an open ear so I only use one bud at a time. I like being able to switch ears and a lot of earbuds don’t have that feature. This pair switches back and forth seamlessly. These are really nice and the unique design makes them easy to use. I’m very happy with them.

title: Comfortable headset with personalized sound
review: This is the best headset I’ve ever used hands down, and I’ve tried a lot of them over the years. They’re super comfortable, even for longer periods of time, and don’t make your ears feel hot. The sound quality is fantastic. The companion app allows you to customize the equalizer settings or choose different modes for podcasts, music or movies. One of my favorite things about this set is the Personal Sound technology. It’s completely personalized. It will play a bunch of different tones and ask you if you can hear it. Once you’ve gone through the process on both ears, which takes just a couple minutes total, it creates a sound profile for you. Everything sounds so nice through this headset. The noise cancellation is great. It’s nice to be able to focus on what I’m watching or listening to without any outside disruptions. I’m a huge fan of this headset and how much it has elevated my listening experience.

title: Good sound quality with ambient noise option
review: I have tried a lot of different earbuds and this pair is one of my favorites. The sound quality is really nice and voices sound balanced. The ambient noise feature is one I haven’t seen on other pairs but is great. I have a toddler so I need to be able to hear what’s going on around me all the time. A must have option for me is being able to use just one earbud. These pair separately so it’s easy to use only one and to switch them out. The charging case is small and charged wirelessly or with a cord. The buds fit in magnetically and are held securely. The Tone Free app allows you to customize the sound, check the battery level and even find your earbuds if you’ve misplaced them, another nice thing with a toddler in the home. One thing I don’t care for though is that you can’t access any of the info unless the case is open or the earbuds are out. So you cannot find the whole case if you lose it somewhere, only the earbuds. Aside from that, I like everything about these. They’re comfortable to wear, pair quickly and consistently and stay connected for a good distance from my phone. Definitely recommend these.

title: Sound quality is nice but features are lacking
review: I will start by saying I’m a long time fan of Yamaha. That being the case, I expect much more from these earbuds...especially at this price point. The sound quality is nice and on par with other products from this brand I’ve used in the past. Call quality is pretty good as well and they don’t make your voice sound like you’re underwater. They’re easy to pair and connect consistently. They’re lightweight and quickly become an afterthought once they’ve been in your ears for a few minutes. While I enjoy how light they are, they feel slightly cheap. The case is terrible. The magnets don’t hold well at all. My husband uses these for work and frequently complains about having to dig for the earbuds in his bag because they’ve fallen out of the case. The lack of an ambient noise option is also an issue since you have to remove them to hear what’s going on around you or talk to someone. I could overlook these things if the price was a bit lower, but at $130 they’re just too expensive for a basic pair of earbuds with decent sound quality.

title: Perfect for active people
review: These earbuds are fantastic. Everything about them screams quality. They took a little getting used to since they fit inside your ear, but after a day or two I couldn’t tell they were there. Once you’ve put them in your ears they’re not going anywhere until you remove them, so they’re perfect for running or hiking. Setup was easy and the Jaybird app is really well designed. You can adjust the equalizer, find your earbuds if you’ve lost or misplaced them and learn everything there is to know about your earbuds. Battery life is great. They only dropped around 10% after a couple hours of use. These are great earbuds that will really come in handy when I workout and go on hikes.

title: Awesome!
review: These are so awesome! For starters, they’re super comfortable. I actually forgot I had them in a couple of times. The sound quality is perfect and the work just as they’re supposed to. They charge really quickly and last for hours of use. There’s a gaming mode you can switch to that really brings life to the experience. They’re very easy to operate though if I had to choose something I didn’t like it would be that there is no volume control on the earbuds. But that’s just nitpicking and doesn’t matter to me. They look really cool too. They’re silver and futuristic. I’m really enjoying these.

title: Wow! Super Impressed!
review: Absolutely super happy with these SoundPEATS mini pro earbuds. Fantastic sound quality. The richness if the sound is amazing. I love instrumental music, like classical and movie themes and I am thrilled with the quality of the sound which makes the music I enjoy even more amazing. Earbuds charge up nicely and are comfortable in my ears. Love these earbuds. Highly recommend.

title: Beautiful Sound But...
review: I like these Alto & Bass Bluetooth wireless earbuds but the left one refuses to work. They are definitely fully charged, on and hooked up to Bluetooth and the sound is amazing but no sound in the left one. Otherwise they are comfortable, fit nicely in my ear and have a nice small case.

title: Good Sound
review: I really like these earbuds.  To start I kind of had to wiggle them around on my phone to get good sound. I was getting a scratchy feedback. Very comfortable in the ear though.  Good sound and I love the carrying case which keeps the earbuds safe in my purse. Great product.

title: Wow Excellent Sound
review: These Panasonic deep bass wireless Bluetooth headphones are amazing. After charging them I synched them with my iphone and played some of my favorite music.  The sound was clear and lovely and the bass was amazing. I am so loving these. Best headphones ever!

title: Awesome Wireless Headphones
review: LOVE LOVE LOVE  the House of Marley, Smile Jamaica Wireless Headphones. They are amazing. I played some of my favorite movie music and Lady Gaga and Adele. The sound is so pure and beautiful with these headphones. The violin music in Schindlers List was awesome with these headphones. The neck piece makes it easy to turn up the volume and is comfortable. These are just excellent!!!

title: Awesome Sound
review: The sound from the V-MODA Forza In-Ear hybrid Sport Headphones is excellent. In the package you are given several sizes of rubber earbuds (the little black rubber attachments if that is what they are called) also different in ear plastic shaped holders to keep the headphones in your ears when running. The sound is just awesome, full and beautiful. I am thrilled with the quality of the sound with these headphones. High quality.

title: Super Sound
review: The TDK Life on Record WR680 Wireless Bluetooth headset is excellent. Perfect crisp sound. Directions are easy to follow. I charged it as soon as I got it out of the box. Easy to set Bluetooth to phone or iPad. I listened to some music and then watched a movie and enjoyed the sound. The headset is quite comfortable and light. Great product and priced right.

title: Great Sound!!!
review: I love these earphones. Great bass sound. They are a comfortable fit sealing out the outside noise. I plugged these into my portable dvd player and the sound from the background music on the movie I was watching was so pure and beautiful of course along with the dialog of the movie. Totally recommend these earphones. Best Ever!!

title: This Hard Case is a great holder for AfterShokz
review: My wife and I prefer our AfterShokz and to that end want to protect them. This RLSOCO Hard Case for AfterShokz (and others) lets us do that. This is a hard case and only fits one headset at a time. It looks great - the outside material is attractive - and the inside is made form fitted to hold a headset and a small mesh spot holds the charger. It comes with a handle-like thing for hooking onto a suitcase or bag. Being hard it’ll protect the headsets from being smashed in a bag or suitcase. We have only tried and would only try one headset at a time - it appears two would not work, thought there is room in there. Overall we are thrilled with this case and would get a second to use for trips or work away from home. Very happy with the RLSOCO Hard Case for AfterShokz (and others).

title: Novel
review: This is pretty novel.  It brings back memories of the 80s when see through phones and other electronics were all the rage.  This is cool.  You can see through it and even the headphones are clear.

title: Sounds Pretty Good
review: These sound great but I prefer wired headphones.  No matter, they still work great and sound good too.  They paired easily with my laptop.

title: Easy To Program
review: This is a tiny little radio and it's very light so it fits easily into pocket or purse and travels well.  It is easy to tune and sounds pretty good too.  However i use regular over ear headphones with this because i have a hard time keeping earbuds in.

title: Great
review:
I am one of these who doesn't like wireless headphones or earbuds, so my only alternative is to use over the ear headphones. These are great because they are longer and I can reach my stereo if I want to without having to either move closer to it or move it closer to me.

The connections are tight and there does not appear to be any kind of a signal loss. The nylon cord also keeps it tangle free which is also a plus.

title: Great Sound
review: I am one of these people who prefers over the ear headphones to the in ear type.  These fit great in my CD player and sounded great.  I love Panasonic products, have for years and these are the same quality I have come to expect from all my Panasonic electronics I have had over the years.

title: Nice For Playing My Vintage Tapes
review: I got this mainly so I could listen to some of my older cassette tapes I have.  It plays them nice and they sound great. I did however hook it up to a stereo system rather than listen with earbuds.  It works great.

title: Very Easy To Use
review: This is very easy to use and actually work without reading the instructions.  It's great for meetings, taking notes, and even ghost hunting!  You can put in an optional TF card and even use it like an MP3 player if you wish, if you add optional headphones.  It comes in a convenient tin carrying box.

title: Awesome
review: This is an awesome CD player.  The best thing about it is the fact that it has a reghargeable battery so you never have to worry about buying new batteries when you run them down from listening to music a lot. It looks and sounds nice and is easy to use.  It does not come with a belt clip or anything so it's probably not ideal for jogging or walking with your music but you can at least put it in a bag or purse and listen that way I suppose.  I'm not too fond of earbud headphones so I used a pair of over the ear types that I had.  This makes a great gift for any music lover too.

title: Second Player From This Company
review:
This is the second CD player I have purchased from Byron Statics. It is just like the other one I have, only a different color.

It is very simple to use and takes two AA batteries. (Not included). I put in rechargeable AAs. It sounds great and has all the same functions as any other CD player like this. It's only drawback is that it does not have a belt clip so if you want to walk or jog while listening to music you will have to put it inside a bag or other type of pack.

I also replaced the headphones with an over the ear pair, because I am personally not a fan of ear buds and can't get them to stay in my ears. That is just me though. If you like ear buds this CD player does come supplied with a pair.

title: Biggest Pro: Reghargeable
review: I love that this CD player is rechargable.  It was easy for me to figure out how to operate it without reading the instruction manual.  I popped in a CD and it played very nicely.  It has rich sound.  I'm not a big fan of earbud headphones however because they won't stay in my ears,  so I used some over the ear with it.  It also has a micro SD card slot so you can also listen to MP3 files on this as well.  It's a very nice CD player and the fact that you can recharage it off of any USB jack is a major plus in my book.  This would make a great gift for any music lover.

title: Lightweight
review:
This is a fairly light MP3 player. Mine isn't white like pictured. It's an odd mix of gray and white. That is OK it doesn't affect function, just an observation. It has a very simple screen to navigate which is similar to that of a smart phone.

I personally have an issue with ear buds staying in properly so switched to over/ear headphones. This takes a mini TF card, you can download tracks to it, or you can listen to the radio on it. I ripped some of my records to a TF card to listen and they played great.

title: Kind of A Learning Curve
review:
This is kind of a learning curve for me, but it's not really much different than working a small smart phone or smart watch. It has a menu similar to a cell phone. I had to read the manual to figure out some of its features but I do enjoy the design. I didn't have any MP3 files, video files or anything like that to upload into my device so I recorded a CD onto a TF card and was able to listen. I am not too fond of the in-ear style headphones however because I have a hard time keeping earbuds in but that's just a personal preference with me. I will mainly rip some of my records onto a TF card and then listen to them on the go.

I wish it had the ability to take a bigger TF card rather than a micro, because I have some excellent concert videos I'd love to be able to take with me to watch when I travel.

The only downside to this is that I tried for over an hour to get the carry strap into the little holes (because I'm not too fond of the Dick Tracy wrist strap) and finally gave up. I'm not sure why it won't thread into the holes, but it flat out wouldn't do it.

Anyway this is a nice little smart watch. That's pretty much what it is. It's wearable, has a feature where you can download an ebook, videos, movies etc.

title: Great For Gaming
review:
I originally selected these so I could listen to music but my son then found out that these headphones had a microphone and borrowed them for his gaming.

They are foldable, tangle free, adjustable and cancel noise really well. The party on the other end heard us loud and clear when we used the mic and music and voices that we were experiencing sounded great as well. The headphones are very comfortable and don't hurt the ears. Very nice quality head phones.

title: Great Sound
review: It took awhile for me to figure out how to use this with my headset. I tend to listen to rock music that my husband doesn't quite enjoy as much as me. So I wanted this to plug in my headset, and I could listen to whatever. I already have a hearing loss due to all the live rock bands I use to go see every weekend when I was growing up. It was way too loud at first. Unbearably loud. But once I dilly-dallied around with it, I got it to lower the volume to a bearable tone. I love music so this is great!

title: Occasionally "skips" a few notes when listening to music
review: This Bluetooth headphone is comfortable to wear and can be adjusted. Personally, I did not find the location of the volume button to be easy to find and operate while wearing headphones, though I might get used to it with time. The power button and the volume button are on the right side and at the lower back side. The sound quality was good for the full range from low to high. However, while the Bluetooth connection did hold in all areas of my house, the music would occasionally skip a few notes like it had very briefly lost connection. This would happen whether I was 2 feet away or at the far end the house. I would've given this a five stars except for this dropping of notes.

title: Odd way of navigating and doesn't work with every earbud or headphone, but otherwise works well
review:
This is a relatively small and lightweight, basic MP3 player. The main challenge I've had with it is that the buttons you use for moving around the screen are different than every other MP3 player I've used. To move up, you click the left button. To move down, you click the right button. To go back a menu/selection, you click the bottom button. So if you want to go one up for one down, you have to remember to click a button on the right or left. Other than this, the menus are pretty easy to navigate through to find what you want. I mainly use this for music and to listen to audiobooks in the MP3 format, and it's easy to load the files in order from LibriVox and then listen to them. You do have to keep track of where you were as it doesn't start up where you left off. If you don't want to use the included earbuds, I'll mention that not all earbuds or headphones make a good connection to the MP3 player. As in, some don't connect fully so you hear nothing. My favorite headphones work with it, but two other earbuds didn't. I also tried the voice recorder. It picks up sound if you're holding it very close to your mouth, but don't expect to be able to hear any speaking that's more than like 3 foot away.

This review is based on over a week of daily use; maybe 5 hours of listening time.

title: Good controls & connection. Fit okay & pretty comfortable. Soft bass, though.
review:
These Bluetooth ear buds were easy to pair with my smart phone and stayed paired even when I walked several feet away from the phone. You charge them using the included USB charging cord. Charging time is up to 1.5 hours. The full charge lasts for: standby time is 80 hours. Music or talk time lasts 7 hours.

The earbuds have a light magnetic attraction on their backs, so you can secure them together around your neck when they're not in your ears. The control bar lands near your neck. It allows you to turn on or off the earbuds, easily increase or decrease the volume, skip forward or back, play or pause. It also has a microphone on the back. It has good volume control (as in, not just three or four loudness selections, and you can get both soft and loud). The earbuds are comfortable and stay in pretty well. They include large, medium, and small sizes for the ear tips and ear hooks to help you get the right fit.

The sound quality was good, especially the high and mid frequencies. I'm not sure if it was the fault of the songs I was listening to, but the highs and mediums seem stronger than the bass. The bass did not seem distorted, just not strong. Sound quality (from high to lows) was better than earbuds I have tried in the past. The earbuds also come with a fabric carrying pouch.

title: nice off-brand buy
review:
Wireless headphones have come a long way, and I'm impressed by these earbuds and their performance because I go through a decent number of wired pairs every year, either because they're put in the wash or they just get banged up while riding in my pockets and during daily use.

These wireless buds are meant to work and look just like a pair of black airpods, and they do a decent job of recreating Apple's typical minimal interface design. The touch controls on the earbuds work pretty well, and the case does a decent job of reporting battery life and storing them when not in use. Range is pretty good too, although pairing them every time you take them out of the case is a bit of a pain, and wireless buds in general haven't yet caught up to the "pull out the cord" method of pausing and re-starting a song or podcast.

Regardless, I like these, and I'll continue using them. The quality is pretty good for an off brand.

title: Good for the price
review:
These are a good quality pair of earbuds for the price. I like the simplicity - it's just a pair of headphones that will do the job they need to do - and they'll work at a great distance. I use these when I'm at my computer and I need to swing my chair around to grab something off of the shelf behind me. I have to say, the uses for a 10 foot cord are quite limited, and these are not exactly the kind of headphones you can wear at the gym, for example, so know what you're buying.

In 99% of situations, I simply think that a wireless pair would work better, but in my office, where connectivity is just a consistent issue because of the concrete everywhere, these are doing the job at a good price.

title: Excellent
review: I've switched to these wired headphones as my daily drivers for nearly a month, having put my last pair through the wash and killed them after over a year of service.  For headphones, I'm not an audiophile - I like them cheap, durable and comfortable for a good price.  These fit all of those characteristics, and the sound quality is excellent for the price range these are offered in.  No, they're not Bose.  They're good enough for almost all types of music, and the cord is protected, the plug is reinforced , the buds fit nicely in my ears, and that's all I can ask for.

title: I like the detachable buttons
review: I got these when our old headset failed from overuse during COVID school, and they work very well for either listening to music or for videoconferencing.  The fact that they come with all of the push button controls on a separate, attachable cord is a nice feature, so that the bulkiness isn't in your way when all you want is the headphones aspect.

title: Sweet spot is on a desk
review: The sound quality is OK, the battery life is excellent, and the flexibility of use is great.  I keep this thing on my desktop and it works fine for some music and Youtube videos, and I find it more convenient than headphones., and it takes up not too much space.  I think that's the sweet spot for this device - it's not really that portable, and it's not super loud, nor does it have truly amazing sound.  It is reliable and it looks good at a desk, and the volume control is very easy to use.

title: Cheaply made
review: These are not well made headphones, but they do look good, and the value of having two mediocre pairs might entice some.  One pair broke almost immediately for us, with one headphone unresponsive.  The other pair works pretty well, and has decent sound quality given the budget nature of the plan.  The buttons work well, the plugs will fit my phone, and that's fine in some circumstances.

title: OK in every way.
review: I find that this pair of earbuds has good sound, fits OK in my ear (the buds themselves stick out just a bit too far), and deliver a decent performance that is in-line with other brands in this price range. I don't think they're my favorite, but for overall performance, these are fine as a low-cost replacement for the factory direct pair.  Don't expect them to blow you away.

title: Low quality
review:
I'm not a huge fan of these headphones, although I like many of the features.

Ultimately, the sound quality is good enough for the price range, and they have features. The magnetic closures work well, and they fit well enough in your ear without being too bulky. The cords are rather thin, as is the cheap-feeling plastic coating that holds these together. They aren't going to last long term, so you're much better off buying something a bit nicer.

title: slightly uncomfortable, great sound, great presentation
review:
These are low-priced earbuds that have an outstanding gift appeal, and very good sound considering the price. The packaging alone for these makes them an excellent white elephant or stocking stuffer gift because you can see the quality that was put into them.

Once you get beyond that, you have a pretty good product inside. Sound quality is high for the price point, and the construction of the earbuds themselves is nice. The earbuds are slightly uncomfortable in my ear because the installed pads are rather large and angled, but the company offers a few replacements in side the carrying case that I exchanged for, and those are very nice.

Overall, this is an excellent product.

title: cheap lightning plug earphones
review:
While they haven't fallen apart yet, they sure feel like they will soon. The cords are extra thin, the earbud pieces themselves feel rather cheap, light, and insignificant. The materials all around are not even up to the minimum quality standards you'd expect from other budget brands - these feel a lot like the quality of earbuds you get as promotional materials.

The sound quality is OK at best. I'd recommend these as a very short-term fix for podcast listeners, but for the price, you can do quite a bit better.

title: All around excellent
review: These lightning cable earbuds are comfortable to put in, work with all modern Apple devices, appear to be well-made and capable of taking a little abuse, and have good sound quality.  They are a step above the traditional included headphones that come with the iPhones these days, and the black color is certainly nice for a sleeker look.  Can't go wrong.

title: Ugly, but good
review: I got the "Metallic" style.  The cord of these headphones is quite ugly and looks pretty cheap, but looks do not match the above average sound quality you get from these headphones.  While these are far from the best sounding headphones I've owned, they are comfortable and well-priced.

title: Good all around performance
review: It's hard to criticize the wired headphones that are included for free with your iPhone - they provide an all-around solid sound and are reasonably comfortable for a free set of headphones.  These are comparable in many ways, but have a soft shell covering for the buds themselves, and a sound quality that is very akin in terms of all-around performance.  I like them a bit better in all areas, in fact.  For audio purists, these will clearly be lacking, but for a good everyday performance earbud for daily use, these will do quite well, and they look nice too.

title: Utility for comfort?
review:
Do you want trade a little comfort for utility?

That's the essential question with these. They have all the doo-dads you'd want with a higher end pair of headphones, including the ability for the buds themselves to magnetize to each other on the move. If you're so inclined, you could even jog with one earbud in, and the other magnetized to it, and you they'd stick. They have the volume controls on the wires to manipulate everything on the go.

That said, they're huge (they come with three size options on the ear shields, but even the smallest is large). They have an odd bulbous shape that doesn't fit nicely in my ear or my hand.

Sound quality is good for the price range, but obviously not a Bose pair. Construction quality is nice. If you want to sacrifice some comfort for what these offer, you'll get a good pair of headphones, but not ones that will do it all.

title: look good, but really mid-grade for the price point
review:
It came in a box labeled with "Frozen 2" and that's enough for my daughter to be really thrilled with them. Daddy has a few concerns. These don't get particularly loud, but they're not labeled as volume limiting or controlled.

She has a knock-off iPod that she uses for tunes, and granted, these don't get particularly loud, but when connected to my phone, the volume does get louder. A simple functionality that prevents them from getting too loud is available for many kid's headphones in this price range is certainly available if you want it.

Second, the pads on the ears are cute, but not too functional. They're flush with the speaker, and don't cup the ears.
It's a comfort thing - the pads appear to be designed with the idea that they fit over the ear, and they'll soon just rest on the ear instead.

They look good, sound quality is good, and they appear to be reasonably durable - about middle-grade for kids' headphones in this price range.

title: Best airpods replacement yet
review:
These are the best Airpods replacement I've seen yet.

They're basic, and they don't pair quite so easily with a phone as their competitor, but these are pretty close. After te first pairing, though, they work quite well. Sound quality is impressive for earbuds, but obviously, you're not going to get Bose quality out of a $30 product. Perhaps their best feature, though, is the case, which also acts as the charger. It's thick, heavy duty, and uses magnetic closures which means that it will really last the lifetime of the product.

I struggle to find a reason why you'd opt for the expensive stuff when options like this exist.

title: Not too loud, nice retro theme
review: I don't know a lot of kids who are intimately invested in the 80's arcade game "Galaga" but if yours are OK with the design, then these are a good set of headphones for the young ones.  Sound control is easy to handle, and they do prevent the highest sounds from reaching your child's delicate eardrums.  Simple to set up, and simple to control automatically.  Nice item.

title: Basic Headphones
review: If you're in the market for a very basic set of headphones, then these will do, and they'll be cheaper than most other brands.  There's nothing special about them, other than the microphone, and audio quality is....well, you get what you pay for.  These are not exactly the low-quality giveaway headphones that you get from promotional materials, but they're not too much of a step above.

title: Good sound quality, excellent comfort
review:
I am not a huge headphone junkie. I have my nice set, which I use when I'm listening to music, when sound quality and fidelity are important, and I have my everyday pair that takes a beating, which I use primarily for audibooks and podcasts. My nice headphones are large, clunky, and unweildy, but have the good sound, while my other pair are cheap, but comfortable. Now, these two worlds can finally merge, as these Wowstar headphones are the first pair of truly comfortable earbuds that can deliver good sound.

These are of the "box and insert" style earbuds which sit largely outside of your ear, but deliver noise through spoke-like antennae that help hold the phones in place. It works better on this model than on others that I've owned, although I'm not sure why - the boxes are the heaviest part of the device, yet are not pulling down with gravity.

The sound quality is excellent. I don't think they could possibly compare to mutiple-hundred dollar headphones or a well-designed speaker system, but for most circumstances, these will bring good depth of sound and well-tuned volume and balance.

title: headphones
review: The sound quality, the fit, and the style of these headphones are all fantastic.  However, while I like the idea of wrapping the cord in fabric, when I take these headphones running, the cord rubs against my shirt and creates a good amount of background noise, which ruins the high sound quality these are capable of producing.  They have become my go-to headphones, but only if I'm not going to be bouncing around a lot.

title: The volume doesn't work on the cord.
review: I paid the extra money to get the volume control on the cord. I was disappointed to find it doesn't work at all.  I got these to listen to audio books. I haven't tried them with music yet. So far the sound is clear. The cord is a useful length. It purple color is like the photo. It was a little difficult changing the ear cushion but that is because it really stays on. It comes with 3 sizes. I use the smallest size.  The earphones are not comfortable for me to sleep with when I lay on my side. So far they haven't fallen out of my ears but I'm not moving that much with them.

title: Great sound and comfortable.
review: These headphones are comfortable. I love the over the ear design because they do somewhat block out the other sounds in the room. I'm not an audiophile but I think the sound produced by these headphones is perfect for the discerning listener. The price was better than I could find anywhere else. Around $15. They are lightweight so they are easy on your head and easy to carry around.

title: Works As Described. Latch Is Questionable
review: These work as promised. Unit is lightweight, yet feels durable. Gen3 earbuds fit into case nice & snug. Wireless charging works right through case & indicator light from earbud OEM case can be seen through the KeyBudz case. You can also charge via USB. My only concern is the latch. To get the case to create a watertight seal, the lid is intended to remain slightly open before fully locking down with the latch. While this creates a very tight bond, all of the strain is on that locking tab. Which appears to be made of plastic & held in place with a small metal pin. This part will take the most wear over time, but unfortunately is critical to this case working properly. If it fails, then the case is rendered useless.

title: Lots To Like With A Few Caveats
review:
Plantronics/Poly got the super fast setup down. No instruction manual to read through. A quick setup card that is attached to the headset. Open the box, see all of the parts you need & get going in 30 seconds. Very nice.

Audio quality is excellent & you will get noise cancelling on the boom mic. Music even sounds good (although will not replace your AirPods or Sony headphones).

Super lightweight & comfortable (compared to my current headset - see pic).

Battery life is through the roof. This thing will go for days on a single charge.

All controls are very easy to learn & access. If you want more granular control, download the Poly Lens app.

With Bluetooth 5.2 (or USB dongle) there is not latency. You can also run off of wired USB if you so desire. You can connect to two devices at the same time. Convenient if you need to switch from PC to phone.

OK, so for the most part, this headset is awesome. As far as the caveats, here you go:

> $149.99 price tag may be a little steep for some
> No extra ear pad (as it will eventually wear out)
> No charging stand. You have to charge your $150.00 headset by laying it on your desk.

title: Good Headset With A Few Caveats
review:
