Ordered these for use with a PS5. Sound quality is excellent with very little to no latency. Very comfortable to wear for long periods of time & battery life is excellent (will get 2-3 hrs on just a 15 min charge & up to 24 hrs on a full charge). I don't use the mic, but it disappears into the headset when not in use. Very nice touch.

However, there are some downsides to this unit that may keep you away.

These will only work with PS4/PS5 & strangely Nintendo Switch. Also will work with a PC. However, XBox is not supported. As well, there is no Bluetooth option. So, if you need to run headphones on your PS4/PS5, Xbox & Bluetooth device(s), you will need to have 2-3 sets of headphones on hand!

I know this isn't the fault of Turtle Beach, but to use these headphones you will have to install a USB dongle. Not the end of the world, but yet another USB device to take up the precious few USB ports on your PS5.

And lastly price. Not bad at $80.00 if it's your only set of headphones. But, if your in the group of users noted above, then you may be better off paying a little more (or even less) for headphones that may give you more options.

title: BT5, Comfortable & Clear. But No Dongle!
review:
Overall, a nice & lightweight headset.

Comfortable to wear with adjustable mic & ear piece. Uses Bluetooth 5 so this will help cut thru any lag or delay & it's also noise cancelling. The construction feels a little flimsy (lightweight plastic), but this helps towards keeping the unit light. Connectivity is pretty seamless (turn your BT scanning on, locate "MX" in available BT devices & connect). No pin required (at least on Android). Audio was clear & volume controls worked well. Mic produced clear audio as well.

So what are the downsides?

There's no Bluetooth dongle!

To be fair, there's another version of this headset that includes a BT dongle for an extra $6 or $7. Not a deal breaker, but this option may be easily missed.

If a BT dongle were included, then this would open up this unit to be used on a PC were it could really stretch its legs. And by PC, I mean a desktop unit that "probably " doesn't have integrated BT like a laptop would.

So, outside of that concern, a good little BT headset overall.

To the manufacturer: Perhaps consider selling only one model & including the BT dongle at a marginally increased price. This would cut down on confusion (you're selling 2 models now - 1 with the dongle & 1 without) & allow for this to be a very flexible package.

title: No Frills Earbuds With A FRILLS Price Tag!
review: These earbuds are solid. Great sound, great battery life & Sennheiser quality. However, you're also paying for the Sennheiser name. At just under $200.00 (at the time of this review), you're getting a basic set of earbuds. There's no ANC, no transparency mode, no smart pause & no water resistance (splash proof). For those options, you need to move up to the Sennheiser MOMENTUM True Wireless 2 earbuds. And those will cost you another $70.00 to $100.00 (depending on the color you choose). Seems like a bit of a money grab to me. However, if you like Sennheiser as a brand, then you know what you're getting into. I say save your money & look at other, less expensive options. You will get all of the features that are missing here & still have some money left over to pay the water bill!

title: Really Wanted To Be More Excited About These
review: I'm not sure what it is, but it seems lately that the more expensive the earbud, the worse the performance. I've tested $30.00 earbuds that outperform these $100.00 earbuds from Panasonic on all fronts. The whole package just feels buggy. From the charging cradle (the earbuds just don't sit properley), to the uneven charging/battery drain (right side is always undercharged), to the flaky app (the just hangs in place with a firmware update notification, but no way to apply it), to the mediocre audio (sounds good, but again, not $100.00 good). And, they're just not loud enough. Why? So, overall, I was expecting a lot more from a solid brand like Panasonic. Unfortunately, all I have here is a pile of problems :-[

title: Great Cable WIth Lots Of Uses
review: A 6' USB 3.0 extension cable can be used in many situations..including USB 2.0 applications (it will just clock down to match the speed of USB 2.0). You can charge phones AND transfer data with this cable. Also useful for extending game controllers, headphones, USB drives or running a USB extension up to your desk from a PC on the floor. Well made & looks like it will last a long time.

title: Average Performance & A Bit Glitchy
review: These earbuds, while nice looking & feeling, are just OK when it comes to performance & usability. The sound is good, but a little hissy (even after EQ adjustments on my Galaxy). And they are VERY touchy. Now this may be a good thing if you can get these to stay in your ears. But these suckers are big! So if you have to fumble with keeping them in position (I had to do this a lot) then you will be constantly pausing, skipping, etc.. And, while the sound is full, I just couldn't get these loud enough to really feel them. Battery life was average at best. Maybe 3 hours on a full charge (not the advertised 6.5 hours). I was really hoping for more out of this set. But at this price (just under $200.00 at the time of this review), save your money. There are WAY BETTER options out there.

title: Solid Performance At An Affordable Price
review: If you need a solid set of BT earbuds, but don't want to spend hundreds of dollars, then just go ahead & grab a pair of these earbuds from Bluedio. They will do everything that most users would want AND then some! Long battery life, easy pairing, great sound quality & fast recharge (via USB C) are just the basics. But they also support Qi (wireless) charging, voice calling, on-ear controls & Bluetooth 5.0. That's an incredible feature set considering that these are under $20.00 (at the time of this review)!

title: Literally great and fits with snowboarding helmet
review:
Bought these for snowboarding since didnt want to bother with wireless headphones for my snowboarding helmet

Love the quality fits perfectly under my helmet and doesn't bother my ears . Thanks for saving me hundreds

title: Very Sturdy, Right Length Cables
review: I purchased two of these 3 feet cables to replace the thin cables that came with my sound bar and to connect my analog stereo headphones to the television via an analog to digital decoder.  I'm very happy with them.  The 3 foot length is just right for my purposes, not too long or too short.  The cable has a nice, sturdy thickness that will avoid inadvertent crimping and the jack fits very securely into the optical ports I'm using.  Good sound from both the headphones and the sound bar.  I'm happy with this purchase.

title: An amazing value
review: Great sound, very comfortable (though a bit warm), great battery life. The noise cancelation is definitely there, I think it could be better, but I lack experience with better NR headphones. The controls work well, though I don't like the funny way it acts when an audio cord is attached — you can't power it on or off with the cord attached. Hopefully a software update in the future could fix this. It does receive software updates through the companion smartphone app. I did use the app to adjust the EQ curve — I wanted more treble and less bass.

title: They fit perfectly
review: Apparently the original earphone cushions are not that long-lived. But these are perfect replacements.

title: Great for the price, does the job
review:
The packaging and overall design is very nice — far above the price-point. The sound quality is good for the size. If you want more bass, you need a bigger driver that needs a bigger housing, so there is a balance that needs to be struck between fitting entirely in your ear for comfortable sleeping vs luxurious sound. These are my sleeping pair that I play white noise through. I use other earbuds for music. The wires are thin, the ear housings are small -- all correct for comfortable sleeping so they fit in your ear and the wires don't leave giant tracks on your face!

Mine failed at about 90 days, but the seller graciously honored the warranty and shipped a new pair.

title: Fantastic sound. So good.
review:
Fantastic sound. You look like a telephone operator, but the mic on the boom is high-quality, and that combined with the proximity to your mouth produces resulting sound quality blows away bundled smartphone earbud sets for voice calls. I get compliments on the sound quality.
However, I don't know what's "noise canceling" about this, because my callers hear everything in my environment, in addition to my voice. But that's a quibble. I wish everyone I spoke to owned a pair. Seriously, it's 2017 and we have all this technology, but the typical telephone call sound is worse now than it was in 1978. This helps move the needle back to the quality end.

title: Audio review: very good, but not audiophile
review:
Out of the box, they sounded like poo, and I considered returning them to the big box store I bought them from. But after playing white noise through them for 48 hours, they are sounding much better. On that first listen, there was no midrange at all, the bass was muddy, and the highs were taking over and very harsh. Now the bass is nice and full, the midrange is relatively accurate and present, but the highs are still a bit harsh. Actually, very harsh and fatiguing. But for the price and for the convenience of having disposable earbuds when you don't want to use your expensive set, these are great. They are also very suitable for podcasts, audiobooks, spoken word material. The mic seems to work well too — no complaints on phone calls.
I like the look, but be aware — the cool flat cord material transmits lots of rubbing noises into your ears if you are walking/running.
Now my only regret is that I paid too much at the big-box store.

title: It's fine, but there are better ones
review:
I prefer the Plantronics Voyager Pro line for better noise isolation and more comfortable fit.
What's nice about this LG is the dedicated sliding on/off switch, and the durability. I can throw it in my pocket or briefcase and not worry about it, so it serves as my backup headset. But others that move the mic closer to your mouth pick up better sound.
The ear loop on this is a torture device. I use it without the removable loop and just jam it in my ear canal like an earbud. Which also hurts after a while...

title: It failed on week 3
review:
It worked great for 2 weeks, but now it disconnects about 5 minutes into a call. I don't know why. I reset it, reset the phone, re-paired the headset, did what I could, but it's useless now. Returning it.
Also, the head band is a bit too tight -- gave me a headache, but I was willing to live with that for the clarity. Oh well.

title: Great while they last...
review:
I really like these headphones, but as others point out, they are not very durable. My first pair broke after a year -- and I am very careful with my equipment. I only use them at my computer, they don't travel or get abused. They fell off my desk and the right channel is now shot. Anyway, the sound was great -- very warm with fantastic bass and accurate highs. They sound nearly as good as my entry-level Grados, but are much more comfortable to wear for extended periods. But buy two pairs now, or plan on replacing them later.
-edit-
Several years later, I am back to say that the two additional pairs I bought are both going strong and they are still the best quality/comfort/price combination in the world. I have more accurate in-ear phones that cost $200+, but for comfort and long listening sessions, these can't be beat. I hope they are never discontinued. The design looks dated and a bit dorky on your head, but once you hear them, you won't care.

title: Great headphones
review: First, I was skeptical about the price. To good to be true prices. These headphones are great, the sound with bright colors is exquisite. Easy on the ears.

title: best wireless earbud for the price if you can get it for discount!!
review: I got this for 10 bucks and it well worth the money!! there is not wireless earbud better than this with this price!

title: Tinny but super comfortable
review: They're comfortable, way more comfortable than any other earbuds I've tried, but the sound quality is a bit tinny and the mic is placed pretty low. For the price, they're excellent.

title: Great little speakers
review:
These are exactly what I hoped for and they even look nice.

Only odd thing is when headphones get plugged in the volume control is a bit touchy- it leans towards the load end. Over all fabulous little things

title: Truly wireless headphones that you can probably skip if you have/had the Powerbeats 3
review: I upgraded from the black Powerbeats 3 wireless headphones solely due to the fact that the Powerbeats 3 cord would really bug me out during workouts. So I purchased the Moss color. Moss is a great color and the headphones sound great with great noise cancellation. However, they don’t sound much different from the Powerbeats 3. And the charging case is too bulky for the headphones to be conveniently portable. That’s the only good thing about Powerbeats 3 cord. Verdict: Great headphones, but Besides the “truly wireless” feature, the upgrade couldn’t be justified. Stick to the Powerbeats 3 if you have them.

title: Great for safety!
review: These headphones are great if you want to still have great sound quality, but still be able to be aware of your surroundings. I work in an environment where you have to be able to hear certain loud sounds, but I still have the flexibility of being able to listen to shows. These headphones allow you to listen to things with great sound quality, but not block out the entire world. They would be great for running so you could hear cars and people approaching. It allows great flexibility. These are awesome.

title: Nice earphones at a Nice price
review: These headphones are a great choice for someone that wants quality headphones at an affordable price. They give you the option of using only one of them, when the need to hear your surroundings, or use both for a fully immersive experience. They are great for music and movies/videos. Great headphones

title: So Awesome
review: These earbuds are awesome. They sound great and are very easy to connect. I like the fact that you can connect just one at a time in case you need to hear your surroundings. If you want to get away for a while, just put both in and turn up the volume. Awesome earbuds

title: Used for work
review: I work in a warehouse and regular bone conduction headphones don't work well with all the machinery - they don't sync up to my phone well.  I added a ton of my MP3s to this bone conduction headset and I'm a happy camper!  Plays without problem and with the bone conduction I can still hear any important stuff from the speaker system as well as talk to my lead when he walks by.  Nice to have tunes when working!

title: Very nice set of bone conduction headphones
review: I have another, similar set but it is made for MP3 play while swimming.  It does play via bluetooth when not in use in water, but  worry that that pair will fail soon because it is a water set.  I mean, no matter what you do, water gets into things eventually.  These fit well for bone conduction headphones and they have good sound as well.  I'm happy with them!

title: A bit different set of bone conduction headphones
review: The "hooking system" for this set of bone conduction headphones takes a bit of getting used to.  I love bone conduction because it allows me to hear what's going on around me while still listening to music.  Being aware of your surroundings is important in this day and age.  I have a pair of bone conduction that is more...solid in how they go around my head and over my ears with the headphone part sitting very firmly on that bone just in front of the ears that allows the music to travel into the ear canal even while leaving them open to sound.  They work, though - just take getting used to them.

title: Bone conduction headphones that are above some of the big name brands
review: I won't mention the bone conduction name brand, but they sell for a decent amount more than these.  The thing is, these have some features I've not seen before which, in my opinion, put them above the others.  Firs is the recharger.  It reminds me of the one my smart watch uses - no actual "input" and that makes sense for bone conduction headphones for swimmers.  See, I have had bone conduction touted to be for swimmers and yet, they used traditional USB connections with a rubber "seal" that obviously doesn't actually seal...meaning that they quit working not too long after using in the water a few times.  Bone conduction isn't going to win any quality sound awards like a JBL over the ear headphone, but they do deliver good quality sound considering they are sending that sound through bone instead of straight through to the eardrum.  Because I have used bone conduction before, these were not an issue for me to wear and they fit comfortably.  I do believe these are the best not just for swimming but if you run or whatever and want to be aware of traffic and other individuals nearby, then bone conduction headphones are the way to go and these are the ones I would highly recommend.

title: Didn't work for my idea
review: But thee do work for older tech like my Creative Zen MP3 player.  I love that little MP3 player!  But it was made before bluetooth and being able to find it instead of attaching a USB cord works for me.  I was using a rather large receiver/transmitter to connect my Zen to a pair of wireless headphones.  I like not using my phone to listen to music because I really do have a ton of music saved on my Zen and using it instead of my phone means it holds a charge longer.  I was hoping to use one of these to get a label printer to attach wirelessly to my laptop, but it doesn't seem to want to do that...oh well.

title: If noted for being used while swimming, then they should be good with water
review: And these are apparently not.  Maybe something wasn't done properly on the line when they were made, but whatever the reason this set of swimmer's bone conduction ear phones.  They started getting funky right after getting in the indoor swimming pool to do my water exercises.  After the 3rd day they simply quit working.  So I'm thinking that somewhere on the production line, something was not done properly otherwise why post them as swimming headphones?  Oh well,  they did sound good for a couple of days but the important part of this sentence is "good for a couple of days," meaning don't get your hopes up!

title: Bone conduction are the all around best!
review: These bone conduction headphones are truly the best thing for all uses (aside from swimming) as you can listen to your music, audio books, etc. but at the same time, you can hear what's going on all around you.  So if you are jogging or taking a walk around the neighborhood, you can listen to your tunes, but still hear and be aware of people and vehicles around you.  I mean, a big, burly guy may feel safe running with earbuds stuck down in his ears so he can't hear anything else, but for most of us, it's important to be aware of your surroundings when out walking/running.  Need to hear cars coming, need to be aware of people running up behind you...it's just that important and I can tell you this Mojawa bone conduction headset will deliver excellent sound without sacrificing that awareness of what's going on (in hearing) around you.  Excellent price, too!

title: This is the one!
review: I had been looking for an updated MP3 player on the same level as my very old, still working Creative Zen.  I do love my Zen, but it has no bluetooth capability (although I did get a great receiving/transmitter that works well to give it bluetooth capability).  Anyway, as I said, I have been looking for an MP3 player that could compare and this is it!  I had tried a few that were in the $40-$50 range (some less) and they really were not good at all - just horrible to try to use, too.  This one, aside from me not understanding that you have to turn it off and back on to see what you've loaded on (I loaded a sampling of 10 songs from my computer) and got frustrated because they didn't show up.  I read the instructions and it said to turn it off and back on after loading and there they were - my 10 songs.  Through my Jabra neck speakers or over the ear headphones, the sound is very good.  I have not tried to add a movie to it but I believe with the amount of space it has, I probably could.  It is small but hefty for it's size so should last for a while.  We'll have to see if it's as sturdy and well made as my Zen!

title: Got these because supervisor at work said no earbuds
review: Not that I was the only one wanting to hear music over the noise in the warehouse, but I could see his point that we needed to hear messages over the intercom/speaker system, so...the first time I wore these in, he came by.  I showed him how they work and even allowed him to put them on so he could hear that while listening to music, these bone conduction headphones do NOT interfere with hearing what is going on around me.  I got the okay to wear them!  I actually really like these bone conduction earphones specifically because they allow me to hear what's going on around me - kids, husband, friends can talk to me while I'm enjoying my tunes and I can still hear them and answer them.  Nothing ruder than having someone with earbuds or total over the ear headphones on that don't even acknowledge you spoke to them, so, want to listen to tunes but need to hear what's going on around you?  These are the best you can get!

title: I have another neck speaker
review: The other one is fine, but the way it is made, it is heavier, the neck section is like a thick rubber band so the speakers can sort of move around as I do and that bothers me.  I like these because the speakers themselves are closer to my ears.  I also have some bone conduction headphones which, after a time, bother my ears, so having this neck speaker set is perfect.  I can turn the music down so it's not blasting to nearby neighbors when out in my yard.  I have a zero-gravity chair and cantilever umbrella that is a wonderful place to hang out on hot days after doing some work in the yard.  I also will pull up an audio book to listen to - I have 3 new ones to listen to at the moment - so listening to my books through this neck speaker is convenient.  These are comfortable and easy to wear with good sound from the speakers.

title: I have a set of "picture speakers" that cost less and sound better
review: Okay, so there are 4 of these, but my other set of wall/picture speakers came with these kind of cute/silly pictures of monkeys wearing headphones that actually made them look like framed art on the wall and their sound is so much better.  For the price, these should be decent and they sound very low-end.  I would not recommend these if you love to listen to music or want to immerse yourself in the sound of a movie through your AV receiver.  Look elsewhere.

title: I have a different pair of Linearflux ear buds that are AWESOME
review: And thought I'd try these to see if the company puts out consistent product and I do have to say that these are every bit as good as my other set.  That particular set has hooks as I have a bad habit of having earbuds fall out.  I don't know if I have really shallow canals or too widely flared or something else, but unless I am just sitting still, I need something that hooks them in place.  So, the sound quality of these is every bit as good as my other Linearflux, but these will be for when I am sitting quietly, like meditating, instead of walking.  My other pair with the hooks will be for when I'm in motion.  At least that way I have a time to recharge each of them while not wearing them.  I'm very impressed with Linearflux audio products.  They "get it!"

title: I really wanted to like these
review: They look futuristic and that's cool - I thought that might be a good thing, but that's part of the problem for me.  I wear glasses - I cannot wear contacts because I have extreme dry eye syndrome so must wear glasses pretty much all the time.  I do have some bone conduction headphones that work just fine with my glasses, but their sound isn't all that great.  I thought these might be better and probably would be fine IF I didn't have to wear my glasses!  So just be aware, if you are a glasses-wearer, these may not be the best style bone conduction headphones for you.  They sure aren't for me.  I ended up giving these to my nephew who participates in walks for police charities (widows, suicide, etc.) and has told me he really likes these as he can listen to and talk to his buddies while still listening to his tunes.

title: Shokz OpenRun are a great bone conduction headset
review: I have every type of headphone/buds/headset on the market and each has good and bad qualities to them.  I worked in a warehouse for a few years and due to some accidents, wearing over the ear headphones or in the ear earbuds were banned because people could NOT hear others.  Co-workers, supervisors, intercom announcements were going unheard.  My first set of (cheap) bone conduction headphones came at this time.  Their sound was not great, but I was allowed to wear them as they did not affect my ability to hear in the warehouse.  Like these Shokz, my first pair did "vibrate" and I got used to that.  I think, too, that heavy bass music causes more of the vibration than if I listen to say classical music.  These Shokz OpenRun bone conduction have really great sound and are comfortable to wear while walking, bike riding or running.  If you've never tried bone conduction headphones before, give these a try - they are so worth it!

title: Nice sound, but they have a "wearing limit" for me
review: Okay, so I have tried every kind of sound delivering wearables - over-the-ear headphones, earbuds, and the type that rest on the ears plus these bone conduction style.  The Shokz bone conduction headphones have one big difference that is worthwhile - keeping the ears open so you can still hear what is going on around you.  I worked in a warehouse that restricted wearing in-ear headphones but they did allow bone conduction as I could still hear co-workers speaking to me, hear important messages broadcast over the speakers in the warehouse, etc. - yet I could still enjoy listening to my music.  The only downside is that the ear hook piece is very stiff and after a bit of time my ears hurt.  I do have to admit that over-the-ear headphones become uncomfortable after a time as well, so it's not just bone conduction.  I like these Shokz - the little stickers to personalize them is a nice idea - but wish that for this price they would include a hard, zip case (I saw one for $16) to store the headset.  Would add to a complete purchase if that makes sense.

title: I have been using bone conduction headphones for quite some time
review: I like the fact that I can still hear "around" these headphones and they are more comfortable than earbuds or over the ear headphones.  I tend to listen to audio books more often than music and found this pair of conduction headphones is good for the books.  As far as music goes, these don't seem to have the "oomph" that another pair of bone conduction headphones I have for playing music.  So, if you are an audio book lover, I can recommend these, but if you prefer to listen to music, you might want to look for another pair.

title: I put these against my Jabra's and the Jabra's won
review: Both these and Jabra's have an app - I actually have both Jabra earbuds and over the ear headphones which are both accessible through the app, but what I'm comparing here are just the earbuds.  I'm not saying that these Nuratrue are bad in any way.  They do have a good sound, but I have a problem with their app not allowing me to change the EQ - I DON'T just listen to rock or jazz or any kind of music.  I tend to listen to audio books quite frequently and obviously hearing a spoken voice narrating a book is quite different than listening to pounding bass rock or the symphonic levels of classical music.  The Nuratrue seems to think, in their app that they can go through a few things with you and figure out what you want/need as far as the sound you hear goes.  I want that control and Jabra allows me that.  So at least for me, I'm not as thrilled by others saying "trust me, we know what you want."  That's how I feel and that's just me - others may like Nutratrue's way of handling sound, so understand that these sound good.  It's just a matter of how you want to be involved with the app.

title: I have one similar to this one that was just an MP3 player
review: And while it sounded okay, it had some issues.  I was happy to find this one does not have the same issues at all.  When I work, I do sweat...a lot.  The other one seem to have issues when I would get all sweaty so having read this can go underwater, I thought, maybe it can deal with my amount of sweat!  It does!  I've loaded a few songs on it and it does play them well, but of course, being able to connect to the music on my phone is great!  I have used earbuds, over the ear headphones and I have a couple of those that simply rest against the ear lightly (they are my absolute favorite) and then these bone conduction.  The bone conduction is my favorite for when I'm outside, walking, in the pool, working in the yard - they are great to still hear sound around me while enjoying my tunes!

title: Once again I tried, once again this style failed for me
review: I think this is the last time I will try the earbuds with "posts" on them.  I don't really know if my ears are that different or unusual, but no matter what size silicone caps I use on this style of earbud, I cannot keep them in my ears.  I've seen and worked with others who use this style of earbud and have no problem wearing them for hours.  They fall out on me.  I can say that the sound from the earbuds seems impressive, but if I cannot keep them in, well...so I took them over to my son and who does play video games.  He had no problem keeping them in (go figure) and he was blown away with the sound.  So, basically, I guess I have goofy-shaped ears that don't work with the posts/pegs style of earbuds, but that these earbuds have wicked good sound based on my son's experience.

title: Okay, I have some serious earbuds and over the ear headphones
review: Heck, I even have bone conduction style headphones, but I have to say that for the most part, I love this pair.  I used to have a pair of Sony "clips" that had this style of earphones that simply rest against the ear.  It depends on my mood and what I'm listening to as to what I prefer to wear.  I have some smart earbuds with a company app allowing me to do some tweaking, especially on the equalizer.  In ear is comfortable for about 4 hours on me.  Same with the over the ear style - after 4 hours my ears are sweating!  Bone conduction is the closest to compare with these, but there really isn't a way to compare them as bone conduction headphones don't actually interact with you ear!  They move sound through the bones just in front of your ear so you can still hear people in the room talking to you. But these, they are soft and don't squeeze against the ears, but simply lay on them without pressure.  The sound is good.  They may not be the amazing bass and soaring tenor of my expensive buds and head phones, but I can get comfortable and wash dishes, mop the floor and do other chores while wearing these and it feels as if I don't have them on.  Love them!

title: Bone conduction earphones have a place...
review: First, of course, is that you can listen to audio books/music and still hear what is going on around you.  These do a good job of hooking over your ears and staying in place.  The fact that they can be used while swimming is great - so few earbuds and no over the ear headphones are waterproof!  The real issue with this bone conduction set is the ability to change to next song or turn the volume up or down.  I have long, natural fingernails and usually have no problem with small buttons as the end of my fingernail pushes in and easily changes the song or volume.  Not so with this set.  Seems the buttons are just not well laid out or large enough or whatever...so if you want to just listen to tunes back to back, this will work.  If not, it's not going to be easy to switch up next tunes.

title: I like them but I wish I could love them
review: I guess having tested a few headphones, earbuds, and bone conduction earphones, plus having some rather awesome speakers (Klipsch and Denon), I can say that these are really cool and as far as speakers go, they are good, but they could be so much better...I mean, I have some Cleer earbuds and headphones that have a phone app that allows me to fiddle with an equalizer to set my own preference for the sounds I hear within my music.  I mention this because the sound quality of these picture style speakers is just okay.  They could be awesome - an app, especially a smart app that sync's to Alexa or Google and that allowed to fiddle with an equalizer - that would make these awesome.  The best part of these at the present time is the fact that they can look like pictures on a wall and still pump out your favorite tunes.  A little tweaking by the manufacturer and these will be awesome instead of just okay.

title: I have a pair of Cleer Enduro headphones that also use the app
review: And am not disappointed in how these Ally Plus earbuds work with the app as well.  They paired instantly to the app once the phone is Bluetoothed to the buds.  Turning the ANC on and off and playing with the equalizer while listening to my favorite music allows me to hear my music the way I like to hear it.  I am not a serious audiophile, but I have found a few things I like and the Cleer items I have are my go-to music carriers.  I have a Cleer Halo neck speaker that is amazing and what I use most when listening to audio books.  I also have Cleer Enduro over the ear headphones that also sync to the app.  The Enduro are my favorite for listening to music because I prefer the over the ear headphones, but I also like these Cleer Ally Plus earbuds for the least obstructive of all the possibilities.  Now, if Cleer made bone conduction style, I would definitely get them as that is also a favorite way to listen to music.  What I can say is that I do appreciate the sound quality and the different styles of music carriers that Cleer does make, including these Ally Plus earbuds.

title: Attractive and functional
review: I have issues using my earbuds - I do have a couple of pairs I like, but for the most part, I prefer over the ear headphones.  I also have three different OTE headphones that I like to switch off and use for different reasons.  Two of them are "smart" headphones; the Jabra set coordinates well with Amazon music and that's really nice.  My other smart set is not as "exclusive" and I also like that about it.  My third set has the most awesome sound and yes, I like that too!  So...whichever one I am using, I have this stand set up next to my recliner and when I am not wearing the headset of the day, it is nearby and easily accessible while sitting on this stand.  The only thing I could wish for is that it had rubber on the bottom - rubber feet, rubber suction cups, a thin rubber mat - something that would hold it in place on a smooth surface.  Not a big deal, but if you reach for the headset and slightly bump the stand, it moves too much.  With rubber feet/mat, it wouldn't be as likely to move.  I'd prefer that over the coasters that it came with.  Other than that, I like this stand and it keeps my headset close for when I need to take it off or put it on.

title: Putting these against much higher-end OTE headphones is a mistake...
review: I have 3 other OTE headphones that were priced either double or triple the price of this set so...I'm trying NOT to lean heavily on the sound from them to evaluate this set.  What I will say, though, is that I bought a $28 OTE headphone for my granddaughter and the sound it produces is equal to or better than this one.  Granted, her set does not fold and pack into a case as this one does, but I did purchase a case for her set that is made for headphones that don't fold...so, as far as the sound produced by this headphone is concerned, it is adequate at best.  The noise cancellation is not the best, but again, my other headphones with ANC are much higher-end headphones that this one, so I can't totally say it's bad...it's just not as good as I would expect for the price.  As noted before, the sound produced by these was not much different than a $28 pair so the price-point for these is a bit high.

title: Price point too high for what you get
review: I have yet to find a pair of earbuds with "stems" like these that fit me well, but I do keep looking.  These fit me better than some, but for this price I expected exceptional sound quality and while it was good, it didn't beat my tiny (non-stem) earbuds that didn't cost anywhere near these.  I keep trying to find a style of earbud like these because if I want to answer my phone, the stem type seem easier to accomplish that without them falling out of my ear.  At the moment, I prefer over-the-ear headphones for that reason.  Still, these Ogg earbuds are not bad - they do have good sound, but I expected great sound for this price and because they should have blown away my $30 pair of earbuds that I like - and they didn't.  So...it's up to you what's important in listening to your music...

title: Sound quality is excellent for this price point OTE headphones
review: I really liked the app for controlling the way I hear my music and find these to be a very comfortable pair of OTE headphones.  OTE headphones are my preferred way to listen to music, podcasts and audio books, especially audio books when I'm up and doing stuff - I can still concentrate on the narration of the book while washing dishes, folding clothes and whatnot.  The ANC works wonderfully - I have a neighbor that I like, but he has an extremely annoying barking dog that just has to alert everybody about everything.  It really is annoying even though I actually like the stupid dog...so being able to put the headphones on and the ANC drowns him out...keeps me from wanting to kick the dog! The only thing I wished for that I have on another set of OTE headphones is the pairing with Alexa so that I don't have to take off my headphones to make a quick call - with that pair, I can just say Alexa, call my daughter and ask her to bring home milk or something.  That's just a nice feature for me to have, but I do really like the sound quality that these Cleer headphones provide me.  Definitely worth the price for excellent quality.

title: Cleer does make great products
review: And these buds are no exception.  I prefer over-the-ears headphones as I have what seems like very small ear canals and most earbuds don't go in or stay in well, but these seemed to work well for me.  I do have a favorite pair of buds that were the very first ones that actually slid in and fit smoothly into my ear canals.  These feel very similar to those buds but the sound they produce/develop is far superior to my little no-name buds so I will be using these Cleer buds when I'm in the mood to listen to music, podcasts or audio books without breaking out my favorite over-the-ear headphones.  The ANC with these buds work much my headphones and I'm impressed since I know that ANC doesn't mean totally silent outside noise, but allows me to still speak to someone should I want to have a conversation without taking them out/off.  Great earbuds!

title: I have a few different headphones
review: Actually, my favorite so far is my Cleer Halo neck speakers which are a bit different than my over-the-ear headphones that I also like.  The neck speakers have a flexible neck piece and they hang from this stand that is attached to the behind the couch shelves that are next to my recliner.  I can reach back and snatch my neck speakers quick, pair them with my MP3 player or my phone and music blossoms.  When I'm done, hanging them on this stand is easy peasy.  Great stand that works well for me.

title: My issue is with fitment
review: I always hope these longer "stemmed" earbuds will work for me, but alas, no, they don't.  They just don't stay in my ears well, slipping out even when I'm sitting still!  Not sure why...I have tried them in different positions in my ears and nothing works.  I have some very tiny earbuds that fit me well, so I'll just stick with them.  The sound from these were good.  I'm not a game-player, but I can say that the sound was really good with these.  Because they would not stay put in my ears, I can't really give them a thumbs up to the very best sound - that would require me being able to keep them in!  Others may have much better luck with them than I did - it may just be in the shape of my ears and the size of my ear canal that means I can't use this style of earbud.

title: I got two different ones, just in case
review: The other one I found a day later and is specifically made as a replacement for the headphones I have.  They work great, but in the meantime, I had this one and tried it as well.  It works fine, too.  The only difference between this one and the made-for replacement is the cord itself.  The made-for replacement cord is a bit thicker and has a flexible, woven cover over it so to me it seemed a bit sturdier than this one.  This one's cord is similar, but just not as thick as the other cord.  I will keep this one as my back up since I've already lost the original cord!

title: I have the Hyper X Cloud headset and the original cord went missing
review: It's somewhere...just don't know where at the moment and I didn't want to not use the headphones until I find that original cord.  This one is working as the original and that's exactly what I wanted/needed to keep using my headset.

title: This is a really cheaply made version of a classic
review: I should know - I still own and use a Creative Zen MP3 player. It is a little larger than this one, but it is so much better than this one.  First, trying to get bluetooth pairing is difficult. I have two pair of earbuds, a pair of neck speakers and a Carlos Santana BT speaker.  I do have others, but of the four I mentioned ONLY TWO would pair with this MP3 player. I thought, well maybe only two can be listed as having been paired with this player so I deleted them and tried again. Nope. It's real sketchy on how/why it pairs.  Now, my Creative Zen is old enough that it does not have BT connectivity, but I bought a pairing unit that allows it to pair with BT items and that little paring unit works perfect to pair with all the items I mentioned (2 pair of earbuds, neck speaker and the Carlos Santana speaker).  I will say also that this MP3 player did sync okay with my computer and I was able to put a few of my songs on it.  With my Zen, I could play artists, albums, genres - and remember, Zens were made in the 1990s. This one, it seems to have some of this ability, but it doesn't work well.  For the price, I think this is barely adequate.  If you are looking for a very small MP3 player for use during a daily jog to listen to music, this might be a good choice.

title: This is my second pair of bone conduction earphones
review: I thought these might be better than my other pair, but they are very similar.  That is not to say there's anything wrong with them but I believe my other pair of bone conduction earphones was around $60 and I thought that was a high price point!  Earlier in the year I had a temp position where I was not allowed to wear earbuds (so I could hear supervisors talking to me about the work/line), but they told me the bone conduction ones were okay since I could hear them while music was playing.  So I got a great deal of use out of my first pair and wanted to try this pair that seemed like it would outdo my other one.  That's why I gave it 4 stars.  It works - works about the same as my other pair.  I don't have any issues with how they are worn or the quality of the music.  I'm not a headbanger, so requiring loud, heavy bass isn't my thing.  If it's yours, then these are definitely not for you!  I'm just slightly disappointed these didn't run rings around my other pair... but oh well...

title: I keep trying these earbuds with the "sticks" on the end
review: It seems most people like these and I truly would like to, but the pairs I have tried don't work well for my ears.  Not sure if I have odd-shaped ear-pans or what, but they don't stay in place well in my ears, dang it.  I can say that the sound quality of these earbuds is exceptionally good.  The only problem I really suffer from is a fitment issue between this style of earbud and my ear canal.  I have a very tiny pair of in-ear earbuds that do not have the "stem" on them and they are the only pair I've had that stay in well.  Maybe it's my jaw movement that keeps these from sitting properly...I don't really know.  All I do know is that they work themselves loose and will eventually fall out within a very short period of time.  During the time they are in, the music sounds wonderful and my audio books' sound clean and clear.  I guess I'm just not physically made to wear this type of earbud.

title: This is my second set of bone conduction phones
review: I love the fact that bone conduction allows the user to hear both their music (or audio book or podcast) without sacrificing the ability to hear all around you.  I see people with earbuds in their ear and think, man, you are a mugging (or even kidnapping) waiting to happen!  With these you can still hear people walking up on you, still hear someone speaking to you, hear a car approaching if you are running and use the side of the road.  The sound is great - it is a bit different because bone conduction does not cover your ears,, but I can say the sound is quite good.

title: For my perpetually cold daughter who loves her tunes
review: I had talked to her about getting a full skull cap hat with headphones for her, but she was all like, "I hate those because they mess up my hair!"  Okay then!  Yeah, my daughter is a diva...but we all have our own preferences, right?  So I got this headband style so that she can keep her ears warm without messing up her hair and at the same time listen to her tunes.  She seems to be quite pleased with this headband so I'm thinking they do keep her always cold ears warm and that the headband's ear phones work fairly well so she can rock out while wearing the headband.  Worth it if you have a diva (either male or female) in your life!

title: Excellent bone conduction headphone
review: I have several different types of headphones and the bone conduction headphones are really great if you still need to hear what's going on around you.  I mean, I have watched runners with earbuds in and know they can't really hear a bike coming alongside them, couldn't hear a car veering off the road near them...a mugger running up behind them...so many reasons NOT to wear earbuds while running!  Bone conduction headphones allows the music to reach inside your ears without covering your ears by conducting the sound through the bone just in front of your ear.  You still get great sound - really great sound with these bone conduction earphones - but you can hear if the doctor's nurse calls you in for your appointment, can hear your boss calling your name as he walks up to your cubicle and more...what I really love about this set over the set I have now is that this one folds.  My other bone conduction does not.  Now, the only thing I would wish for is either a hard, zip up container so I could carry them with me wherever I go or at the very least, a nice drawstring bag - either one would keep the headphones cleaner/neater in my purse or pocket.  Bottom line, this is a wonderful bone conduction headphone!

title: I love these!
review: This headset is absolutely perfect for listening to the television or streaming on the laptop late at night when others are asleep in bed.  The setup is fast and easy - just about anyone should be able to do it (I'm a 64 year old lady) on both tv and laptop.  It is nice being able to hear the show you want to watch without bothering your husband/wife sleeping next to you or even if you are out in the living room and have little kids that might end up getting out of bed because the tv's sound woke them up - so worth keeping the peace if you can't sleep or are just a night owl.  Definitely worth trying these out!

title: It's not just the silicone eartips...
review: See, I have apparently somewhat small ears for accommodating earbuds and while I have tried changing out eartips to some success, many earbuds just do not stay in my ears very well.  These do and that's a big deal for me.  I'm no expert on the sound quality of earbuds but these have great sound for both music and audio books.  I tend to listen to audio books a lot as I have some eye issues that keep me from reading like I used to when I was younger.  I have used over the ear headphones, but after a time they 1) create heat and 2) become somewhat painful pressing on the skin around my ears.  So earbuds are a better way to go.  And as far as earbuds that I have tried, these are great for my smaller-sized ears.  They stay in well and the sound is great.  Oh, and the case is very small!  I have another set of earbuds I will probably give to my son in law that are big - they are too big for my ears and the case is quite a bit larger.  Last, this pair is similar to that bigger set in that these can be listened to separately - I mean one at a time.  Sometimes that can make it difficult to get them to sync together, but after about 5 minutes I got them synced and once they have been synced, it's much easier the next time using them.

title: Cute in pink and good for music
review: I'm not so much one that uses earbuds to talk on my cell phone.  In fact, I don't really like talking on phones, period, so I'm not the go-to for how well these work when answering a call on your phone.  I'm just more of a texter person.  As far as listening to music or an audio book on my phone, these earbuds work great!  I love the ANC, noise cancelling properties so that I don't have to listen to people talking around me or just a noisy environment.  I did have to change out the plugs to small - I have fairly small ear canals - but that's not a big deal.  I also like that the case has a charge time - meaning that it doesn't have to be hooked up each time the buds need charging.  If you are out for most of the day, you can put the buds in the case for maybe an hour and get several more hours of playtime before the case itself needs charging.  I have had another set of earbuds that pair individually and found them a bit difficult at times to pair simultaneously, but this set doesn't have the same issues as the other.  If I did NOT pull both buds from the case at exactly the same time on that other pair, I would only get one of them to pair with my phone!  These did not have that problem and paired with just a bit of messing with.  The sound quality is excellent in my opinion and the case is small enough to slip into a pocket of my purse making them highly portable.  Cute in pink, sound good, long play time and easy to take along - what more could I want!?!

title: These are both good and bad
review: For me, that is.  One, these have EXCELLENT sound!  They really do.  I don't really get the chance to see how long the charge lasts as I don't commute more than a few minutes to work and I'm really not able to wear headphones at work because I'm on the phone about 3/4ths of the time I'm at work.  Two, I really like the fact that the case itself holds a charge so that when you place the ear buds in the case, they will charge without having to have the case hooked up each time.  That's a big plus.  Now for the bad part - I have very small ear canals and this type of ear bud does not fit well in my ear.  I mean, if I'm not moving around too much they will stay in my ear, but if I am walking around the kitchen or putting clothes in the washing machine, they work loose and if I don't keep fiddling with them, they will fall out.  It may just be me...I do really appreciate the quality sound and case charging, though.

title: For the price I expected more
review: I have an inexpensive one that I think I paid $18-$20 for that works okay.  I don't often wear it as a sleep headband because the two earphone speakers are thicker and not comfortable if you sleep on your side.  It's okay when I fall asleep in my recliner, but just not when I pull my pillow up under my face when on my side.  When I saw this one and at this price point, I thought, wow, maybe I just bought the cheap-o one and this is the real sleep headband I should have gotten.  Well...that was just a thought.  This isn't a better sleep headband.  It's almost exactly the same.  The internal earphones are, it seems, the same - too thick to sleep on and interestingly, this one's sound is not as good as my $20 one!  So...my suggestion is, if you sleep on your back, look for a cheaper one that this.  You'll be happy with it and have more money in your pocket!

title: Looking at this, I thought it would be a bit bigger
review: Don't get me wrong - having it come to me smaller than I thought isn't a bad thing.  What is the problem with this little MP3 player is just about everything else.  The touch screen is extremely touchy.  I tried to update the time/date on this thing and was so frustrated trying to get into that area and make the changes.  I also had issues getting this paired via bluetooth to a pair of headphones.  If you have more patience than I do, you might like this little MP3 player.

title: I am very impressed with this headband
review: I have tried earbuds, over the ear headphones, bone conduction and I even have a cool pair of neck speakers that are way cool, but these are like my first and probably favorite small headphones.  What I used for many years had ear hooks but were over the ear, small headphones (so no "headband" between the ear pieces).  These were all wired ones and of course, I prefer wireless these days.  I did not lay down on these as they show in the pictures, but considering the thickness of the one "controller" piece, I wouldn't want to lay down on it!  It would hurt!  What I mean is that the piece is too thick to be comfortable laying on.  The other side probably would be fine, though.  The sound this headband produces is quite good considering.  I could see wearing this on a walk or while working - it's a really nice audio headband and will be using it when I take my daily walk around the neighborhood!

title: This is such a cool take-along
review: I love how small and portable this is!  My only wish is that it came with both the usb C and the usb 2.0 micro plugs as those are the most common two ports I have on rechargeables.  My phone definitely uses the usb C which is great since I can tuck this little charger in my purse for emergencies, but most of my earphones/buds use the usb 2.0 micro plug to recharge.  Just took a star for that - not a big deal - but the more useful an item can be, the better, right?

title: Had to change the cushions
review: Not sure why all earbuds seem to be fitted for the largest ear possible, since the ones on this set were so big I couldn't even attempt to insert them in my ears, but this wireless headphone comes with a set of cushion replacements in different sizes.  I changed them out for ones that fit well and am pleased with the sound and how these work.  I have been afraid of wearing wireless earbuds when doing physical work (and sweating) - didn't want one of the earbuds dropping out and then having to throw the other one away when I couldn't find the dropped one, so...these solve that problem.  If one slips out, it isn't going very far!  The neck piece is "invisible" as it is so lightweight I don't notice it at all.  The wires from the neck piece to the earbuds are the only thing I see.  That's okay since I know those wires will keep the earbuds from getting lost.  As I said, they sound great and for what I want them for, these work well for me.

title: These have amazing sound!
review: I have a couple of pairs of earbuds and most have decent sound, but I have to say that for me, these had excellent sound.  Easy to pair and hard to put away as I was so enjoying the music I was listening to with these earbuds.  Well worth the price!

title: This is a wonderful wireless over the ear set of headphones
review: The fact that Carlos Santana has lent his name should indicate that these are a step above many other wireless headsets, but also, Santana has an organization that earmarks some of the money from sales of his items (like these headphones) to fund agencies/organizations that provide services for underserved children in the United States.  Not only are these a great over the ear wireless headset for immersing yourself in quality sound, but at the same time you are helping kids in need.  That's a win-win and one of the reasons why you should get a pair for yourself!

title: Okay but man, read the instructions!
review: These are able to be paired to your phone separately, but DON'T!  Just leave the left alone and one the right is paired, it will successfully pair the left as well.  This is a good pair - wonderful sound - just be sure you read the instructions which I didn't at first...nice set of over-the-ear earbuds.

title: Not just for men!
review: I like a good-sized purse and I prefer a crossbody style bag.  This canvas bag is really just my style.  Now, if it had been in soft leather, that would have been way cool, but I'm not unhappy with this being canvas at all.  I often carry my Kindle with several books downloaded on it, plus wallet, cell phone, earbuds...lots of stuff and this bag will hold it all!  The color I chose is the medium brown which I think looks distressed a bit.  Not like someone has beaten it, but that it just appears it was older.  Nice bag that I will definitely be using often.

title: I was impressed with these
review: When I really want to check out sound quality I try a few Vangelis instrumentals that are so full of depth and range that the buds either pick them up or don't.  Chariots of Fire is a beautiful piece, but it's Alpha and Himalaya that have such unique qualities that if I hear some of the subtle input Vangelis uses in these pieces I know I'm listening with quality earbuds.  I do with the controls were a bit easier to feel and I do find it odd that there is no "next" or other features on these, but then, it's the music that's important, and that is definitely what I heard with these in my ears!

title: These are pretty as well as having awesome sound
review: I got the rose gold pair and they really are pretty with a different top.  Most earbuds have a hinged lid, but this pair has a magnetic lid which could be problematic should you forget to put it back on right after putting the buds in yur ears.  The sound quality of these earbuds is awesome.  I will be keeping these close by - at the house or dropped into my purse for when I'm sitting in the doctor's office or just hanging out.  Love these earbuds!

title: Really great bluetooth headset
review: I am very impressed with this active set - the earbuds fit well in my ears and having them on a wire ensures that should you be running or maybe getting sweaty and one bud slips out, it won't disappear into long grass somewhere along your run.  Instead, the wire around your neck should allow the bud to fall onto your upper chest so you don't have to break stride to put it back in your ear!  The sound is excellent as well - wonderful set of earbuds!

title: Small in size but not in sound
review: This is one cool, small and extremely portable little speaker!  Having earbuds to listen to tunes is great, but sometimes you just want to hear your tunes, right?  Like grilling out or working in the garden, hearing some music adds to whatever you may be doing.  Set this little speaker nearby and enjoy the songs you like to hear!  Oh, and don't worry if it gets a bit wet - it'll keep playing your music!

title: For the price point, these are great little earbuds
review: If you compare these to $80 earbuds, then it's not a fair comparison, right?  But for the price, these earbuds charge well, sync up to my phone quickly and feel good in my ears.  The sound is fine - it isn't concert quality, but as I said, for the price point, these deliver good sound.  The only odd thing is the case.  Most earbuds have a full case that protects them when not in use.  Not sure why the manufacturer thought this was a spiffy idea - it isn't.

title: I picked up a tiny little MP3 player
review: The mp3 player is the size of a jump drive and it has incredible sound, but if I'm walking, I really don't want wired headphones.  This transmitter is also very small and plugged into the mp3 player and paired with earbuds, I can walk unencumbered by wires and listen to my music.  For those who have an audio item like an mp3 player that is not bluetooth compatible, just get this little transmitter.  It works great!

title: I have been using a gaming headset
review: I teach ESL online and have a rather bulky, heavy headset that works fine, but I got these as they are made more for what I need a headset for, plus they are light weight.  The sound quality is great and they fit me better than the gaming headset!  Excellent headset!

title: Works great for what I needed it for
review: I had an over the ear headphone set that came with a fairly short cord - why, I don't know, but in replacing the original cord, I gained the ability to distance myself from the sound source just a bit.  Not that I'm trying to walk all over the house, but if I am in the kitchen and wanting to wear the headphones instead of buds, I can put my Kindle on top of the microwave and stand at the sink washing dishes while I'm listening to one of my audio books.  That is worth having this cord!

title: Great sound with these wired earbuds
review: The cord is really good as well.  Stronger than the average cord so if you are rough on corded earbuds, these might be the best ones for you!  As I mentioned, the sound is great, the earbuds fit well in the ear - excellent pair!

title: Attached to my bedroom television
review: Sometimes I want it to be quiet so that I don't disturb others when watching television late in the evening.  I have this attached to the audio port of my television, paired it with a wireless wrap-around headphone that fits comfortably on my head when sitting up in bed and easier to remove when I'm ready to retire for the evening.  I would also imagine this being helpful for those with some hearing loss - they often want the television up really loud which bothers everyone else in the family.  So if they are able to hear the television without bothering others, then that alone will be worth it, right?  I know I have a friend that had enough hearing loss that when going to the movies, she wore the headphones they provided to her at the theater.  That was the only way she could follow along and my thought was with these, she could hear her favorite shows when at home.

title: I have these tethered using a wireless transmitter
review: I received a wireless transmitter that allows me to use my old and beloved Creative Zen MP3 player as if it was bluetooth enabled.  In order to do that, I needed a pair of wireless earbuds and these were just perfect.  I charged them up and tied them to the wireless transmitter plugged into the audio jack of the Creative Zen.  Selected a song on the Zen, hit play and music blossomed in my ears - full, rich sound that sent me away.  Great buds for the sound that came from them!  I'm also happy with the size, too - the case is very small.  About 2x2 inches, paired with the transmitter and the Zen is a very small package if I want to take them with me.  Very happy with these!

title: Made for bigger heads than mine
review: I was excited to try these out and totally disappointed in the fact that they are NOT adjustable and because of that, putting the earphones in my ears meant that the "headband" was about AN INCH ABOVE MY HEAD!!!  I did try to get it to fit me by moving the band up and back and...it just doesn't fit.  I mean, I may have a smaller head than some folks, but that sure as heck doesn't mean regular over-the-ear headphones don't fit me as THEY have the ability to adjust to fit different head sizes.  I swear I felt like such a goomba trying to fit these on my head...so as far as I'm concerned, this pair was an epic failure on the part of the manufacturer.  I'm sure for those who have a bigger cranium than I these are probably good, but I don't know that since they can't and won't fit me...

title: Bone conduction music and audio books...
review: They are the best!  I still will use in-ear headphones when I need to drowned out other noises, but there are more times when being able to hear what's going on around you is very important.  I mean, I see people walking down the street with their headphones in, texting on their phones and paying absolutely NO attention to their surroundings.  Any yahoo can walk up to you and stick a gun or knife in your ribs and abduct you if you are not aware of your surroundings as well as who is around you.  Running with these bone conduction headphones allows you to have your music or audio book or podcast on, but still hear cars going by, people talking around you, etc.  At least that's why I like these - being able to hear what I want to listen to without affecting my ability to be aware of my surroundings.

title: Excellent earbuds!
review: These are awesome earbuds for the sound, for the battery life, and noise cancellation - I am very pleased with them!  Price, for what you get, is great as well.  I would recommend these to anyone looking for the best bang for their buck in wireless earbuds - can't go wrong with these!

title: I still have an original Creative Zen mp3 player!
review: I love my old Creative Zen mp3 player, but I wanted something smaller, more portable even than my Zen and this little guy is just perfect!  About the same size as a flash drive, it delivers amazing sound for something so tiny.  I have a ton of music stored on a 3 terrabyte external drive and as soon as I unpacked this mp3 player I plugged it into one of my laptop's usb ports and dragged music from the external drive over to copy onto this player.  I then put the supplied earplugs in, powered it up and "went away" with the music.  It was crisp and clear, played my music back to back alphabetically by artist.  The supplied earplugs are not terribly comfortable though they delivered the music well enough so they will probably end up in a drawer somewhere after I choose what type I want to use - earbuds or over the ear headphones - and then I will be in listening mode with this mp3 player!  Want something small for a kid or if you are a runner/jogger?  This is perfect!  I couldn't be happier with it!

title: For the price and sound, these are a nice set of ear buds
review: I paired them without issue and opened my music - sounded great!  These also feel really comfortable in my ears and the case having the ability to charge the buds without having to be plugged in each time is convenient.  Definitely would recommend these to anyone looking for a handy set of earbuds.

title: Quick and easy to pair and sound is amazing
review: I'm not an aficionado of wireless earbuds, but these are GREAT!  Paired them with my phone and wow, the music sounded like I was in the recording studio or in the audience if it was a live piece.  They fit snug in my ears and I didn't hear a thing other than the music - perfect!  As far as moisture wicking, I'm not sure I can speak to that since I don't run and wear earbuds.  I do love listening to music with these earbuds and that, I think, is what you want, right?  Earbuds you don't want to take off!

title: Hooked it to my phone and it sounded great
review: I have wireless buds that I just most often, but pulled out my wired headphones and it did enhance the sound to my headphones.  It would fit fine in a purse, but it isn't as thin as my phone (not as wide or tall as a phone) so I'm thinking this is something for listening to music at home or when you aren't going anywhere for a while.  Maybe sitting in the library doing homework/research or waiting at the doctor's office.  Being a lady, I do carry a good-sized purse - not sure how a guy would handle carrying this unless he's into man-purse messenger bags.  But as far as how this little guy works, it's a simple plug outlet for the mp3 player/phone, a plug outlet for the headphones and then turn it on, adjusting the volume and the H/L gain as needed.  Comes with a usb charger, but I didn't have it on for more than 30 minutes the first time before charging it so I'm not sure how long the charge would last.  Nice little amplifier!

title: Four stars because this set does not include at least one other size replacement buds
review: I have another wireless set that I wear around the house and listen to audio books while doing housework and like them, but I have had wired earphones with the earhook like these and thought these might be a good way to ensure that when I'm bending and stooping to do things while listening to my audio books, these would stay on without issue.  They can and do, but what bothered me is the rubber ear buds are fairly large.  They do fit in my ear, but I just didn't like the feel.  Lucky for me, I do have a set of replacement buds and will replace the ones on here with one size smaller.  So many of this style earphones do include 2-3 pairs of different size ear buds that I would have liked to see some included with this one.  The other thing I noticed was how short the cord is - I don't want it really long, but it seemed just a bit too short - maybe 1-2 inches more would have been appreciated.  Other than that, the work fine and I do like having the ear hooks to keep them in place.

title: Light and easy to wear
review: My daughter just started a customer service position that requires her to have a usb headset.  They would purchase a set for her and take it out of her first paycheck (such a joke since they choose it) or she can supply her own.  I read the sheet they gave her regarding the requirements for the headset and this set fits what they require.  I tested them and they do feel quite light on the head and the pads feel comfortable on the ears.  The controls are large enough to manipulate with a touch.  Useful headset for day-long wear.

title: Has all the features you could need
review: None of the flashy, over-the-top, USB headset, but a good, reliable model that is comfortable and will work well for my needs.  I'm not a gamer, but do use headsets for some work from home business that requires me to Skype and MS Teams for meetings and interviews.  This is a comfortable set to wear and works as it should.

title: Unfortunately mine arrived broken - unable to charge
review: I plugged it in right after I received it - usually JVC is a good product and I wanted to get these paired with my Kindle so I could listen to my Audible books.  It charged all night, I saw the red dot when I plugged it in, the next day I unplugged it and tried to pair it.  Kindle on, ready to pair...can't get the earphones to come on.  Plugged them back in and wow...after about 12 hours, these are showing they hadn't charged at all.  Obviously, there's something wrong with the internal battery or the connection to the internal battery.  Nothing I can do about that, but be sure to check yours right away to be sure there isn't something wrong.  I'm very disappointed with what I received.

title: Really great bluetooth headset
review: I paired this with my cellphone and talked to my sister using this headset.  It is very comfortable to wear, the mic picks up speech well and the background noise seems to be at a minimum.  I could see this being used by long distance truckers to talk to family and or checking in for appointments to deliver while on the road.  If you travel by car a great deal, this would work as well.  I also thought it would be good for Skyping with family since you would not be tethered to the computer and could pick up a child to show grandma on the other end without feeling you will get stopped by a cord.  Highly recommended to those looking for such a headset.

title: I am an Audible-phile and these are perfect for me
review: More people are listening to books these days and I am one of them.  I have a Kindle Fire with quite a few Audible books and these headphones work for when I am trying to clean the house and keep up with my book "reading!"  Yesterday I was washing dishes and listening to a great horror book.  That's about the extent of my multi-tasking abilities, but it was nice being able to keep up with a boring task like washing dishes and still be interested by the narrator of the story I was listening to.  I have always had good luck with Sony products and this one is no exception.  A great wireless headphone if you are looking to purchase one.

title: Comfortable
review: For use during exercise or if, like me, your work (transcription) requires the use of headphones, this pair has turned out to be one of the most comfortable to wear long-term.  As far as the quality of sound, I am not an audiophile, so I can't attest to that, but I can say that the sound quality for the spoken word is excellent.  For the price, these are a good pair!

title: Great case for the Apple earphone pods
review: Great case for the Apple earphone pods.  Love the little silicone covers to get them to fit securely in your ear.

title: $10 for ANC, great fit.
review:
First time charging was a bit confusing. There is only 1 charging indicator LED, and the pattern for a fully charged case and a fully charged earbuds are opposite of each other. It was easier to remove the earbuds, fully charge the case, then charge the earbuds, then again fully charge the case. This was no longer a problem after the first initial cycle. I wish there was a way to see the battery percentage.
Fit has been excellent for me. I like that the control touchpads are not the entire outer surface which makes it easier to push in the earbuds without accidentally changing the music.
ANC has off/on/transparent modes. Noticeably blocks out most ambient sounds, however it isn't perfect. It really struggles with wind noise, so much so that I disable ANC on windy days. In all other environments it was excellent.

title: Excellent sound quality. Earpads aren't that bad.
review:
I'm very happy with these headphones. The sound quality is superb! The two included cables made for easy swapping between desktop and mobile use. No noticeable vibrations from cable movement are transferred into the headphones, the headphones only ring if you grab the metal wire frame on top. They are easy to drive and can get dangerously loud, for desktop I only needed them at 10% volume, for mobile about 20%. These are open headphones which means outside noise is not blocked, but I was pleasantly surprised by how little these headphones leaked outwards at reasonable volumes.

Other reviews had me worried that the included earpads would be unusable, but they are fine. They certainly aren't breathtakingly plush, but they aren't uncomfortable. The earpads do not interfere with using the headphones, the only downside is they form a small sweat spot. I may upgrade them in the future, but definitely not a must.

The packaging could be improved, the cardboard flaps that hold the headphone earcups caused dents in the foam that covers the drivers.

Highly recommended for music, games, and general use.

title: Sound good
review: These earbuds are very comfortable. Sound is pretty good considering the price point. Cord doesn't tangle easily, which is a plus. Only one thing and it's me, not the earbuds, is that the plug is wrong, it's the same plug you would normally see on a set of earbuds that has a mic. They work on all my devices, so it's no issue, just wanted to bring that up in case someone sees the pictures and thinks they're the wrong product.

title: Not a lot of bass
review: These earbuds sound ok for the price, not a lot of bass, but the mids and highs come through crystal clear. They're very comfortable to wear because of the design, and the cord doesn't tangle like most earbuds. Maybe after a break in period they will sound better. As far as noise isolation, they might block 50%-60% of ambient/outside noise, but at this price point, you're not getting the best, nor the worst, you get what you pay for, and these are priced accordingly. All in all a nice set of earbuds at a fair price with decent sound.

title: Great sounding budget earbuds
review: Great sounding earbuds for a great price! Great bass, nice mids and highs. Comes with a ton of different sized buds for a custom fit. Very little wire noise as some earbuds have a lot of noise when the wire hits or scrapes against something. Noise isolation is on par with similar earbuds. Overall happy with these and they come at a great cheap price for a quality earbud. Definitely will buy again if needed. A++

title: Don't listen to the negative reviews
review: Don't listen to the negative reviews. I've owned these Phillips earhook type headphones for almost 10 years and they're still going strong! I didn't get these on Amazon, I bought them at a big box department store. They sound terrific and are comfortable to wear all day long and I have from time to time went to bed listening to music and fell asleep with them and they never fell off nor did they hurt or chaff my ears. For the money spent, these are very hard to beat in both quality and sound. If I'm ever in the need to buy another pair, I'll buy these again without hesitation. A++

title: Works for me
review: Just what I needed for my headphones. I opted for the 25ft cable as I like to listen to music late at night and don't want to disturb my neighbors, but also wanted something long enough that allows me to walk from room to room without having to take my headphones off. This fits the bill nicely. No signal loss, doesn't kink up much and looks to be of good quality. I have several other KabelDirekt products and they don't disappoint. I'm happy with this purchase and my neighbor are sure to be happy I'm not blasting them out of their beds at 1am.

title: Great sounding headphones!
review: Best bang for your buck. Sounds great and has plenty of bass response. Mids and highs are clear as a bell and the cord is plenty long enough for me as I'm using these headphones with my guitar amp as to not annoy my neighbors late at night lol. Fit snug and unless you have abnormally large ears, these fit over, not on! Hoping to get a few years out of these, but for the price I would buy again.

title: Maybe my head is strange
review: So this is the 4th pair of headband headphones I have tried.  They all just don't fit me comfortably for sleeping or laying down while using.  It very well could be my misshapen melon.
