I’m not pro at headphones, just a regular person who loves music, and I am thoroughly enjoying these headphones. I have some great pictures I took of them when I first got them, will add when I get back home. And will also have another chance to use them on the plane again. So far I love these! I guess I’ll add a quick pic from the hotel safe via my phone. 5 stars from me!

title: Very nice gaming headphones
review: These are a great set of headphones for the Xbox. We especially like the mics ability to be muted simply by pushing it up. Sound quality is awesome. Easy volume controls on the side of the earphone. Can’t go wrong with these. We’ve used Turtle Beach products for years. Never disappointed.

title: Great Headphones!
review: These headphones are really nice. They fit great and I really like the red color. But, what is even better is the clear sound. Even the deeper, bass notes come through nicely. I like that the music can be paused by pushing the button that is attached to the wires. It is easy to reach for that to pause when needed. I definitely recommend these headphones.

title: Great Quality
review:
These are great! We use them in our house for our VR headset so we can play games like Rec Room and use the mic. Sound quality (both input and output) is impressive. Fits super comfortable even with the VR headset on.

Pros:
- Suprisingly nice fit. Comfortable
- Plugs into VR HMDs great (Valve Index, Acer WinMR, Oculus Quest (no mic))
- Plugs into normal stereo ports great for just headphones
- Works great without the USB attachment
- Mic sounds great, not too much extra noise
- Headphones have good bass / highs (not an expert)

Cons:
- Looks a little clunky
- Wired

Highly Recommend!

title: Nice headphones.
review: Great battery life, decent sound quality.  Fits good and rather comfortable.  Good quality..  instructions were easy to understand. Headphones are pretty good overall.  Recommended.

title: Highly recommend
review: These truly are nice heAdphones.  I’ve owned a few pairs of wireless headphones and these are some of the better ones.  They have really realistic sound quality.  They also do a great job of holding their charge.  I have smaller ear canals and these are very comfortable for me to wear.  Recommended

title: Good sound quality
review: Very good headphones, great fit, very comfortable.  Sound quality is pretty good.  These don’t make you sweaty either which is a huge plus.  Recommended.

title: Comfortable buds
review: Good little earbuds,  very comfortable to wear. I like the color as it’s so bright they’re easy to find when I misplace them.  Good sound quality. Fit is nice. Recommended

title: Great sound quality
review: These are great headphones.  They’re everything I hoped that they’d be.  The sound is really nice and high quality.  They pair seamlessly with my devices also.  Highly recommend.

title: The noise cancellation is bizarre
review:
I adore the style and convenience of my gen 1 AirPods, so I was looking for some cheaper "dupes" that I could keep around as backups.

My main complaint is how noise cancellation is overall implemented with these earbuds. The buzzing of the noise cancellation is very obvious and can overpower audio played on low volume (as one should). It also is always and only active when audio is playing, so there's no option to have noise cancellation only (unless you play an empty music track or something like that).

That said, I think these are strong earbuds as far as Bluetooth concerns go. The battery life seems to be pretty good, the connection is very stable, and I have slightly greater range with these than my AirPods.

Finally, the earbuds ship with no instruction manual at all. It wasn't hard to find my way around these, but this is a very poor practice for selling electronics.

title: Battery life is absolute crap
review:
I have two major complaints: (1) the battery life is crap (it claims to be 10hrs, but I only got 3hrs off of full charges), and (2) the volume of automated messages (like "battery low" warnings and "pairing" status updates) are terrifyingly loud and do not seem to respond to volume buttons.

To me, these are major problems and I will absolutely be returning these earbuds. However, there are some good aspects that I appreciate -- the sound quality is much better than the other bluetooth headphones in the <$40 price bracket that I've tried, the earbud tip is very comfortable and comparable in shape to Apple EarPods (but a little bit larger), and the magnetism means that it is hard to lose these when not in ear.

title: Excellent product
review: Very happy with these magnetic twist ties! I am very happy with the durability and versatility of these little things -- works great for headphones and all kinds of cables, even heavy duty ones. I definitely anticipate ordering more of these in the future.

title: Very good quality
review: I bought this as gift for my dad. He really likes the sound quality and battery life, but complained that there isn't a way to monitor the charge on the headphones.

title: Great adaptor for Apple compatible headphones on Windows machines
review: Works well to allow me to use my Bose headphones with an Apple compatible cable for Skype calls on my Windows laptop from work.

title: Direct Sound stands by their product
review:
What a great company! I bought these headphones as a Christmas gift for my husband. A hinge broke off from the headband after about two months, too late for an Amazon refund. I emailed Direct Sound Headphones, and John Gresko immediately wrote back offering a replacement part; three days later it was in our mailbox, no charge. Terrific, responsive service! Thank you, Direct Sound!

PS My husband loves the EX25 headphones.

title: Do yourself a favor and buy these!!
review: The Bowers & Wilkins PX7 Over Ear Wireless Bluetooth Headphone, Adaptive Noise Cancelling - Silver really impressed me. We are no strangers to headphones/headsets in our household (we are not experts though). We have bose and beats and gaming headsets as well. These boasted a nice clear crisp sound, have great volume control and the option to use with noise canceling and other options. The noise cancelling works almost perfectly. I used them while having 7 adults carrying on loud conversations and  couldn't hear them, but when it was on the one thing I could hear was when I was doing the dishes and the silverware was clinking around, but barely. My favorite feature is that if I'm listening to a song and I take the head set off they pause the song and when I put them back on they resume the song by themselves.

title: Great head set.
review: The Turtle Beach Recon Spark Universal Gaming Headset turned out to be a great head set. Turtle beach has never let us down before and these were great. We are loving the more "girly" colors. We are a family who plays together a lot and 3 of us are girls. The headsets we have are some sort of black or black/color, so to have such a softer color was nice. The sound quality is great and the flip mic is great. We use the headset with an xbox one controller with no problems. The padding on top and the ear is really comfortable. This headset has been comfortable fitting a 5 year old and a 40 year old. I would definitely recommend this headset.

title: Truly noise cancelling!!
review: These headphones are amazing. I am usually not a fan of headphones that go in the ear, but these are very comfortable. They give you the option to then on/off ambient noises/noise cancelling or nothing. I have 4 loud children and a husband, so I decided to see how truly noise cancelling they were. Popped them in while my husband was on the phone, tv was on and toys were going off and could only hear my music. That right there won be over. They also have the ability to take phone calls. Connecting via bluetooth was extremely simple and they charge right in the case via USB-C. Do yourself a favor and buy a pair, you won't be disappointed.

title: Very comfortable.
review: This headset is very comfortable. It plugged right into our controller and worked no problem. The sound quality is really nice. The volume is on the back of the left ear piece and I like how you flip the mic all the way back to mute.

title: Very comfortable.
review: The headphones were very comfortable to use. I was able to use them and so was my husband with the different size ear pieces and it fit us both very well. They lasted for the 3 hours easily. I really like that you they have a charging case you put them into and plug that in. Pairing them with my phone was super easy too. They don't have much base, but the sound is still really nice. They also did a great job with the clarity.

title: Good for budget headphones
review: For a bulk set of headphones on a budget, these are nice. They're not high quality, but they've mostly worked and my children have appreciated having them. One of my children wears them often and they don't seem to bother him all that much. They do hurt my other two children, though, so they can't wear them for long, especially the one that wears glasses. They've been able to use them for schoolwork, watching videos, listening to music, and playing their video games. They've worked well for some of those, but only okay for their game communication. They seem to echo, and it bugs some of the other players. Overall, they're not the best around, but we've been mostly happy with them.

title: Handy....
review: This is a super handy device. It's worked well for us so far and we've been happy with it. It makes me feel a little safer having it during a storm. It has several features all in one. There's a flashlight, which includes multiple brightness levels, along with flashing mode. (To turn it off, you have to press it down solid for a few seconds.) There's a radio, an sos siren, and a solar charging panel on the top. There's even a hand crank for generating power to it. You can also charge devices with it and there's a place for headphones, if desired. It's great to have around.

title: Nice for my children...
review:
We wanted something simple for our children to be able to listen to music with. Having these gives us better control of what they're listening to, though there is still a radio option on here. We tried out 3 different ones, so each of our children could have their own. Though two of them have different brand names, they all look exactly the same. They even have the same packaging. We haven't noticed anything at all different about them, so I'm using the same review for all three.

These have worked great for us. The quality of them looks nice. They're small enough that my children can easily put them in their pockets when they want to listen to music on their walks(or any other time), but not so small that they get lost. When they all want to listen, the speaker allows them all to hear, but if no one but them wants to hear it, headphones can be used. These do come with basic wired headphones, but others can be used. My children prefer a sturdier type of headphone, as opposed to these. It also comes with a cable for charging, but you'll have to plug it in to a charging box, a computer(which is what we're doing), or something similar. There are extra features that my children don't need and use right now, but it's still nice to have those options ready for future use. It's easy for them to use and my husband said it's easy to load their music on them. We've been pleased with them.

title: Nice headphones...
review:
These are nice headphones. They're incredibly comfortable, and the ear covers are very cushioned. It doesn't block out other sounds completely, but it does a much better job of it than any of our other headphones. They are on the big and chunky side, though, so if you want headphones on the less obvious side, these aren't the way to go. They do have a great quality to them, both in looks and feel.

They have connected well to our bluetooth devices, with no trouble. The control buttons are right on the headphones and easy to use. They have a great battery life. We don't have super high needs for our headphones, but we've been well pleased with the sound quality and just overall.

title: You'll need speakers, since the monitor itself has no sound.
review:
If you could call a monitor beautiful, I'd have to call this one so. The frame around the screen is white, and I happen to find that refreshing! The curved screen is pretty magnificent, too.

First of all, you will need speakers of some sort or headphones to use this monitor. Without them, you won't hear a thing. Since our use of it is mostly consisting of streaming usage, we bought a set of speakers. It works beautifully at steaming videos. The picture is bright and clear.

To turn the monitor off and on, you will have to press a button on the back a few times. (Press it, press angling down a bit, and then press it again.) Turning it on only requires pressing it once, though. This same button is used for ALL adjustments.

Again, we've mainly used it with steaming videos, but we've been extremely pleased with the picture quality.

title: Comfortable and Cool!
review:
I love the looks of these. There are so many headphones out there that look ridiculous, and I'd be embarrassed to be seen wearing. These are cool!

Also, they are comfortable! They don't feel awkward on my head, and they don't constantly fall off. They adjust so much that they also fit comfortably on my little guys(3-7) when they are doing computer learning. It helps to block out loud brother noises and distractions. I mostly use these for listening to audio books and podcasts, so as far as sound quality, they work perfectly great for us. They aren't noise cancelling by any means, but they do take the edge off of outside noise.

title: Pretty Great!
review:
There really isn't set-up involved with these headphones. Just pull them out of the package and turn them on. (Of course, make sure bluetooth is turned on on your device.) Otherwise, you're good to go!

These headphones DO charge in order to work. A charging cable that you can plug into a USB port is included, but if you want a wall charger, you'll have to buy that separately. That means these headphones are wireless. The claim is 30 feet, and I'd say that's correct, if walls aren't in the picture. Walls do cut a bit off that range.

The sound quality is pretty good. There was some cutting out, but I believe that was more of a wi-fi issue, as opposed to the headphone's fault.

If you're wanting these for jogging/running/walking, they DO get hot(as in sweaty hot, not "catch-on-fire" hot).

Overall, these are pretty great headphones!

title: ...Mic quality poor
review: I returned these because the mic is not as good as my $10 wired earbuds with a mic.

title: Sound and Bluetooth work great.  The ear buds? Not so much.
review: Four or five stars for the battery,  sound quality and Bluetooth but only two stars for the ear buds.  At least for me the flap thing that fits in your ear tends to twist and come off but the real irritating thing is the piece that fits in your ear canal  can stay in your ear when you pull the earphones off and you end up digging for them.  I chose the buds that fit my ear the best but digging them out of your ear canal is a pain.  I mean I can pull the piece out with my fingers but just barely.

title: Great for activities
review: These sound good and are waterproof and stay where you want them during vigorous activities. The sound quality is great and no negatives to be noticed these are top notch earphones.

title: Awesome
review: If you have purchased a Samsung product before then the name anker will sound familiar to you. These far surpassed the ones that came with my s10 plus. The earphones fit comfortably and unlike others the shape allows you to comfortable lay down while using. The sound quality is awesome and very loud while in ears but make no sound out. These have built in noise reduction that actually works and speakers of course for calling. The charging box is top of the line and uses USB c as most do now. Overall these are my new go to headphone.

title: These hit so hard they vibrate. Great sound killer bass
review: These come in a nice box great presentation and durable carrying case is included.  When I first touched them they felt a bit substandard as the plastic felt cheap but that was just misleading as these are well made light weight plastics that are pretty solid.  These have buttons to adjust the volume on them easily accessed and a bass slide lever that of course adjusts the bass. With the mass on maximum I forgot I was reviewing these headphones and jammed out for 30 minutes untill I remembered what I was doing. The bass hits on these like a car with a system of subwoofers hits. These will vibrate on your head with bass. For the price you get better sound than a 300 dollar pair of jabra elite 85h that I own but not downing those they have many more features. Overall if these are just to jam out to some good music with great bass for a good price tag then these are the way to go.

title: For average task it gets job done
review: This is a decent cheap option if you want a good sounding set without paying an arm an a leg. This isnt a high quality gaming headset but it will get the job done and wont let you down. This is comfortable on your ears and has decent sound quality and a decent mic. For the average person this will get it done I recommend this product.

title: Listen to my old mix tapes and laugh
review: This is a bit of nostalgia. The first thing I did was show it to my kids to see if they could guess what it was and they all failed. The player has no static the music quality is as good as your headphones allow. It has am FM radio function and comes with earbuds and if you can find some blank tapes you can even record an old school mix tape.

title: Wow
review: Wow just wow these are great headphones. One of my favorite features the headphones auto pause when taken off ears and auto resume when put back on. The music is comparable to a car with a sound system. Call quality is great and the person on other line can hear you even if you whisper because of the 9 yes 9 microphones in the headset. It is Alexa compatible although i don't use it. Love the auto turn on and connect feature just by unfolding the headset turn off same way by folding up. The battery life is amazing and charges rather quickly.  Comes with a nice carrying case. I could go on and on about this product and highly recommend it.

title: Five Stars
review: Great product ordered for kids a different color per child to keep up with earbuds.

title: Serves purpose
review: Cheaper earphones but will do for what I bought them for. Children will destroy or lose them no matter the cost so i am happy.

title: Sound great/clear & reach high volume!
review: These headphones sound great all around. For the the avid entertainment adventurer these are awesome. By no means are they studio quality but that's not what they were built for! (having read some ridiculous semi pro user reviews) If you are looking for a great set to watch tv, listen to music (stream or flac), or play a game they are awesome and definitely worth the investment.

title: No. No. No.
review: Oh my god, who designed this thing?!? I needed to replace the cheapo wireless headphones I used to watch TV with while my kids are alseep/doing homework/not in the mood to listen to Downton Abbey and I relied on Sennheiser reputation when buying these headphones. Not only is the sound quality unacceptable but the absolute worst part is that if the headphones don't get a signal for a certain amount of time (3 minutes maybe?) the base turns off automatically and your ears are assaulted by the most awful screeching sound. So, for example, if you're in the kitchen cooking dinner with the headphones on and the show ends, or your song ends...you have to whip those puppies off your ears pronto or else you will be scared sh***less when the buzzing/shrieking begins. So, just be sure to never have your hands full when the music stops.

title: Pricey but worth it
review:
Love these headphones! I bought the Sennheiser 120 set first and found them unusable (see separate review), but these are amazing! I use them both for watching television, and for listening to music. They have a pretty good range, but my living space isn't all that large so I don't really test it that way. I can wander outside to my deck without loosing any signal. The microwave does cause interference, but how often does that matter?

Overall an amazing set of headphones. Pricey, but worth it.

title: Five Stars
review: These are great. I have tried DOZENS of bluetooth headphones/sets/buds and I decided to keep these. Sound is great!

title: Expensive, but suede more comfortable than originals
review: While somewhat expensive, these suede replacement ear pads make the headphones much more comfortable than the originals supplied by Sony. I can wear the headphones now for longer periods of time without sweating around the ear.

title: Comfortable even with glasses and sound terrific
review: I like the looks of the headphones, the very good sound they produce, the option to use them wired or wireless, and the feature that allows me to hold my hand over the right ear cup to mute the sound and allow me to hear voices around me.  I wear glasses, and at first the headphones were not as comfortable as I had hoped, but after a week or two of using them, they are very comfortable and I can wear them for hours without adjusting the fit. The  headphones have two of the most important features for me: comfortable to wear with glasses and sound terrific.

title: Three Stars
review: Not comfortable to wear. I bought these Sony headphones because they were clip-ons and also had retractable cords. I wanted headphones that took up less space in my bag. I have been using for years the Koss DSC75 headphones, which are clip-ons and very comfortable to wear with excellent sound. While the Sony headphones do take up less space, they do not sound as good or as comfortable to wear as the Koss headphones.

title: ... replacement earpads for the Sennheiser headphone are much more comfortable than the original earpads
review: These replacement earpads for the Sennheiser headphone are much more comfortable than the original earpads.

title: Highly recommend - Good fit and sound
review: I bought these headphones to use at the gym and am not disappointed. They fit well and the sound is very good. I bought a pack of replacement cushions, since they will surely need to be replaced someday and I have found with other headphones that they may not be available years later.

title: When one achieves a good seal, the sound quality is good
review: First rate concept with second rate execution.  When one achieves a good seal, the sound quality is good.  Without a seal, the sound quality is hollow.  The app does seem to be able to shift levels of noise cancelation by monitoring your activity, which is impressive.  Again, with the appropriate seal, the combination of noise cancellation/isolation does create an immersive experience, even on a NYC subway.  However, I found it difficult to achieve and maintain a good seal.  The earphone needs to be inserted quite deep within the ear which left me both emotionally and physically uncomfortable.  I was left worrying about how the product might affect my hearing, as slight movement created a vacuum that stretched my inner ear to a problematic degree.  I am disappointed as a wireless, noise cancelling ear bud would greatly improve my daily routine at the gym and on my commute.  I would greatly prefer a more open design, like that employed by Bose's QC20s (which I have used extensively for years).  I am returning these and will keep my eye on the market...

title: Works great with teams
review: Overall these are decent headsets for teams.  I’ve had a lot trouble getting something to work with teams and these just work.  The sound is ok for on ear headphones and according to others the mic is decent.  The range is really great. I’ve walked all over the house, even up two floors without dropping connection.  Battery life is ok, lasts about 2-3 weeks between charges, but given how often I use it I was expecting months between charges. One thing i find annoying is I get a slight feedback from my mic into my headphones.  I can tell it is the mic because when I mute them I get zero feedback. Comfort is ok but over the ear open back headphones are far more comfortable.  Would recommend if you need something for teams, but for anything else I would not recommend.

title: Good mic, bad attachment mechanics
review: This mic is ok.  The mic itself actually works really good.  It picks up my voice with no problem and it sounds really clear.  The problem with this thing is the way you attach it,  It attaches to your headphone cable.  Placement is important because too high and the angle doesn't catch you voice just right while too low and the same problem.  I have a large headphone cable and it doesn't want to always stay attached resulting in falling on the ground.  Then the day came when one of the plastic prongs which attach to your cable broke.  I accidentally stepped on it and broke it.  It was my fault but now I have a completely useless mic.

title: review
review: These earphone tips simply rock. They really block the outside noise. These tips also make your earplugs sound much better than they used to. This product is amazing.

title: Absolutely love these headphones
review: Absolutely love these headphones.  Great start to an audiophile path.  Not "the best", but still very good and if you like good quality sound but don't want to pay a ton (there's a set of 1000$ headphones that apparently blow you away in quality) these are for you.  Shame about the color, don't mind anymore.  Comfort is fantastic.  Puts anything else I've listened to (speakers) or put in my ears (headphones) to shame, and there's still room to upgrade.

title: So great to be able to use my own headphones on the plane
review: Plane earphones/headphones stink and these have been great to allow me to use my own noise cancelling earphones on the plane. One of the 3 is a little finicky where if the plug is rotated, the distribution of the sound between left and right changes, but the other 2 don't do that. I'm satisfied.

title: Sound quality when used with headset is meh
review: Really easy to install, but if you use this for a headset the sound quality is pretty disappointing.

title: Comfortable but fragile
review: These are the most comfortable headphones I've ever worn. I use these 8-10 hours straight at work and feel no discomfort for extended use. The biggest issue is the cheap plastic extender. If you take these off and use too much force (spreading the ends too far apart) the ear pad will easily break apart. However the quality of sound is nice and can get quite loud if need be. I wouldn't recommend for young children but for someone who is gentle with their stuff.. These headphones make a cheap alternative to beats or other high dollar headphones.

title: Awesome sub-$100
review: If you are looking to spend $100 or less on headphones, and you care about sound quality and don't care so much about looks, buy these headphones. I would not wear them on the street, because they are closed (sound isolation is pretty good) and because they look like $30 headphones. But my oh my, they sound fantastic. I also own a pair of Hifiman HE-500 headphones and Sennheiser HD-650 headphones. For the money, these cans are fantastic. Both of those audiophile-grade headphones sound better, but these hold their own. Notably, there is no clear peak in the frequency response - they aren't bass-boosted, but the bass is strong. Highs are clear, without being sharp. They don't distort or rattle. They do sound like "closed" headphones, though - forward, and not laid-back and open. In short, they sound better than anything I've heard for under $100. They just make you look like a news cameraman, is all.

title: Great product, fantastic customer service
review:
I bought SE 530's they day they came out. I have been delighted with them. Sound quality, comfort, isolation, features (the PTH unit, and now the iphone microphone cable). The sound is comparable to my Sennheiser HD 650's, but unlike the Senns, you can take these with you! I recently returned them due to volume attenuation in one monitor. Customer service was completely helpful - they went out of their way to keep me a happy customer. Shure is a great company - great product, great follow-through - and I trust them with my business.

I can't believe the amazing prices these headphones are now selling for!

title: Small iPod W/ Great Sound
review: I purchase this iPod Shuffle 2GB for my mother. As she is 60 years old and is not tech savvy, she was able to learn how to use it very quickly. She mainly uses it for work out sessions and normal use. The headphones are not the best for someone that is active and goes to the gym a lot, so its suggested getting an appropriate active headphones that secure in to the ear. The buttons are soft and simple to press, the audio range does go very high that I was even impress how much amplification this little product has. Overall my mother was satisfied with her Apple iPod.

title: Lasted barley a year
review: These were 'fine' headphones, not quite worth the price but fine... and then the battery life just died off. They last maybe two hours on a charge. I don't know what's happened to Anker product but I think I'm done with them across the board.

title: Poor sound breaks after 2 months
review: I was excited for an affordable wireless sleeping headphone. The sound quality on these was mediocre, but fine for audio  books. Weirdly choppy like it's reconnecting every time the speaker pauses. There were also issues with poor bluetooth connection with it  cutting in and out if I laid wrong. Then. Just two months after I recieced them, the right ear completely stopped working. Argh! I really wanted these to be my sleeping sollution, but they're just poor quality.

title: Incredible deal for the price with the added benefit of having great sound dampening for people nearby.
review: Great headphones. Better then my very expensive overear headphones for not being a rude @#!$%* on public transit and "sharing" my music with everyone else. Sound quality is pretty solid for the price.

title: As soon as I plugged in a set of headphones ...
review: As soon as I plugged in a set of headphones I heard ground hum.  I didn't try the USB port.  This will be going back.

title: These in-ear headphones are comfortable enough to leave in for the entire duration of ...
review: These things are witchcraft. Magic. Sorcery. Put them on and the entire world just disappears. I've been a big Bose fan and owned a pair of the Bose QuietComfort 2 over-ear model. They worked well but were very bulky and -- for those of us who wear glasses -- a bit of a pain!  These in-ear headphones are comfortable enough to leave in for the entire duration of an international flight, and fit easily in a pocket. Worth every penny.

title: Headphones Great. Noise Canceling bad.
review: Nope. Big fail for these headphones. I have owned the M4U-1's for about a year and love them. I work in a noisy environment and have been wanting to try these for awhile. When the price dropped $100 I bought them having read so many great reviews. Man was I disappointed in the noise canceling aspect of these headphones. This is where PSB has failed. When the noise canceling is off these headphones are amazing. All sound is crystal clear with no emphasis on any one area of sound. Details are present and real sounding. Highs are clean and pleasant to the ear. Bass is good and solid and not in your face. These are truly well balanced headphones, but that all goes away when the noise canceling or just the amp is turned on. Highs become annoyingly tinny. The midrange becomes compressed and bass is now over emphasized. To make matters worse there is an annoying hiss being generated by the noise canceling process. Why have noise canceling if it's going to generate noise. I sent these back. So disappointed. I'm surprised PSB would produce such bad noise canceling when their standards are so high in the audio world. Bummer.

title: For the price I was disappointed
review:
I own several pairs of ANC headphones so I'm not some audiophile but in general I've purchased enough to have a good idea of what I like.

PROS:
Sleek looking - so they look great in the box until you put them on (see CONS)
Comfortable - let's be honest, that's important!
Noise level - good until it gets too high

CONS:
These look GIGANTIC on my head
The ANC is "meh". I tested these against my Taotronics and Treblabs and they work better than the Ankers headphones which were honestly surprising given the Taotronics and Treblabs are a year old.
There's a loud hissing noise when you turn up the volume

Overall I'm not sure if I got a bad one since these are a brand new model, but I can't recommend them when there are other brands that have a better ANC functionality AND cost less.

title: So good I bought TWO!
review: I picked up a pair for my wife so that she could work in a coffee shop amongst the noise.  Amazingly, these work very well!  Now compared to the Bose quiet noise headphones, their quality and tech pale in comparison but honestly, my wife was just looking for something to help reduce the noise distraction and these were perfect!  I spend $20 at Walmart and since she loved them so much, I picked up a pair for myself!  They definitely reduce the noise and with music on, it drowns out everything else.  Quality is great as we’ve had them for 6-7 months with no issues and for $20 bucks I can’t complain.

title: Happy with my purchase
review: Was looking for a pair of wireless headphones that weren't way too expensive. The Backbeat Go2 were in my price range, if the headphones are in and I turn them on they give me a warning of the battery level. It's a 4 hr battery, it fits comfortable in my ears and with the clothing clip I keep the chords behind my neck, though they are completely unnecessary. I'm happy that I made this purchase.

title: Work great for my SounTrue Black/Green Bose Headphones
review: These worked perfect for my Soundtrue black/green Bose headphones.  I feel like I have a new set.  Did have to have patience to get each new cushion snapped in appropriately but perfect once done,

title: I really don't recommend it
review:
I bought a pair of these last year, and within one week one of the earbuds came off the wire. So I contacted Amazon, and they were very kind to send me a second pair, which lasted a little longer, but ended up with the same problem. I hate generalizing, but it seemed to me that these earphones were horribly designed. They would remain put together if you sat in a chair every time you listen to your MP3 player and didn't move, but we know that that is not the case for most of us: we walk, sit, stand, lay down, etc. with our earphones plugged in. Obviously the designers didn't think about this when they made the product.

As for sound quality, I didn't honestly find them to be much better than your average pair of earphones. You do get pretty good sound insulation, but the JBuds which are only a fraction of the price accomplish a similar effect. The innovative around-the-ear design seems nice at first, but, for me, it got old extremely quick. I may have odd ears --I don't know-- but they didn't ever remain inside my ear canal; they kept slipping out and forced me to go out of my way to adjust them every five minutes.

The final word: horribly designed, average sound quality, very uncomfortable. I paid around $40 for them, and now I don't think I would have them even for free.

title: Mediocre, volume control erratic
review:
These earbuds are functional but sound quality is middling. The volume control is very problematic. It tends to get louder and louder during calls for no clear reason.
I would certainly not recommend paying more than $10 for them

title: The best headphones I have ever owned;
review:
The best headphones I have ever owned; totally comfortable after many hours of listening and great clarity of sound.
A bargain at $47.

title: Excellent quality and sound great; excellent performance for price.
review:
Excellent quality and sound great; excellent performance for price.
I have another pair of Klipsch earbuds; they are the best brand I have owned.

title: Sound quality sub-par for this price range;
review:
Sound quality sub-par for this price range; I returned mine for a refund.
Build quality was quite robust, however IMO $40 earbuds should sound
noticeably better than my $9 Panasonics.

title: Great headphones
review:
My headphones get heavy wear. I'm always looking for ones that can withstand heavy usage. Most last me about 6mos. I've had these a couple weeks now, here are my thoughts:

Pros:
- the battery life is unbelievable! I use them 12-16hrs a day and the battery lasts for days.
- with the end being more bulky than others, the weight makes it so they slide around on my neck.
- I only wear one side at a time so the wire guide is great, I can pull the one I'm not using around the back and it keeps it out of my way.

Cons:.
- I've had some issue getting them to fit in my ears well. They pop out fairly easily, it's a bit annoying.
- the bulkyness makes them less descreet.
- their combatability with my pixel 5 isn't the greatest. It won't unpause if my phone is asleep.
- no fast forward button

Overall, I'm happy with them and the battery life alone will keep be coming back after I wear these out. Maybe I'll get lucky and they will last me longer than others too.

title: Great... While it lasted
review:
I'll start out by saying I wear headphones all day every day. So they get heavy use. Overall I really liked these. Quick charge, light weight, lasted all day. Sound is great.

I've had them 6 months and the right side gave out. Super bummed. Should have lasted longer.

title: Great while it lasted
review: I loved them while they lasted. But now 2.5 month later the right earbud has lost a lot of its loudness and quality. I had to change the settings on my phone to feed more to the right one so they're kind of the same volume again.

title: Excellent comfort, unparalleled sound.
review:
World's most comfortable headphones! I didn't know you could get sound this good without spending an arm and a leg. The fact that they feel like you're wearing nothing is just the cherry on top. I can't ever go back to buying cheap headphones again. The fact that they're such low impedance means you don't need an amp if you want to connect the headphones to your phone.

My only gripe is the EXTRA long cable. You can find replacements, but even the replacement cables are ~$15.

title: Great for the money
review:
After seeing review after review saying this sound card completely changed the way their music sounded, I thought I was getting away with something when I got it for so cheap. I have a pair of Sennheiser S598s that I was using with an Audigy 4 (which had 192 kHz btw).

I wasn't particularly blown away when I listened to some .flac files on my computer for the first time with these. It certainly sounded good, but the only thing that really changed was the sound stage.

The S598s don't really require a headphone amp since they're 50 ohms, but since my old sound card didn't have one, I figured a headphone amp built in couldn't hurt. I wouldn't buy this sound card specifically for the headphone amp unless you have some really high impedance cans that could use some more oomph.

For less than $30, this is a fantastic sound card. I wouldn't expect it make me want to relisten to my music collection. It is certainly better than onboard audio, but if I had the money I'd certainly go for a higher end model with more features.

If you have speakers AND headphones, you can't really switch between the two unless you have a splitter.

title: My kids love it
review:
My son's favorite color is green, so he was super happy to get these bright green headphones. I got purple for my daughter, then I found out her favorite color is blue. I thought it was pink or purple. She still likes it, and they like that they are matching, but still different.

I was thinking that they would limit the volume a lot more than they do though. It does get quite loud. It was loud enough to be uncomfortable for my ears.

The folding feature is pretty good. It's still pretty bulky when folded, but at least it's smaller. And I like that the cord is easily replaceable with a new 3.5mm cord. Although I see a lot of potential for the cord becoming lost. I love that you can daisy chain the headphones together so they can both listen to the same thing. Overall a great buy

title: Decent earbuds, but stopped working within a month
review: Not the best sound quality, but fine for what I needed them for (working out). Little too heavy on the bass, and the highs aren't as clear as I would like, but these aren't very expensive in the first place so whatever. Unfortunately they seem to have started malfunctioning after only about a month of use -- I can only get through maybe 3-6 seconds of a song before it pauses and I have to hit the play button again to keep going, which is pretty detrimental to the whole music-listening experience. Rest assured I've tested it and this is a problem with the earbuds and not my phone.

title: Best headphones I've ever owned.
review: Had these for over a year now, and they still work great. Amazing sound quality. Pads suck to be perfectly honest though -- I would suggest getting Cosmos Velvet pads. The $10 is worth it for the increased comfort. Otherwise, an amazing pair of headphones and a definite steal for the price.

title: Great earbuds
review:
I'm absolutely impressed with the AirPods Pro. Coming from non-noise cancelling earbuds to these are a world of difference. They sound great and the noise cancellation cuts out a lot.

I have an Android phone and these work just as good as any other pair of Bluetooth headphones with it.

title: Great sound and comfortable
review:
First let me say that I have the denon c350 earbuds, i dropped one of the buds in hot tea and it stopped working.

These sound much better than the 350's, i can hear things much clearer. The treble, bass balance is great.

Why not 5 stars?
1. The cable is short but comes with an extension. What is the point, seriously? Just make it longer and lose the extension.

title: Comfortable
review:
I am not disappointed in this product. It provides decent sound quality and is pretty comfortable to wear for a good while. The folding features is even more convenient than I expected as I can safely fold them into a backpack without worrying too much. They are inexpensive and I don't expect audiophile sound quality. They are perfect for a beach bag and lazy hours on the beach without worrying about ruining an expensive headset.
They don't claim to be noise-cancelling and they aren't. Only use these if you are in a quiet room or you want to be able to hear what's going on around you.

title: Poorly construced earbugs flake and disintegrate after a year of very light use.
review: The sound is amazing, and I love that the ear pieces cover the whole ear. But the "leather" on the earphone pads started coming apart after very little use--like a couple of times per month over a year--which was disappointing given the price.

title: Perfect
review: These are the best earbuds I've ever purchased!  I would definitely buy these again.  The volume control slider is a great touch.

title: Exactly what I needed..
review: This is the best low cost option to run any headphones that require Dolby Digital Live.  If you're running 2 or more GPU's there is a good chance that your PCI-E slot is covered up.  This was the solution I came up with and it's worked perfectly.

title: Not a snug fit, not stereo quality, not enough bass, and weird marketing material
review:
The earbud tip is like a cut in half earbud tip. For this reason, it does not allow for a snug fit.

The sound is too airy and is weighted more towards mid and treble. Kind of sounds distant like listening through a tube.

The amount of bass left you wanting more. This is slightly due to not having a snug fit.

Not a fan of the "congratulations winner" card in the box. On the back of the card was directions to email a strange email address.

title: Exceptional headphones
review:
I bought these to replace my broken Creative Live Aurvana headphones. The CALs are great in sound quality, but they are rather flimsy (granted, the damage to the headphones was completely my fault). I was looking for headphones with exceptional sound quality and a solid build quality.

When I first got the ATH-M50, I noted the weight of the headphones. Quite heavy, but not excessive. The headphones are completely solid in build quality. These things look like they're made to survive for a couple of decades. The cable is thick and seems to be built to last. The cups can swivel 180 degrees and fold up.

Now for the sound quality. These sound similar to the CAL headphones. I give a slight edge to the ATH-M50. They sound very good straight from the box. In my opinion, the bass is very adequate (keep in mind, these are studio monitor headphones so they won't be muddled with bass like Beats). Mids and lows sound good. Highs sound good too. These headphones are also reasonably loud.

The isolation is exceptional. There is definitely no sound leakage and are very good at blocking out outside noise.

Overall, these headphones live up to all the hype. I would recommend these headphones to anyone looking for great sound without breaking the bank.

title: A great purchase
review: These are my first full sized headphones. They are in comparable in sound to the Bose QC15s. Mids and lows are very good. The sound is very clear and the bass is quite good. There's little to no sound leakage. I wish the cable was removable and that they folded, but otherwise, these are very exceptional headphones.

title: Awesome
review: These are great earbuds, the sound and clarity are excellent. I have spent way more money on others that are no where as good as these. I will and have recommended these to family and friends and would buy 1MORE products again

title: Perfect Fit!
review: These fit my older-generation Sennheiser PX-100 earphones perfectly.  Great replacement.  Not quite as plush as the originals but they feel fine.  Totally worth the price to keep the earphones in good shape after years of abuse.

title: female end doesn't fit many jacks
review: I tried using this with a number of headphones.  Any that have a 90-degree angle male jack probably won't work in this.  If the male fitting is too large, it also won't fit.  What you can't see in the image is that the female end of this is actually fairly deep.

title: LV digital: Alleged OEM Apple headphones literally fell apart after a few weeks of light use.
review: Bought mine from LV digital / "elvee digital".  Alleged OEM Apple headphones literally fell apart after a few weeks of light use.

title: Wow, what are you guys thinking?
review:
I have no idea why these headphones are so well rated. I am astonished at the poor sound quality. I have several other pairs of "freebie" headphones that come with various electronics I've accumulated over the years that sound far better. Yes, these do have reasonably decent bass, but the upper range is virtually nonexistent. It sounds like I have them occluding my ears, even though they are placed correctly. I don't expect my workout headphones to sound like my pair of $300 Sennheiser headphones, but these are intolerable.

Also, I found the fact that they push against the back of my neck really irritating. They're going back to Amazon today!

title: Fine
review: Exactly as advertised. When they first came I thought there was no way they would stretch enough to fit over my headphones, but they did!

title: 5, but for Filter replacements
review: Sound is excellent, beyond reproach, really excellent. Service is excellent, mine failed, Etymotic fixed without complaint.  Not so happy with having to replace Filters when earwax fills headphones. Buyers should be aware of this necessity. All around good, though.

title: Great headphones/Poor Alexa Music Capability
review: As far as Sony delivering on it’s part for the headphones I would write them a five star. I have to take one rating away because of the limited Alexa functionality for controlling music with the headphones. And this is not a Sony problem. The headphones could be of any brand. The problem is, Alexa works through The Amazon Alexa app. You can’t really interact with the “music app” because when you do it cuts off the Alexa functionality. Using the Alexa app for Music is extremely limited. And that has been the most frustrating thing to me. I have relayed my concerns to Amazon to fix this problem. Amazon Alexa app which you have to use, does not communicate with the music app and vice versa. That music is clear if you use the music app with these headphones. But, you cannot use the Alexa functionality when playing music via music app. Amazon needs to fix this. Sony can’t do this or any other name brand headphones seller. This is an Amazon issue.

title: Great earbuds for the price
review: Love these earbuds and had to buy a second pair for my husband after he borrowed mine one day.  They are comfortable, noise cancelling and are great for running -- they do not fall out.

title: Range is terrible!!
review: The range on this was only about 20 feet. I have about $20 headphones that the range goes further. Disappointed!!

title: They sound wonderful
review: I have used Aftershokz  for a week now and I just love them.  The noise cancellation works great when on the phone so the person I am talking to does not hear the background sounds like they did with my old headset.  I am very happy with the sound quality while listening to music.  Taking public transportation I love how I can still hear what is going on around me and be aware of my surroundings.  Best headset I have owned

title: They stick the earbuds in your ear better, but become uncomfortable to me after a while
review:
They stick the earbuds in your ear better, but become uncomfortable to me after a while.
But the rubber is soft, and its a good addition. Maybe a bit more expensive that i would thing they should be at $10.

title: Great audio quality but mic quality not up to par
review:
I used a Bose 700 headset for most the pandemic, and was hoping these would be an upgrade. Alas, for calls, the microphone in these is inferior. I did random tests, switching between the two headsets, with coworkers, and every single one said I sounded far better on the other headset. The AirPods Max has a mic that’s about on par with standard AirPods, but nowhere near as good as what Bose currently has.

I hope Apple fixes this with a future AirPods Max 2…

title: WARNING: Won't connect while charging; battery not replaceable
review:
So frustrating to spend $400 to only learn some limitations: these headphones DO NOT WORK while charging, which means there's no way to use them without functional battery. The battery can't be replaced either -- so for $400, plan to throw these away after a few years of heavy use...

The pairing / bluetooth connection is also annoying.

These worked for me without the app, and I refuse to use any headset that requires an app because invariably the app will stop being supported, wether one year or ten years away... basically: these have a limited life but look great at first.

title: New cushions make your headphone Bose feel like new
review: First things first, they are an absolute pain to put on.  However, once you have the new cushions on it will revitalize your Bose headphones.  My headphones were pretty ragged from kicking around in my backpack and a lot of use in general.  Now they are like new, problem solved.

title: Aesthetic, sturdy, serves its purpose well. I used screwing instead, protect your HEADPHONES! Few bucks VS what you're hanging?
review:
These are good! I dont want to risk my couple headphone and gaming discontinued rarity headset to drop off of the wall thanks to tape peeling the paint off or adhesive tape giving out so I carefully drilled in them, its most likely fiber glass fortified plastic, very sturdy.
Only I wish that the headband rest would be round, I originally believed it is, unfortunately its flat and only edge has a curvature to it to prevent accidental pulling. Still nice pieces. Possibly worth way less but then who cares. Get 'em!

title: Better than expected :) Quality product.
review: Im pleased with the product, Finally I have more than decent headset stand. Screws fit in the holes on the actual hanger so theyre not sticking out so theres no possibility to scratch or tear up your headsets rest part. Im happy with it.

title: Impressed.
review:
I love this headset. I can hear things I never heard before and it's VERY well built. I've stepped on it at one point and yanked the release cable out. Still going!

If you're looking for affordable Audiophile headset, you shan't look further.

Note: Using Razer Surround audio, but the stereo is great too.

title: Very nice, snug fit, good sound.
review:
I am not an earbud expert, but I am a consumer of quality audio products. You don't buy earbuds to get the best, fullest sound - clearly. These do sound very good. I am pleased with the sound quality, and I imagine anyone on the market for this product in this price range will be.

Fit: they come with different sizes of rubber covers, and fit in my ear very nicely. You can run around and they will stay nice and snug.

title: I like it.
review:
This is probably not as great as I think it is because I"m not an audio snob. I put them on and listen to books on the bus. I like the "no wires" feature - and the phone feature. I was listening to a book on my phone when Sofie calls me up. I hear the ringing through the phone, select the answer on the phone and just start talking through the headphone mic. Very nice!

It takes a nice charge that will last me 2 or three days. I use them about 3 hours/day.

They are not flimsy - but I would not sit on them if I were you.

I keep waiting for someone to say, "Wow Steve! What a cool looking head set!" No one has.

title: Cheap but you can tell. Decent though.
review: Not great sound but a good deal. I wish the ear cushions were a hit softer. I wear glasses and I can feel the headphones pushing the earstalks into my skull.

title: Heavy on the ears
review: I wanted a headset that went over the ears because the in the ear buds sometimes bother me. The sound is excellent, just the heaviness of the ear covering is sometimes awkward and wish the back of the headset was made with softer material.

title: Moved the microphone function out of my headphones so I could focus on getting good headphones for audio playback
review: Completely removed echo problems from my Google hangouts.  Moved the microphone function out of my headphones so I could focus on getting good headphones for audio playback.

title: I mean, for the price... !
review: These things are pretty loud for the price!  Normally I listen to music on my MacBook with three little squares of volume, but with these things I've had to take it down to one or two squares of volume (the two lowest settings).  Sound is good, bass is there, treble is balanced.  The construction is also reasonable for $30 headphones.  I've got a big head and they're a little tight, but I'm thinking they'll loosen up or I'll get used to it.  For normal people the fit will probably be pretty good.  These are excellent if you travel a lot because you can lose them / break them / get them stolen by TSA / whatever, and you can do that 10 times and just get new ones and still come out ahead of buying a $300 pair of Beats or B&Os or Bose.  So... you know... you get what you pay for holds true, but these somehow turn out to give you a little more than what you pay for.  Somehow.

title: but they produce nice sound for the price
review: These are decent headphones for travel or casual use.  They're not studio headphones, but they produce nice sound for the price.

title: Punk rock, bitches.
review: They're pretty good.  The sony headphones are better, but these are stylish and cheaper.  I get lots of comments on them from coworkers.

title: Good but the Aplen2k is better IMHO, even with wires
review: I use V-MODA crossfade wireless 2 headphones, they are completely amazing. I currently run the Fiio Alpen 2k with this setup and it totally rocks. Crisp highs and deeeeepp lows, quality midrange. I was bought this for the Bluetooth because the Alpen2 gets crazy with the wiring situation. I was very disappointed. Bluetooth was simple to setup and works great, just the sound quality was very poor compared to my old setup. I wouldn’t spend the $350 on this DAC/AMP. I’ll keep it old school I guess with a dongle here and another there if it means the sound quality is better.

title: Amazing Hi-Res audio.
review: Awesom DAC and AMP, superior sound quality. Just a good device. Wheel is ultra legit, best way to hear Hi-Res audio. Pair this with V-Moda headphones and you won't regret it.

title: AfterShokz OpenComm Headset -- No! I Can't Hear You. Can you hear me? No?
review:
Well, I thought this AfterShokz OpenComm would be the ideal low-profile Bluetooth headset for Zoom using my Surface Book 2. But, no. Pairing is successfully confirmed by both the headset and the laptop. But when using Zoom, Webex, Teams, Skype or any other videoconferencing app either the mic works or the earpieces work, but not both. Or both are intermittent. Or both are garbled low-res audio.

I have tried resetting the device according to the series of button presses recommended by AfterShokz, but that only makes the headset speak Chinese and doesn't improve audio quality.

It's a shame, because the low profile of the OpenComm could make it a really discreet, nondistracting tool for videoconferencing.

I can't comment on poor battery life, as others have, because it's not really functioning to the point that I can use it.

title: Kinivo BTH220 Bluetooth Stereo Headphones offer same function as much higher priced sets
review:
This is a brief review of the Kinivo BTH220 Bluetooth Stereo Headphones

Pros:
Works seamlessly with iPhone 5 (to pair, just turn on bluetooth function of iPhone, hold down the Kinivo's function button until the indicator flashes rapid blue/red, then accept the pairing on the iPhone)
Comfortable behind-the-head design.
Stayed put while exercising (elliptical at 130 cycles per minute, freeweights, and machines)
On the ear speakers did not transmit motion noise like in-canal earpieces do
Good audio balance
Good voice quality for mobile phone calls
Full charge in 90 minutes
Great price for this quality and function
Free shipping with Amazon Prime

Cons:
Not noise-canceling

title: Worth it.
review: My favorite headset yet. I am an active person and these things stay with me. And they are comfortable to wear for quite a while.

title: Fantastic everyday radio!
review:
Perfect size, and the build quality is great. The AM reception is spectacular! Haven't had enough time to wade through all of the SW stations, but this radio comes with the full set of SW bands, and you can fine tune down to the 1 kHz increment. Very happy there is an auto-scan feature that works in all bands, so you can quickly build a list of presets. I also didn't think I would use the world clock or alarm features, but they are actually helpful in planning times for SW broadcasts. Get a list of broadcast times online, determine the current time in that broadcast time zone, and set your alarm to go off near that time.

Overall, very happy with the radio! The sound quality is great, and I like the interface quite a bit. Good range of features for the price point, and most importantly, the RF receiver works well.

Minor gripes: Certain buttons take multiple presses to register. Also, I wish it had bluetooth so I could use set the radio down outside and play over my headphones while working in the backyard.

title: Great headphones!
review:
I exchanged my Bose QC35s for these and am very pleased overall. I like how these fit better than the Bose headphones, which were too loose IMO. These have a much snugger fit on the head so they don't get jostled around as easily when you are moving. Sound quality is also better since there is no active noise cancelling.

Where these fall short compared to the QC35s is battery life, but I think 12 hours is more than enough.

title: Poor audio quality
review:
You get what you pay for with these. Sound quality is poor, with flat highs and lows. Build quality is good, however.

Spend a little more and get some decent headphones.

title: Good noise cancelling, good audio quality, loose fit
review:
All things considered, I think these are good headphones. The noise cancelling is an improvement over the QC15s (what I upgraded from), and the sound quality is good overall. Where I disagree with most people, however, is in the area of comfort. While there are no pressure points to speak of that lead to discomfort, I feel the combination of the weight and soft cushions contribute to these headphones fitting somewhat loosely on the head. If I shake my head from side to side, the headphones slop around, and when I lower my head, gravity pulls the headphones down a bit. I wish they fit more securely. I don't have a particularly small head either.

Another minor annoyance with these is that sharp bumps cause the noise cancelling to skip for a split second. I find that if I try and walk around with these on, the effect of my heel impacting the ground causes slight audio disturbances.

I am not sure if I would buy them again as I feel they are a bit overpriced at $350.

title: Beware of the cost cutting
review:
I had an older pair of these headphones I bought back in 2007 and prefer the design of those over these new ones. The new ones feel cheaper - including thinner and shorter cable. The cable on my older ones was six feet long, allowing me to sit comfortably in my chair and hook up the jack to the back of my desktop computer located on the floor. The cable on the new headphones is now too short to reach the back of my desktop, so I was forced to buy an extension cable.

Aside from the cable issues, the sound quality is very good for the price.

title: UNbelievable...
review:
I'll admit, like others, I had reservations about dropping $300+ on a pair of headphones... These things are unreal! Build quality is impeccable, sound quality is great, and noise cancelling FAR surpasses expectations. These are not your $50 noise cancelling headphones. If you've tried the cheapo versions in the past and aren't sold on the technology, seriously try the QC-15's! There is no comparison... The range of destructive frequencies is much larger, and unlike the cheaper versions, these headphones have sampling mics both on the outside and inside. The result is absolutely incredibly noise reduction, even with high-frequency noise, which is something the cheaper versions fail to suppress well.

I am seriously in love with these things. My only complaint is the inability to listen to music unless the noise reduction mode is on. Luckily however, these headphones use a single AAA battery, which is very easy and convenient to replace.

title: Does its job good, but the headphones
review:
Actually, I bought the RP2376 model, but it is pretty much the same.
The player is really nice and has a good design. There arent a whole lot of features, but it does offer what you need including programability, 45 second anti-skip, bass boot/surround sound, shuffle, repeat and your normal play, pause, stop, eject functions.
The surround sound feature sounds nothing like surround sound in part from the stock headphones. These headphones have little to no treble, so it sounds like your listening to an old 1930's AM radio.
If your looking to listen to some music and need a relatively inexpensive cd player, you found the one.

title: Hurt Your Head
review: The over the head speakers are very cheap quality and hurt your head after 30 minutes. Only gave an extra star because the earbuds are decent. Don't recommend at all.

title: First wireless headphones we've had to return
review:
My wife and I have been using wireless headphones for the past 10 years or more. We've gone through 3 or 4 of them between the two of us. This is the FIRST one that neither of us could wear. She felt the ear pads were too small, so hurt her ears. I found the ear pads themselves ok, but with my bigger (longer) head, they just wouldn't fit on my ears comfortably (there was upward pressure being applied by the head band). So we never got as far as trying them out with actual audio playing, as they were clearly not acceptable for either of us to wear.

This pair was supposed to be for my wife, who's been using a JVC pair that has been giving her some problems recently (they're about 4 years old). She decided to buy the same JVC headphones again, rather than experimenting with yet another choice.

title: Very good for the money
review:
I use it for Skype. It sounds clear. People tell me the mic sounds good. It does exactly what you would expect it to do.

Drawbacks? Well, it's a $14 headset, so it's not built like a tank or anything. The earpieces are a tad small, but I've used it for as much as 3 hours straight with no comfort problems.

If you're looking for a cheap, no frills headset, I doubt you could find a better one in this price range.

It's not a 5 star headset based on quality and features. However, I decided to give it 5 stars rather than 4 because of the value that it provides.

title: Worked for my needs
review: Bought these to use with the Cardo system for half helmets. They stay in place well and sound quality isn’t bad. I really like that they’re super short so I don’t have to deal with a 6’ headphone cord with the helmet.

title: I have yet to find a better pair of headphones at any price.
review: I have had these headphones for well over a year and they just seem to get better every time I use them. The sound quality is exceptional, with rich and detailed mids, deep bass and beautifully-balanced reproduction overall. I've thrown everything at them: rock, metal, hip-hop, classic and more and the ATH-M50's handled them all with aplomb. The build-quality is excellent and it's obvious that they're built to last. The only drawback is if you're looking for something very portable then the workhorse design, bulky construction and very long cord means they won't be as sleek as many of the other selections out there (although they may get you nods of approval from well-informed audio enthusiasts). Personally, I like listening to them at home when I can just kick back and enjoy the experience. Makes wonder what more dropping $500+ can possibly get you beyond this...

title: Disappointing sound quality and bass.
review:
Having found myself in position of needing to replace a 10 year old set of Logitech z-560s, I opted for another set of Logitech speakers. These, being highly reviewed and at a tolerable price threshold, were what I opted to purchase.

I immediately noticed a severe drop in the quality of audio and almost no bass output whatsoever. What it does pump out is hollow and sounds terrible. It also seems mistimed frequently, at least when used in conjunctions with Fallout: New Vegas. Pretty much any pair of earbuds does a better job of sound reproduction. The highs are also a little grating on the ears.

I can easily say this is the most disappointing Logitech product I have ever purchased -- Look elsewhere or find a deal on something cheaper; chances are the sound quality will be about the same.

title: Check your ear compatibility before you buy
review: Look up "Sony | How to wear the LinkBuds Truly Wireless Earbuds" and make sure the rubber hoop will work with your ears. I don't have the "ridge" that the hoop is supposed to fit underneath to keep the earbud in place; my ears are flat there and there is nothing to hook into even with the largest size hoops. Traditional earbuds work just fine for me because of suction and friction but there is none of that on these.

title: Beware the earrings
review: Please look closely at the picture of the guy wearing the earphones; you will notice that dangling under his ear lobe is a piece of gold metal on the cable. Maybe these things won't bother you but personally I can't "unsee" these earrings and I think they look completely ridiculous. I'm not sure what they're for but they're impossible to remove and they also bounce around annoyingly if you try to run while wearing these earphones.

title: Great quality, questionable usefulness
review:
Sound quality is fantastic for this style of headphone
However, I'm not sure what sort of role they fill these days
-over the ear headphones are better for home listening
-earbuds are more portable, less prone to being damaged, and are more isolating for when you don't want to hear or bother other people, like on a plane
-on ear bluetooth headphones are better for runners who want to be aware of their surroundings and not have wires get in their way

Aside from that, the only real complaint I have is that the cable is very thin and twisty. A thicker cable would be more durable and wouldn't twist as much.

title: Good for small children, but hard to pack
review: I got these for my very petite 2-1/2 year old to use w/ a portable DVD on a plane.  They fit her well enough with plenty of room to grow (the ear cups slide on the headband to expand some), and I think the animal faces helped her to accept them.  Sometimes she just let them hang around her neck, but at least that kept the sound of her movies from traveling too far from us. Sound quality is adequate for this age.  They did not, for some reason, work well with SOME armrest audio on the planes.  It did fine on a newer plane (with headrest video screens), but, as I read in another review of a similar product, it seemed to amplify cabin/plane noise on an older plane that just had the audio options.  That probably has more to do with the plane than these headphones.  The only problem I had with them was packing them.  They do not collapse, fold, or twist, so they take up a bit of space (and you don't want to crush them).  In the "relaxed" state, they form a roughly 6" circle, and the tiger's face/ear cups are about 2-1/2" wide.  I would recommend these and would probably buy them again, as there are not many options out there for very small children.

title: Nice, low profile headphones with good sound quality for bluetooth connection.
review:
While they don't sound as good as my wired Shure headphones, they are way more convenient. My days of critical listening are over and most of my time is spent listening to lossy music files while I'm doing something else (mowing the law, working out, etc.). For most environments, the sound quality is sufficient. What's nice about these is the bluetooth connection and the relatively low profile design.

I had no trouble connecting them to my iPhone 7+ and the JayBird app is a nice addition to tweak the sound setting depending on what you're listening to and where you're listening to it. I do experience the occasional hiss, click or pop that I didn't hear with my wired phones but I'm willing to put up with it.

The only things, aside from better sound quality, that I'd like to see is the announcement for battery life and the charger connection. The phones announce how much battery they have when turned on, but only tell you that they are powering down when you turn them off. It would be nice to hear how much battery life you have left when you are done with a listening session. Also, the connection for the charger is, to say the least, finicky. It's a really small piece of plastic that you have to insert the charging port of the headphones into in just the right way, or it pops out. It's kinda annoying. I suppose that they had to do this to keep the overall size down, so I probably shouldn't complain too much.

title: I've owned these for 4 years now...
review: And I can say that they are the most comfortable headphones I have personally owned. The sound quality is fantastic and the Bluetooth capability is (sometimes) a little funky for me, but I believe thats more of a Windows issue than the actual headset. After 4 years, the ear cuffs are finally starting to wear down, and I am strongly considering ordering the same pair because I've enjoyed them that much. I am a gamer, music lover, and avid cinephile and these headphones are top tier.

title: Outstanding for the price
review: Outstanding for the price, though clearly looser bottom and less defined mid-range than cans 3-4x the price. Reasonably comfortable, though I can't wear glasses when I have these on because they squeeze too much. I really like the choice of cords and plugs. Also, these are very efficient - no need for separate headphone amp. I take them out of my receiver and have to turn the volume down or they blast me.

title: Okay, but not aesthetically great
review:
I bought these so I could have a nice pair of over-the-ear headphones to wear outside. I won't wear these outside. The band that goes across my head is too wide and boxy, and forms a strange shape. It doesn't sit flat against my head, but rather arches up awkwardly.

That being said, these are nice for indoor use when I want to listen to Netflix or music without waking anyone.

title: noise cancelling
review: I did not want to spend $300 for the best noise canceling headphones.  These headphones cancel most of the noise when I am flying so I can listen to my audio books to pass the time.  I am very pleased with them for the price.

title: Jlab Go MP3 player is better for running.
review: I already own the Jlab mp3 player headphones and they are fantastic for running.  They are waterproof, sweatproof, and they absolutely will NOT fall off no matter how fast you run.  I love them.  But I wanted to try tracking my distance using the GPS on my phone so I thought I'd start bringing my phone on runs with me.  Immediately I went to check to see if Jlab had a bluetooth version and when I saw these I thought they would be pretty much the same as the MP3 version.  Nope.  The wire is bendy and not very firm so the buds fall out when I'm too active.  Also not waterproof or sweatproof so it's not likely to last long if I take it out on runs.  These seem like they would be great for more passive users, but for sports definitely stick with the MP3 version.

title: love them
review: I don't know how Customer Service is because I've never needed them in the months I've owned this, but I'm very happy with this purchase.  The sound is amazing for wireless headphones and the range is really good.  Not only do I get clear reception in every room of my apartment, but I can also leave my apartment entirely with the door shut behind me and walk all the way down the hallway and then make a right towards the laundry room before the reception cuts out.  I like them so much I was also hoping I could find this exact thing except with speakers instead of headphones, so I can hook it t my phone every night in my bathroom and keep the speakers in my bedroom.- That way instead of just shutting off the alarm in the morning and drifting back to sleep, I'm forced to get up and go to the bathroom to shut the alarm off- the idea being I'd likely start brushing my teeth, etc at the sink rather than fall back to bed.  Unfortunately they don't seem to make a speaker version of this product and wireless speakers I have tried so far have very poor reception compared to these excellent headphones.

title: Right Bud, Right Sound, Right Price
review:
I'm not a huge audiophile but I do appreciate clear sound with a decent bass. My last pair of earbud lost one channel and so it was time to replace them. I like the Sennheiser name but didn't want to spend more than $30 for earbuds. This pair has pretty much filled the bill. The sound is clear and crisp, the bass is not muddy or shallow and the price was just what I was looking for. My only beef is a minor one. I missed that they were asymmetrical. You're supposed to wrap them around the back of your neck and have the cord hang from one side. Maybe I'll get used to it but I prefer a symmetrical cord configuration.

I'm not complaining though, they sound wonderful.

title: I'm so happy with these that I bought some for my parents ...
review: I'm so happy with these that I bought some for my parents too. Since they fold up, I can toss them in my purse and they have been pretty durable so far. It's nice that I can control the volume, songs, etc without pulling my iPad out of my purse. I tend to use headphones like this to replace earmuffs in the winter too. Yay for finally having cordless headphones! Also, I tested the range for my parents. They have an average-sized American home. The computer is on the top floor and a a little more than halfway across the house. The headphones were able to sync to it through the entire upstairs and downstairs except the very far corner of the downstairs room. That's a pretty good range and will allow them to do household chores and such without dropping the signal. Highly recommend.

title: hearing a buzz....
review:
It really saves space and is easy to plug into.
The only thing is I hear a consistent buzz coming from it... it's not terrible, but gets annoying when I'm working without my headphones in.

title: Destined to fail
review:
Meh.. I'm done buying headphones that don't have removable cables. They invariably get pinched and develop intermittent issues. It would of been nice if the cable that came with this was coiled. These are just a couple of things you don't realize until you use these.

I will point out that the top of these headphones are not all that comfortable. I'm not sound quality expert so I'll just leave that part out.

title: Very thin wire easily breaks.
review:
I bought two of these. One of them for my SO and she pinched the wire in a drawer on the desk and one of the speakers was no longer getting audio. In her work she does board level repair on everything from laptops, smart phones, and desktops, but regardless was not able to fix the issue with a soldiering iron. The wire is mostly rubber, the metal they use is extremely thin, which is probably why it broke so easily in the first place.

My headphones still work, but the ear pads are completely worn out. I realize I can buy new pads, but I shouldn't have to.

title: Cheap headphones
review:
These headphones are cheap, not just inexpensive, but also poorly constructed. When I went to change the interchangeable rubber earbuds, the speaker actually detached from the body. It seems like they used cheap glue to put everything together. Since this happened within minutes of opening the product, I returned them. Even if I had been extremely careful (now knowing they are quite delicate), these headphones would clearly have eventually broken in the same way from normal use.

I'm assuming most people will throw around their headphones in their pocket or bag or wherever. I doubt these would stand up to such mild "abuse." Overall, I was hoping that these were high-quality, inexpensive headphones, but sadly, they're just cheap.
