I suggest forgoing these and instead purchasing higher quality products, as those will easily stand the test of time and be worth your while.

title: Best earbuds on the market
review: Finally tried the ear buds after the redesign. Fit great, sound great, and noise cancelling is great. I haven't worn my over ear WHXM4s outside the house since buying these...these are just more convenient to carry around and sound great for earbuds

title: Tinny sound and narrow viewing angle.
review: I'm pretty disappointed with this TV. I bought it for the kitchen. The sound is tinny and not easy to understand. The picture is also pretty hard to see unless you're looking straight at it. If you're going to use an external sound source or headphones (it has an 1/8" stereo jack) then it would be acceptable for watching if you're not moving around and watching from multiple angles.

title: Spectacular sound quality for this little headphone.
review: All I can say is Wow.  I did not expect the sound quality out of this little headphone for what it cost me here on Amazon.  My opinion with my ears, I would say, its sound quality easily bests headphones costing 2 times (strike that) 3 times (strike again), several times more.  The build and durability is up in air at this point, as I recently received them, so I can't vouch for them, they seem reasonable for what I payed as far as build, but the sound quality far exceeds the price.

title: Good stuff
review: These fit the eb-3 earbuds that come standard from Galaxy Audio. They are much more comfortable and reduce the noise better than the generic Shure EAYLF1-10 and aren't bright yellow or orange.

title: Not quite as indestructible
review:
They sound pretty good. The build quality sadly didn't hold out through the 2 year warranty mark. The V plates broke and screws came lose and no amount of tape or glue helps put it back together. These were used as gaming headsets so they didn't see much action outside of my desk or exposed to elements, so they definitely weren't in unfavorable circumstances. This is also an issue a friend of mine who purchased an M100 shared so it's not just me sadly.

They sound great overall, they pack a lot of bass but it does level out over time as you burn the headphones in. My biggest gripe is the build quality though especially considering its a selling point of these, the headband has weak points that need addressing in the next iteration (the V plates/adjusting band.)

title: Good Headphones for the BASS & Comfort
review: These are probably the most comfortable headphones I've tried. They have great bass and with an amp they sound pretty decent, if you don't have an amp a simple equalizer setting makes them sound wonderful. I would definitely recommend these pairs if you're in search of headphones that are under $70 but if you have a slightly higher budget I'd suggest the M50's.

title: Great Amp
review: My first headphone amp so I don't have much to compare it to but it's great and boosts sounds to an amazing level. I just dislike the fact you can't charge it and use it at the same time.

title: Best Quality Headphones for the Price
review: These are awesome headphones they're punchy, crisp, and warm. In my opinion I haven't heard anything that has sound so good for it's price range. One thing you gotta do though is replace the horrible ear cuffs that come with them with some nice soft cushioned ones. The factory style ear cuffs aren't breathable, very stiff, and your ears will start hurting within an hour. Once you have some different pads on then you'll be fine. These headphones will certainly last you until you want to move up in the world and get a $300.00 set and amp.

The S9 has a Two Step adjustable SRS WOW setting The 10 does Not adjust. There are plenty of like new or new or Refurbed S9HD's out there ive 2 sets in black .w case.. 39.98 rt here. title: Small house, big noise. Problem solved
review: After three years I figured out the blue tooth on my onkyo receiver is receive only so no matter what I did no attempt to get it hooked up with my Bluetooth headphones ever would work. The day I learned that I saw these Sony rf headphones. Work beautifully, easy setup, and shoot em ups don't bother my wife and daughter any longer while they watch girl stuff

title: Great for the price!
review: I'm on my second pair of these headphones. Great deal for the price you pay. The first pair lasted about 2 and a half years, and finally broke. Decent Sound. Great for working out. I would not recommend if you need them to last more that 4-5 hours. The charge will expire in about 4 hours, so I'm constantly charging it.

title: Not worth the $$$
review: I was hoping to use these as my work/play earbuds but they cannot connect to my dell laptop and the buds are not secure enough for working out.

title: I'm crazy about these headphones
review:
This MP3 headset has been amazing addition to my workout. The product is beautifully designed, the materials are great quality, and the performance is aces. There's a wonderful bluetooth version that's also waterproof (I own both), but it's not suitable for swimming because bluetooth transmission is diminished through water.

I know MP3 seems old school, but with 4GB I feel it's more than sufficient for my 3-4x week routines. Unlike in ear models you have to jack the volume extra high, the "bone induction" works much better at a reasonable volume. I really enjoy this product and think everyone will.

title: The leather weather down quick
review: I've had these headphones for a few years now. They sit at my desk and plug into my Bose Companion desktop speakers. However, They've got this cheap leather/pleather covering and its been flaking off like dry paint. It makes 'em look real ugly. If you're not into the look of it at all then you should be fine, but I don't know, when I pay 200 for a pair of headphones I accept them to be made of durable quality.

title: Surprising quality.
review: Very impressed with the sound quality and loudness, for the price. As good as any cheap pair of earbuds I've bought for 3-5x the cost. I go through earbuds like crazy, going to order the 5 pack too.

title: Holds a long charge and convenient.
review: This thing is AWESOME. The charge lasts a long time and it's a great way to safely transport my headphones.

title: Good value
review: Unit is comfortable, The sound quality with Zoom is fine. The USB/volume control disconnects to allow use as a Headset for older iPhones using a TRRS phone jack. Honestly I couldn’t tell if the noise cancellation was working or not; no one on the other end has complained about the mic sound.

title: Perfect replacement
review: Items are easy to install, and make the headphones feel like new, without that black grit coming off on ones ears

title: Not a good mic, pretty decent webcam for the price!
review: Okay if you want to use the microphone on this, it isn't good, and I don't recommend it. Picture quality wise, it's not amazing, but very functional, reasonably clear. It's not overly nice, but it's great for it's price. I only use it to talk with friends on Discord with a camera, and I don't do it all that often. For that reason, why would I want a more than 40$ webcam? This one does the job, and I recommend it. For conference calls, working from home, talking with friends, this is the one to go. If you're needing outstanding picture quality, bigger fields of view, and more features look elsewhere. I also never recommend webcams having good microphones, buy a separate mic or headset to go with the webcam. It makes no sense to bundle those two together.

title: Disliked these, but Love Tozo t12
review:
I bought these hoping to have a pair for jogging and utilizing the passthrough tech. Unfortunately I didn't like these that much.
The case is finicky to insert the buds, the lid shuts too easily, the buds insert in an odd way and it doesn't stay upright and falls over easily.
The earbud fit isn't as comfy as the T12s. This fit required me to turn it so the bottom rod pointed about 20 degree forward and as a result it pushed against my tragus in an uncomfortable way.
They came almost entirely uncharged but enough to light up so at first I thought the left ear bud was broken, but it just needed to charge for 5 minutes first.
The passthrough listening isn't loud enough to be useful unless the music is ABSURDLY quiet. Now if you just want that for a work environment I could see pressing pause then enabling it and it would work, but if you want music to play it won't cut it in any safe way jogging or running.
So my dream of a second TOZO pair is dashed with these.
I prefer the T12 in every way to these. If you need isolation just buy comply ultra isolation tips and the fit will be better, more comfy, and plenty isolating.

title: Amazing value, best when paired with Comply Isolation tips
review:
The quick review is, buy these with Comply Isolation foam tips for better isolation, more solid fit and more balanced sound quality.

Out of the box I was super impressed with the presentation and quality. Well built, sleek finish, wireless charging, waterproof, and solid build.
The initial sound and fit didn't quite work though. This is pretty common with earbuds IMO though so I don't blame the company. The rubber buds create a bit of a bass boost and I couldn't quite get them to fit like I wanted in both ears.

However, I swapped the earbuds for the COMPLY Isolation Plus Tx-500 Mediums and they are perfect. The overall sound is more balanced without the huge sub (though still bass focused which is fun). The fit is tighter both ears and more comfortable.

The call quality is great and I'm told the microphone is clear on the other end.
The touch is a bit sensitive but I like that and it didn't take long to adjust how to hold it around the edge not to trigger that. I prefer sensitive to not sensitive here.

Overall I'm super impressed and recommend it highly, especially with the COMPLY isolation tips :)

title: Spring gimmick will likely cause ear damage.
review:
So these headphones have a great battery life, and feel decent for consumer headphones. The main gimmick is the "haptic bass"... the haptic bass is just two springy metal pieces that resonate at specific frequencies making the sound much worse and likely hitting decibel levels of ear damage!
If that isn't bad enough just taking a step or moving or tapping near the headphones causes the metal to resonate in a weird way.
I opened them up, and cut out the spring part of the headphones, and now they're decent isolating consumer headphones.
Beware, the slider haptic bass gimmick sounds bad and is likely harmful to your hearing so I'd go with another pair without that!

title: A great, accurate
review:
A great, accurate, detailed, clear converter for listening. It pairs well with the T90 headphones for an absurdly detailed experience. It works great to eliminate pc noise from the on board audio and isolate your listening experience with better conversion and amping.

I prefer this with the T90s for an honest listening experience with clarity.

The Aune t1 MK3 with a gold lion and Fidelio X2s however are better for a laid back, fun, relaxing experience of an average listener IMO.

I think it all depends what you are trying to go for.

title: Unbeatable for the price-point
review: Given the price of these earbuds, I was shocked at the sound quality, battery life, and comfort. The added benefit of a wireless charging case is also wonderful in such a small package. The multi-function touch controls on the earbuds can be a bit finicky at times, but overall I am happy with the product.

title: Great starting Bluetooth headphones
review: This is the first pair of bluetooth headphones I have owned. The sound quality is very good for the price and the bluetooth stays connected at all times with no drop outs. The battery life is very long and it only takes about 3 hours to charge. I can use these headphones for an entire day pretty much (not constant use) and charge them at night. These will connect to any device that has bluetooth technology and it is a pretty simple process. The only thing to consider is the special touch gestures on the side of the headphones. These gestures will not work on iPhones or Fire TV. I have yet to use these with another product so I can't say for sure whether or not the gestures will control android devices.

title: Bad build quality
review:
The sound is fine, the bass is overemphasized which might be beneficial in some situations. I had fitting issues which caused me to constantly fiddle to make sure they were fully in my ears, regardless of the rubber insert size used.

Mainly leaving 1 star because while cleaning one earbud, the cloth driver screen came out, quite easily. This causes the sound in one earbud to be much louder than the other, also allowing your lovely wax down into the driver chamber. I contacted raycon customer service to which they replied the earbud would still work perfectly fine, they offered no solution.

I dealt with it until I ordered a pair of anker earbuds (which have metal driver screens) & the ankers ended up being better in every practical way while also being less expensive. Raycons are very expensive for what you get, I didn't realize that until I tried other earbuds.

title: Well built, but small and too bassy
review:
These headphones are, without a doubt, very well made and a piece of functional art.

There are a lot of videos on the web going over the details, which are very positive. You should definitely watch those if you're thinking about getting these headphones.

You should NOT get these headphones if:
a) you have a large head--they just won't fit. You will have to move the headband closer to your forehead if you want the speaker on your ear.
b) want a less colored / flat / neutral response in your headphones. These are very bass-heavy IMO; so much so that I was trying to find a knob to turn the bass way down.

I have a pair of studio headphones for mixing--AKG K271 MkIIs. So, neutral headphones are covered. These came up for sale on the Treasure Truck. After watching the reviews, I decided to try them out. They are certainly nice to look at and very well-made. I will probably give them to my wife or kid. If I had paid $400 for these, I would've been very disappointed with the purchase.

I also have a pair of Bose sound cancelling headphones, which I am quite happy with. I should've just stuck with those.

title: Poor quality skip this set
review: Mine broke a couple months after buying them. The wires are exposed near the jack and they died in one ear channel. These headphones suck don't waste your money.

title: Great product
review: I love wearing these on airplanes. Keeps the noise out, and people also see them on you and don't try and spark up random meaningless conversation with you. If anyone knows what I'm talking about then you know having four hours of your life not being wasted by that person who can't shut up and let you sleep or read is worth it. This product is great and folds up fairly compact. I prefer this style to earbuds because it covers you're whole ear and doesn't come off like an ear bud.

title: Not impressed
review:
I'm disappointed. This is the first Amazon/Fire/AmazonBasics product I've not been fairly impressed with. The construction and looks are fine, nothing wrong there. I would prefer the finish not be so shiny, but it's fine.

The sound, on the other hand, is really poor. I've not used any other bluetooth speakers, so this has no point of comparison other than my headphones. The sound is very muddy, no definition. There is practically NO treble or bass, only mid-range. I'm not a bass-a-holic, I just like clean sound. This speaker does not provide clean sound. It is a mid-range and muddled.

Pros:

- it gets loud. definitely loud enough to fill my apartment.
- not a lot of distortion when turned up
- Price is good, typical AmazonBasics
- appears well made

Cons:

- color is shiny (not my preference)
- bluetooth connection (iPhone 5s) stutters @ 7.5 feet (measured)
- sound is muddled
- no treble/bass
- Pairing/turn-on sounds are LOUD and unbelievably irritating. I may return it based on this alone.

title: I like this but volume control deteriorating over time; low end bass is absent
review:
I've been using several of these every day for a few months and I like them very much. They are extremely light and comfortable, barely know I'm wearing them. Sound quality is generally excellent once you get used to them, and I am an audiophile.

I'm very conscious of bass, and I tested them with a terrific fidelity tester on Youtube. It sends a tone with descending frequency and it tells you what frequency it is in real time while it's changing. Bass response disappears below 50 Hz. Even so, I do get good bass response when listening to bass-heavy music, just not extremely deep. It would be unrealistic to expect any better from this type of product.

After several months of use the volume control on one of these is starting to malfunction. Volume at the ear pieces changes abruptly and not continuously as you slide the slider, and balance between the left and right sides is disrupted.

Overall, these headphones are super-cost-effective. The price is microscopic compared to the quality and utility, a smart buy.

title: Unbelievable sound quality and completely reasonable microphone. Tremendous value.
review:
These earbuds are startlingly good. They punch *way* above their weight. I've used these almost daily for a couple months and have been very pleased.

The bass is rich, the separation reasonable and the treble bright without being shrill. With some music, the bass was a little heavy, but that was easily resolved with a minor EQ adjustment. The sound is way better than you would expect at this low price.

Phone calls are pretty good. If you hold the mic up a little bit, the sound quality is great. If you let the mic dangle, it sounds similar to a conference room speaker phone - decent and intelligible, but not great. Of course, "conference room speaker phone" quality is totally acceptable in professional environments, so these earbuds will actually meet the expectations of the people you're talking to.

The fit is good. I found the combination of rubber ends that fit me well and they are comfortable for all day use.

Overall, these are a remarkable value, highly recommended.

title: Great Product well design
review: I know the WH1000XM3s are out now but this headphone was a game-changer when it was released I still have my pair and they're still going strong.  Great sound quality, explosive sound, and fantastic noise cancellation. At the time the price was right when I bought it and haven't looked back since!

title: Great product feels well made and sturdy
review: Bought this stand recently and just moments of putting it together (yes, you have to put it together but it super easy) it felt well made and very sturdy. It looks great on my desk and cradles my Sony WH-1000XM2's perfectly. After spending $350 on these headphone I wanted a stand that I could trust to hold my headphones with damaging them (from what I read of other headphones that are not to sturdy and easily fall over) and it does that job! Inexpensive and practical can't ask for more.

title: Quality product
review: My kids are notorious for earbud destruction and they now all have these. They have great sound and are good quality. We couldn't be happier. We have had two pairs for over a year, now, and still perform well. The third pair is 6 months old and still doing wel. A miracle in our household!

title: Well, I use the product all the time.
review: Connection with iPhone is flawless. Connection with windows laptop is easy. Not much to complain about. The noise cancelation is alright for ear buds. The only earbuds that ever fit in my ear without falling out while running. (Because of the silicone tips)

title: These are great, and a good price
review: I bought these because I was too cheap to buy Bose, which were supposed to be the best. Then after having these for awhile, I thought, Okay, I'll bite the bullet. I got some Bose and didn't like them nearly as well! These sit better around my ears so they actually block MORE sound than the larger Bose ones. I love turning on the noise cancellation feature - it's so restful. I even use it on car trips - definitely reduces my fatigue. These also work well for listening to music, skyping (though there is no microphone), plugging into the headset jacks on planes, etc.  They only take one battery and it lasts a long time. Great product, great value, major improvement in my travel quality of life!

title: The sound quality is great. However
review: The sound quality is great. However, I find that the headphones become uncomfortable, even painful after more than a couple hours of use. In addition, the headphones do not block out any outside noise. Wearing the headphones is almost like listening to an external speaker, except that you are not bothering the people around you. I would not recommend using these headphones in any loud areas (e.g., public transportation) because you will have difficulty hearing unless the volume is turned up very loudly.

title: They come with silicone and foam ear tips in various sizes so you can find your perfect fit. They do not have noise cancelling c
review: These headphones are phenomenal. They come with silicone and foam ear tips in various sizes so you can find your perfect fit. They do not have noise cancelling capabilities, but because they fit so well into your ear, they effectively block out a lot of ambient noise. The sound quality is very high and the control buttons (located on the right side wire) are easy to use and intuitive. I highly recommend these headphones.

title: PHONY BOLOGNA
review:
These headphones arrived today. Although they were sold by and shipped from Amazon, THEY ARE COUNTERFEIT.
No serial number sticker on the box. Inside the right headphone, they are called "Major 3" instead of "Major III." Also inside the right headphone, there is what appears to be a QR code, but the code won't scan in various apps. See another reviewer's photos of the inside of real ones vs. these fake ones.

title: Good sound quality
review: I had a pair of the [[ASIN:B0018NU3KU Sennheiser  MM 50 iP High Dynamic Soud Earbud Headset Compatible with iPhone & MP3 Players]] in-ear headphones before these but the wire broke so it was time for a replacement.  The sound & bass aren't as good on the Klipsch, but they seem more durable and it's definitely good enough.

title: Good sound, but too flimsy.
review: I really liked the price to sound quality ratio of these headphones HOWEVER the jack is very flimsy. I broke my first pair sitting down with my phone in my pocket. The jack bent, and from then on I had to hold the cord at a particular angle to get sound in both ears. I assumed the fault was mine and bought a second pair, but within a week the cord got caught on a doorknob I was walking past, and with very little force, the jack snapped right in half, leaving the metal part in my phone. I don't think I can afford to keep replacing these every month.

title: Fantastic HD Music Streaming Device
review:
I purchased this to stream music for listening on headphones. Setup was a breeze, taking 10-15 minutes tops. I simply installed the WiiM app on my iphone, then used a digital coax cable to connect the Pro to my DAC, then plugged the Pro into an AC outlet and followed the directions on the app for the setup procedure, bing bang boom and done.

It streams Amazon Music Unlimited with gapless playback in bit perfect 24/192 HD, using my WIFI connection (so the Wiim app on my phone is only for control), although there are many other ways to use it was well.

It sounds great, the user interface is easy to understand and use, and it uses very little battery power from my iphone to control it. Highly recommended.

title: Good Value Headphone Cable for Hifiman Headphones
review: This cable worked perfectly for hooking my Hifiman headphones to a headphone amp.  It seems to be made with high quality parts and sounds great, as well as being quite reasonably priced.

title: Worth Every Penny
review:
It's funny, I hadn't really realized how lopsidedly compressed the old ear pads on my HD 580 headphones had gotten, and I kept thinking that one of the drives was going bad because the left side was louder than the right side, but after replacing the old ear pads with these new ones, everything has come back into balance. Yeah.

Installation couldn't have been any simpler, and I'm just happy to have my wonderful headphones back in proper working order.

title: Simple & Elegant
review: Not much to say, really, except that is uses high quality materials and fit my needs for a headphone hanger quite nicely.

title: Just Get It : )
review:
Oh man, this is such a cool accessory for the Voyager 5200 Bluetooth Headset. I'm a professional driver, so I use my 5200 everyday at work, all day long (sometimes all night as well), and it's so nice when my shift is done to be able to pop the 5200 into this case, see all the little lights flash (showing the current charge level in both the headset AND the charging case), the put it in my bag and know that the headset will be fully charged the next time I pull it out.

I'm very impressed with the level of design and engineering that went into making this product not only versatile, but virtually foolproof.

By foolproof, I mean, when you put the headset in the case, it has a magnet that connects it to the charging circuit, so it makes this little clicking sound when it gets seated correctly, and then there are two sets of little blue LED lights that begin to flash. There are 3 LEDs in each set, showing the charge level, and they flash sequentially showing that they are charging. One of those sets is for the headset, and the other is for the charging case, so it's easy to see if you need to plug the charge case in, which I need to do once a week (I carry a 12 volt USB converter in the car and it only takes less than hour to charge case back up to full.

Anyway, this really is one of those accessories that should be a "no brainer" for anybody who purchases the Voyager 5200.

title: Good Build Quality
review: I needed a long run for a stereo headphone cable, and this 25 foot Hosa cable fit the bill just fine.  Nice build quality.

title: fantastic
review: used it to fix the terribly uncomfortable headband on my gaming headset. worked a charm. super comfortable.

title: after 3 RMAs I gave up
review:
Pros:
It's wireless
it has acceptable surround sound

Cons:
if you are a petite person this headset will never fit you properly
It's incredibly heavy, wearing it for any duration is going to leave a sore spot on the top of your head
RMA'ed the product three times in 6 months, gave up, ordered a different headset from a different company
RMA 1) headset refused to charge
RMA 2) sound cut in and out every minute or so for about 3-4 seconds every time i tried to use it
RMA 3) wireless issue again, and headset would refuse to turn off unless i reset it manually with a push pin

title: 2YearsLater
review:
These headphones initially impressed, there is no disputing it's sound quality. But there are major flaws in its design.
1.the cable noise, for the price there
should be no irritating cable noise.
2. Flimsy cable construction that WILL not last more than 2 years guaranteed.
3.Dealing with warranty issues is nonexistent with this company.

I'm sorry klipch I have to break up with you guys until you can conduct better business practices.

title: The good and the bad
review:
The good - great sound at a price much lower than other high quality headphones.

The bad - they really are extremely uncomfortable (I wear glasses and perhaps they wouldn't be so bad for someone w/out glasses). My set is falling apart after a few years of use. I use them a couple of times a week, usually to watch movies.

In all, get them for the sound but don't expect comfort or frills

title: Very short, good quality, fine for my purposes
review: I use these to make my headphones just long enough to listen to music in bed with my phone on my nightstand. Sound quality is good. Only had a problem with crackling once and they weren't plugged in all the way. I've only used these with my earbuds and iphone. Just note how short they are- not much of an extension. (Under 2 feet).

title: You get what you pay for
review: These headphones were ok until it stopped working within 6 months, the headphones don't work anymore but the mic still does so I use it for the mic only because it's at least better than my acer standard laptop mic, but because it did not live up to the reviews I'm giving it one star, the mic isn't even that clear but I guess for 11 bucks you get what you pay for, I recommend spending a little more on a 5 star rating headset, but i'm also starting to think reviews are biased due to being bought off by the companies so it may be a little bit of a risk, just my two cents.

title: Thank goodness for replacements
review: I’m so happy Bose offers replacement pads. I’ve had my QC25 headset for I think 4-5 years now and the pads finally gave up the ghost after all that time being used around the university, coffee shops, home use, bus rides, and numerous trips around the US, to Mexico and Africa. With how long the originals lasted, I expect just the same out of the replacements. And I’m happy they have them and not making me get knock offs or new headphones. I forgot now nice new pads felt compared to my old ripped up ones

title: Does its job
review: It does what it's supposed to. Easy to setup and it doesn't feel like it's going anywhere. The one thing I wish for is just a little lip at the end so if I knocked my headset with my hand then it wouldn't be able to slide off. However, I haven't had that issue yet

title: Just what I needed
review:
I've only had to use this for a few sessions so far, but I have to say I am not only very pleased with the audio quality, but also the whole design of the ModMic 5. First: I bought this over the ModMic 4 because of the shorter cable option as well as the fact that the cable is replaceable if it breaks.

What I like most about this is how the physical mute actually works! On my last headset, people could still hear me for whatever reason. It is also very easy to attach/detach which was huge for me because I don't want a mic on my headset all day long. They also mounted on my Philips SHP9500 headset nice n easy. Be certain to follow the part that says to let the 3M adhesive cure for an hour. I also like the little carrying case. Very neat! If I don't use it for my headset, I often have other small things that could be stored in it, along with the extra pieces Antilion gives you

title: Good quality unit
review:
So when I bought this, I bought it more out of word of mouth. Rather, Amazon reviews, and lots of people on the Internet giving this a thumbs up. And I have to say I agree with them! I bought this because I got this awkward stutter from my dedicated soundcard, and I went from a pair of headphones with an inline volume adjuster to one that didn't. Which meant I was using my OS to manage volumes, and my audio just sounded FLAT. Putting this inline has really brought that audio back to life, as well as an easy way to manage my volume. I keep bass boost off and enable the AMP switch in the back, and play my music through Philips SHP9500 headphones. I think this is a very worthy buy if you want an external DAC/AMP for under $100. I also like that this guy is mostly made of metal, the volume control is smooth, and I like that there is a setting for it being completely off!

Lastly, some people complained about the blue light on the front being too bright, and I don't have that issue. It's the same brightness as any of my other computer lights (like HDD light), so no complaint there

title: Frankly - Excellent
review:
I got these as a gift for a friend who just can’t wear earbuds. I decided on Anker because of my good history with this company. Their customer service is really solid. I had an issue with my buds a while back and reviewed about it. They sent me an upgraded pair, no charge and they were great.

To the headphones; the sound is superb, and they’re quite comfortable. I like that they have both Bluetooth and a 3mm jack. And the sound canceling is pretty damn good.

My friend loves them and she even uses them for phone calls.

I rarely rave, but there it is.

title: Works great on my iMac
review: Love it. Just plug it in and you're done, system automatically picks up the headphones and mic and adjusts everything. I got it for skype and hangout calls. It's super comfortable. I only wish the microphone wasn't fixed and could move up and out of the way.

title: Go with Sennheiser
review: I was expecting better.  I have a smaller pair of foldable JVC headphones that I've had since 2006 and they blow these away.  This was underwhelming and I think I've honestly used these maybe 4 times.

title: High Quality Audio Sound Product
review: These headphones are a well made product using high quality materials; they are adjustable, you can lengthen or shrink the unit around your head.  The part that touches your ears is a soft, cushion like material that doesn't irritate your ears (at least for an hour for me).  They are set up to plug right in to your ipod, and they do a very good job of making the sound that comes to them sound very good.  They actually have written on each side left or right, so you know how to put them on your ears to hear the proper stereo sound.  They block out most extraneous sounds by the nature of how they fit over the ear.  I have an old set of headphones from 30 years ago that may have a slightly better sound, but they are also heavier.  This set is relatively light and just reeks of being well made.  The bottom line, however, is sound quality.  I think these sound very good (but I am over 65 and my hearing may be somewhat suspect). One more thing (this is an update), the unit has another plug that fits into the ipod plug so you can plug into an amplifier or other audio product that doesn't take the ipod connector.  Slight warning:  when you are unpacking the unit, be careful that you don't miss that additional plug as it is kind of in a separate part of the packaging and can be missed.  I almost missed it, but when I was throwing the original box away I happened to spot it.

title: Works as expected
review:
The earphones work as I expected them to. I haven't used them solo connected to my laptop. I have used them with an Audioquest Cobalt amp/DAC, listening to ultra high definition music on Amazon music unlimited. With those connections, I expected the music to sound outstanding and, it didn't disappoint.

I have used them with another dac/amp combination and they still sound great. I guess the real test is to listen to them straight from my laptop. I will update again when I get to that point.

title: These stock tubes work just fine
review:
Before I received the amplifier, I bought a pair of upgraded tubes. I had read that the stock tubes would cause noise in the music or at least that I would notice that noise. But for the last two days I haven't noticed any noise at all except the music. This little amplifier really kicks ass. I thought I might have blown my ears out when I first turned the music on. The P20 easily powered my Sennheiser 660S 150 ohm headphones. The next test will be to see if it can power my 6XX cans at 300 ohms. I've been using the single ended inputs so far with a Enog2 pro balanced DAC. Sounds sweet!

Update: 11/10/19 – – I've now had this amplifier for about a month and everything is working as expected, excellently. I still have the stock tubes on there and no problem with noise so far. I don't see a need to use the replacement tubes I bought ahead of time. I'll hold onto them anyway and try them out at some point in the future. I am now using a balanced connection with a set of 6xx, 300 ohm headphones. The amplifier easily powers those.

title: Good-looking and well-made piece of wood
review: Considering some of the other reviews I read about this particular product, I was concerned I may get a similar detective Omega style headphones stand but, mine looks great! I'm happy with my purchase.

title: Sound good and look great
review:
These are pretty good sounding headphones. They have become my number one headphones. I don't know how they could have mass-produced these things because it looks like very meticulous work with all the metal work, and the other work done; that must have taken quite a bit of time to do.

After using this for about a month, I still have to say these are well-made headphones but, they are not worth $600. I believe I saw them on Massdrop $499 or $390, which to me, is still overpriced. These headphones do sound good but they are over-hyped, in my opinion.

title: Doesn't sound good to me
review: I don't know what the problem is with these headphones but they do not sound good to me. I saw a video about these headphones on YouTube and the guy also thought the sound was a little muffled. He showed a remedy about that; he took this and that off of it and claimed it sounded a lot better, anyways, I'm not about to go through all that. I'm in the process of sending them back to China. I was told they wanted a 20% restocking fee plus I'll be paying for the postage too. I should still recover a good amount of money back. I forgot to look into a return policy before I bought them so, this loss is on me.

title: It's a good-looking headphones stand
review: I have this good-looking headphones stand on the corner of my TV cabinet holding up a pair of Hifiman Sundara. The large ear cups fit perfectly on the side of the headphones stand, as does the head strap across the top. The stand is sturdier than what I thought it would be, which is a pleasant surprise.

title: Love how secure they feel in my ears
review: For those of you constantly adjusting your AirPods these are the earbuds for you. Compatible sound quality & features, but with the added bonus of a snug secure fit & color choices. Would absolutely recommend as a first choice earbud

title: I was a good cable but not what i needed because the Technica ...
review: I was a good cable but not what i needed because the Technica headphones has a little lock mechanism that prevented the cable plug to completely connect all the way in.  The cable is great.

title: My 1MORE headphone ear pads were failing within 1 month.
review: I found a post about using this type of ear pad to replace those.  You need to use your finger nail to pull off slowly the ones from the mount.  Take off the old fake leather covering from the ring.  Easier to start at one section of the plastic ring and then remove the material  You'll need the plastic ring to remount the ear pads.  Take your time removing the glue from the ring and from the headphone area.  This company supplies another glue strip in the package.  I had to cut mine into sections to get it to cover the plastic ring for attaching to the head phones.  I just tried to center the plastic ring on the ear pads.  It won't be perfect. but it allows you to Re-use the head phones.  I was close to throwing them away. 1More doesn't stand behind their warranty.  I posted a review, but they only have 1 - showing on the web site for the headphones.After 1 month of use, the headphone material shouldn't be starting to fail.

title: I Like the Head Set.
review: Its well made.  The storage case is large.  Wearing the headphones is a bit of a learning curve.  They are different from other headphones I have.  Sony, Jabra, Plantronics.  These Headphones have a quality feel, that is really different than the standard headphones. The cable on this unit, is the only thing I didn't care for.  I bought a different cable from NewFantasia Replacement Audio Upgrade Cable, offered on Amazon at 4' plus other lengths.  The ends fit into the headphones.  They are narrow than the opening.  I take care removing the cables and on the insertion.  These other cables flex easier, have very little memory unlike the Focal.  I did email Focal and asked if they have other Cable options.  I still haven't heard anything.  I did get a form email when I sent in my question.  I didn't see any accessory options on their web page.

title: I use this for my Focal Elegia
review: The cord that came with the Focal is stiff and keeps a memory of the cord wrap.  I like the headphones, so the part that plugs in the headphone is narrow, but fit will.  I'm careful with the headphones, so far no issue.  This cable flexes more easily than the Focal one.  Focal, never replied when I asked if they offered other options on cables, plus I didn't see any options on their website.

title: I like my Jabra 75T better than this unit.
review:
The device was nice, but considering the cost, the app. I felt the Jabra, or my Sony's, even my PLT Pro are better. I wear headphones a lot, so I alternate my sets. On the plan I take my Sony. Work Sony or Jabra. Jabra with a phone call is Great.
The quality construction of this device was A+. I returned this. Try a refurbished pair. With Noice Cancellation off, the sound was better.

title: This is my go to headset now.  I'm using this more than my Sony's Or Plantronics
review: Comfortable to use for extended periods of time for me.  I'm wearing these for several hours at a time.  When you fold them flat, they turn off, extending your battery life, which I like.  Jabra App gives you options for sound.  People can hear me fine when I get phone calls, and I can talk to them while I have both earphones on my head.  I was using the PLT pro 2, since they put the music on hold when I take the headset off.  they get a touch warmer, not much.  So far the sound canceling is great.  I can't hear the neighbors or the construction that is happening next door.

title: I still have the 1000X from 2016
review: Wanted to see what this version had.  Very pleased.  I do wish Sony would include Amazon Music in the selection field, so we can listen with the optional features.  The download folder you can't change which isn't great.  I took 1 - star off for that.  Reason you get head sets is to listen to your music collection.  I like that you can adjust the Noise Canceling feature.  My other headset will be for work, this one will be for travel.  Also glad they give a cord so we can connect it to the airplane audio system.  Wouldn't be able to watch movies when I travel without it..

title: I was amazed
review: I had Bose 2's that lasted 4 yrs roughly.  Then they stopped working.  For the price I wasn't happy.  Were I work people get noisey, and I needed something quick to block out those around me.  I didn't want to get another pair of Bose.  I tried my sister Dr. Dre Noise cancelling headphones.  I was impressed, blocked out exterior sound, but the price was high.  So I purchases these and try them out, if they don't work, I was going to get the Dre's.  Well for the price, I was surprised.  The quality of sound is just what I needed for the office.  I select songs that have a easy and continues flow of sound, they block out a lot of back ground noise when I have them on.  I need to note, I have a shaved head, so the pads sit tight around my ears.  I wasn't too sure about the head phones when I got them, the cable looked tacky with the gold thread.  But for the cost, and the comfort and no battery to deal with either.  Two thumbs up.  If you wear a pierced earring, you might have to take that out for comfort.  I keep the box they come in to store when I leave.  For the price these meet my needs.  I wouldn't travel with them they don't fold down.  I noticed Phillips offers a sound cancelling set, I might give those a try for travel since they fold.  I'm very pleased with the product.  If you have extra money, try Dr. Dre, or Bose.  If you buy the Bose, see if you can get a warranty past 4 yrs, especially if you plan to use them often.

title: Decent sound, garbage mic
review:
I’ve have a set of wired M50s and the sound has always been decent — not spectacular but good enough. These seem about the same as long as they’re connected to something with decent Bluetooth/codecs.

The mic is garbage though. I don’t mind lower bitrates so much (being primarily limited by Bluetooth bandwidth and all that), but it seems to have sort of “noise cancelling” audio processing that garbles things when I start talking. If these could just have a connector for a cardioid or hypercardioid condenser mic on a boom (like some of audio-technica’s gaming headsets) without any extra processing they’d be my favorite headset. As it stands I still need to keep a separate headset or modmic around.

title: Full body soft sound good for extended listening
review: The earpiece fit secure and tight, the rubber edge is comfortable, good external noice blocking, has magnet to keep the erarbuds hang on the neck safely.  Like other B&W products, it’s a bottle of fine wine that takes some time to wake up the sound stage, so don’t jump into conclusion in 5 minutes.  Bluetooth distance is better than average, I can go to a room next door and stay connected.  Battery life and frequency range are better than comparable priced B&O.  Decode in aptX only, unlike Sure BT2 with multiple decoding standards.  There is remaining battery life indicator, kind of annoying.  I paired it with an iPhone 11 and a B&W Formation Audio, Formation displays brighter image as expected.  My usual Bluetooth earbuds is Shure 535, bought this because 535 is not comfortable in bed, the behind the ear cable breaks easily but 535 has superior sound.  Share 846 is also better but way overpriced.  Well, be honest, none of these Bluetooth can match wired sound.  Overall, it’s a great choice for the price.

title: if you've never heard the echo of a violin or felt like an opera singer is standing two feet from you
review:
The first time I used these headphones, I kid you not, I started tearing up.

I got them based on InnerFidelity's placement on their Wall of Fame. That spot is well-earned. You won't just hear snare drums, you'll hear the fabric of the drum reverberate. You can hear the pick slide on the guitar strings. EDM lovers, DJ's entire job is to make tracks that are well mastered, and these fabulous cans will send shivers up your spine with every bass drop. Classical music lovers, if you've never heard the echo of a violin or felt like an opera singer is standing two feet from you, you need these headphones.

I used to listen to music passively, in the background. With headphones this good, sometimes I'll just lay on the couch, close my eyes, and let them immerse me in the music.

Seriously, stop your search for headphones here. Unless you've got $150, in which case get the ATH M50x, but these are absolutely stellar and the price is unbeatable.

title: Screaming children? No problem for this tiny powerhouse pair of headphones.
review:
These little puppies have solid sound for earbuds. You absolutely must ensure they seal in your ear. It should feel like plugging your ears. Check out their sound charts on innerfidelity: they are not close to what you can get over-ear, but for $10 they are a steal.

There was a screaming child right behind me on an airplane and thanks to the fact that they are sealed in-ear monitors, I napped for over an hour.

title: Great until they die on you.
review:
These have been great little earbuds. The ANC function isn't anything to write home about but the sound quality, ease of pairing and battery life were great. Unfortunately after a year and a half of daily use, the left earbud gave out and none of the fixes Jabra support offered have worked.

If you're the type to always buy a new pair of earbuds every 12 months then they're great! If you're like me and expect high end earbuds like these to last 2-3 years then I'd look elsewhere.

title: Cutouts don't match :(
review: Even though I made certain this cover is made for my specific iPad model, the cutout for the headphones didn't match up! Shame, because this was a very nice quality case, and very pretty! Had to return :(

title: First one broke, but works well for the price
review: I bought this to clip onto my headphones. It worked well, with good sound quality, until one day it broke out of the blue. I scratched my head and ordered another one, and that one still works. They're very cheap, so value-wise, I'm not sure this can be beat.

title: worth the money
review: best earbuds for the price in the market right now. compared to airpods that's way over priced.

title: 1 ear bud stopped holding charge
review: the entire thing is useless after 3 months as one earbud will not hold a charge anymore. lame

title: Love em'
review:
These are my new favorite headphones. I had to put my B&W & VModa headphones to rest. My ears aren't comfy in them anymore and hurt after a few hours. The build quality on these are just amazing . I can fly with these from LA to JFK and my ears feel great. Very easy to pair. Tested the Bluetooth distance I can go upstairs and leave my phone downstairs and still hear a signal. Highly recommend. The clarity and sound are top notch. And sound better than my previous head sets. Adjusting the head size is huuuuge. No clicking! It's just smooth. Works great with Google assistant. I like how you can change the noise canceling. I turn it up high on the plane. I turn it down in public. They're just comfy. Sound great especially with high frequency & FIDELITY. They just feel phenomenal and they feel like they're built to last. I'm not a hardcore audiophile. I just want something that feels great,sounds great,looks great,and easy to use.

And I have to throw this in there. I get so many compliments on how they look 🤣 not that matters to the sound quality lol. But it does add to the fun factor of using them.

title: Should have a mounting jack on the end instead of a plug
review: (FYI, I have a 2006 Mazda 3.) I'm very happy with this. The only deficiency is that it has a TRS plug on the end instead of a jack. I had to cut it off and solder on one of these http://amazon.com/dp/B000ML4A2Q and drilled a neat hole next to the cigarette lighter. Looks incredible. Really, who wants a loose headphone cable dangling around at all times?

title: Excellent value for a kid headphone - WORKS FOR THE PLANE
review:
I had bought a pair of JLab kid headphones for my daughter a year or so ago from Wal Mart for about $15 and they were essentially garbage. The combo of a steep rolloff of high frequencies (I'm guessing around 13Khz) and the volume limiter made them impossible to use for any kind of noisy environment like an airplane or even a car.

...These are a huge upgrade from that AND at a lower price. They have a full frequency response (which allows you to listen at lower volumes due to being able to hear detail) and the 93db volume limit allows for listening in noisy places without risk of hearing damage. They are durable for my 2 & 5 YO. The daisy chain feature is also a great bonus. Now, the overall sound quality isn't going to compare to any serious headphone (obviously) and the background noise isolation could be better but for the $$, it would be tough to find something better.

title: Great Product
review: I always break my earphones. Whether it's from the vacuum cleaner, dropping them (and the iPod, which survived the fall intact), or the wires becoming disconnected at the base, earphones never seem to last long for me. I have not had these for very long, but I have a reason to believe things will be different this time. Today I accidentally ran them through the washing machine and dryer, and they still work perfectly! Additionally, they feel nice in the ear, seem to have good sound quality for the price (although I'm no expert on these matters), and come in lots of cute colors. If you need a set of earphones, get these!

title: Clarity 5 stars, durability 1
review: Third set I have purchased, yes they are expensive it so damn good I keep coming back to them.  Just wish the connection between the ear bud and the wire didn't fray all the time  I have found the life span on these to be 2 years max.  For clarity they get a five, for durability one star.  I settled on two because I did want to recognize the fact that they are good headphones

title: Can't get them quiet enough
review: Can't get the volume low enough to be comfortable in quiet environments or in bed--with both phone and headset controls on lowest without actual muting, they're stll not quiet.  Otherwise they're quite nice.

title: Too occlusive & reflective
review:
Excessively occlusive of ambient sound, and too much reflection/amplification of my own sounds, things that are desireable in sound-cancelling headphones worn on an airplane, but not good for everyday use when you want to hear a quiet knock on the door or a softly meowed request for attention.

Returning, and buying some SoundSports instead, hope they have the good sound without excessive occlusion, like the previous model, the

Bose SoundTrue In-Ear Headphones Model 715593-0040

Which worked great until feline intervention severed one earpiece cord.

title: Handy
review: I love that this both works to hold onto a shirt or necklace but also makes a neat keeper for the headphones when not in use.

title: 2 years in, still going strong after daily use.
review: Bought these back in 2012, and they are still going strong, my favorite pair of earbuds. I'm not an audiophile, but can just say that they isolate incredibly well, as well as are enjoyable to list to.

title: Just what I needed.
review:
I sweat A LOT. So the Jabra are just perfect. I have been using them for almost 4 months and they have not disappointed me. I like to run long distances, and they have not fell, not even once. When sweat gets in the ear canal, it does not affect the quality of sound (something that happened with my regular apple headphones).
Battery life is good. They charge fast.
They felt kind of weird for the first weeks, but then I just put them on, at forget about them. When I'm in the gym, I found myself accommodating them now and then, just because it feels like they are going to fall but, believe me, they never do.

title: Perfect
review: Case is perfect for my dj headphones. It even has a small pocket where I keep a few smaller cables. Now I don't have to worry about my headphones breaking while traveling

title: Works with external DACs
review: I'd worried that this wouldn't work with my external earphones, since they have their own in-cable DAC and therefore, unlike EarPods, aren't expecting pre-processed audio. It works perfectly, making me a very happy camper. One catch/caveat: the order of connection matters. If you plug this extension into the phone, and then plug your device into the extension, the phone won't recognize the device. You have to connect your device to the extension first, and then plug the combination into the phone.

title: Does its job, and stays out of your way
review:
I used this to split the optical output of my TV, directing it to both my soundbar and the DAC that drives my headphones, so that I can switch over to the headphones without having to plug anything in, or unplug it afterwards.

It works exactly as I’d hoped: well and unobtrusively.

title: Best of its kind
review:
I have tried many different kinds of headphone stand, and they have almost all failed me. The curved-loop kind not quite wide enough to evenly apply pressure to my earpads. The kind whose centered stem wants to wedge itself between those same earpads. The freakishly short kind designed for children‘s headphones, maybe, or wireless ones, because there‘s no way that an adult‘s headset can rest atop them without practically folding the cables underneath it.

But not this one. Oh no, not this one. It’s tall enough to accommodate even elongated headphones, while its offset design ensures that neither the earpads nor the cables will have to make space for an intrusive stem. It’s eminently stable, too.

The only catch is that the resting area isn’t *quite* wide enough to levelly hold Audeze’s redesigned, extremely wide headbands. For those, I’d recommend something like the BRAINWAVZ Hooka. But for just about everything else, it’s the stand to get.

title: Excellent build quality, but a little twangy
review:
I have to agree with E.C. The straight plug is very nice if you're looking for an alternative to the right-angled angled plugs used by both Logitech and Shure; the memory plastic that loops around the ears is functional without being bulky.

However, the cable is remarkably stiff, to the point where it seems to resonate with any stimulus. If, while wearing the earphones, I hold the end of the cable in one hand while gently running my fingernail over it with the other, I can hear every little bump.

For me, this isn't much of an issue: I tend to use the earphones at my desk, sitting still while typing, and in any case the sound isn't quite so obvious when music is actually playing. It might, however, be a concern for someone using the cable while walking, exercising, or doing anything else that involves movement.

title: Comfortable fit
review:
I like these headphones very much and I think they're a steal for the price.

I found the medium ones to fit well in my (lady) ears, although your mileage may vary on that. The sound is clear and crisp. The cord length is perfect and it never tangles (!!!). The mic button works perfectly to pause music on my Android.

The mic itself is so-so. Not nearly as clear as the phone itself, but works in a pinch when I have my hands full. There is also some noise when the cord is touched, but that's expected for headphones in this price range.

title: VR BEAST!
review: What a BEAST! I got this to run my HTC Vive headset, and this thing works like a charm! Holy crap, this thing has TWO power supplies! The BEAST is getting used for way more than VR now. Video editing, photo editing, music, graphics...programming in Unity. It never stops! I love this magic machine and the ULTRA POWER it provides. I don't usually buy machines with overkill power like this, but I had to this time. I wanted the portability. I've been able to bring this in a simple backpack along with the Vive to bunch of events, all with great results!

title: Not worth $80. Does not work as expected.
review: There is a delay in audio and you have to re-pair with your headset every time you turn it on and off. Also, it does not transmit to two headsets worry-free. When I turn on the second headset there is static in both headsets. Turn one set off, and audio is clear. Not worth $80.

title: Drop in quality
review: I have used these headphones for a long time. I have occasionally had to replace them when I pulled the wires out of the speakers. The last two pairs were very brittle and broke easily just below the hinges, two pairs in three days. This has not been a problem until now (Feb 07) and previously I found these headphones to be perfect for my needs.

title: Great, Great, and Great... Save yourself some money.
review:
I purchased these for my wife a while back (over 3 months). They're great, look great, sounds great, and feel great over your ears.
I've had great success with Sony's mid level headphones, even to the point that I've worn out cables, padding, and repaired them myself. Great for the $$$, the flat cord is just a perk (easy to keep untangled).

title: OK for a first try
review:
This is my first Borg implant, so I'm not sure what I should have expected. It seems to work ok. The ear piece doesn't fit in your ear and the ear loop is a pain to use. The mic does seem to pick up well and I can hear it ok. The connection to my phone doesn't seem particularly solid. I get lots of static and break ups if the phone is on the opposite side of my body from the heat set. Another head set I have (Parrot SK4000 Helmet Headset) has a much better connection from several feet away.

Since I planned to hack this thing anyway, most of those short comings don't matter. If you want a headset, there probably are better options.

title: A great pair of buds
review: I tried and returned at least five pairs of earbuds before these ones, including the SoundTrue. For the non-audiophile - I guess that's what I am - these do what they promise: They have great sound (both music and audiobooks), they're comfortable, and they block out lots of noise. Durability? I've only had them a month... so far, so good.

title: Audio jack is useless. Headphones don't fit.
review: Took this case traveling and realized that my Bose headphones for the iPad / iPhone don't work in the jack. I guess that's a cut out issue? Very disappointed. Won't be taking this on upcoming trips where I might want to watch a movie on my iPad. Useless.

title: A good backup, but you can do better for daily use
review: I got this as a backup for when my Bluetooth headset acts up, as it can work as either a 3.5mm headset or USB C.  Since my laptop can use either and my phone can use the USB C, it's a handy backup that I can keep in my bag.  For those uses, it's great.  For daily use, it's a bit too flimsy, uncomfortable, and lacking in audio quality.  It's not bad (none of the negatives I listed are dealbreakers), but you can definitely do better.

title: Perfect, save for the missing clip
review:
I've used the BTR3 and BTR5 Bluetooth DAC/amps, and I love them. I still recommend the BTR5 for anyone using IEMs, but I always wanted a bit more for my headphones, and that's where the BTR7 comes in.

The BTR7 can be used as a USB DAC/amp, but I've never tried that. It's a remarkable Bluetooth DAC/amp with all of the CODECs, ample range, and that sweet clean sound. It can power IEMs, but so can the smaller BTR5 and smaller still BTR3. Where this shines is headphones. I use with my Focal Clear and Eligia headphones, and they're getting all of the juice they need. I find that my Sennheiser HD6XX and Hifiman Sundara sound sublime as well. I find that they're not quite up to my uber powerful desktop amp, the Topping A90, but that's a whole different ballgame. It's not a really a fair comparison, and the BTR7 sounds 98% as good as the desktop setup.

The controls are competent, and the included sleave is a nice touch. My only complaint is that the unit is glossy and lacks a clip to attach to your shirt, pocket, or headband of headphones. I use the BTR5's clip a lot on the headband of headphones (along with a short cable) to create more of a Bluetooth headphone vibe. Supposedly a case with a clip is being designed.

Highly recommended for listening to headphones on the go.

title: Great for Zoom, podcasts, voiceovers, etc...
review:
I'm a corporate trainer by trade, so I lead virtual instructor led training calls, record podcasts, and add voice over to online courses. Any of these could be accomplished with a modest microphone (USB or 3.5mm), but having a clearer recording does help add polish to all of those tasks and greatly enhance the learner experience.

This microphone does all of those tasks very well. I put this on a boom arm to have it handy when needed and swing away when not. The fact that this can connect to a boom or any mounting is a plus, as some USB mics lack that ability. Using USB C is a plus too. As a mic, this is easy to use, offers the right patterns, and sounds great. It's all hardware and out of the box Windows drivers, which is great for using on a managed PC provided by your employer. There's also built in headphone out, but that's easy enough to disable (disabling is best if you don't want to use, as Zoom, Teams, etc... won't try to use that output).

I love this because I've gotten great feedback (no pun intended-nor actual feedback ever experienced). It does all I need very well and checks off all of the right boxes. I'd recommend for frequent users. I've had good experience with cheaper ~$50 generic USB models, which may be better (in terms of value--not results) for some people.

title: Sturdy and easy to assemble--best for headphones with a rigid band (vs suspensions)
review:
I've recently gotten the audiophile bug, and that's yielded a few planar magnetic headphones and a pair of dynamic ones. They range from 300g-1kg (ouch!). This holds them all quite beautifully, and it does a great job with those that have a solid headband.

A couple have straps that are suspended below a band, which can stretch. I like to sneak the hanger below the band, but this is too bulky to do that. It's also a single (albeit large) point, as opposed to more of a cradle to disperse the weight. These complaints really only apply to a specific subset of heavy suspended headphones, and chances are that's not you. Anything else works great on this setup.

title: You likely won't need this, but it does work well
review:
I have a variety of headphones from Sennheiser, Behringer, Hifiman that could be powered by a PC, laptop, iPod (I still have a classic), or phone (if it has a 3.5mm jack), but they can demand more power than these devices can offer. That's where this comes in--it can give a device that already has a 3.5mm jack (this won't help a phone without one) a boost to fill the headphone with richer sound. If this sounds like you, it's a great fit. It doesn't have a DAC, it isn't Bluetooth, and it won't help at all if you don't already have a 3.5mm source.

The device is compact, has all cables attached, and easily charges via USB C. It has basic controls for phones, and its simple to use. I find my Sennheiser 6xx sound richer and fuller, as do my Hifiman Sundara. My 250ohm Behringer 770 pro sound better (they're way too much for a phone), but this amp is a bit lacking for those. That last bit leads to the other limitation--this is not a replacement for a desktop headphone amp or a much bigger portable one. It'll work for 90% of headphones (closer to 99% if you include IEMs and basic models--less so for audiophile gear), but it's a compromise for mobility and cost.

Clarity is spot on. That's what you get from this THX AAA design. It simply takes what comes in and adds oomph.

title: One of the few 2.5mm balanced to 6.35mm singled ended aqdapters
review:
This is pretty much all I've seen that can turn 2.5mm balanced headphones into 6.35mm single ended headphones. I use this with my xDuoo TA-30 and Sennhesier HS 6xx headphones. It works brilliantly. My only concern is the length, which is prodigious. My setup works fine, but I'd prefer a right angle connector.

Since there's nothing else out there that does this and this works well, I recommend this.

title: Tremendous battery life, ok audio quality, and lacking in comfort
review:
I've never used a headset with the battery power of this bad boy. Leaving on overnight doesn't even stop this from working well in the morning or even all day. That along with great mic quality make this a worthwhile choice. The price, complete lack of comfort, and so-so sound make this not my first choice. I find all of my other headphones are more comfortable than these, and all have better incoming sound too.

If your priority is outbound sound quality and battery life, this is likely for you. I find the compromises just don't work for me.

title: Great if you don't want a traditional headset
review:
I've used more than my share of headsets, and I'm not too keen on this. For starters, it's up in that "it better be great" price range, and it's not really great. It's good, and if it's your type of product, that may be enough. I ended up using these for a week and these giving up.

The packaging is typical Razer. There's really no setup, and you'll get started quite quickly. I wear a few different in ear monitors for music, so I'm not opposed to wearing in ear doodads, but they never fit right. They stayed in place and they seemed to seal well, but I never took them off without feeling relief. The mic worked well, but the lack of a simple mute made it less than ideal, and the whole look made me feel like I was working a driver through at a fast food joint. I didn't have any issues with glasses, and I did appreciate the lack of a traditional headset messing up my hair. The audio quality was just ok, as was the mic. This just doesn't feel like a "pro" or $80+ product.

Recommended if you're looking for something different than a typical headset, otherwise $80 on a headset tends to sound better and feel more comfortable.

title: Compact and powerful
review:
I use this to charge my laptop, phone, and any number of other doodads. Using a C to C cable, it delivers as much power as my devices can consume. The USB A ports are a bit more modest, but they can still charge wireless headphones or trickle charge my camera batteries. The unit is compact and easily fits in any number of pockets in my backpack. That compact size and versatility make this a welcome companion to my travel go bag.

Recommended

title: Attractive travel backpack with comfortable straps
review:
This backpack can store enough for travel but isn't too big to bring into the office. It's got better than average looks, comfort, and durability. The looks may be due in part to the lack of external storage, but there still are a couple options. It carries 5-15lbs well. Any more and it's exceeding it's capabilities, but these days you can have a laptop, charger, headphones, and a few other items and still be under 10lbs.

It's worth $70 if you travel a lot or like the look, but I'd feel more comfortable recommending this to everyone for closer to $50.

title: Looks great, sounds good, poor build
review:
This is a tough set of cans to review. I've used some great Panasonic ones over the years, albeat 10-20 years ago. Most of the stuff more recently lacks polish and ambition. This set lacks polish and ambition. It shoots for 4 stars and barely makes it.

The look is nice. I really like the blue, and it has enough execution to not seem overly cheap. The actual materials are overly cheap. Way too much plastic and again limited ambition with materials. The build is closer to 3 stars. Sounds quality is good, not quite very good. Comfort is good, but not very good, especially for larger heads.

Basically Panasonic designed a decent set of headphones for people who are discerning headphone users.

title: Solid value, but not the same as a $250 pair of Sony headphones
review:
These headphones are better than $50 headphones and worse than $250 headphones. That's not a surprise given the cost, which falls between the two. It's also not a bad thing, as it's prices much closer to the former than the latter.

Overall fit and finish is good. Like $100 headphones good, not $300 headphones good. It's definitely enough for most people. Audio quality is good, but it's definitely not great. It's Altec Lansing good, not Audio Technica good, and a far cry from Sony good (their wh1000xm3 is amazing). Range is very good, and noise cancelling is more of an idea than a reality. As another reviewer noted, these are noise dampening, not noise canceling. The net result is better than a $50 set of headphones, but it won't suffice for audio files, and it likely won't be as good of a value for regular users as a deal on refurbished Sony wh1000xm3.

For occasional or less demanding users, these are worth considering.

title: Affordable and viable--just not great
review:
For one reason or another you may need to replace ear pads on a head of headphones, especially headphones that cost over $200. Having these options is great as it can add life to a valuable device, and if well done, it can be an upgrade. These are not an upgrade. They seem to be wearing faster than the originals, they aren't quite as comfortable, and they offer nothing the original don't. Even if was an upgrade, it would take a lot to overcome the fact that it's quite a pain to swap them.

If you need a new set, these are viable, available, and affordable.

title: Could use a heavier base
review:
Everything about this is good enough, but the base could be better. It tends to fall over, especially when taking a snug fitting set of headphones. Adding weight, a bigger base, or some form of adhesion/suction would help.

The unit is tall enough for headphone extended for bigger heads and the top can accommodate wider headbands. It's a solid effort, but I kinda hate needing to use two hands to get headphones off without knocking this over.

title: Wonderful solution for many different headphones (not just Shure)
review:
While not perfect (ergonomics and battery life could be better), I really love this set. I use them with Fiio FA7, but given the ubiquity of the MMCX connection for higher end earbuds, you have a ton of options. The sound is amazing. Not 99.9999% perfect, but that's not my thing (don't use fancy silver balanced cables or listen to 24bit 192hz tracks). It's every bit as good as a wired connection to my S10+ (admittedly not the best DAC/amp). Anyway, it's loads better than my Bose Quiet Comfort, Bang & Olufsen Beoplay E8 2.0, or any other wireless headphones.

Sound for me is perfect. Ergonomics, is another story. The cable is too short to put in your pocket, which is fine, but it's too long to just sort of wear behind the neck. I can wear around my neck like some pendant, but then using the buttons is just odd. The bulk is too much to just be a "cable", but as we'll get to soon, the battery life afforded by the size is lacking. 10 hours is a bit charitable, though it could vary by codec, placement, and volume. For me, I get a good 8 hours of constant use, but intermittent use likely is closer to 6-7 hours if those uses are spread out over a few days. It's OK, but not perfect.

Hopefully v3 adds LDAC, 25% better battery life, USB C, and better ergonomics.

I still love these. The sound is amazing.

title: An upgrade from the OEM cable
review:
The OEM cable uses an uncommon (not non-standard) 2.5mm end for the headphones (who knows why), so many ready made 3.5mm solutions (on both ends) won't work. This cable has a 2.5mm plug on one end and 3.5mm on the other. In between you have some added functionality. Nothing special, but it replicates the buttons available via Bluetooth.

The use cases are limited, but if you want to get more time between charges or prefer a direct (and not lossy) connection to sound, it's a great solution. As I lost my original cable, it was a great fit for me.

title: Cheap and novel, but not built to last
review: These are OK as semi disposable earbuds for kids.  Audio quality is decent and definitely not bad, and they're relatively comfortable.  Durability is a bit poor (audio only coming out of one ear after a few weeks of sporadic use.

title: It works!
review:
I don't think I'll ever need a 5 way splitter, but it works ok with 2-3 headphones. It's not magic, so there's some loss of signal. Most devices have some headroom to accommodate this signal loss.

There's not much else to say. It works!

title: Horrible Bluetooth range limit an otherwise good (not great) set of earbuds
review:
I really wanted to love these, and there's still a lot to like. These simply are too limited.

The packaging, accessories, and the like is nice, but the fact that the case has a rigid (but not durable) bit to present the earbuds that's not really useful for the long haul doesn't help. The buds fit my ears as is, which is a huge plus. The comfort also is spot on. The noise cancelling is better than none, but less than my Bose Quiet Comforts. I wouldn't use these if I needed noise cancelling, but it's a nice plus.

The controls are a bit of a chore to use and not intuitive. The mic is ok, but much less than I'd expect from high end Jabras. The big issue--wireless range. I use these with my new S9+ and they cut out when in my jeans pocket. Wearing jeans and a t-shirt, these cannot be relied upon! They work ok when the phone is out of my pocket, but this limitation is comically bad.

title: Looks great, well made, and offer decent sound.  Sadly very sweaty ear cups.
review:
These were easy enough to pair, lightweight, and comfortable. Sadly they simply get too sweaty. Audio quality is good but not great. I'd describe these more as fashion headphones vs true audiophile ones. They hold their own, but not so much that they eclipse offerings for even half the price. The fit and finish and style do, and if they weren't so sweaty, they would be a much more viable set.

Will be looking for some replacement ear cups.

title: Good sound, amazing comfort, and a great price
review:
Compared to my Jaybirds, Klipsch, and UE headphones, these are quite a step down. Compared to $20 headphones however, and these are great!

They're sturdy, stay in place, and offer a good, though not great sound. The sound is a bit muffled, and nothing sounds amazing. These are plenty fine enough for workouts, podcasts, etc. The comfort is amazing. I'll take good sound, amazing comfort, and a great price any day.

I've lost enough fancy headphones to appreciate a great bargain, and these are just that!

title: Cheap, easy to "install", and works
review: I had some issues finding the right fit for my headphones, as it got quiet at times without fidgeting with the cord. The buttons also seemed a bit useless. On the positive side, it's cheap, easy to "install", and works.

title: Cheap, easy to "install", and works
review: I had some issues finding the right fit for my headphones, as it got quiet at times without fidgeting with the cord.  The buttons also seemed a bit useless.  On the positive side, it's cheap, easy to "install", and works.

title: Excellent headphones, but the clean neutral sound can leave some wanting a warmer sound
review:
I've had the pleasure of using a variety of wired and wireless headphones, and among wired closed back designs, these offer the cleanest most neutral sound I've heard. The Planar Magnetic design is unique at this price point (well Monoprice has their own set coming out soon), and from what I hear (quite literally), nothing was lost in bringing it to more affordable levels.

The fit is a bit tight on my enormous head, and replacement ear pads are in my future. In terms of overall impression, I really like these, but I'm also rather keen on a neutral sound. That sounds great, but it means losing some of the boost at the low end many are used to, and it can also feel a bit lifeless. The closed nature tends to limit this feel, and the combination here can be stark. Then again, you know what things truly sound like. These can really serve as a monitor.

These fold flat for travel, and don't need added power (any phone or media player can drive these), though they certainly wouldn't say no to good clean power from a dedicated amp. All in all, I give these five stars, but I hesitate to recommend them to one and all. Much like snow tires, these are a bit of a niche item, and they excel in that scope.

title: I could not recommend these more--great for Audio-Technica ATH-MSR7 Sonic Pro
review:
Having already tried the angled earpads, I kinda knew what to expect with these, and the "hybrid" nature of these fixed my main issue with my other pair--sweat. These block sound rather well, fix with amazing comfort, and lead to absolutely no ear sweat. That's all that I could ever ask for. They fit my Audio-Technica ATH-MSR7 Sonic Pro headphones perfectly.

I really don't know what to say except that these deliver everything I could ever ask for and I could not recommend these more.

title: Whether angled or traditional design, Brainwavz makes great earpads
review:
