I was a bit hesitant to order these for my [[ASIN:B00PEU9CFA Audio-Technica ATH-MSR7BK SonicPro Over-Ear High-Resolution Audio Headphones, Black]]. They looked a bit big and clunky, and I never tried angled earpads. They work great!

Installation was relatively easy, though at first it may seem like you're damaging your fancy headphones. After pulling away the old ones, they went on easy enough. A thin (but not sharp) tool may help, but it's not needed. I immediately realized how nice it was to always know left from right (the cord should help, but not always for some reason). The fit was good, as was the seal, and the comfort, while not perfect, was both better and very good. I'm not one to appreciate all of the minutia of open sound stages and the like, so I cannot say it sounds all that different or better, but I know I like these, especially the fit.

They look a bit clunky but I don't care. I simply like these.

title: Fits my UE TripleFi 10 great!
review:
I have a pair of [[ASIN:B0019RBJOE Ultimate Ears TripleFi 10 Noise Isolating Earphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)]] and I never had luck with the oem tips and frankly tips for these are hard to come by (large tube), especially that fit my mid sized to small ear canals). These work great!.

My only complaint (and to be clear, I'll keep buying these) is that the foam does become a bit unlaminated from the inner hard plastic tube, and it does so seemingly quickly. It could be my own habits (I don't put these in a case or take extra care to wrap these just right).

title: A good option if you don't have a lot of 2.4ghz devices/networks
review:
I've used a few wireless headsets over the years (mostly Turtle Beach), and these generally compare well, but there are a few flaws that make me a bit reluctant to recommend these.

Let's star with what these do well. They are comfortable, even for longer sittings, and they aren't as heavy as they look (lots of plastic--for now that's a pro). The audio is great and surround separation is top notch. The mic is clear, and it's easy to mute and know its muted. Wireless works well (most of the time), and the range is very good. So far so good!

Things start to fall apart with wireless. While the range is very good, and the audio generally is great, there's a problem. The audio cuts out intermittently, likely due to 2.4ghz interference issues. I live in a condo and between my own networks, microwaves, etc... and my neighbors' networks, it's a minefield. There is a solution, and Logitech seemingly is oblivious to it--offer a dual band headphone. Turtle Beach and Astro do this. The plastic is a bit cheap and the overall look isn't my thing, but really it's the dodgy wireless that's the issue.

In the end it comes down to the wireless, and in my mind it's a no go, but many people live in single family homes with at most one 2.4ghz wireless network. If that's you, consider these as a good option.

title: Fancy IEMs are only as good as the fit and seal
review: I was having issues finding tips for my Ultimate Ears Triple Fi 10 that fit my ears.  My ear canals are medium to small and the Triple Fi has huge flanges.  This worked great!  So comfy and almost total silence.  Bass response is improved, and everything sounds crisp and clear again.  With any IEM, it's the fit and seal more than anything, and those fancy headphones were sounding like rubbish without a good fit.  These did the trick!

title: Great switch with splitter built in
review:
This sturdy device does a great job as a four way switch and a two way splitter, which helps with sound bars and other components that still rely on optical in and lack switching. My sound setup fits this bill, and this device works nicely with my Harmony. The multiple outputs is nice, as it allows my headphones to have an independent output of the sound bar.

Note my ViewHD HDMI splitter uses similar remote control commands, which created chaos with my setup. Ultimately I swapped the HDMI splitter out, and this device works great.

title: Worse than what came with my headphones
review: The tips enclosed didn't upgrade those provided with the Gaga headphones made by Monster, nor did they fit some of the other models advertised.  Basically these will never be used, and I regret buying them.

title: Awesome for what they are, wish they were more
review:
I've used some rather nice modern 5ghz digital headphones, such as the [[ASIN:B006W41W4Q Turtle Beach Ear Force XP400 Dolby Surround Sound Gaming Headset]] and [[ASIN:B006W41X1S Turtle Beach Ear Force X32 Digital Headset]], but these are a step above in common functions. Frankly there's nothing these do that they don't do well. Specifically:

* Uber comfortable
* solid build
* easy setup
* excellent sound quality (in a rather congested wireless environment)
* rather good virtual surround

What's lacking?

Well this is a pure PC setup, so unlike others, there's no hooking to up Xbox 360, PS3, Blu Ray, or even directly to a TV. This severely limits usefulness for non gamers, but I do use them with my XBMC setup with great success (albeit with a few clicks to switch audio drivers). I wish there was some kind of other inputs, as everything else is amazing. I'm not going to take any stars away, as it is what it is, and if that's what you want, this is an amazing wireless setup.

title: Not bad, but be wary if you have WiFi
review:
In a different era where WiFi wasn't as ubiquitous, especially in living rooms, this would shine amongst mediocre 900mhz offerings. That being said, these days with laptops, iPads, and various gizmos hooked up to TVs relying on WiFi, there's a lot of 2.4ghz signals in the living room. They use the same frequency range as these headphones. Interference can hinder either the headphones, your WiFi, or both. It's not static on the headphones or poor WiFi performance, it's unacceptable WiFi interruptions and horrible headphone performance. Unusable in either case. When I moved the setup elsewhere it performed better (4 star better), but it wasn't phenomenal. You still have the battery issue mentioned by others, the audio quality is good, but not great, and they're not that comfortable.

Look for a 5ghz capable setup, perhaps one of the more gaming oriented ones. They have microphones, but often they can be removed if not needed. I like the [[ASIN:B0093DHP4O Turtle Beach TBS-2265 TBS-2265 -Ear Force X32]] or [[ASIN:B008J5646C Turtle Beach TBS-2276-01 Ear Force XP400 Wireless Game]]. Both work with 5ghz as well, which isn't as crowded. Audio performance is way better.

title: Not bad, but there are better options in the gaming realm
review: I rely upon wireless headphones to watch TV while the misses is asleep, and these get the job done, but surprisingly I found much better options available to gamers.  While I do play an occasional video game, I don't ever use a microphone or anything while I play, so I never considered one of them until I started hearing good things about the digital wireless headsets available. When I tried one, I was blown away compared to the hissing found in these old school 900MHz analog models. Do yourself a favor and consider [[ASIN:B006JSPLA6 EarForce X31 Headset (Refurbished)]], which cost marginally more ($58 as a refurb when I type this) and offer better comfort and much clearer sound. You have to hear the sound to believe it. Just put the microphone out of the way and call it a day. They run off of 2.4GHz and use a WiFi signal, so if you have a router nearby (which can cause issues), splurge on the [[ASIN:B006W41X1S Turtle Beach Ear Force X32 Digital Headset]] which adds the 5GHz frequency. Either are so much better than these. Sennheiser makes great headphones, and these aren't that. They're wireless tech is lacking, and even if you take the hiss and other issues out of the equation, there just not that comfy nor is the sound (ignoring the hiss) that good. Look elsewhere, even somewhere you may not of thought of looking.

title: Decent, but check out the ones for gamers
review: I rely upon wireless headphones to watch TV while the misses is asleep, and these get the job done, but surprisingly I found much better options available to gamers. Look elsewhere, even somewhere you may not of thought of looking.

title: Great little device
review:
My laptop has onboard sound, but it isn't the best, and I'm stuck doing loads of VOIP for an online class. I invested in [[ASIN:B002BH3JDA Creative Labs HS-980 Fatal1ty Professional Series MKII Gaming Headset (Black)]], which is a great headset btw, and in order to get the most out of the noise canceling, a compatible Creative Labs sound card is required, thus I decided to take the leap.

The leap was worthwhile, but a USB sound card is a bit of a pain. Were it built in (or ExpressCard), well then it would even be better. The software should be an easy install due to the onboard storage, but I still had to go online for a very slow update (it's rare to find drive downloads that slow anymore). Afterward, and after a few reboots, all was well. The software is a mixed bag, and really only the driver is required. The DSP effects are fun and all, but not really necessary. The crystalizer does work well, as does the noise canceling (with the proper headset), and well that's about it. Kudos for the extension dongle, but it would be better if it had a less stubby plug (kinda defeats the purpose), and the cap on a string is a good idea, but it rattles a bit in transit.

All in all, it's not bad at the right price and for the right need.

title: Decent, but not great
review:
If ~$10, I'd give these 4 stars, but +$20, it's 3. The comfort is ok, and to be honest at the low end of the price spectrum, that's really all I care about (that and not being worse audio-wise than what you get with your iPods). A few weeks of use has seen my try some different tips, which seems to have found a nice comfortable (2-3 hours of use comfortable) fit. That's the good news--well that and the Amazon frustration free packaging. The neither good nor bad news is that they're decent enough sound wise.

Now for the bad news, they already seemed to have seen better days after a few weeks. That kind of quality is unacceptable. The units themselves are falling apart (ironically where the image above says "meticulous craftsmanship) and the cable seems about ready to snap. This isn't cool even for $10. I can be worried about these failing on the go, so they're off to die in a drawer unless I become desperate.

I could offer a more detailed review, but really it isn't necessary. There are better cheap headphones than these. Look elsewhere.

title: Great for Training and Podcasting
review: I develop online training and podcasting that require me to record others in an office environment (if we're lucky a closed conference room) and on sub par PCs.  Up until recently we had to use an inexpensive ($30) headset, which frankly sucked.  This is a dramatic improvement, blocking all background noise (in both a recording and playback context), and it's quite comfortable.  The output is simply amazing, as you almost sound like you've used a recording studio.  I recommend using the USB connection unless you have a high end sound card (placing the circuitry outside the PC helps dramatically due to less electronic noise & hiss).  I no longer dread playing back recordings, and I thoroughly recommend this item.

title: Very very small
review:
I am not a very large person, but these headphones were very very tight. They do not have extensions. Consequently, they only covered the top part of my ear.

These would work fine for a child, these are not adult sized.

title: Got something better. The reviews are pretty accurate online
review: resold them. Got something better. The reviews are pretty accurate online. The best quality of these headphones are the comfort! never had a more comfortable headset, but the sound quality is lacking, much better products on the market. only reason I got them is they were 60 bucks (not bad for that price)

title: Awesome earphones 👍
review: Purchased as an easy on the go headphones with little expectation and these blew me away. They sound great and they look pretty premium.

title: nice comfortable headphones
review: very comfortable ear cushions, and a nice price. the bendable mic extension is made of metal and is rugged.  it unplugs for use as just headphones, but plugged in the mic works great, These are well made.

title: I'm so happy I bought these!
review: I would never have made it through 28 hours of flying without these things. I really wanted a pair of active noise cancelling headphones but I didn't want to spend a ton of money. I had never heard of this brand before and I was a little concerned about ordering them but I'm so glad that I did! They work great! They cut out almost all of the humming from the airplane and did exactly what I needed them to do. They weren't as good as my cousin's $300 Bose headphones, but that's to be expected. They come in a nice case, which was a little bulky carrying them while traveling but totally worth it. I really recommend this for a low cost active noise cancelling headphone.

title: decent
review: decent headphones, but nice price so I can't complain. They can get uncomfortable after wearing them for more than an hour or so.

title: Good Noise Cancellation, Some Problems
review:
I've had these for a month using a Pixel 5, transitioning from over-ear headphones, and I mostly like them overall. Their battery is lasting forever, and that case recharges them -- you just have to recharge the case occasionally. The buds fit in, rotate into my earbuds pretty well, they just don't always remember their settings.
I wasn't a fan of the constant switch between Ambient Sound and Noise Cancellation, so I changed the left bud to volume control, and the right bud controls play/pause.
Still, there are unexpected blips in my earbuds, with no changes otherwise. And the Ambient Sound still pops up occasionally.
If you're walking around outside, you can typically hear your footsteps very clearly.

title: The park where the band means the cuff cracked on one side and is beginning to crack on the other
review: Great value if they actually didn't fall apart with average use. I own 2 pairs of airpods and these headphones and I rotate through each. So functionally I've used these for about one-third of a year before they started to fall apart. I used to like Anker products but they seem to be putting out cheap crap lately. My Soundcore 2 speaker from them also stopped working and all they were able to offer me was 15% off another purchase from their official site. Garbage.

title: Worst mic of all time.
review:
I wanted so badly to love this headset, but I couldn't. It was fairly comfortable, it had impressive virtual 7.1 surround sound, and the LED's were really cool.

The mic.... IS HORRIBLE. When I say horrible I mean it's FAR worse than both the Apple in-line mic that comes with iPods and iPhones. It's INEXCUSABLE how bad the quality is.

I even ended up contacting SteelSeries support about the issue, only to have someone respond and tell me that the mic quality is part of a "Carefully evaluated design scheme.", whatever that means.

Bottom line: If you intend on talking to your friends over VOIP - DO NOT BUY THIS.

title: Another great set of buds!
review:
Having owned two other pairs of earbuds from this company, I was excited to try out another pair.
The fit and feel of these buds is the most comfortable I’ve worn. The spoken audio quality is excellent, and phone call audio is good. The music quality is average, but not bad at all.
Truly impressed by the battery life. Haven’t gotten to the end of the life of one bud just yet, but after whole day use and no power loss, I’m happy.
There is some passive noise cancellation, on par with several other pairs I’ve owned.
The case is premium in feel and looks, though a tad large.
Highly recommend, especially for the price!

title: A little disappointing
review: These were fine overall and we got such a good deal on them that we are mostly happy with the purchase. However we were disappointed that anyone within earshot of you can hear what you are listening to, albeit muffled. Kinda negates the whole point of headphones.

title: the best ANC headset
review: This is the best ANC headset so far.  I also have the T65 and there is no comparison.  It fit more comfortable.  Also with the wireless charging feature, i don't really need to worry about the charging cable anymore.

title: great work fromhome tool
review: After getting a new job, there are so many web meetings and con calls.  This Evolve 65T is a perfect tools.  I just need to plug the USB dongle to my work phone and the wireless earbuds just work.  The sound quality is awesome, the best is the microphone reception.  It won't collect too many of the background noise and nobody complains about the sound quality.  The only thing is a little pricy comparing just the regular Bluetooth headphones.

title: Sufficient, comfortable
review:
These are very comfortable and feel very light on my head.

The sound is sufficient for gaming. Treble is just a little muddy and bass is reasonable. Mid-range seems "warm." My opinion is mainly in comparison to a pair of Audio Technica ATH-M50s.

Volume control and mute on the cable are very convenient and do not seem susceptible to being adjusted accidentally.

The cable is pretty short but comes with an extension that is really long. I would have preferred a longer base cable and a shorter extension.

Retractable mic boom feels solid. Overall appearance of this headset is great!

5 stars for comfort, reasonable sound quality for price, convenience of controls, great looks; -1 star for cable length.

title: Can-Do headphones - great price
review: Good deal for the price, the noise canceling works reasonably well, the sound itself is okay but not great.  They are very comfortable and can wear them without pause on a 10 hour flight.  All in all a good deal for the price, but do not expect incredible sounding headphones - for that you need Bose.

title: Cans Crimp Ears
review: I bought these to replace an old pair of Denon noise canceling headphones that I loved but quit after 2 1/2 years (they are no longer produced).  I fly a lot and need comfortable headphones for the plane.  The Audio-Technica were solid in terms of noise canceling but I found them to be so uncomfortable that I ended up sending them back.  I could wear them about 30 minutes before I had to take them off.  Even when I loosened up the top piece they still felt very tight.  They were also heavy and I found them hot (I recognize this is kind of strange and I can't explain this phenomenon).  For me the discomfort was not worth it.

title: I can't really hear you...
review:
At the price these came at - $136.00 - they are an excellent deal. I am no headphone maven and in fact these are my first pair. I travel overseas a quite a bit and I really enjoyed using them. They cut down immeasurably on the regular ambient plane noises - esp. the "rushing" inside a cabin and were just fine for the on board movies etc. After a while they do hurt the ears a bit - say 4 or 5 hours - but I'm probably a bit sensitive to that anyway. For the price I got them at, a great deal.

Fast Forward Sept. 2012 - I've had these headphones for almost 2 1/2 years and the right side has quit working, making the headphones pretty useless. Not sure what the life span is for this kind of product but I was hoping for longer than 2 1/2 years. Thus lowering my rating to two stars...

title: Great functionality at a reasonable price
review:
I have been using the Kissral earbuds intensively every day for a month, mostly on the street and at the gym. I am very happy with them. Good fit in my ears (comfortable, and stay put while running), good battery life, excellent charging case, work well even when sweating profusely.

No big cons. There is no active noise cancellation, but I knew that when purchasing the earbuds. Before buying the Kissral earbuds I considered buying the new Sony WF-1000XM3, but not only they cost five times as much, but they are also not waterproof (important for gym use) and they have mediocre reviews. The sound quality of the Kissral earbuds is not great, but good enough for me in the street and at the gym. At home I use over-the-ear headphones with much better sound quality. Finally, the battery in the left earbud runs down faster than the right earbud--still, it provides about five hours of use, and you can quickly get a partial charge from the charging case.

Overall, I am very happy so far. No regrets whatsoever.

title: I liked the prior generation better
review: I liked the prior generation better. the buttons and switches on this one are less intuitive and easier to accidentally hit when adjusting the headset. The sound and pairing are all the same though, so I'll keep it.  I also dislike the shiny chrome-ish accents, which are actually buttons.

title: Decent fit
review: I had a set of SOUNDPEAT Force Pro headphones with fins that kept popping off and getting lost.  I picked these up for a replacement.  They were a bit longer in the fin than I would have liked but they stayed on and worked well.

title: Great headphones
review:
I have been pleased with these headphones. The sound quality is good. The controls are responsive. They are easy to pair and unpair. They fit my very small ears very well.

The only complaint I have is the little wrap things. If they come off, the earphones are unwearable because the edge that is covered by them is very uncomfortable. I wish it was a smoother edge and wasn't necessary to use them. They don't help hold the headphones in my ears. You are given 3 sets with the headphones of different sizes but they come off easily. I have lost them just walking around when the headphones became separated from one another.

title: Good headphones for small ears
review:
I love in ear headphones but I have extremely small ear canals, so finding a decent quality set of headphones that don’t hurt is always difficult. I picked up these and a set of the Linklike wireless headphones (which I also reviewed), and these were much better.

The good - The sound quality is great. For inexpensive wired headphones, they more than meet my expectations. The sound was very similar to my LUDOS headphones. They fit my ears with very little fiddling and haven’t caused me pain. The noise canceling is solid. I couldn’t hear my kid talking to me until she poked me, and I didn’t have the music up loudly. I made one phone call, which was short, but the person on the other end said the sound quality was clear.

The bad - My only concern is that the wires for these headphones aren’t covered. I am a little rough on headphones. I stick them in my pocket when I’m running around, they get tangled, they get wound and unwound. Without a nylon covering they are going to tangle a lot more, and I am concerned that the wires are going to be very fragile. I suspect that they won’t last long, so I have to decide if I am going to keep them or return them.

title: Good at first but didn't hold up
review:
It is difficult for me to find anything that fits my small ear canals, and these fit fairly well with the smallest ear pieces. My commute is over an hour each way and I use headphones at least 5 days a week. Overall the sound quality wasn't bad for inexpensive headphones and the mic was clear and I was easy to undestand. Unfortunately over the last two weeks the sound output has gotten much softer. Then the mic started echoing any time I was on a call. Then when I was on the phone or listening to music the headphones would drop the call or stop the playback. I have had them less than 3 months.

Disappointing that they didn't hold up.

title: Decent budget headphones with mic
review:
I was looking for a set of wired headphones with an in-line microphone for when I need to take calls because the ones I had been using died. I have very small ear canals so it has been hard to find good ones with a reliable mic. These headphones have some pros and cons. Lots of different sized ear tips from XS to L. I love the braided cable, but it is only braided up to the point where it splits, which is odd. The controller buttons are very rattle-y which doesn't bode well for their longevity. My biggest complaint is that the sound is good but I have to put the volume MUCH higher than normal on my phone to hear the music. The noise canceling is ok. I commute on a bus (rather noisy) and a train (moderately noisy) and these don't dampen the outside sound nearly as much as I would like. Better ear pieces would help a lot.

They are inexpensive, have good sound and are worth it. If you are looking for higher quality you need to spend more.

title: Good replacement earpads
review: The pads on my old Logitech headset in the H390 family disintegrated.  I was going to buy a new one when I found these.  They fit perfectly.  They are comfy and lightweight  like the originals.

title: Comfortable in-ear headphones for small ears
review: I love these headphones.  Mine died after daily use for two years and I picked up several pairs since they have been discontinued because they are some of the only headphones that don't hurt my ears.  They have oval earpieces under the coverings (comes with a large and small set) which fit in my very small ears.

title: Impressive clarity and power!
review: PLEASE start listening at a lower volume than you normally would on the average/good headphones you probably bought these as a step up from. The mid range and higher trebles on this set of headphones are crystal clear and will hurt your ears if you are used to listening to music on lower quality cans. I found my ears hurting from the powerful and clear mids and trebles after a half hour and have adjusted to listening at a lower volume which works perfectly because this set of Grado's have flawless sound throughout the audible range. This is only a first impression review, it does not speak to durability.

title: High quality with flexible mounting options
review: I love this bracket. Very sturdy, all metal construction. Looks great in m office and holds my headphones around the corner of my desk without issue.

title: I really wanted to love this dock, but that's not possible
review:
One port to rule them all sounded amazing until I used this thing in practice. I started with OWC's previous model (the 12-port Thunderbolt 3 dock) before returning it for this newer model. I have it connected to my 15" 2018 MBP with Radeon Pro 560X. I have it connected to two 4k Dell monitors.

Most of the time, the monitors work great, but at least once per day, one will flicker off and on -- usually when I'm right in the middle of something important. Occasionally, they'll both completely go on the fritz (static and colors explosions), and the only solution is to disconnect the dock and reconnect it.

The audio port is also abysmal. It causes me more grief than anything. The sound output is often decent, but the line-in from my headset's microphone (Sennheiser) is terrible. It's often faint, even if my input gain is maxed out. I've since switched to the audio jack built into the MBP. That works better and is more reliable, but it somewhat defeats the purpose of having a dock at my desk.

title: I have a new-found love for so many songs now that I can actually ...
review: The sound quality is phenomenal. I have a new-found love for so many songs now that I can actually hear everything. I generally can't wear headphones for extended periods, but these are the most comfortable I've worn. Still gets warm after a while, but i can wear them for an hour or two without issue.

title: Sound fine.  No pause/play controls. pricey return.
review: they were fine sounding earbuds but i needed the pause/play function. return cost 1/3 of the purchase.

title: Best value and great fit
review: I bought these as I've had some more expensive headphones that I've lost, broken and just generally trashed.  For the money, I've never had a better pair of earbuds and at this price, you can buy a few of them.

title: Reception issues.
review: The headphones are comfortable and fit my ears well. However, I am not able to get steady reception if I place my cell phone into a bag or a pocket. I have to hold the phone in my hand to have steady reception when I walk. I don't know if my particular unit is defective or if there is a design flaw. However, it does fit my needs, so I am not planning to exchange. My phone is also a BLU G91 MAX, so these earphones should not have any problems with my phone, but they do. I cannot recommend these for anyone who wants to listen to music or radio on the move.

title: Solid improvement over HD 280 Pro Headphones
review: My former at desk pair of headphones was the HD 280 Pro, these are in a few words a solid improvement on everything the HD 280's do well. Noise isolation improved, sound quality improved, comfort and fit - huge improvement here. The new design takes a few days to get used to but once you do the comfort for all day wear is greatly improved. Overall buy these if you need an awesome set of headphones that keep noise out and your music your music.

title: Totally blown away
review:
I am totally blown by the quality for the price.

Purchased during a lightning deal on a whim because I wanted a truly "in ear" headset. These fit very comfortably with the stock tips. They cut the external noise and battery holds very well even with heavier usage.

Connection both to my phone and to each other is seamless.

The sound is amazing to me. All my songs are crisp and clear. Treble and bass are excellent. I listen to mostly rock music, but I found them good when listening to bass heavy rap songs also. Call quality has been great considering the waterproof rating. I make most of my calls at home. I find it works better when I have both in.

Overall I am definitely happy about this purchase and I definitely recommend buying this product for someone looking for in ear IPX7 waterproof headphones.

title: decent for the price
review: was looking for a cheap pair of over-ear headphones and these seem to be ok so far.  compared to others I've used, these seem significantly larger in diameter, and are more circular than oval-shaped (not a tight fit over my somewhat large ears).  The cable hangs from the left side, so you don't end up with the ever-twisting Y-shaped cable at the chest/neck.  I didn't notice any major difference in EQ, etc., though I mainly use these with an old I-pod to block background noise at work (not using these for pro studio monitoring, etc.)

title: Excellent, but so boomy it gives me a headache
review:
To keep things brief:
- *Everything* is done through a fairly decent mobile app. I'm fine with this, especially since it makes some things very simple (e.g. switching between multiple devices).
- Bluetooth connectivity is stellar. Latency is invisible (FAR better than anything I've tried except the competitive Bose headsets), switching is very quick (like 1s), no stuttering or issues whatsoever.
- It's a little sad / surprising that LDAC isn't supported when using multiple connections... but meh. AAC still sounds great.
- Noice cancelling is absolutely top-notch and incredible. But you already know this.
- EQ is.......... bad. Plain and simple. There's no nicer way to describe it. There are worse EQs out there! But this is well below average.

But.

BUT.

HOLY COW is this "boomy". So much so that it gives me a headache after about an hour at my normal relatively-low listening volume, even without noise-canceling. The Bose QC 35 ii are better at this, and I feel like the 1000XM3 were better too. You can turn the "clear bass" literally ALL THE WAY DOWN and it stops booming, but then it's clearly imbalanced.

Returned. Still looking for a bluetooth headset that doesn't have ridiculous issues. Maybe a firmware update of the Aonic 50 will fix their connectivity issues and improve noise canceling, because those sound absolutely *phenomenal* by comparison.

title: Large but good
review: Slightly larger than would be convenient for my earbud case, but sturdy and smooth volume adjustment (no static!).  Serves its purpose.

title: Good build quality, but I very much prefer the hard one.
review:
The inner pouch is convenient, and there's a bit of padding... but I think I prefer the hard case. This is noticeably larger while having noticeably less room, and they squash the pads on the earbuds just sitting out there on its own, much less when tossed in a backpack.

Still, functional. I'll just stick to the hard ones from now on.

-- edit after using it longer:
Yep, I'm going back to hard. The case has held up flawlessly (absolutely no complaints about the build quality), but it's just too big with zero benefits over a small hard case. I got an LTGEM thing recently, far far happier with it already.

title: Two dead microphones, sticky controls
review:
I like almost everything about these better than the stock cables... But the microphone has died (super super quiet) on both pairs I've owned in months (I'm extremely gentle), and both controls "stick" - press a volume button, and it races to max/min and keeps "pressing" repeatedly so you can't correct it.

And, since it still *has* a microphone, it takes over my phone's and I can't use them at all for calls.

v2 I'll be happy to try, but these seem fundamentally flawed. If I can find a way to *fully* break the microphones these will be nicer headphone cables, but they're a periodic pain until then.

title: Fantastic headphones
review: Easily the best headphones I've ever owned.  I'm not an audiophile so these are about as expensive as I'd be willing to pay for headphones, but I'm glad I did.  They sound great and feel amazingly comfortable, even to the point that I sometimes forget I'm wearing them.

title: this is still my favorite headset I've ever used
review: After around 6 years or more of using this headset, this is still my favorite headset I've ever used.  They fit so comfortably on your head and around your ears.  The padding is nice and soft and cushiony and the sound quality is great.  I busted my last pair by tripping over the wire and immediately went and bought a new pair because I loved them so much.

title: Great Soundstage and balance. No EQ needed.
review:
Oh these are great. Some online reviews prompted me to give these a try. As with any I'm, the Silicon tips that are included do not work well. Get some foam tips (Comply brand or make some out of earplugs) and they sound 400x better.

Treble is crisp. Bass is detailed and not overwhelming (get VSD1 if you want more bass). With EQ you can crank the bass if you want, but stock I think the levels are nice. Soundstage! These are comparable to a pair of on-ear semi-open headphones that I have. Instruments sound like they're over there - - - > and over there - - > instead of all right in your ears.

title: then these are great. They did take me some time to get ...
review: The sound is what I would expect in this price range.  If you are a sound aficionado, these will not do.  If you are simply looking for everyday headphones, then these are great.  They did take me some time to get use to, although that is simply because I wasnt use to in-ear headphones.  They performed as well as I would expect for this price range, and also helped to block outside noise.

title: These buds had High marks, so I go them ...
review: These buds had High marks, so I go them for my daughter. They didn't last too long. The silicon ear pieces fell off constantly and eventually the earbud itself detached from the wire.

title: Impressed
review: I'm blown away by how well these sound.  I was looking at Beats X and the Bose wireless earbuds but at $100 to $150 I was hesitant especially since I'd just spent $120 on a pair of Pugz that died after 13 months.  After looking at other options on Amazon and finding these I was pretty taken with all the positive reviews so I decided to spend the $39 and take a chance and boy am I glad I did.  They are packaged extremely nicely, and seem to be well made. They paired quickly and easily with my iPhone but then when I heard the sound they were better than anything else I've ever had, wired or wireless.  They certainly sound as good to me as my wireless Beats Solo headphones which I think are pretty awesome.  So thanks to all you prior reviewers for steering me well.

title: Best headset for under $25
review: The Microsoft LifeChat LX-3000 Headset is an outstanding headset for under $25.  Because so much is right, and there is nothing I could find that I don't like (I even like the fact that the cord is extra long) that I think the purchase is a 'no-brainer' (in the best sense).  Controversial as Microsoft software may be, I generally have found their hardware (which is OEMed) to be first rate, and often best in class.

title: Great all in one turntable
review: My sone loves this turntable.  He has a small apartment and a music room/office. He can’t turn up the volume, so this is a perfect solution. It drives his bookshelf speakers and headphones.  He’s a musician who still jams with his friends.  He has a few vinyl records and this was a perfect solution.

title: Great sound, extremely comfortable
review:
Despite the size these are incredible light headphones. They put almost no pressure on your ears or head -- you'll barely notice that you have them on.

Sound quality is quite good for the price -- punchy, clear, and present. The sounds is as good as headphones that are three times as expense.

One thing to note: these are not over ear headphones. While the ear pads are large they do not cover your ears, blocking out ambient sounds.

title: Flawed for phone use, overpriced for music
review:
I have been using Sennheiser headphones for 15 years; this is the first time this usually outstanding company has faltered.

In-ear headphones simply do not work for phone calls. They block so much outside sound that you cannot hear yourself speaking. It's simply awkward to have a conversation with someone where you cannot hear your own voice. It leaves you wondering if you're talking too loud or too quietly.

What's particularly baffling is that earbuds do not have volume control. If you have to reach for your phone to adjust the volume, that pretty much defeats the purpose of "hands free." The only control you have is answer/hang up, which also functions as play/stop.

Sound quality is reasonably good for earbuds without the problems that often affect buds, such as shrill highs and boomy bass. But I don't think the quality is any better than Sennheiser's lesser priced earbuds.

I cannot recommend this product. It simply doesn't work well for phone calls, lacks volume control, and the sound is no better than cheaper priced Sennheiser earbuds.

title: Not too bad
review:
The best thing I can say about Jabra headset is that people on the other end of a call cannot tell that I'm using a Bluetooth headset. The fidelity of my voice is no different than if I was talking into my iPhone.

As for the sound quality on my end, it's a bit constricted and there is a noticeable drop in fidelity. I'm guessing that this has more to do with the bluetooth bandwidth than the quality of the headset's ear-bud. It's still perfectly useable, buy be aware the sound is simply not has good as the hands free headphones/mic that come with the iPhone.

My biggest gripe is that it the volume control on the headset is hard to get at when it's in your ear, and when fumbling for it, it's very easy to accidentally hangup on someone.

Overall, the performance is about what I'd expect from a mid-range headset.

title: Good travel product
review:
My expectations were pretty low for these speakers. Small cheap speakers tend to sound small and cheap. Often the sound they produce is unlistenable due to the highs being painfully bright, there being no mid-range and/or the bass being boomy. The Diamonds do not have any of these extreme traits.

I've primarily used the speakers for listening to audio books, podcasts and streaming radio on my iPhone/iPod/laptop in hotel rooms when traveling. The speakers do a pretty good job with the spoken voice. With music the results are not as good, and I rather just use my Sennheiser headphones to obtain much more accurate sound reproduction. The output sound can be impressively loud without distortions for such a small device. When used outside, though, you need to be within several feet of the speakers to hear them over ambient sounds.

The advertised (rechargeable) battery life is six hours; I've gotten more playing time out of them.

The clever design of these speakers also needs to be mentioned. All the wires retract into the speakers like a vacuum cleaner.

If you're looking to buy travel speakers for similar applications as mine, I have no hesitation in recommending the Diamond Mini Rockers. They're small, cheap and do a good job.

title: Why is it that only Sennheiser knows how to make headphones?
review:
After allowing for a two week burn in period, testing the headphones on my iPod, CD player and SACD player, the sound on these earbuds remained shrill, muddy, with little mid-mid range and too much bass. My $15 Sennheiser earbuds produce a warmer, cleaner sound.

Over the two week period, I was also never able to get the buds to stay in my ears. When walking, and especially running, they would frequently fall out.

As a long time owner of many Sennheiser headphones, Sennheiser simply makes a better product, if not the best headphones.

title: Disappointed
review: I was excited for these headphones when they first got to my house. I opened up the box and took them out and immediately turned them on. When I started playing music on them I realized it was only coming out of the left ear. So I figured maybe it just needs to be charged. I charged them and turned them back on to find out that the right ear was still not playing anything. Disappointed that from right out of the box these headphones were broken.

title: Great headphones, except they turn on randomly all the ...
review: Great headphones, except they turn on randomly all the time since it's just a press of a button and then when you want to use them they are dead.

title: Would have been good if both earbuds worked
review: I've had a few different sets of earbuds, I tried the Sabbat e12's and although sounded good and had decent features, was ultimately disappointed with the fit and feel being overly cheep. With getting a new Samsung Note 10 I was hoping the Galaxy Buds would give me a more premium feel and comfort. Initial impressions are the case and buds themselves have a great feel and fitment, but for some reason can't even get what 30$ dollar earbuds can achieve, actually working. From the reviews I've seen with a new samsung phone you should be able just to open the case and it should display the buds on the phone like the airpods do, no such thing ever happened for me. After pairing manually and downloading the wear app you are prompted to download another app through it for the buds. They setup and recognized fine, except the right earbud was DOA. I tried multiple times to do their "restart" which is just putting them in the case for 7 secs then pulling them out, charging them fully. Nothing worked, and looking at the forums and reddit this is a known issue and no solution other than return them for a new set. For 120$ you had your chance Samsung, I'll stick with my 30$ Haylou's that actually work and have a true reset method.

title: No active noise cancelling, it's only for the microphone/calls
review:
After looking at review and wanting to upgrade from my current Haylou GTR1s I settled for the Sabbat's. eBay had them for 50$ but had no mention of the active noise cancelling as mentioned here, so I took a gamble. First off the sound is great, basically a level above the Haylou's. I have had airpods before and they are clear but lacked bass due to no noise isolation. But these have no active noise cancelling other than for the mic or on calls, they need to fix the ad and specify that outright. Otherwise these are a great set of earbuds for the money.

Cons:
Lid / hinge feels flimsy and cheap
Earbuds look cheap when compared to the Haylou's or other sleeker options
False/Misleading advertising on the active noise cancelling

Pros:
USB C
Wireless charging
The sound is amazing
Battery time
Plenty of silicone tips
Ear fitment

title: Recommended
review:
Great sound. Strangely, I have difficulty pairing it with my iPhone to use the bluetooth feature. It takes a few tries. I don't understand why; I have two pair of the Sennheiser MM 100 bluetooth headphones and they pair easily. Otherwise they have great sound. This is my first pair of noise canceling headphones and I'm finding that feature quite useful.

As some other reviewers mentioned, the loudest setting is still not super loud, just barely loud enough for me. I wish there was a way to increase the volume a bit more.

title: Great Product
review: This was for my son, I refuse to buy expensive headphones because they always get broken or lost.  My son said these sound better than most economically priced headphones (under $10).

title: Gain train with these bad boyzz
review: It is so nice when you lay back on a bench and get ready to destroy 225 lbs and not have to worry about your cellphone falling out of your pocket and tugging the cord to your headphones out of your ears and you immediately get pissed. These are very high quality are a very reputable company. I would buy these again and again but I don't have to because they are very durable.

title: Beats are awesome
review: bought for my wife.  Great pair she likes the color and so far so good they keep working just great.  A lot of bass but not too much.  I have a pair of bose and I really like these.  She think they look good and I have to agree too.  Great headphones!

title: good battery life for bluetooth
review: these headphones really are great.  they synced up with no problem and were really comfy.  I havnt not taken them on a run or done any crazy outdoor stuff yet but they feel good in my ear and they sound good.  good battery life too

title: Great for my bose ae2i over ear head[hones
review: great replacement for my bose AE2i headphones.  click in and work just fine.  I would give these a shot

title: plush and great
review: really cushy for my vmoda headphones, great upgrade a must if you have the mvodas

title: Excellent quality to price point ratio!
review:
Very well made and sturdy, tight connection, excellent product esp. considering how inexpensive it is. Gotta go my headphones are calling!
Thanks.

title: Perfect for 7506
review:
Perfect fit and pretty much identical to the stock (but very worn) pads on my 15+ year old 7506 headphones.

Installation took maybe 45 seconds per side. Not sure why people say it's difficult? Just requires a bit of tugging to pull into place.

Soft and comfortable. I'll grab another when these go. Maybe I'll treat myself and use this pair for only 10 years!

title: One Hour In -- Amazing
review:
You can take this review with a few grains of salt because I've only had the box open for one hour, but I already felt compelled to share my feelings:

A) Got a seal immediately and with absolutely no problem, using the tips that the earphones ship with (silicone). I haven't even tried the Comply tips yet -- I'm sure they'll give an even better seal.

B) Earphones pop out of your ears? Happened to me, too, for the first two minutes. Then I took a moment to read the manual. Wondering why the cable is stiff at the end? These aren't designed to be worn "down" like normal buds. Wrap the cable up and over your ear, and they won't move, no matter how hard you jostle your head.

C) Build quality: I can already see a small kink near the stiff part of the cable, so I already know where it will fail. But one of the reasons I bought these is the fact that the cables are replaceable, so I have no serious worries in this regard, unless the cables fail really, really quickly (new ones aren't exactly cheap).

D) Most importantly, sound quality: Awesome, awesome, awesome. I usually break in new earbuds for a couple of days, but in this case there is no need. Straight out of the box they're just exceptional. Crisp highs, deep bass that's not at all muddy, totally clear mids. I'm very much looking forward to hearing them change over the coming days as I break them in.

All in all, an easy 5/5 despite the obvious cable issue.

title: Terrible
review:
These headphones, for me, are incredibly uncomfortable. It takes me more than one try to get them to "clip" on properly, and if I'm doing anything even slightly physically active they tend to fall out of place.
There is absolutely no sound isolation either way... so I can hear everything around me, and everyone around me can hear what I'm listening to.
Finally, after about three weeks of not-so-heavy use (30 minutes/day, maybe), they started buzzing every time I pumped somewhat heavy bass through them. And by the way, the bass wasn't so good to begin with. For headphones supposedly "designed for the house and trance fan," these are a huge disappointment.

title: Works mostly as expected but with silly issues.
review: The headphones work well and replace an older set. The internal battery is a positive step and battery life is good. Noise cancellation is only marginally better than the old version. The 3 settings is useful but only functions with Bluetooth connection. A cable connection does not allow the same flexibility which makes little sense. I find the cable connection to be quite sensitive requiring care connection at the headphone socket. The biggest problem is the BT app on an iPhone at least. Connectivity to the app is easily lost forcing an on/off routine to connect but even that often does not work and a new pairing is required. It’s annoying.

title: Great sound quality and comfort!
review: I really don't think you can beat the sound quality and comfort that you get from these headphones for the price. Absolutely outstanding. I primarily use these at my desktop computer for movies, tv, games, and music. Absolutely great comfort and sound quality.

title: Good headphones for a workout.
review: Got this for exercise for myself and these do the trick! Great sound, and sweat proof. Would not suggest these to someone who wants to listen to music and just sit around, while the sound quality is good, it is not great and there are better headphones which aren't sweatproof for this price. But this is exactly what I needed.

title: Good sound quality for active people!
review: I got these headphones for my fianceé for our gym time and she loves them. They are a perfect for her ears, very comfortable, and she loves how they sound. Great for active people who want good sound quality.

title: Replacement Batteries Not Available
review:
I love these headphones!

However, Li-IOn batteries last 3-5 years. When the batteries need to be replaced, Avantree does not sell replacements: making all of the wireless headphones throwaways. Not the way I like to live.

title: these are perfect. Price is right
review: Second pair of these headphones I've owned--for those of us who can't wear in-ear buds and don't want something huge to wear when out and about, these are perfect.  Price is right, and the sound is gorgeous!

title: So happy to find an inline mic for Audio Technica m40x
review: Looked everywhere for an inline mic to use with my ATH m40x headphones.  I had been planning to use a standard inline cable until I realized the Audio Technica headphones use a non-standard connector between the cable and headphone.  I was almost going to bust out the soldering iron to make a cable like this and then I found this one.  The listening sound quality is indistinguishable from the normal cable.  The mic quality could be better (it is quiet, distant and thin), but it should be fine for gaming on PC and calls on android.  The mic is comparable to other inline microphones--I wasn't expecting better.  The pause and volume buttons work fine on android.  My cable was marked android, so there may be an iphone compatible cable out there.  Note the TRRS pinout for android and iphone are different.  I'll report back if there are any durability issues.

title: Good price, not comfortable.
review: Great price, but smaller and less comfortable ear cups than most over the ear headphones. Can only wear for an hour before needing a break.

title: 1 Star Headset, 5 Stars for Amazon
review:
I purchased this headset for the home office. It worked well at first, but within the first week it was very staticy like I've read in other reviews. I'm usually pretty gentle with electronics, but maybe it was the way I stored the cord by wrapping it around the ear and support pieces on either side of the headset. If that's the case it's very touchy since I wrapped it loosely. That being said, Amazon refunded my money without me having to send the headset back. I tossed the headset in the electronic recycling bin. My company purchased a Plantronics MX500i 3-in-1 Headset (also sold at Amazon) and it works great. It works well with the home office analog phone and VoIP software phone. I also use this when I travel so it stands up to not so ideal storage in my backpack.

Since there's so many positive reviews for this headset, I'd recommend trying it out because you may get a good one. If it doesn't work, try the Plantronics headset mentioned above.

title: Great earbuds
review:
Edit 8/7/19

I recently bought the blue version of the headphones, and after just a few months of light use at work the headphoens are no longer working properly. The sound has started to cut in and out. I'm really disappointed with the quality of this pair.

I bought this to replace the standard earphones that come with the iphone. I really like these buds since it does a better job of muffling outside noise, and provides decent bass. Would recommend.

title: Doesn't provide as good of protection as the case made by Chord
review: Doesn't provide as good of protection as the case made by Chord. First of all, the side where you plug the headphones in is completely unprotected. The kickstand is setup completely wrong-- if you use it, you can't have headphones plugged in (even if you had a 90 degree adaptor to use with it). Also, this case will not allow you to plug in the micro usb fully. The only thing I can say that I do like about it is that it fits the mojo very snugly, other than that I would spend the extra $30 and buy the case made from Chord.

title: Good, but just not for me.
review: I got these for $50 when amazon had them on sale the other day, for 50 you will be hard pressed to find a better pair of iem's. The reason I returned them though is because I was getting alot of static in the cord when moving around, and the bass just wasn't enough for me. I'm no bass head but I really enjoying hearing a good little thump when it's supposed to be there. If your looking for a great pair of headphone that do provide clean sound these will suffice.

title: Top notch for what your paying
review: Excellent headphones at this price point, I was very pleased with the sound quality coming from such a cheap headphone.

title: Best Dac On the Market At This Price Point Without A Doubt
review: There's to much to say about this little thing, I am currently using it with my denon ah-2000 headphones and this thing just makes them sound awesome. Once you start listening to this thing with some high quality cd rips you'll never go back to just normal audio. It doesn't matter what i plug into this dac it will improve the sound quality on anything you throw at it. I dont think there's anything that competes from 100 to 250, once you hit the 250 mark though there are some other options but not many.

title: Work Great
review: Excellent Desktop microphone highly recommend if you don't wanna use a headset. Has decent quality and noise cancelling.

title: If you need a place to hang your headphones then this the product you want
review: Wow what a great product! I love purchasing something with no BS, you get exactly what is advertised. The product was extremely easy to install and the function is excellent. It feels very sturdy and holds my rather large headphones with ease. My main concern was that it would be hard to find the hooks under my desk but it's no trouble at all. Love this, can't recommend it enough.

title: Does not fit
review: I bought these because they came highly recommended for exercising, but they do not stay in place. I have tried them several times and have been more annoyed with them than with any other headphone. During my runs, I have to constantly put them back in my ears because they do not stay in place.

title: Works fine, but latency issues are a deal-breaker, alas.
review: Very small unit. Paired easily with my BT headphones and worked well. The issue was latency. Sound was pretty good, but when I spoke during video conferencing, I was hearing an echo of myself. When others spoke, the sound didn't sync properly with the video. I know this is an issue with BT devices, and maybe I just can't use them for video calls at all. Will have to research further. I was trying to get away from being wired to my station and also from having to wear obvious and bulky headphones during chats, preferring smaller BT earbuds. Thanks. -- ffg

title: Ear Loop Problem.
review:
I used a few of these until each died, replacing it with the next one. Usually what went wrong was that the ear loop fatigued and failed. Logitech is a great company, and they would replace the whole unit, which was nice, but the ear loop would then fail after six months or so.

Electronically, the headset seemed to work pretty well. I would say that it has a practical life of about a year. The battery, after that, finally gave out and would not hold a full charge. I used the headset a lot, pairing it with a Motorola V551 phone.

The windstop technology does work. This model is discontinued, replaced by the Mobile Traveller, which is very similar in function, and also has an ear loop fatigue problem, though if you are very careful, you can avoid this.

Not the sexiest looking headset. But, hey, I'm a geek, anyway.

I wish Logitech would release an improved version of this series. They are a very reasonable company to deal with.

Hope this is helpful for you. By the way, I never paid more than $30 for one of these.

title: Good kids headphones, great customer service
review:
We purchased two of these headphones in 2017. Both worked great until earlier this year when one of them stopped producing sound in the left ear. After contacting lilgadgets they are sending us a replacement. I am very satisfied with the product and customer service received.

Only complaint for the headphones is that they don't go a little louder - on airplanes it can be an issue.

title: I love them. Great for clean clear audio in the ...
review: My second set of these in 15 years. I love them. Great for clean clear audio in the studio. I've made the mistake of wearing these out and sweating up a storm, but that's my own fault - these headphones are studio all the way.

title: Neat!
review: The price was amazing for these headphones.  I'm a marathoner so I'm hard on my gear, and these are awesome.  They come with several silicon cushions so you can fit them just right to your...ear hole?  Anyway, the color is bright and cheerful and the sound quality is very good.

title: Stella
review: I'm Listening to Tubular Bells 50th Anniversary. I am running a Topping A30 on Medium gain just over halfway. It took me a while to find the right tips to carry bass. Maybe they are breaking in too. It's great. Nice details, great tonality, soundstage is outside of my head not around my nose. I was listening to metal and other headphones these are different. Not as forward with bass but it's not lacking or slowing down the driver. I turned the Loki EQ off. I like EQ everything responds a little differently to EQ. These take it with a gentle shift. Very refined. Sometimes when being analytical we miss the big picture. Focusing on faults and miss the nice layering and soundstage these have. Dynamics are good. Attack is excellent, Slam is not standing out as missing. I listen very loud they are holding together.

title: Nice
review: Wanted to try an IEM with my Topping G5. These had great reviews. Build is great. Cables have a nice connection. I was concerned about not having a balanced 4.4 but they are easy to drive. Bass is strong but not super low or punchy or tight. Bass is ok. Mids and highs are smooth but not super detailed. Nice not great. I almost wonder if the tuning is to make them easier to listen to over a long period of time. I base my review on what I am use to hearing on other headphones and another pair of IEM’s I got. Fun well built easy to listen to. Satisfying bass. Relaxed mids and highs. Sound stage is ok. Wish they were a little tighter and a little more detailed to be a preferred pair.

title: I was skeptical based on price but they were really good and my daughter loves them
review: These work very well. I was skeptical based on price but they were really good and my daughter loves them. Great value for blue tooth and kids headphones.

title: Comfortable, Isolating and Perfect Fit.
review:
I bought these for my AudioTechnica ATH-M50s headphones. The original pads were about 5 years old and starting to crack and become very stiff and uncomfortable. I also have a pair of relatively new ATH-M50x headphones at the office. I bought these pads to replace the ATH-M50s pads. The fit was perfect. I did a comparison between the old pads, new stock ATH-M50x pads and the Wicket Cushions pads. Obviously compared to the 5 year old pads the replacements were miles better. What I was more skeptical of was if they'd be more comfortable than the stock new pads. Still, even compared to these, the replacement pads from Wicked Cushions were significantly more comfortable. In addition they are softer and as a result more comfortable for extended wear and form around the contours of your head better than the stock pads blocking out more outside noise. For me this is great because I work in an open layout office and use these headphones on airplanes when traveling to reduce cabin noise. I also noticed a reasonable boost in low end response from the better seal.

I would highly recommend these replacement pads to anyone looking to replace old worn out pads or anyone looking to get a little bit better sound isolation from their existing AudioTechnica headphones. I liked these so much over the stock pads that I'll be replacing my still relatively stock new ATH-M50x pads with these.

title: Terrible Sound
review:
I'm not sure how this speaker has such stellar ratings, it sounds pretty awful. I understand that in the sub-$100 soundbar market, expectations should be tempered, but this thing sounds like airplane headphones. The sound that comes out is tinny and completely without depth. No bass whatsoever. I didn't expect much since these are 10W speakers, but there's nothing here to speak of. The volume control is also very poor. The difference between levels of volume is quite large, so it doesn't leave much room for fine volume control.

"Impressive sound for both movies game and music," nope don't have that.
"Enjoy immersive, cinematic audio and virtual surround sound in your living room," 100% don't have this.
"you can feel the best sounds from AKIXNO sound bar," you definitely can't.

With the sound quality this speaker produces, there's absolutely no reason not to spend $25 less and just get a $30 bar. Nice form factor, but definitely not worth the money.

title: ... volume but on higher end mp3 players/ipods they sounded great. I also love the flat cord
review: These headphones are a bit hard to drive with my phone at full volume but on higher end mp3 players/ipods they sounded great. I also love the flat cord. Packaging and everything else was above par. Reason for 4 stars is that I wouldn't have paid full price for these.

title: Three Stars
review: Not as great as previous Sennheiser headphones I have bought in this price range.

title: Complete Junk
review: 3.5 mm jack is staticy no matter what you do. The issue is both with wired headphones and with my car audio jack. It constantly statics and pops and has sound drops. Absolute piece of junk. Charging is also painfully slow.

title: Great Case for Cloud Alpha
review:
I really like this case (since I was previously carrying my headset in the original package). I travel weekly and I needed something smaller than the original package to fit comfortably in my backpack for flights.

Pros: Sturdy and easily fit the cable bag inside; I don't worry about damage to the headset at all
Only Con: Very tight fit for cable bag with the headset; which isn't a bad thing really

title: Still my favorite bluetooth device, in spite of a few small things
review:
Sleek, pretty easy to set up and use, excellent sound quality, and a sleek and compact form factor.

The "small things" have to do with how easy it is to accidentally flip forward and back a track (or 3), especially when your stash it in you pocket between uses and forget to power it down. That's most annoying with audiobooks.

Still, I like the sound, the versatility, the seamless switching between sources, and the good fit with the iPhone.

One thing... I much prefer the model listed above, which is a Sony MW600, not the Sony Ericsson MW600. Sellers arbitrarily substitute the latter, which they think of as substantially similar. And for most purposes it is. But the Sony has larger characters on its display, and it has earbuds that I like more - for fit and for style. Note that the Sony only appears to be available in black, while the Sony Ericsson is available in black and in white.

title: Cool looking, good functionality, but awkward and not great with iPhone
review:
I really wanted to like this item. It looks cool, it has the basic functionality that the MW600 has - multiple bluetooth targets, an FM radio (for, e.g., listening to NPR), and good controls (I like the volume control better than the unreliable volume control on the MW600). And the sound quality is great.

But the SBH50 is quirky, limited, and doesn't have great battery life. Quirky in that you can switch between radio and a "preferred" bluetooth device, but to switch among devices, you have to navigate through some setup menus (on the MW600, you can set up at least 3 devices - I have an iPod, and iPhone, and a MacBook set up - and it's easy to switch among them). I get approx 1/2 the battery life between charges, and the push-button on the front does not prompt Siri (more importantly, does not appear to prompt voice dialing).

Also, there's a good bit of functionality that's not accessible because the s/w and update capabilities do not work on Macs.

One more thing... If you order the white (for summer styling) be prepared to get the white earbuds with the black unit. The MW600 Sony-Ericsson is all white or all black.

I would have bought another, but can't get past these issues.

title: Solid headphones for the money.
review: These headphones seem to be well made, and my son liked them. The storage bag is useful, and I found the cord to be well made as well. Certainly better than just a wire one. The only thing I found a bit annoying is that the receivers on the headphones aren't labeled. So it's easy to plug the wire into the wrong port, which results in no sound. It's not a hard thing to figure out, but when you're wrestling to small children it can be easy to plug in the wrong port. A simple label or symbol indicating which one is for linking to the device and which one is for attaching additional headphones would go a long way.

title: Not for iPhone 7 Earbuds!
review: Does not work with the new earbuds that com with the iPhone 7.  (The ones that have a lightning plug instead of a 3.5mm plug.)  The lightning plug is too fat to fit through the tiny rubber holes.

title: Yup, these break because of bad design and if you're out of warranty, Bose won't stand behind them.
review: There are three types of reviews here: 1.) The folks who correctly note that they aren't the best sounding headphones for $200 and give them 2, 3, or 4 stars. 2.) The people who give them 5 stars because they're good at noise cancelling. 3.) Those same people after the headphones have failed and they've been jerked around by Bose, who give them 1 star. And that tells the story.

title: Works great.
review: I use it for my iPad, headphones and earbuds tucked into the zippered pouch. The lightest and most practical solution. Don't expect years and years of durability though. It's only rubber, but it does hold up for a reasonable and expected time. Buy two, they're cheap enough! Works great.

title: Audiophile headphones for cheap
review: Sennheiser PX 100-ii is arguably one of the best sounding headphones and best value on the market. This is the second pair I've purchased, to replace my aging PX 100 which are looking kind of shabby after 5 years and being stepped on a few times ;-). Lightweight, comfortable and superb sound. The fold up design makes them easy to tote around.  I use them in the house, at the gym---everywhere. I also have Sennheiser ear buds; also great sound but sometimes I prefer headphones resting gently on my ears instead of stuck in them. You can usually get them for around $50. Comes in black or white. [[ASIN:B002VPDOH8 Sennheiser PX 100-II Supra-Aural Mini Headphones - Black]]

title: Replacement for Focal Elegia
review: My one year old Focal Elegia headphones started having problems with the left earphone and I determined that it was that wire that was on the fritz. No problem, I hated that wire anyways. Started shopping and quickly realized a replacement would in the hundreds and more. So I was quite happy to find this replacement after a bit of research online. Did some comparisons with my original cable and quite frankly, I can't tell the difference. Highly recommend this product, at least as a replacement for the Elegia. Had I known about these before, I probably would have switched them earlier cause that OEM Focal cable is terrible. I will update this review if something changes at anytime.

title: Works as intended
review: Got this so that I could have a little more range for my headphones when I am listening to records. So this is hooked up to a Yamaha 303 receiver to my Focal Elegia headphones. Works great as I had hoped. Sound is not as great as when I hook up the headphones directly, but I wasn't expecting this cable to be as good, so that is not a problem for me. All I wanted was more length when I need it and this does exactly that.

title: Works as Expected!
review:
UPDATE - After 14 months of use, I have to admit that these never came off the wall. The reason for this update, however, is that that is a double edged sword. I recently moved out of the apartment where these were installed. DO NOT install these on the wall! These will rip the outer layer of the wall right off. I tried heating the plastic, I tried removing it gently, I tried everything and nothing worked! If you intend to move these or if you live in an apartment I suggest that either 1) you install these with 3M removable strips instead of the provided sticker or 2) look elsewhere.

These little things are really quite impressive in terms of quality. I use these for two pairs of headphones (package comes with two stands) - a pair of Sony Sony WH-1000XM2 and a pair of Ultrasone 900 Pros. Have had these headphones on the stands for a couple of days now with no problems whatsoever. They look great, too! Plenty of room to hold the cable as well. Would not hesitate to recommend these.

title: Sound cuts out at a modest volume. Thinking about returning.
review:
=== UPDATE: 2019/07/02 ====
The issue with the volume cutting out seems to have gone away.
If it stays gone, I may add a star.

====== Original Review ======
I'm mainly using this so I can use my Bluetooth headphones to listen to my TV. I'm also going to use it to enable my phone to play over my stereo.

My main concern is that the sound cuts out when the source volume is moderate, and there is no sound for a few fractions of a second. When this happens, the background hiss abruptly clicks silent, then when the sound starts up again, it clucks on, but it misses the first bit!

So the first part of words, or sometimes the entire word itself, gets lost!

This is very disconcerting when it happens! Both when the audio cuts off, AND when it starts back up again!

I can a avoid this by cranking up my TV's volume all the way, and turning down the volume on my headphones, but this is NO solution, because it wouldn't work for an Audio Out! I'd just be stuck with it!

Is this some kind of power saving device, for the transmitter and headphones? (I imagine that sending no signal causes both devices to use less power.)

Or maybe some failed attempt at noise reduction?

Thinking about returning it, for this reason, and because I cannot hook it up to send Bluetooth Audio to my phone.

title: Works well - Battery life is a bit short
review:
It works very well as a receiver for my Apple Watch either with headphones or powered speakers. No connectivity problems at all, and the sound quality is very good for a Bluetooth connection. I'd say it's roughly the equivalent of a good FM signal or a mid quality MP3.

I use it plugged to a power supply, as my headphones (Beyerdynamic 880, 250 Ohm model) are very power hungry and I get at most 3 hours out of the battery. Consumer oriented headphones or buds would likely get much better battery life.

title: Good, But Too Flexible.
review: While it’s easily installed (be sure to allow 24 hrs for the supplied adhesive to “set’), and the use is obvious, the flexibility of the vertical column means that the weight of my headphones - Beyerynamic 880 pro’s at 10.6 oz - pulls down on one hook till the other almost touches the table under which it’s affixed.  That makes putting the looped cable or a second headphone on the other hook a two hand operation.  Were I to buy again, I think I’d go with a metal version.

title: Works well.
review: Great  price on a recently discontinued product. I use it with an available single sided headphone accessory.

title: Left earbud discharges in the case.
review: The headphones sound great but the left earbud is almost dead when I go to us them. If that problem was fixed these earbuds would be perfect.

title: Perfect for Dual Listening
review: This enables my wife and me to listen to music together on our headphones. They work fine.

title: Very high quality headphones
review:
The sound in these earphones is awesome! I love how clear they are and how great the bass sounds in them. I've been able to hear parts on may favorite songs that I didn't even know existed with these headphones. They're also extremely lightweight. They do advertise how lightweight they are, and so I felt they overhyped it a little. They still have some heft to them, but they're light enough that they won't weigh down your pack or cause your head to get tired.

The design is very professional. They look great. The ear pieces fold up and into the head band. The head band doesn't bend, but just the ear pieces make this able to compress pretty small. They're not noise cancelling, so make sure that you're in a quiet place to get the full effect of them. Also, because this is also a microphone, it comes with a special cable to plug into your phone, and it only works one way.

Also, it's not Bluetooth at all. It's just a regular, corded headphone. But, it's very high quality, so I recommend it

title: Great wireless headset, works for Android, too
review:
[[VIDEOID:6f7a95dcd7ebe1fef170bef250c7b7ba]] Even though this is marketed for iPhone, it also works on Android phones. I tested this on one iPhone and two Androids, and it worked well on all the devices I tested.

The sound quality is great. These have some noise-cancelling technology, but they're not real noise cancelling headphones. So the sound sounds pretty clear, but you'll still hear some background noise.

These are great to be able to leave your phone in one room, and listen to music and receive phone calls in another room.

Pros:
+It gets a lot of hours out of each charge
+Easily pairs to an [[ASIN:B004ZLV5PE iPhone]] or Android device
+Great sound quality on Bluetooth
+Very easy to switch between music and phone calls
+Great battery life
+Built in microphone works very well

Cons:
-I didn't like the color at first, but it did grow on me.

title: Chose over the Sony1000xm2s
review:
I struggled to choose between these and Sony's 1000xm2 - purchased both and trying both, decided to keep these. The sound is significantly better. Other reviews highlight how sound quality diminishes when using the ANC at it's highest level. I've not needed to turn it past the "office" setting which is the lowest. My building is currently being has construction for seismic retrofit for earthquake going on and it is pulsing with construction noise. With these on, I all but forget about the outside noise. The snug fit takes care of most of the noise which the Sony's softer more comfortable fit does not keep out. The ANC takes care of the rest of the noise except for the most noisy bursts.
Things to consider:
They take a little break in before being comfortable - give them time to loosen up.
They sound better after time - a break in period.
Pros:
Best sounding wireless headphones out there - period.
Cons:
They do not fold up but do lay flat in their soft case which fits next to my laptop and don't take up too much space. That said, if you travel all the time, I would say these aren't for that. They are heavier than the Sony's 1000xm2 so if the total weight of your bag is being considered just make a note.

title: Amazing sound, yet uncomfortable for long periods.
review: I'm not going to say much about the sound quality--it lives up to everything the other reviews say. I purchased this as much for sleeping (I travel a lot, so I use earbuds/IE earphones as earplugs on planes and in hostels), and find that wearing these for more than two hours just isn't very comfortable, and I can't really recommend them for this purpose.

title: No good for crowded gyms
review:
pros: good fit, battery life seems to be pretty long, they sound pretty good for the price, easy to use

Cons: if you go to a crowded gym these are awful. They constantly cut out from what I assume is interference from other BT earbuds and headphones. When I’m at the gym and it’s not crowded this isn’t a problem. They must have a very weak antenna? My last workout I couldn’t go 20-30 seconds without sound stuttering

title: Best cheap earbuds I've ever had
review: I have 2 pairs of these (one for the office, one for home) and I love them. They fit my ear perfectly and sound fantastic for what I paid for them. I've owned these for 3 years now and one pair is still perfect, and the other just started having some trouble with the left earbud (it's much quieter than the right and sounds muffled) - so I just ordered a replacement. I'd say that's great value for something I listen to almost every day

title: Good headset
review:
Pros:
-Good sound quality
-the earbuds stay in my ear fine (some products, like apple earbuds, tend to be a bit loose for me)
-no crackle or static
