-syncs quickly when swapping between my iphone and my pc
-surprising range. Was able to walk a fair distance from my desk with no audio degradation

Cons:
-Battery life is probably around 6 hours, so you might not be able to listen to these for the whole workday, which leads to my next con..
-Can't listen and charge at the same time. This is a big annoyance for me
-Setup on pc was a bit trial and error for me. Had to work with it for about an hour before I got the drivers working. After that no problem tho

title: ... away made phone call tested sound does actually work like our aircraft noise cancelling mics
review: Microphone is noise cancelling I turned vacuum cleaner on stood 2 feet away made phone call tested sound does actually work like our aircraft noise cancelling mics. Active noise cancelling on earbuds is just enough to knock Spike's out.

title: Crackling headphones
review: These earbuds have a relentless crackling sound. Even if you just connect them and don't play a song/video, you can hear the random crackles. It ends up distorting any audio you do listen to.

title: Legit replacements
review: I love Yurbuds, as they’re the only earbuds that fit comfortably for me. I bought replacement covers from another seller and receive low quality knockoffs. I was so happy when these arrived to see they are real and the same quality as the originals. For people saying they’re too small: Size 4 is meant for the ladies’ Yurbuds. Men’s are larger. I’ve attached a photo of my ladies size 4 next to a men’s with size 5 covers.

title: Fit and Control Issues
review: Got a pair free for making a donation, so I did not purchase through Amazon.  I am older with slight hearing loss. These don't amplify a whole lot (not like iPhone buds e.g.), but they are good enough in quieter environments.  I use them to watch videos rather than exercising. They were not intuitive to pair, but I eventually figured it out. The controls rely on one button for numerous functions, which takes some learning.  However, once paired, they seem ok.  The design seems like a winner in theory, but, in practice, the earbuds don't fit securely or stay in place.  I have the same problem other have mentioned with the right-side ear bud not staying sealed, which, over time and with movement, results in an unacceptably loose fit.  I am not sure I would pay more than $30 for these, and I didn't!.

title: Should come with tweezers so you can get them out of your ear
review: They don’t stay attached to the headphones. They either fall off and get lost or—worse—stick in your ear and you have to dig them out with tweezers.

title: These are great headphones but my pair has an issue with my ...
review: These are great headphones but my pair has an issue with my iphone 6+. It triggers the forward/back/pause/Siri on my iphone when it shifts in the jack. This seems to be a problem with Apple's design and not the headphones. See here: http://thewirecutter.com/2015/03/a-word-on-the-iphone-6-iphone-6-plus-and-third-party-headphones/

title: fell out of my ears, plasticky, button doesn't work
review:
I returned these. They seemed plasticky and low quality for what they cost, and they fell out of my ears. sound was fine, but i prefer the v moda remix remote. ALSO: if you buy from amazon then the warranty is not valid, as amazon is not an authorized retailer.'

UPDATE: unwisely I bought another pair of these. Build quality very low. The button stopped working after two months and I had to send it back. Then a month later the jack on the replacement pair came loose from the headphones. Dealing with customer service was not the most pleasant experience.

Update 2: button on the THIRD pair stopped working. The volume up and down buttons get permanently stuck.

Update 3: the fourth pair also failed. this time the sound just stopped coming out of one earbud. If I blew on the earbud sometimes the sound would come back.

title: breaks frequently; expect to make use of the warranty service
review:
I ordered these in June 2011. They broke a few months later and I received another pair through the warranty service. Over the course of two years this happened three more times. In May 2013, I sent the third pair in. Now, Sept 2013, the fourth pair has broken. Usually, sound would just stop coming out of one of the earbuds. I would think of this as a two year subscription to a headphone replacement service rather than as the purchase of a pair of headphones that will last. The warranty return service is very easy -- no questions asked; just send your original receipt and they happily send you a new pair. But no pair lasted more than a few months. I also own the [[ASIN:B002HR0YLY V-MODA Remix Remote In-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone with 3-Button Apple Control (Blush)]]. They seem to be of higher build quality, have a similar but bassier sound profile, and in certain colors can be cheaper than the klipsch.

UPDATE 8/30/2016
Somehow I forgot that I had owned these previously and bought them again. Sure enough, within two months of getting them they stopped working. Now Klipsch is charging return shipping so you are out a pair of headphones for a week or more while you wait for them to receive them and send you new ones, plus you have to pay ~$8 each way. Assuming they break every three months over the course of a two year warranty, plan on an extra $64 in shipping.

title: tricky with iphone
review: won't say anything about the sound quality, which is amply addressed by everyone else--but these don't fit in the iphones with recessed jacks unless you do some handiwork with a razor blade. it's actually more difficult with this set of headphones than with many others. i've modded about 5 different kinds for my iphone, and the plastic on the er6i's is the hardest.unlike previous er6is, the jack on these is l-shaped, which i also don't like as much. but then the jack on my previous ones broke (which is why i reordered), so maybe they changed it for a reason.

title: The actual headphones are great quality, but they're good enough for a child ...
review:
The actual headphones are great quality, but they're good enough for a child who just wants to watch YouTube videos on the phone.

I ended up buying two, and giving my daughter the headphones and I kept the macaroon case for myself.

title: Great budget powered speakers
review: Bought these specifically for use with a Chromecast Audio. It's a plug and play scenario, and these speakers get the job done excellently. The magnetic speaker grills were a nice surprise. I'm no audiophile, but to my ear, these sound amazing. These easily beat out my Bose computer speakers, Bluetooth speakers, and any headphones I have.

title: Pair easily, sound quality is good
review: Pair easily, sound quality is good.  Can use as wireless headset to talk on the phone.  Holds charge for long period of time.

title: Fits Sony MDR-7506
review: I used these to replace those nasty denigrating original ear pads on my Sony MDR-7506 headphones, These pads are very comfortable to wear and your ears stay dry. I save $100 by not having to buy another set of earphones.

title: Decent sound, bad bluetooth
review:
Good:
Better overall sound quality than other speakers in the $300 price range. Highs and mids are clear, bass is fairly clear but fairly overpowered which is what most consumers seem to want these days. I recommend turning off the Dynamic Bass EQ, which makes the bass extremely overpowered at all but the highest volumes.

Bad:
Bluetooth functionality is quite poor. My iPhone 12 and Sony headphones can connect to each other reliably at distances of up to 50ft. My iPhone can connect to the Klipsch R51PMs reliably at under 10ft and unreliably at up to 20ft. At 15-20ft the audio starts to break up and there are seconds-long gaps in the music. I've connected multiple phones and multiple laptops and none of them can connect reliably from more than 10ft away. That's unacceptable at this price. Klipsch knows speakers and amplifiers, but apparently doesn't know wireless technology.

title: Good, not amazing
review:
I was reasonably happy with these headphones. Previously I had been using Apple Airpod Pros.
Compared to the Airpod Pros,
- the XM4s have slightly better sound quality. Better clarity across the entire frequency spectrum. Out of the box, ridiculously overpowered bass, which some people will like. I appreciate Sony including a 6-band equalizer in their app, so I could adjust the bass down from 0 to -7. That having been said, the XM4's are nowhere near audiophile quality. Not even close. And although the XM4's have slightly better sound quality than the Airpod Pros, they actually sounded worse on first listen because the noise cancellation was better so it was easier to hear the limitations of their sound reproduction.
- the XM4s have noticeably better sound cancellation, wearing comfort, and battery life. I brought both the Apple Airpod Pros and the Sony XM4s on several flights and the Sonys won, hands down for use on a commercial airliner.
- the XM4's are obviously bigger and heavier. Airpods fit in your pocket. XM4's require a shoulder bag or backpack.
The XM4's had trouble switching between bluetooth sources. Several times I had to turn off my phone to get the headphones to connect to my laptop. They're good headphones, but I wouldn't say they're a significant upgrade over competitors.

title: Good, not great
review:
These headphones aren't as good as I hoped they would be.

Sound quality is fine, but not terrific. You can get slightly clearer, cleaner sound at the same price from the Bang & Olufsen E8, but those are incredibly buggy and unreliable. Sound quality overall is a solid two classes below the Etymotic ER-4 series, but of course those aren't wireless.

Build quality is fine, I wouldn't say it exceeds any expectations.

title: Broken after a few weeks of light use
review: Sound quality is good, comparable to a $200 pair of Shure wired IEMs. Unfortunately, both the case and the earbuds were malfunctioning and unusable after less than a month. Very poorly made product. I'm sending them back for a refund.

title: Comparable to ER-4S, good for people who listen to rock and hiphop
review: I've used the ER-4S for about ten years now, and it's absolutely my favorite set of headphones. I only use them with the foam earpieces. They're incredibly transparent, which means they might sound a bit weak if you mainly listen to rock, hiphop, and other genres that like heavy bass. So even though my ER-4S's still work fine, I bought these. At first I thought they were more muddled and not as crystal clear as the ER-4S, but then I switched to the foam earpieces and did a side-by-side comparison, and for classical and acoustic music, they're just about identical. As advertised, they have a slightly boosted bass register. If I were king, I would have given them slightly less bass boost, maybe 80% as much, but I'm just picky. Overall, they're a terrific set of phones. I wouldn't recommend buying them as a second set, unless you just have a lot of extra cash lying around, but if you want a pair of absolutely top notch earphones, and you listen primarily to rock and hiphop, you're not going to find any better than this.

title: Well Below Typical Sennheiser Performance
review: Definitely not worth the price. These sound like they were made to compete with Dre Beats. The sound quality is awful compared to similarly priced headphones from Sennheiser and other manufacturers. Save yourself some money and buy one of the Sennheiser HD400 or HD500 headphones.

title: Surprised at quality
review: So these things are steel. Not like flimsy metal - like, if I hit you with this thing it would really hurt you. Which is cool because I set a couple of Mackie CRX studio monitors on this thing and I'm pretty certain they are not going anywhere. Also the adjustable feature let me set the preamp and some headphones on them. A bit expensive - but they are heavy duty so fair enough.

title: Not too practical
review: The earbuds keep falling out of my years. I think the old bell shaped earbuds work better.

title: Inconsistent performance; failure at 100 days
review:
I really liked the comfort and convenience of this headset. Good battery life. It readily connected with all my devices and was easy to switch between them; however, at times it would randomly disconnect, or change to another device, or stop playing sound despite still being connected. (Very frustrating when in a meeting!)

The right earbud abruptly failed at ~100 days (warrantied for 90) - it seems to be an issue with the cord as it will crackle in and out if I pull/shake that side, but I've never handled it in an indelicate way before so there's no reason it should have failed so soon. Pity. I think some upgrades to quality would make this a really nice mid-range headset, but as is I cannot recommend it for reliable performance.

title: Uncomfortable but decent sound and microphone
review:
I find this headset quite uncomfortable with glasses on (it seems to be okay without) -- the cups press against my ears in a very uncomfortable way.
The sound and microphone seem solid though, but I'll probably end up using another headset for almost everything.

title: They fit my tiny head!
review: I searched and searched and searched for quality headphones to fit my apparently abnormally small head and was ecstatic when I finally found these! They are so incredibly comfortable, they look great, they come with a nice sleek carrying case, and they are really great quality. I love them!

title: Great sound quality and battery life
review:
Pros: Great sound quality and battery life!
The clips to hold the wires didn't last long, and my cat thought the headphones where fascinating haha

title: Great for blocking out chatty coworkers
review: I used to clown on my coworkers that had these, but I get it now. If you don’t find the stock headphones comfortable, then don’t even bother with these. If you’re someone who likes to have one earbud in to drown out inane work conversations, then these are for you.

title: These are fantastic! I was thrilled to find affordable headphones
review: These are fantastic! I was thrilled to find affordable headphones, to use while I swim... I pair these with a little drybag and my old iPod Nano~ they all work seamlessly together!

title: Save your money
review: What a piece of crap. Horrible reception even in the open outside. Max volume is way to low and headphones are uncomfortable and wear out way too fast.

title: wtf sony
review:
i usually love sony headephones.. I HATE these THEY ARE THE WORSE HEADPHONES I HAVE EVERY OWNED
1. ok they work, big deal
2. they are not comfortable. since they have a split on the top they fall down easily. these are for sitting down only! no walking running jogging or shaking your head.
3. the bass is ok, sony provides there
4. the noise cancelling is nice but you have to remember to turn it off. in turn, this is very innovative because i always find my batteries running low
the reason I hate these is because I wouldn't expect sony to make such crap headphones. get some bose around the ear headphones that actually stay of your ears. sheesh!

title: They are very comfortable for my ears
review: These are fair earbuds for the price. They are very comfortable for my ears, and stay in the ear nicely with how i wear them with the wire going up and over the top of my ear. I'm not picky about my earbuds and can't really say much on the finer points of sound quality, but I feel very satisfied with what I hear. My last pair fell apart after about 15 months of daily use - I started losing audio in one ear intermittently, and then one bud just fell to pieces one day. I have purchased a replacement pair of the same kind, and feel like $10 is a good deal for another 15 months.

title: just fine
review:
these headphones I bought in-store locally as a replacement for the Panasonic RP-HTX7-G1 Monitor Headphones which has a jack that breaks if you look at it wrong. They sound just fine for the price and I'm reasonably happy to wear them for hours at a time. When i first bought them they adjusted easily and stayed in place whatever i was doing, but after some time the sliders must loosen up because the simple weight and motion of the cords were constantly pulling the ear cups down out of place when I moved (which is most of the time I wear them). An easy solution was to wrap the sliders in rubber bands while at the desired length - they stay in place just fine since. Another thing to consider - like all on-ear headphones these do press against my cartilage piercings and cause a bit of discomfort if the piercings aren't seated just right. Most people with piercings discover this problem with on-ear headphones pretty quickly, but it's good to mention. All in all - an okay pair of cheaper headphones. Not my favorite, but they do the job.

Update - they broke about about 3 months of daily use.

title: twice burned
review: I really liked the fit, style and sound quality of these headphones - so much that when the jack failed only a few months after purchasing I bought a second pair. I hoped that the first one was just a mulligan and the jack could have given up the ghost from my own abuse, but the second pair's jack lasted even less time even with careful use. You might say third time's a charm, but I'm not going to take the risk. I guess that's the lesson you learn for throwing a little cash at some cheap pretty thing  - I've moved on to a different brand.

title: Glad I found this
review: Cool solution for headphones at my desk. I'll have one at every desk from now on.

title: They are great
review:
They fit great on my 8 year old Grado SR60's. They may be a tad stiffer than the original pads, but not enough to change the comfort of the headphones. The longest I have listened to them was about an hour and it really didn't phase my ears that much.

If you need to change the pads or want to change the look of your headphones, these are great.

title: This is basically a sham product
review: The build quality looked good but it basically doesn't work at all. The inline controls on your headphones wont work. The microphone on your headphones wont work. There is a static every time sound comes on and sometimes just randomly. I returned them and bought two from apple store. The apple store ones work perfectly.

title: useless in my car
review: Great ergonomics, works fine in the house, but I had consistent problems getting people to hear me when in my car.  I drive a Honda CRV, and while it's not as whisper-quiet as a luxury sedan it's not all that noisy a vehicle.  As far as I could tell, the noise cancelling capabilities advertised have no value whatsoever.  So, great headset for the office, but not a good buy if you're looking for a headset to use in the car.

title: Not Apple Quality
review:
Even though they show the Apple display on this, be forewarned this is not up to the Apple bar of quality, at least in materials. It is light plastic.

It's solid enough. I use it to elevate my MacBook Pro next to my secondary display; I'm sure it would hold pretty much any flatscreen.

It's not very high. You can see that in the measurements, but I would prefer it be higher for my purposes.

Also note that it is not compatible with the single out 4-post/segment plugs in use on Apple computers headphone/mic, that is, their included audio/mic cable won't work with Apple computers because it requires the separate headphone/mic ports.

Still, it's good enough for my needs and it is cheap, so I'm okay with it.

title: A Bit Disappointed
review:
It arrived with dark smudges on it. I was able to clean them off. My main complaint is that if you pull the earbuds all the way into it and start wrapping, the bit that has the controls rests awkwardly over the top edge. To get it to not do that, you have to leave some cord sticking out.

I am using the new earpods, so I guess maybe it wasn't designed for those.

I expected more from Quirky.

title: thought this would be a good value alternative to PortaPro... I was wrong
review:
I just broke my 3rd pair of Koss PortaPros in like five years due to running in them every day (doesn't seem worth it to ship a $25 headphone to them to repair of it) so I bought these, thinking they're a decent enough alternative in the Koss lineup that possibly have the same shelf life.

I was wrong.

The audio quality on these are awful compared to the PortaPros, which admittedly are really really good for $30 headphones. These are straight up standard airplane headphones you get for free. If that's all you need, go for it. If you want decent balance/bass/etc just buy the PortaPros or SportaPros (honestly not sure what the difference is, both sound the same to me).

title: Does the job, stands up to laundering!
review: Love the pedometer, the color, the size, the simplicity - it's just what I need for the gym. I also love the fact that it came through a wash/dry cycle intact. YIKES! I'm deducting one star because the included headphones don't have a pause/play function.

title: Great headphones. Better if you like origami.
review: Great headphones with exceptional clarity, and very high quality. I would have preferred a set without the folding feature that makes them smaller for travelling only because it makes it a little harder to put them on - but then, I was never any good at origami either. Once properly unfolded, they are very comfortable and the sound is great.

title: Sound quality isn't amazing
review: Sound quality isn't amazing, but what do you expect for something in this price range haha.  Works great for what it is, a cheap around ear headphone.  I've been hard on them and they still work great (kept in a bag with books and banging, no damage!)

title: Not workout headphones as advertised.
review:
My Jaybird Freedom headphones were purchased through Apple, however I thought it would be important to share my experience.

The headphones were amazing out of the box and I would've rated them 4.5 stars. However, after running with them 3 times a week for less than a month, they broke. They will no longer power on and the best part about it is that customer service is not responsive. Luckily I have American Express and I can file a claim with them. Terrible experience.

If you don't use these headphones for working out, I'm sure you will enjoy them (beautiful, sound great and comfortable). If you work out and sweat on them, please be aware that they may die and customer service may not respond.

title: Make headphones harsh
review: I tried de velour version with a Meze 99 neo and the m50x, disappointing. The bass almost disappear and make both headphones sibilant, dry and harsh. Hybrids work better for me.

title: Prefer Audio Technica M50x
review: Great build quality, If you have big ears will be uncomfortable. I expected better sound quality, closer to ATH-m50x but no. For gaming is great. But no for listening music if you have better headphones.

title: Great headphones
review: A little bit uncomfortable and heavy because built quality, great sound, the best for under $200. Much better than any bose available. I tried the V-moda, QC25 and the noise cancellation is pretty good but the sound is much better in these headphones. Sennheiser has great quality but at a higher price.

title: Like em enough I bought them twice..
review:
I use these for gaming & listening to music at my computer. I have a bunch of different headphones (sony MDR7506, sennheiser px100s, Audio Technica ATH-ANC7B's) and I really find these to be comfortable for extended use wear.

I'm a glasses wearer so I have trouble finding headphones I can wear for a long time, especially when gaming, so these fit the bill.

My first pair broke (stepped on) so I ended up just buying a second pair of these.

They aren't my primary music headphones, but I do prefer them for gaming over anything else I've tried.

title: These are the best earbuds I've ever owned
review: These are the best earbuds I've ever owned.  I wear them while woodworking, jogging, drumming, and working in a Data Center.  The noise reduction is great.  They're very comfortable. The mic is great for phone calls.  I use them on average 2 or 3 hours a day, and I only have to charge them every couple of days... We have 4 pairs, one for everyone in the house!  I'll buy them again.

title: Exactly what I wanted
review: I was so tired of earbuds that "sweat" out. I had a pair of over the ear loop ones that worked but were not that comfortable. I am also not going to pay a lot of money for a really nice pair either. These are perfect. They've not slipped out once, I can clearly hear my music and they were economical. Win.

title: I unique experience that might take getting used to.
review: Review for AfterShokz Air: Being able to hear around ear damage is a nice thing. Because you are bypassing the eardrum you will never have the full richness of eardrum focused audio drivers that some people just have to have. I would compare the sound quality to Skullcandy earbuds you can grab in a checkout line. Little heavier in the low end then the highs and the mid-range is going to dominate. You can certainly get your jam on with these. You can certainly crank them if you want, but you loose the functionality intended with being able to hear your surroundings. My favorite use for these is for hands-free phone calls. I've never been able to hear a conversation so clearly while at work. Even if I only ever used it for that function alone I would deem it worth the price!

title: Love these so much — great if you have several Apple devices
review:
These are really well made, quality headphones. The build is perfect, just like an iPhone everything fits perfectly and is well finished. There are clever little design touches like the removable earcups — you can buy new ones when you get grossed out by the old ones. The spinning knob feels great and can be used to get exactly the volume you want, perfect when you are trying to fall asleep. I find these comfortable enough to wear almost 24/7. The sound transparency is top-notch, actually helps me understand people as I’m hard of hearing. They don’t have an off-button but they go into a very low power mode automatically so I don’t miss that.

Using this with many different Apple devices is the best improvement over my old headphones, I used to spend ten minutes switching my other headphones in an app and in settings — having more than two Apple devices is probably the best use case for this product. Well, that and also I can use these with the Apple TV, there is no lag and it connects quickly.

Drawbacks: 1) apparently these are not for really high-end listening to lossless audio, but they sound great compared to other Bluetooth noise canceling headphones 2) they are heavy (actually made of metal) and might put too much pressure on the head for some (less comfortable than Bose 35s) 3) too fragile for workouts and not a bit water resistant 4) case is completely useless.

10/10 would buy again.

title: Buying another set for other people, Keeps AirPods Pro from falling out
review: These are great additions to my AirPods Pro. I just can’t get a good seal with the Apple tips but these improve the fit and also the sound. Seem to pop on the earphones perfectly. Comes in a handy little plastic box for storage, and another family member has used one of the other sizes.

title: Bluetooth switching terrible, otherwise good
review:
The manufacturer said in answer to a question: “So while you're watching video on the connected iPad, the headphones will automatically pause the video to answer a call from the connected smartphone.”

This has never worked and irritates everyone who calls me. Even when I am watching a movie on my phone it still doesn’t work! Also, when I leave the headphones for a while and come back, they are always paired to the wrong device and take ages getting reconnected. Not recommended if you need more than one device to pair. I had to buy separate headphones for my iOS devices.

The sound clarity is not good for podcasts.

BTW the Beats and Apple headphones switch beautifully. However, these Bose headphones are particularly good for long-wearing comfort and noise cancelling. And the lack of voice assistant and finicky touch controls are a blessing. The ear pads are easily replaceable and while the battery isn’t, it is still fine after many years of daily use. They’ve been dependable.

For a sale price of $100 these would be great. And I would buy another set.

title: meh
review:
I bought these for my husband so he can listen to music late at night. However, he still prefers his audiophile speakers and says his old Audio-Technica noise-canceling headphones are almost as good. I like them fine (for listening to Podcasts and books on tape) and find them comfortable, though.

Replaceable cord is a nice touch! It got eaten by our cat already so we should buy a dozen replacement cords and mic when I find them.

title: Isolate your ears and light up your mind
review:
Upgraded to the QC25 from the very popular ~$35 Sony noise cancelling headset that you can find on Amazon. The difference is spectacular, which is very welcome considering the "slight" difference in price. An amazing piece of technology that is of exceptional sturdiness and quality. I got the Samsung version and the in-line cable controls work perfectly for my Galaxy S6 Edge.

On to the actual quality of the main feature. The leather ear covers are soft, sweat/oil repellent, and don't leave any marks on my skin afterwards. The inside of the ear cups are slightly curved, I'm assuming so that the sound is project more directly into your ear. I have quite large, protruding ears and these fit perfectly. The noise cancelling feature is outstanding - I am sitting next to an aquarium with multiple fans, pumps and filters on and if I was blindfolded I wouldn't be able to tell you if I was in my room or in the middle of a park. Sound quality is the best of any headphone I've ever used, leagues above any stock earbuds. You will hear the individual piano keys being struck in a classical piece, and the subtle breathing inflections of a singer.

title: Simple, great value noise cancelling headphones
review: Unbeatable value - not as effective in the noise cancelling or sound quality departments compared to headphones 10x the price, but then again you get what you pay for. I would recommend this to anyone who is looking to experience the difference between the typical ear muffs that are out these and the beauty of isolating your ears from the white noise of the world.

title: Best for IEMs.
review:
Enough power to get any headphones kinda loud. But they shine for in ear monitors (IEM).

Separate the Bluetooth tech from the actual headphones to let you get good sound from any phone.

title: Triple Flange are better
review: I bought these before finding the triple flange. These don't fit as well, don't sound isolate as well, and put the hard part of the headphone in your ear which is not as comfortable as the triple flange which only puts soft stuff in your ear.

title: Pretty nice
review: I bought this for my son as a Christmas gift. He is a big computer gamer. He said "The trademark suspension headband is very comfortable and durable, he was a bit worried at first because the wires looked very thin but it definitely works. The retractable mic is really nice, it blends in well and other people say they hear me much clearer than before. The overall sound from the headset is very nice and clear. The lining is very strong and rubber coated so it doesn't get easily cut. The only complaints would be the sweating around the ears and the very twisted jack lining, he cant make it straight".

title: Loved it!
review: I bought this for my 14 year old son for Christmas. He loves to play video games and wanted a nice headset, so I took a chance on this one and he love's it! It was a really good price compared to other brands. The cords were nice and long and has great sound. The only complaint he had was his ears were a bit sore from them at first till he got used to them.

title: The best I've ever used....EXCEPT
review: I had reviewed this right after getting them almost a year ago, and I loved them. Technically I still do really love them. The sound quality is fantastic, the build quality is great, and and microphone is also very good. The one thing that has killed this headset for me is the inline volume control. The volume wheel is so sensitive that I can't even really touch it or I will lose sound in either one of the earphones, or the sound on both earphones will go out or get VERY quiet. A friend of mine has the Cloud headset and he ran into the same exact issues with his volume control. If HyperX can fix this issue and put the volume controls somewhere else, perhaps on the ear piece, it will be a top notch headset.

title: I really liked this headset but I started to notice that if ...
review: I really liked this headset but I started to notice that if there was any background noise at all, people had a lot of trouble hearing & understanding me, and I had to shout into the phone, even with the microphone right next to my mouth.  Very frustrating. For this reason, I have set the Emerson headset aside and I am trying out a new, different one today. We'll see how it goes!

title: Excellent isolation
review: Use them when riding my motorcycle and for studying in loud or noisy areas. Basically this is an earplug that has a speaker built into it. The quality of sound is quite high, although if you are looking for headphones that have built in external bass amplification these are not it. They are more of a studio monitor type sound without built in amplification of bass like the BEATS headphones that are quite popular right now.

title: Astounding quality for under $100
review:
These headphones sound great. I recently replaced a pair I've had since 1998. They're especially great for listening to music made with modern instruments, including rock and some jazz. They are possibly a bit too "technical" for classical music, and will certainly expose flaws in recordings that you wouldn't ordinarily hear on lesser headphones. They're comfortable enough for multi-hour listening sessions and fit comfortably.

I listen to these through my Mac via an Audioquest Dragonfly 1.2 DAC and typically listen to music encoded with a lossless codec (such as ALAC or FLAC) played back through Amarra Symphony.

There are certainly better sounding headphones available through Amazon, but all of them cost twice as much as these, which are a bargain anywhere under $100. I've listened to music through a lot of different equipment and I've never heard over-the-ear headphones that sound anywhere near this good for less than $250.

title: Doesn't fit most phone handsets
review:
Instead of using your nice clear landline connection, make and take calls on a broken cell phone from the bottom of a sealed mineshaft. It will still sound better than your phone will sound with these things on it.

I don't know what phones these designers have, but unless you have a handset from the late 1980's, these won't fit properly so that connections will sporadically come and go. You and your caller will still be "connected" but whether you can hear or be heard seems random.

On other words, this particular "cure" is worse than the disease. Save your money and buy a headset or something.

title: 3 second fade in.
review:
Every time there is a pause in what you are listening to it turns off (I don't mean it disconnects from the source but that output turns off). Every time something starts playing it spends 3 seconds fading in. Best I can tell, it doesn't even start fading in until after the first second of sound from the source. After confirming with an Oontz Angle and Bose headphones that the audio source was not at fault I packed it up and sent it back. For me, it's completely useless because I want something exclusively for listening to audio books and the first 3-4 words of virtually every sentence being chopped off is completely intolerable.

Connection is quick but I didn't test range, as it's useless to me. The sound was good once it started playing so if you listen to continuous music you may not notice this major flaw once it gets going.

title: Bluetooth problems are not insurmountable
review:
I bought this because my old player didn't have Bluetooth and I wanted to use my noise canceling headphones while watching on the treadmill. Unfortunately the connection sounded horrible.

I called tech support and they were [almost] useless. After some troubleshooting they said they would exchange it but when the new one arrived it had exactly the same problem. This lead me to dive into settings because it didn't make sense that $350 headphones would have connection problems. It turns out that the default connection settings in the machine were wrong for my headphones and after making a change, both players worked fine. I sent one of them back so as not to be charged for 2 but the real problem was a combination of the wrong defaults in the machine and useless tech support.

The picture is just fine. As is the sound when plugged directly into my surround system. So, overall, it's a great value.

title: Not Better Than The Rest
review:
These sound great. That's why you want them. Unfortunately, at this price point, you need more than great. These don't meet the measure.

The sound, in my opinion, is not better than the rest. I've used a lot of headphones, earbuds, and other variations over the years. I listened to Netflix, Amazon Video, Spotify, a podcast, and other sounds. The sound was as good as any buds I've worn. Not as good as over ear, but the highs and lows felt right.

They charge quickly and stay charged.

They fall off/out of my ear. I've tried every bud size. One size even tore as I removed it. Flimsy. Maybe it is the weight or balance of that weight. I don't know, but in trying to use them for long walks -- I tried many times (I walk a lot). They always fell out. I don't trust they will stay in.

Taking calls was good.

All good except for them falling out, but not the value I expected.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com

title: Excellent Quality, Easy to Use
review:
As I write, I'm using the headphones. I'm watching the Haunting of Hill House on Netflix. The sound is great. Surround sound? I don't think so. Incredible for the money? Absolutely.

I've also listened to Prime Music and watched Prime Video flawlessly.

Set up was just connecting the audio wire into the monitor and plugging the electric cord in. That's it. Another button press or two and I'm good to go.

I like that it is genuinely wireless, not a fuzzy Bluetooth tech piece that buzzes in and out.

I also like how it recharges on the wireless relay.

The ear pads are replaceable. Nice.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com

I'd get these again.

title: Great Balance of High and Low
review:
There are two sides to these headphones: Sound and Comfort.

For comfort, I give it 3.5. Long-term listening (all day at work) is only so-so. They feel sweaty and my ears are a little raw.

The sound, however, is 5+. I've listened to metal, classical, light jazz and folk music. All of it sounds great. The bass is low but not overwhelming. Fine notes (think: classical guitar) come through without any tinniness.

Overall, I'm happy. These are great to listen to an LP or two and enjoy it all.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com

title: Are These Buds For You (for all you do?)
review:
These buds are easy to like if you are a runner. For others, maybe not so much. They are sports earbuds after all. They aren't meant for Netflix.

I found them useful on my treadmill. I want to jam while I'm running, but I'm already competing against the treadmill and the pounding of my feet (always louder on a treadmill than outside). Wires on a treadmill especially are a pain, so these are welcome.

I'm not using earbuds for sound quality. You won't find that here either. I'm using them to convey a song well enough to get me going and this gets the job done. I'm jamming to Queen, not Verdi or Chopin. I have great headphones for "The Four Seasons."

The earbuds stayed well-enough in my ears.

Controlling volume, etc., mid-run, was trickier than expected. You'll need to get a feel for them.

I'm not impressed but I am satisfied.

Anthony Trendl
americanspeechwriter.com

title: Light, Excellent Headphones
review:
This isn't my first Bluetooth Headphone set. This is the first I actually like.

Why?

These are light, with minimal wires. I barely knew I wore them. Pairing was a breeze.

When I wore them during a drive from Chicago to Atlanta, using them to talk on the phone, hear instructions from my GPS, and listen to Spotify. The battery never ran out. I plugged it in randomly, never pushing the battery, but it lasts at least for several hours.

I'm pleased.

Anthony Trendl
AnthonyTrendl.com

title: Sturdy Bag Good for Daily Use
review:
This Icon computer bag is great for throwing in your laptop, headphone, sundry papers, as you make your way off to the library or cafe.

This is not a sleek bag for carrying a tiny laptop. It is intended to be used daily, but it isn't pretty. Function won over form, but it looks well enough, and most importantly, it gets the job done.

I've had mine for five years, through several laptops. There's enough pockets to keep separate what needs separation, and enough room for most anything. It is good, too, for use on the plane when you plan to store it above your seat. You've no worries as other passengers cram things in there as well.

I fully recommend the Icon computer bag.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com

title: Pleased With Product, Not Customer Service
review:
My Roku 3 replaces a Netgear NeoTV device I've used for several years.

Set-up was frustrating. I had to contact Roku to be able to register mine without using my credit card. The person seemed to avoid guiding me to directly do this. My reason was to limit security issues, as well as avoid accidentally buying something.

I primarily use it for Netflix and Amazon Prime.

The Netflix interface is great -- clean, easy to navigate.

The Amazon Prime one is frustrating, as, unlike Netflix, Amazon mixes products for sale in with the movies I can stream via my Prime membership. As such, I rarely watch movies on Prime. This is more of a problem with Amazon, not Roku, though I think Roku needs to address this.

I love the voice search function. There's a tiny mike on the clicker. You need to speak articulately but it beats typing.

Also cool is being able to connect headphones to the clicker. Late night action flicks needn't wake up the rest of my house.

As a device, I love it, but since customer service is part of what I purchased, I can only give it 4/5 stars.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com

title: Impressive, Powerful, Useful
review:
For a small apartment or office, these are perfect.

The sound from any computer's speakers is awful. That goes without saying. The Presonus Ceres C4.5BT 2-Way Powered Speakers with Bluetooth (that's a mouthful) aren't those speakers. These are the ones you want.

I'm not an audiophile, but I listen to music throughout my workday in my home office. You might say I am a serious amateur. My musical tastes range from Led Zeppelin to classical to jazz. I ask a lot from my speakers and these have delivered.

I have excellent headphones, but really, those aren't my first choice. I want music ambiently flowing through the air as I work.

Why I love these:
* The sound. I hear notes otherwise hidden in my cheap desktop speakers. The song I hear is the same, only better.

* I've adjusted the acoustic tuning. This helped manage the music, particularly useful as much of what I listen to is online. I'm able to reduce the related distortion.

* The Bluetooth feature is nice. I've used it to send music from my phone easily from across the room.

* The size. These are small enough to fit on my shelves.

The Downside
* Speaker hiss. I don't know why. I hope there is a way to resolve this. I see I'm not alone in this (from the other reviewers). If there's a way to stop this, please let me know.

In all, I'm in love with these speakers.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com

title: Great Sound, But Not Overwhelmed
review:
I like these headphones a lot. The sound is impressive to me, a non-audiophile. Outside noise is reduced, and the clarity of the music I listen to (from delicate classical to heavy industrial punk) comes through as well as on my stereo.

My expectations, however, were higher. I was not blown away. Not all outside noise was excluded, and the sound was not as close to being at a concert as the price point might imply. At some point, maybe I cannot tell the difference whilst a more experience music aficionado might appreciate this.

For me, the Sony XBA-4IP headset was more than I need, and I am satisfied. When I am on a train or at my desk and need to be discreet, these will be my choice.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com

title: Decent Headphones, Horrible Packaging: Childproof and Adultproof
review:
These are basic headphones useful in any music system. The sound is as good as any with headphones at a related price point and functionality.

That's the good news.

The bad news, and the reason I dropped this review from five stars to two stars, is regarding the packaging. It is simply awful. Encased in a beautiful hard, but flexible clear plastic shell, the product was well-protected. Too protected. The engineers who developed it clearly have no sense of the human experience. The product managers overseeing it all, as well as the marketing people, apparently just shoved this past their supervisors without involving common sense.

It took 15 minutes to open it. During that time I tore the paper instructions, scratched several fingers, and otherwise became extremely frustrated.

True, the product itself is adequate. However, moving forward, I am less likely to buy JVC products. I can buy the same quality product from a dozen other manufacturers at the same price without th trouble. The headphones are not good enough to bother with the hassle.

Sorry, JVC, but you failed.

Anthony Trendl
[...]

title: Nice, But Not For Running
review:
Wearing now the Altec Lansing MZX206 MUZX Headphones, I am listening to Bjork singing "Headphones" from her 1995 [[ASIN:B000002HH2 Post]] album. It seemed apropos.

The short of it: Much better sound than the headphones which came with my iPod. However, they keep falling out of my ears. Despite the three different sizes Altec provided, not one will stay easily. If I move, and the cord tugs even the smallest amount, the pull out. This is tolerable at my desk, but only then.

Since the major attraction of headphones for me is to use them as I run, I am disappointed. I will use them at home, but not likely elsewhere.

Anthony Trendl
[...]

title: For Skype and Internet Chats, I'm Satisfied
review:
My Logitech Internet Chat Headset does the job. I use it to occasionally chat with friends internet to internet on AOL and Yahoo, or through Skype. The headset has successfully connected me to Hungary and Indonesia, as well as places around the USA.

I have dial-up, but have used it on a T-1 and wireless lines without trouble. The sound was great, limited only by my connection. The headset feels comfortable for short calls; I never talk longer than an hour. The mike is to the side, and picks up my voice perfectly.

What did I need? A cheap microphone and headphone set. That's what I received. More money would get me a better quality device with more features, but this will suffice.

Do better devices exist? Probably, as the technology behind these is basic. The point is, this one is fine. If you need CD quality audio, shop elsewhere. If you just want to call on a few friends now and again, this is enough.

I fully recommend the Logitech Internet Chat Headset.

Anthony Trendl
editor, HungarianBookstore.com

title: Great inexpensive headphones!
review: I needed new "I'm busy"/"you're the loudest person ever" headphones for the office. For the price point they are great! The ear cups block out sound, and they music sounds great. The cord is super long too. I'm really happy with them,

title: Pricey, but so far worth it for my AirPods
review:
I was hoping to get by with my old silicon inserts from my apple earbuds after I upgraded to the new AirPods. Unfortunately, the old inserts did not have a cutout for the AirPod sensor, which was annoying...but even more so annoying was how loose the AirPods fit in the insert. They wiggled around like crazy. So although the insert remained secure in my ear, the AirPod itself was moving around in the insert, making the sound quality less than ideal.

I will admit it was tough forking up $12 for only 3 of these sets, but after using them solid for a week, I'm fairly satisfied! The cutouts are lined up perfectly with the AirPod and the sound quality is great. They fit snuggly in my hear, but best-of-all, the AirPods themselves fit snuggly into the insert allowing them to stay in place. I have ran 20+ miles with these in my ears thus far and these have been great! My only fear is that they will eventually "stretch out" over time because of the need to remove them every time you charge them. You have to stretch the silicone a great deal in order to get the AirPod in...so I'm curious to see how they do with their longevity. I'll update my review down the road.

title: no cord problems yet....
review: Reading the reviews confirmed one thing: If it weren't for the poor cord connection, these headphones would be incredible!  The fact that they were only $13...I figured I'd try them out.  I've had them for 3 weeks now.  I run 3x a week.  Like all of the other positive reviews, these things are incredible.  I'm amazed by their sound quality.  They are extremely light, and they stay in one place on my head virtually the entire run.  I've never had to fumble with them, or even worry about them during a run!  I've treated them like I'm carrying a raw egg on a spoon...so I haven't destroyed them yet by the dreaded "accidental tug of death."  If you are willing to take care of them, the $13 risk is an absolute no-brainer with these!!!

title: May produce noise blips while connected
review:
I do hear some noise generated on left earbud by bluetooth I believe,
i have found several other issues reports over the internet but no solution found.

title: and larger silicon earplugs that provide a better seal(I hear more bass) but are a little too ...
review: The only other IEM I've owned is the Vsonic VSD3S. I use either my laptop or iPhone 6 to drive headphones, After listening to both, I prefer the KZ ATE S. I hear more bass, have more isolation, and the ATE S has stress reliefs for the wire as well as a horizontal jack. I still have some concerns for how long that the cord will hold up, and I'm needing to buy different earplugs as well. The KZ ATE S only comes with a medium sized foam earplug that are a little small, and larger silicon earplugs that provide a better seal(I hear more bass) but are a little too large and uncomfortable for my ear.  However, I can't complain too much because I don't think I'll find better headphones at this price. I recommend the KZ ATE S as a college student who commutes using public transportation.

title: Great headphones when you are out and about
review: Great headphones when you are out and about. Excellent sound quality for the price. I haven't really had a problem with durability.

title: WOW I am now a believer
review: I've never been one for apple products other than the iPhone. However these are a game changed. In addition to some absolutely insanely impressive sound, the noice cancellation will have you questioning your own sanity. I have many other earbud / headphone sets with "noice cancellation" but these blow my mind. Finally the last touch that I love is the "transparency mode" which allows you to have normal conversation and hear everything as if you have no headphones in at all.

title: Mediocre
review:
It's okay-ish.
They don't sound great, but neither do any other true wireless earbuds I have listened to. They are certainly better than the sort of stuff offered by Samsung or Apple.
My first set, the batteries died after a few months. The company (after a very long wait) replaced them for me.
The case is bulky and poorly designed. The charging connecting is inexplicably inside the case, making charging a bit wonky.
None of the included plastic ear tips fit well, so I had to order some foam ones, and they won't charge with the foam ones on.
Overall, I'm disappointed. I expected a lot more from this product.

title: Does the Trick
review:
What can I say? It works great, and it looks pretty good.
I ended up upgrading my headphone amp to a tube amp, so I mostly use this guy as a DAC for my PC now, but it's great to be able to just plug in my headphones any time I want to use them for my computer audio.
Aside from the useless 2.5mm jack, this thing has a balanced XLR out, which is pretty nice and not something you get everywhere.
All in all, a pretty solid piece of kit.

title: Awesom
review:
This little thing rocks.
To be fair, I don't have much point of comparison, but I've been using this with a set of open-back over-ears and a high-res player for quite some time now, and I can't find anything to fault.
It looks nice, is works perfectly, it's nice and portable, and it sounds amazing.
All you have to do is plug your player straight into your headphones, then switch to this bad boy to hear the immediate difference in power, clarity and roundness of sound.
Highly recommended.

title: Unbeatable at this Price Point
review:
I thought these were very solid for full retail price.
For the current price point, you simply can't beat these headphones.
These were my first foray into the realm of "better" headphones (not cheaper cans or IEMs), and I have been nothing but happy.
I paired these with a nice high-res player and a DAC/amp, and they sound great.
I find myself getting lost in the music, and music I've heard a thousand times excites me all over again.
If you're looking to dip your toes in audiophile waters, you can't find a better entry point anywhere near this price level.

title: Defective
review:
I really did like this, but they went bad quickly.
They started making a crackling sound, which is apparently a known issue.
They asked me to spray them out which electronics spray, which I did, to no avail (it got worse).
Klipsh refused to stand behind the product, citing a one-year warranty (lots of faith in their products).
They told me to purchase a new control unit and replace it myself - $70, and wouldn't do anything about it.
I bought some new speakers instead, and unfortunately will no longer go with this company. Good products need to last, and they need to be paired with good service.
I'll use another brand for my speakers and headphones from now on.

title: Great
review:
I used to have a pair of E2Cs. Unfortunately, I lost them. This is the newer version of that product.
I have been using a cheap pair of earbuds by another company, and haven't been happy with the sound quality. Luckily, these sound just like me E2Cs. Great low end for earbuds of this price, and a very nice and powerful sound across the full spectrum. You may not have the mids and super-fine details of a more expensive set, but you would be hard-pressed to find something better for this price.
The headphones are well-constructed, they come with a great selection of cushions, they have a solid and removable cord, and they fit perfectly in the ears.
If you are looking for a great mid-range pair of earbuds, these are a great choice. My music doesn't sound muddled and not "full" anymore!

title: Okay
review:
These are definitely three-star earbuds, but I am giving four stars because you can't expect much more for the price.
I lost my old earbuds, so I needed some new ones on a budget. Unfortunately, my old ones were Shure EC2 headphones. So, there is simply no comparison between these and the $250 model I lost. So i can't even make a comparison.
For the price, these are about where I expected. They are cheap, and they sound cheap. I like to listen to some harder rock, and these really don't handle the sound well. I find that these work much better with quieter music like Soul or soft rock.
The bass is okay until the music picks up, then it easily gets lost. I find that the music lacks substance and overall "fullness." These also don't get too loud. However, that is okay, because the music easily gets muddied and poor at higher volumes.
I also find that the "sound isolating" buds simply don't work well. They don't isolate anything, and none of the sizes fit well. They are made of cheap, flimsy rubber, unlike what you would find in better headphones.
Overall, these sound like exactly what they are: $15 headphones. You can expect exactly what you are paying for. They sound better than what you would get at the dollar store, but if you are looking for audiophile quality or a rich, full-sounding music, you can start in a higher price bracket.

title: great headphones, especially for this price range
review:
This was my introduction to entry-level audiophile gear, and I am thoroughly impressed

pros
-It is relatively neutral sounding
-Amazing sound stage
-SUPER comfortable, I have forgotten I have these on only to run out of cable length on occasion.
-clean sound, by this I mean it doesn't sound "muddy" like most cheap headphones/speakers do, I prefer this to my cheap woofer, as it the output is *slightly* muddy, more expensive headphones I suspect would be even better, but for the price the sound is jaw dropping.

possible(?) con
-opened up with an external DAC/AMP, I use FiiO E10K, may want to consider

Also, I didn't believe in burn in before using these headphones for a while, but they continue to get better.

title: Sound great, stay on your ears, survived laundry
review:
I've had two pairs for about 5 years now, they work great. One just accidentally went through a washer and dryer, and still works and sounds great.

Good: Because of the memory wire these actually stay on my ears despite movement, and there is no dangling-wire noise. I have peculiar ear canals that seem to eject any in-ear headphones, but these are able to stay in once I find the right tips. The sound is quite good, especially for the price. I have a pair of Sennheisers and I can't tell the difference.

Bad: They tangle easily. This is expected since the memory wire is effectively shaped like a hook. This is probably why they come with a hard case.

title: Does what it says
review: Permitted me to use an old but comfortable 2.5mm mono cordless phone headset with a smartphone and a laptop.  Mic works, earpiece works, enough said.

title: Fall out of my ears constantly, other problems
review:
1 Star
I don't think these are genuine Apple Air Pods. People I know who have them don't have any of the problems I've had. See below.
• Frequently can’t perform functions asked through Siri, just says “working on it” then drops. Ironically none of my non-apple earpieces have any trouble, ever, only Apple EarPods fail, often so I think they are knock offs.
• unless you put them back in their case when you’re done using them they will continue to answer your phone, sometimes mid-call when you aren’t wearing them. You can go to settings to turn them off, but every single other earpiece or headphone I've ever owned disconnects when you take them off.
• they are worthless if you are doing anything other than sitting still in one place. They fall out of my ears constantly and if I don’t have music playing at the time I don’t always notice and have to search for them. The newer version may be better, this version is a ridiculous, inexcusable design flaw.
•Since you can only recharge them or pair them with a devise when they’re in their case if you misplace the case you’re out of luck and buying a new one is not cheap.

title: After one year, still very happy
review:
after one year, still very happy
Pros:
•sound quality is good, controls make it easy to skip songs and adjust volume.
• headphones work pretty good when I take the time to get them situated properly. I run the ear bud cords from iPod to ears under the mask strap to hold them in place and limit jostling by water. Swim cap provided would help, but I hate swim caps.
•swam 5 more laps today than usual yet it seemed like I spent about 10 minutes less in the water. Music made the time fly.
Cons: if I think of one I’ll let you know.

title: Terrible phone sound quality
review:
These probably aren't a 1 star but no one reads the 2&3 stars. I'm only commenting on phone quality since that's all I wanted them for. I made several calls right away from a quiet room and the sound quality was awful, people said I sounded like I was in a tunnel. I called Bose customer service and said I had a question about my new Bose headphones. She said “I’m sorry, I can’t hear you clearly” I said I know, because I’m calling using my new Bose headphones. She was not amused, I was terribly amused.
With each call, I called back from my plantronics earbud to rule out a bad connection and the sound was fine. I even left a message and listened to it before sending to judge for myself, really really bad. They claim to give crystal clear reception even in windy conditions, yeah, no.
• they also were uncomfortable on my ears, too much pressure, though I have this problem often, just the way my ears are laid out.

title: Work reasonably well but more sizes would be good.
review:
These worked well on my Apple/beats earbuds.

I tried them on a set of Anker buds and they didn’t hold on well enough and got stuck in my ear, requiring help from my daughter to fish them out. I haven’t tried the smaller size on those, but this size appeared to fit well.

So, I’d recommend you give them a try, especially if you have the $50 beats.

title: Incredible performance for the price
review:
Based on the initial performance, these earbuds are a tremendous bargain. I am forever losing them. Usually i end up spending $15-$20 for the highly-rated panasonics - which I still like very much. For four bucks, though, these are a steal.

I haven't done a direct comparison with those panasonics; I don't care. They sound OK - good enough that podcasts are intelligible, and music doesn't anger me.

I have a good stereo system, and good headphones for listening to music. Those aren't disposable like these are, so these have their place.

Can't yet comment on their longevity. They seem reasonably well made, though.

title: Thumbs up, a great value - but don't expect a miracle.
review:
I constantly lose earbuds, so I have tried a variety of cheap ones. Recently I've tried three different sets.

I bought the [[ASIN:"B00UE3SVQ8" Jlab Jbuds Metal Pro]] at a daily deal site and they are garbage. I only paid $4 a pair, but I feel like I wasted my money. They sound terrible, and the button doesn't work on my iphone 6.

I bought the [[ASIN:"B00E4LGTYC" Panasonic RPTCM125A]] and they are nice. They have somewhat better build quality than these. They both sound "OK" to me; I haven't tried a side-by-side listening test. They are also several dollars more (when I last bought, they were $17; they are $11 now, still more than these).

Assuming they don't fall apart quickly, the monoprice buds are a great value. They sound OK, the button works.

Maybe my headline is wrong - maybe these are a miracle at the price point.

title: Works, but not very durable
review:
I have purchased three of these over the past few years. All were, as far as i could tell, genuine headset buddy products. When they work, they work perfectly.

The first one failed pretty quickly, after less than a year. Later, in October 2011, I purchased two more, on the theory that the QC might not be great. Again, one of them failed fairly quickly, but the other is still working as of March 2014.

Note, I do not use this product very much, maybe once a month. THe ones that have failed were connected to my headset and hung from a hook on the inside of the "monitor hutch" of my desk. Not a difficult environment.

title: Incredible sound for the price - fit me well
review:
Not much new to say here, but I am very pleasantly surprised by these earbuds. The sound is incredible for the price.

Assuming they last, for the price I can't imagine getting anything better.

I see that other reviewers say there are problems with fit. They fit in my ears well; for the price it is worth the gamble.

title: Pretty but don't last
review:
I bought these earphones at a brick & mortar retailer after my previous pair failed.

I didn't have high expectations, since I'd had a previous ifrogz product that failed quickly, but I didn't have many choices so i went with them.

They sound OK; certainly reasonable for a product at this price level.

The plastic earpieces frequently come off while i'm removing them.

Finally, now, 2 or 3 months in, the right earbud has gone out; it's a bad connection at the microphone. I have carried them in a pouch left over from my other pair, and don't really use them much - only a couple times a week for an hour or two.

title: Decent audio quality, comfortable, low range with Macbook
review:
The sound on the earpiece is OK, but limited in audio bandwidth. Lots of low frequency and high frequency missing. Mostly middle frequencies of voice. Voice is quite understandable, but you can tell your voice bandwidth is being band pass filtered.
Mic sensitivity seems OK, and I am not able to test the ANC.

However, range is not great. On my Macbook Pro 2018, the built in Bluetooth and this headset only go line of sight. Any wall at all in between and the voice starts to drop packets fast.
As opposed to my Bose headphone which keeps in range much farther than this headset, with same Bluetooth host on same Macbook Pro.

title: In-ear not for everyone, even these
review:
first of all, the left channel was dead on arrival, but this was an Amazon Warehouse deal, so there's that.

However the working channel just did not sound good at all. No bass, very tinny treble.
I'd suggest it's mainly the compatibility of my ear structure and these in-ear headphone concepts.
I've tried very few, but never had good results. Even Apple ear pods, while sounding much better, have to be crammed in there to get decent sound. For me over the ear headphones work better, but they just are not at all travel friendly.

title: Decent but NOT for iPod....
review:
First of all, there is only one way to hear these headsets... if you swap ends, which you might think nothing of, the ear cups seem cheaply made and want to slide off your ear. Not until I got the orientation right did the whole headset seem right with the world and seal well to the ear.

Noise cancellation is decent. Let's face it, we're talking $70 here, not $400 for the latest Bose. Given what you're getting, it's a darn good deal, but not the excellent and almost total cancellation of the high end Bose units. I can still hear conversation - I would say voice is attenuated by around 6dB or so. But outside car and street noise is... well, absent. So it sort of achieves the goals I had.

The big issue is the volume! The sensitivity of the drivers is too low. The iPod of my son at max volume produces not near enough volume. Even my daughter with her younger ears was left wanting here. However, hooked up to my laptop, there is plenty of decibels and sound quality is decent. I say this owning Wilson Audio X1 speakers, so I am used to good sound :).

Overall, I am happy, and keeping the units.

title: Excellent sound and noise cancelling
review: Excellent sound AND noise cancelling technology. Worked great on a flight to muffle screaming children. Do not purchase if you want to sit in silence - the Bose QC35 may be better for that purpose - but do purchase if you are searching for the best sound quality in a wireless noise cancelling headphone. Sony's new HiRes LDAC wireless codec works flawlessly with Android 8.0+ devices (and hi fidelity music!). And, extra features are available with Apple devices via phone app or via the SBC codec on Android.

title: Great product
review: The price was right, and the product works as advertised.  It's the best wireless headset that I've used, and it works seemlessly with my razr.  No complaints here, except that the sound quality could be better at times, and there is some interference... but nothing major.

title: I'm in love with this product
review:
I'm in love with this product.

It's simple, small, energy efficient, and powerful.

Sure, it can get noisy, but I can handle it. After all, I have an air purifier nearby running at maximum fan speed and my apartment ventilation always running, and also have noise cancelling headphones. Honestly, I think it isn't too bad and you can still set it to throttle itself even more to keep it quieter while enjoying a good balance of horsepower for movies, games, and general productivity.

I've posted several photos of my unit in a [H]ardForum thread at http://hardforum.com/showthread.php?t=1825745 including disassembly and internals. There is a hidden full size HDMI port on the motherboard that is covered up by the back panel (removeable), not sure if it works.

Box comes with mini-DisplayPort and mini-HDMI cables and VESA mounts.

title: One I bought had defective jack
review: I bought one of these as a Christmas gift for my wife. The jack on the one we received was defective. When you plugged in the earbuds that came with the unit, you had to spin the plug in the jack to find the magic spot that made the connection -- but even then the connection did not hold. We tried another set of earbuds and high-quality headphones with the device, without success: The defect was clearly in the jack of the MP3 player. We requested a refund and the Amazon return procedure went off without a hitch -- so 5 stars for Amazon but only 1 for the Samsung YP-K3JAB (only because you cannot rate an item as zero stars!).

title: Works well; seems solid and durable; doesn't travel
review:
I have a 2-year-old ultral lightweight laptop that gets too hot for comfort. I used a Targus Chiller Pad for over a year, but it broke. All three Chiller Pads that my family has owned have broken down after a year of use. Thus, I was looking for something more durable this time around. The Cooler Master NotePal works well and seems built to last.

Your mileage may vary: I'm using a laptop that's much smaller than the widescreen NotePal, and I prop the front end up on the front edge of the NotePal rather than set it down flat on the surface of the thing. This allows more air to circulate underneath. It also allows me to access the volume control easily and the plugs for the headphones and microphone. Finally, if you need something you can haul along with your laptop frequently, I don't think this is what you'd want.

title: Overall good headphones, just minor complaints.
review:
I'm not really an audiophile so I won't comment much on the sound quality. I have no gripes about sound.

I only have two minor complaints about these headphones:
1. For extended periods of time, the ear buds can get a little uncomfortable. That could be said for many in-ear headphones though. So I just gave a half-star tick.
2. Slow to start/stop. This is just a personal nuisance. I can understand the 6 second button hold for learning a new pairing. However, pressing the power button for 6 seconds EVERY time I want to use the headphones is a little annoying.

title: Mediocre Sound, Cool Design
review:
I'm a bit of a self-confessed audiophile. Not the "I only listen to LPs on $20,000 speakers" kind of audiophile, but more of the college-student-budget kind of audiophile. To give a perspective on where I'm coming from with this review, my normal listening equipement is a pair of Bose QC35s, and I've also owned some nice Sennheiser over-ears. I rarely, if ever, use earbuds, but I needed something cool for general use with my computer.

THE BAD:
- These don't have any better sound quality than typical earbuds. In comparison with Apple's lightning connector earbuds, the Apple buds are a clear winner. They share the flaws of virtually all earbuds--horrifically tinny high mids, a distorted low mid, and sadly faint highs and lows. Take the other reviews about their amazing sound quality with a grain of salt. But, on the flip side, $200 Beats earbuds are a scam. Buy good headphones instead.
- For $20, well...at least try to beat Apple, you know?

THE GOOD:
- They look awesome! The colors and the wood styling are fantastic, and they look seriously cool.
- They are not nearly as bad as most consumer-level earbuds, and are for sure better than the old round-frame Apple earbuds that most people are still using.

Overall, these suit my needs and look cool while doing it, but they're nothing to write home about.

title: Minimal style, just the basics for a notebook and a few accessories
review:
In brief, the Brenthaven ProStyle SlimPack is definitely a minimalist take on a notebook backpack. I primarly wanted something to carry my MacBook Pro and miscellanous accessories. If you're the type of person who carries a lunch to work, look elsewhere. Here's an idea of what I carry:

- 15" MacBook Pro
- Charger w/ extension cable
- iPad 2
- A couple pens and pencils
- Earphones and sync cable
- Notebook

Anything beyond that requires a larger bag. Occasionally I can get away with a slim tupperware sitting on top of the internal opening, but then the flap barely reaches the button clasp.

Regardless, understand your needs for a pack like this. If you move to and from work with a light gear footprint, this bag works great.

title: Glad I bought them
review: I thought my earphones were going into the trash when one of my pads ripped off. But my son-in-law told me I could replace the pad. I found these after doing a search. They were at my door the next day and Way more comfortable than my factory pads.

title: Affordable, durable, adaptable
review: Decent sound. Comfortable in my ears. I like that they come with smaller sized "plugs" for different sized ears. The play/pause feature works well with my iPhone and iPad for music and Netflix watching. The color is great - not too bright (not gaudy), but also not black - so I can actually find it in the bottom of my backpack! These are good at blocking out most sound, so they great to study with. I'm not an audiophile so can't tell you anything about the specific sound qualities, but at this price - I'm not worried. I just needed something portable as my Sennhieser HD558's aren't exactly that. The cord length on these Skullcandys is standard and it is flat, as opposed to cheaper style headphones that have the rounded coating. My daughter with autism uses a set similar to these and loves them - no sensory issues with them at all.

title: Works great on mac with Skype but cords get easily tangled.
review:
I have a macbook pro and use Skype for most of my work calls. This headset works quite well with that set up -- call quality is good and I don't get any complaints from folks on the other end. The built in mute and volume control is very handy -- especially for ease of muting the call.

The only part that gets annoying is that the cords for the ear pieces continually get tangled up. That really sucks when an incoming call is ringing away and I'm busy trying to untangle the cords.

title: Well worth buying: awesome battery life and sound quality. Works with phone and computer.
review:
I was looking for a bluetooth headset I could use with my phone (Droid X) and more importantly, my MacBook Pro. The reason is is that I use Skype and Google Chat a lot for work calls and I was getting tired of being tethered to my computer with my headphones and using the internal microphone on my laptop (which would pick up my typing and be annoying for the folks on the other end of the call).

This headset has pricing on Amazon ranging from $45-$69, which is a great price and well worth spending.

The audio quality is superb and it is very easy to use and set up. The battery life has been to spec (what is listed in the description).

title: Great sound quality and great to use during exercise!
review:
For some reason I have never had any luck with standard ear buds. They always fall out and require constant attention on my part to keep them in place. I've also found they do not sound great (primarily because they have to face an odd way so I do not get proper alignment of the speaker into my ear). The ones that have the spongy piece you can insert in your ear canal are uncomfortable for me.

I was looking for earphones that:

1) Sound really good (good bass response and are not tinny sounding).
2) Are compact for travel.
3) I can run with them (which meant they will not fall out of my ear and require constant fiddling with).

This pair gets an A+ for all three of those requirements.

They speaker part is adjustable up/down and the part that hangs over your ear is adjustable also so that it is comfortable clamping around your ear.

Well worth the money.

title: Great for phone conversations. But decent audio quality is not in the cards at this price point.
review:
I bought these to listen to music while hiking. They seem well built. They pair easily. They stay in place. Sound rejection on the mic is good. Basically, these are great headphones for talking on the phone and a good value. But I'm fairly picky about audio quality and these just didn't work for me. No bass response and and unpleasant thinness on the high end made listening to music quite un-enjoyable .

I decided to spend more on a pair of Jaybird X3s. Frankly, the Jaybirds are not as good for phone conversations. And they are more than twice the price. But they have the audio quality I'm looking for, which is my priority. I'm pickier than most people about audio quality. If you're not an audio snob, these are good headphones at a decent price. Also, if you listen to music from the native iPhone music player, you can use Apple's sound equalizer settings to tweak the sound a bit and increase the bass. But the equalizer doesn't work if you use a third-party music player (Spotify, Pandora, Tidal...).

I doubt you can do much better in this price range, so I'm giving them 4 starts even though I returned mine.

title: BlueAnt T1
review:
I've been using a T1 for a few months now. It's a good news/bad news situation.

Voice quality is good on both end of the calls. Setup is easy. I don't find the voice control particularly useful, but some people might. The biggest problem is securing the T1 to your ear. The over the ear option is clunky and not particularly comfortable. The in-ear pads are comfortable, but not secure. Even with the largest ear pad, the headset is constantly falling out of my ear. Worse, the ear pad's are difficult to put on do not stay securely on the headset. That means if you keep the T1 in your pocket and pull it out to use it, you're likely to find the ear pad doesn't come with it.

Because the ear pad is constantly falling off, I managed to lose it, meaning I had to pay $16 (including shipping) for 2 replacement ear pads just to be able to use the headset I paid $60 for. The USB recharging cord is also ridiculously short, but it's a standard connector, so you can pretty easily find a replacement.
