At times, when you adjust the volume on the headset, the headset decides to drop the connection and reconnect (i sit really close the base, so it's not range). It doesn't drop your call, it just drops the connection to the computer.

Also, several of us have had issues with the computer not seeing the headset at times. It can be working one minute and not the next.

Other than that, the Savi 740 is a good unit. Range is fantastic and sound quality is excellent. If you're using it for voice calls mainly, you'll be a-ok. If you're using it for voip, prepare for a few hangups along the way.

title: Best eartip ever made
review:
The "black olives" as these are known can't be topped when it comes to comfort and sound isolation. I only wish they were compatible with non-Shure headphones.

I have nothing bad to say about them.

title: Solid pair of cans but there is room for improvement
review:
Many reviews make these headphones seems like they are the absolute best. They're a solid choice, but don't be fooled into thinking you're going to have a euphoric listening experience.

I'm an audio hobbyist and have experience with some moderately nice car audio SQ gear and have made some nice home audio speakers as well. So those experiences alter my perspective of what good music can sound like and the experience it can give you. You won't get that from these headphones, but they are still nice. I use them pretty much every day on my computer. If I want to have a fun listening experience I go to my living room or car.

title: 24 foam buds is a lot
review: I bought these because my foam earbuds from my previous headphones ripped. These worked great, except buying 24 of them was very unnecessary. I replaced the old ones about 5 months ago and they are still working just fine. Now I have 22 foam buds that are laying around my house. Still, a great product!

title: Amazing Device
review: This radio is brilliant.  Choose your favorites from thousands of crystal clear stations in every genre imaginable.  Log in to Mutant's affiliate website on your computer to formulate your favorites list which will be wirelessly transmitted to your device.  No wire required and no fees either.  A clear instruction manual is provided.  The included USB cable is used only to charge the battery, which, by the way, will really power the device for over 10 hours using the built-in speaker.  I clocked the run time to be sure.  It would probably go even longer using headphones.  (Initially use the fully charged battery until completely dead once or twice to ensure the longest run times.)  Pick up one of these.  You'll love it!

title: if you must..
review:
Not impressed at all.. I'm on my second pair of Apple Airpods and have used them almost exclusively for the gym. Sadly after about 14 months my first pair was shot. It was likely due to sweat "rusting" the charging rings. Not willing to see what Apple could do I went ahead and purchased a second pair, this time careful not to throw them back in the charging dock immediately after each workout. Well after about six months now I've started to experience the same issue I had with my first pair... Which lead me to bite the bullet and pay through the nose to get these water-resistant Beats wireless headphones...

As soon as I fired up Spotify I could not believe how bland the sound was.. Wow, paying $100 more for these I foolishly believed the Beats moniker would at least have a slight upgrade over the Airpods but nope, not to my ears..Listening to Podcasts sounded exactly like Airpods too.... All that said, I realize I'm a slave to Apple so am willing to pay the $$$ for what is often an inferior product just to stay in their eco system.. So it's on me... I just hope I don't have any issues with sweat degradation and if that turns out to be the case then (gulp) the price will be less cutting.

title: These earbuds fit comfortably in my ears and they STAY in
review: These earbuds fit comfortably in my ears and they STAY in, unlike the ones that came with my iPhone, which are painfully uncomfortable and fall out easily. I was pleasantly surprised with the sound quality considering the price.  I use these at work and at the gym to listen to music and watch shows/movies, and they do a pretty good job of blocking out external noise as well.  These are nice, inexpensive earbuds, and I like the fun blue color too!

title: Sleek and Long Lasting Battery!
review: The design is so sleek and fits in my ear perfectly! The battery is also really long-lasting for my long days, love these headphones for everyday use!

title: Like a glove.
review: Great product, just the right size for my Sol republic headphones. Pockets hold all the parts of the headphone when apart and even my iPod. Great for traveling.

title: Wonderful headphones
review: Great headphones! They do block out outside noise at the gym.  They make my ears hot when working out in the warmer weather.  But great for me in the winter.  Sound is wonderful.

title: They work great.
review: Not quite as comfy as I had hoped, but they'll suffice as replacements for my earbuds.

title: For the price it can't be beat.
review: These headphones are phenomenal for the price point. It might not be up to the standards of some audiophiles out there, but you won't likely find better headphones in this price range.

title: Great value!
review: They say that earbuds can cause hearing damage and we should stick with around the ear headphones.  I wanted to spend as little as possible on a quality product to listen to pandora with.  I am quite happy with these.  I can hear the layers and texture of the music well.

title: Never out of style
review: These aren't my first Porta Pros nor do I expect them to be my last. Koss' delightfully lauded budget headphones are a testament to the lasting longevity of a good design. While they may look *ridiculous* at best and horribly un-trendy at worst, the design is at least so laughably startling that you can't help but notice other PortaPros wearers (like a secret club). But who cares about looks? The true merit here is the remarkably good (well, acceptable) sound quality for such an otherwise inexpensive pair of headphones. I have a few significantly more expensive headphones and while these don't compete really at all with them, you're hard pressed to find a better sounding pair of headphones under the $50 range. I decided recently to pick up a new pair after losing my old one years ago -- might get an old walkman and really go all in on the outdated tech train. Jokes aside, Porta Pros are a great buy at any age, they should be everyone's go to for a cheap, lightweight and transportable pair of better-than-expected headphones. 5/5 forever.

title: Good sound but not great for using while on the move
review:
I bought these headphones as a cheaper alternative to a more robust pair of wireless headphones, like the pixel buds or airpods. Really, I bought them in late 2019 as a hold out for the pixel buds 2 and the USB C cable on my pixel 3 keeps giving out and I just didn't want to deal with the hassle of wired headphones any longer.

The sound quality is good. As someone who is used to listening on a respectable set of AKG 702s or Sony MDR-7056s they obviously don't stack up, but it's better than I would have thought to achieve for the price point, especially in the width of the soundstage.

My main gripe is the in-ear feel. They encompass your whole ear canal with sweaty, grippy plastic. The bad kind. Like the kind that makes it really hard to talk while wearing them, or when you move you hear a muffled rumpling with every step. I personally can't stand that and would prefer a more open ear feel, but that's just me. Just be aware of what you are buying, I find it hard to take calls wearing these as my voice seems to reverberate all throughout my head.

I keep them in my bedroom, where, if I want to doze off to some tunes they provide a decent option. Also, they are good for airplanes as the mild noise cancelling and isolation will drone out even the heftiest of plane sounds. As everyday headphones or workout headphones they are a no-go for me though.

title: best portable headphones i"ve used
review: I don't recall how I was directed to find the yuins, but after a series of bad portable headphone related disappointments I caved and bought these. They're amazingly good, far better than any other portable models I've used. I lost all of my fuzzy ear pieces, but they work just as well without them. I've had them for over 2 years now and they've been the best (and longest living) portable headphones I've had. Great purchase and great company.

title: Awesome headphones
review: I've owned several mid-high end headphones over the years, and a moderate audio enthusiast. I didn't mind spending a good chunk of cash, if it really made a difference. These are easily the best headphones I've owned, or heard in the price range. Comfortable and easy to wear for hours on end. I plug mine into an M-stage amplifier, and the sound is phenomenal. As with most things in this price range, though, if you're interested you should really try out all options available. Listen to some sennheiser or beyerdynamic models in comparable price ranges and see what works best for you.

title: What the ... HECK?!
review: I own a cheap pair of Soundpeats and an expensive pair of Google Pixel buds. For the money, the Soundpeats are good. The same can be said for the Google Pixel Pro buds, which are much more expensive but are also worth the cash. However, these Anker Liberty buds are surprisingly good. So good, they may set the bar in a whole new level. They are quite comfortable, which contributes to my criteria for a good fit (don't wiggle, good seal, don't fall out, don't cause ear pain). I spent several minutes completing the sound calibration in their app, which is slick and easy to use. After the sound calibration (which revealed my old ears are unable to hear certain frequencies), I was astonished how clear and clean the music sounded. I skipped around my library enjoying music from various genres and artists, enjoying the rich sound. The transparency mode is certainly better than the Google Pixel Pro buds. Don't get me wrong, I like my Pixel buds, but they are no longer my favorite buds. I only rated a 4 for battery life because I haven't had them a full 24 hours yet, so I can't rightfully evaluate the overall performance of the battery in either the buds or the case. I'll report back if I need to change that rating. Overall, these are stellar earbuds! I appreciate the app design, I love the form factor of the case and buds ... I'm going to carry these in my pocket as part of my EDC!

title: No end size keeps them from falling out of my ears.
review:
Wanted to like these, and honestly I do like the sound, and the "low power" voice warning is far less annoying than other pairs of wireless earbuds I have tried.
Seem to hold power nicely too.

But - I can't keep them from falling out of my ears.
I've tried all the different sized ends - smallest to largest.
They fall out of my ears.

Sigh

title: Awesome!
review: Love this EarPhones headband. I use it to watch TV on my computer in bed. FYI, you'll need to turn on before you connect to a device in order to sync properly.

title: Hard to change the soft earpiece part
review: Great sound out of these earbuds but trying to change the size of the earpiece part is a real challenge.

title: Nice place to store my JBL Flip 5
review:
HOMEQUIP's Hard Shell Case for JBL Charge 4 and Charge 5 Speakers, while it may run a little big for my JBL Eco Flip 5, I still liked the overall styling of this case better than the ones I found for the JBL Flip. Even though there is more room for my Eco Flip 5 to get jostled, I doubt that's going to make much difference in this hard-sided case for this tough little speaker, with room for my JBL earbuds too.

The Bottom Line: I know I made the right choice going with the HOMEQUIP Hard Shell Case for JBL Charge 4 and Charge 5 Speakers; at $9.99, it is so, SO much less expensive than any JBL portable speaker case I've looked at, and even though this runs big for my JBL Eco Flip 5 this is an excellent, secure hard shell case.

title: Excellent low volume headphones.
review: My kid loves them, thinks they make her look cool, but she can't figure out why they are not that loud. These headphones work as promised; her hearing is protected so Mama is happy.

title: So happy with this purchase
review:
So happy with this purchase. I came in faster than expected and was very easy to
put on my noise cancelling headphones. It's great to know I can replace the ear pad whenever I need to.
I would absolutely buy these again.

title: Surprisingly happy.
review: I decided to upgrade my headset and saw this on sale. I decided to give it a shot and am very impressed with it. It works well and is comfortable on my head. The Bluetooth setup was easy to use.

title: Not bad.
review: Got these for my daughter for school. They are good headphones but kinda confusing for her to set up.

title: Great quality
review: These headphones work great for me. Due to some ear issues, i need practical headphones for working out. These fit the bill to a T! I love them. The sound is great and they even sound really good when talking on the phone. Don't hesitate to purchase!

title: Good quality sound!
review: I purchased this for my wife because has a job in which she can use earbuds and this seemed perfect. The first thing I did upon getting the watch was to put the two pieces of the band together in my hand (with the watch face up) and shake it vigorously to see how well the earbuds stayed in place. They didn't budge!! I love it! The earbuds are small and discreet, the sound quality is great, the volume is great, its just an all around great watch.

title: Nice headphones, BUT!
review: I like them so far except for two issues which could make me decide to return them. 1. The overall fit! If I pull the back band down to rest lower on my neck, it places a lot of pressure on the back of my ears. OK, I have big ears. I like to wear them with the back support band under my long hair, so it does not tangle. I would prefer a headband over top of head better, like conventional headphones, or make them adjustable! 2. The EQ filter does not work! "Standard mode" is fine but "Vocal Booster Mode" causes heavy distortion, most noticeable while listening to conversational audio.

title: Very Good Value
review:
Just received the Avantree Audition Pro and I really love these headphones.
I have a low Latency Transmitter coming from Avantree for my OLD Samsung TV but in the interim i was able to pair to the Fire TV Stick (old Version). As expected there is about 200ms audio delay which I can compensate for inside of the Kodi App.
The headphones have plenty of volume control and the sound quality is very good although a little heavy on the Bass even with bass boost turned off. If I had the extra money to spend I would have selected the Aria Me which does have a frequency Equalizer built in.
I find the fit to be very comfortable for extended wear and although they are not noise canceling, they do block out most of the ambient room noise, especially from things like a room AC.
For the money, these are a very nice set of headphones!

title: Love These!
review: I connect to my Samsung Galaxy Tab S7 and to my iphone and have had minimal issues. The sound is clear and the connection range is great. I've never owned wireless headphones before so I'm not sure if they should have a wider range but I live on the 2nd floor of a condo and I can go downstairs to walk my dogs with my phone on the kitchen counter and they stay connected. I once went around my building and lost my connection so not sure if others would have stayed connected that far but for me it's fine.

title: My Son Says 5 Stars!
review: I bought these for my son and he has nothing bad to say about them. The sound is clear with no feedback. The headphones sit comfortably around his neck and the earplugs are comfortable as well.

title: Great Headset!
review: i ordered this because my fiance's other Plantronics headset died after using it daily for about 10 years. Because it lasted so long, he only wanted to purchase the same brand and this one works great and he highly recommends it. It never fails to have a nice, crisp sound...no weird feedback or interference. He's able to go from our home office to the kitchen, which is about 300 ft., and it sounds perfect! Once again...highly recommended!

title: Great sound, price, colors & durability!!!
review: Great color & so far durable, these are for my extremely picky yet destructive 11 year old daughter who has been through about a pair of earphones a month (I started getting them at the dollar store and they seemed to last as long as the others she had but at a fraction of the cost) we tried these on a whim, the colors are really nice and the price was reasonable. I’m glad I did, they’ve lasted for a few months now & they still work. The sound quality is good, the color selection is awesome, reasonably priced & they are really durable. Yayyy. We’re completely satisfied with these.

title: Took some fiddling, now they fit & sound great!
review:
I love the idea of wireless & Bluetooth... It’s great, they charged quick, paired to my iPhone instantly & with no extra apps or effort. The sound Is pretty good (as long as you have them wedged into your ears correctly) At first try they didn’t really fit right and sounded tinny, you somewhat have to fiddle with them to get the right fit & sounds. If you have them in right, you can drown out all outside noise, kids, barking dogs, complaining spouses & at a pretty low level. That’s a win right there. Getting used to how many times you have to tap the buttons on either left or right bud to control volume & rewind & forward, is still a challenge, but just one tap on the right one answers calls or pauses music. Great to use with my Amazon music. They’re an awesome pair of earbuds. So glad I gave them another try.
